mau.ten: Acer R3 (SCBC device R3, Realtek RTD2841A), India, Android TV 14 (SDK 34), build UKR1.251116
mau.header:
Acer R3 (SCBC device R3, Realtek RTD2841A), India, Android TV 14 (SDK 34), build UKR1.251116
Fingerprint ACER/ACER/R3:14/UKR1.251116/1236:user/release-keys. Plain Android TV, not Google TV:
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith is not installed on this unit, so there is no Wi-Fi/Home
handover trap from that app. Same SCBC/Realtek platform family as examples/acer-ar55ar2851udpro
and docs/devices/acer-ar55ar2851udfl.md (Realtek rtd2851m there, rtd2841a here).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.ps1 examples/acer-ar3-r3/debloat.txt   (or tools/disable.sh)
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.ps1 examples/acer-ar3-r3/debloat.txt   (or tools/restore.sh)
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (priority 2, isDefault=true). The only other HOME
claimants are com.apps.tvsettings (priority -999) and com.android.tv.settings (priority -1000),
both FallbackHome-style, not real launchers. set-home-activity stuck directly here: no
stock_home_redirect / HomeKeyService fallback was needed to take Home.
HDMI/AV: com.apps.passthrough. Live TV: com.apps.livetv with com.apps.atv / com.apps.dtv / com.apps.atsc / com.apps.isdb.

Applied and checked on one unit on 2026-10-29, in one batch with a screenshot before and after, then
one cold boot (power cable out): Home, Live TV's HDMI1/HDMI2/AV listing, HomeKeyService's Home button
and the launcher's dock all verified before and after the reboot. Every package below stayed disabled
across that reboot (pm list packages -d), confirming this Android TV variant does not re-enable
packages at boot the way the Google TV R4G note (docs/devices/acer-r4g.md) describes for a related
platform. com.google.android.videos (Google Play Movies) is not installed on this unit; its line is
commented out below so the list can still be applied as a whole.

Kept on purpose, do not disable:
- com.apps.passthrough, com.apps.atv, com.apps.dtv, com.apps.atsc, com.apps.isdb, com.android.providers.tv,
com.apps.livetv: HDMI, AV and the tuners.
- com.realtek.android.globalkeyhandler, com.realtek.keyinterceptserver, com.apps.smartkey, com.apps.virtualkey,
com.mk.tv.fivekey, com.apps.bluetoothremote: the remote's keys (Input, Settings, YouTube hotkey).
- com.apps.sys, com.mk.service.tvmidware: TV middleware (as the Haier com.cltv.mal note warns, #1578).
- com.apps.tvsettings, com.android.tv.settings, com.apps.smartmenu: settings UI and the picture menu.
- com.realtek.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer: supplies the Inputs button on tvlauncher.
- com.realtek.power, com.realtek.energymode, com.realtek.display.monitor, com.realtek.hw.configprovider,
com.realtek.media.notification, com.realtek.mdnsoffload, com.android.tv.mdnsoffloadmanager.
- com.realtek.factorytools, com.apps.factory.ui: factory menus, never launched (do not open them either;
see PROMPT.md and docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md on CVTE/Haier factory menus flipping a factory-mode flag).
- com.apps.ota, com.apps.authota: the firmware updater, left enabled; keep unless you have a reason not to.
- com.google.android.tv.remote.service, com.google.android.tv.dfuservice, com.google.android.presetup.bluetoothpair,
com.android.bluetooth, com.android.localtransport: remote pairing, firmware updates and Bluetooth.
- com.google.android.katniss: Assistant / voice search (mic button).
- com.google.android.apps.mediashell: Chromecast built-in.
- com.creative.fastscreen.tv: FastCast Miracast receiver (screen mirroring).
- com.google.android.inputmethod.latin, com.google.android.gsf, com.google.android.gms, com.android.vending,
com.google.android.webview: the on-screen keyboard, Play Services and Play Store.
- com.apps.logapp, com.apps.plugins: unclear/unknown-benefit system packages (logapp shares the system
UID; plugins reports the remote's battery level), left alone as this repo does for ambiguous packages.

Quirk on this firmware:
- The remote's YouTube button (keycode 2030) is intercepted below Android's input layer by the
persistent system service com.realtek.keyinterceptserver, which starts com.google.android.youtube.tv
by a package name hardcoded in its own compiled code. With that package disabled, every press throws
ActivityNotFoundException inside that persistent process, which Android then restarts in place
(harmless, but the button does nothing and logcat shows a crash/restart on every press). The
launcher's app_keys/InputKeyService remapping cannot reach this key at all: RtkInput's own log line
("ap decide result is 1") shows the vendor driver already claimed and handled it before Android's
normal key dispatch, let alone an accessibility service, ever sees it. Comment out the YouTube line
below if you want the button to open the real YouTube app without crashing anything; it cannot be
remapped to a different app on this firmware. Same limitation as the sibling
examples/acer-ar55ar2851udpro list.

New launcher: HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh (tvlauncher is disabled below; Home then
resolves straight to the new launcher with no redirect needed). Keep HomeKeyService bound even though no
stock_home_redirect is set: it is still what gives Home its long-press fallback and the Settings/Input
key mapping hooks, should you ever need them. If you enable it with the default key_filter=true and find
a held Volume Up/Down only steps once instead of ramping, this is the documented trade-off in
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md ("A key helper is bound and a held remote button stopped repeating"): set
key_filter to false in config.xml (or a theme) to get the ramp back, at no cost on this unit, since no
settings_key_keycodes/scancodes, input_key_keycodes or app_keys are used here. Confirmed on the remote:
both the volume ramp and config.xml's tile_menu (hold OK on a tile for Move / Replace / App info) work
correctly with key_filter=false.

mau.header:

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/acer-ar32hdigu2841at/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV and inputs: com.apps.passthrough.

DO NOT disable launcherx or com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith on this TV. The firmware re-enables
setupwraith early in every boot, so with launcherx off its RecoveryActivity loops and takes Home on the
next cold boot (see docs/devices/acer-r4g.md and examples/kalley-43g200).
Also, setupwraith owns the saved Wi-Fi network (dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*').
Keep launcherx enabled and use HOME_KEY_SERVICE with stock_home_redirect=com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
to redirect Home to the new launcher without triggering RecoveryActivity loops.

Cold boot behavior: Acer/Realtek's modified settings runs SetPmodServiceJob at cold boot which re-enables
packages from a hard-coded list (see docs/devices/acer-r4g.md). On this firmware, 7 packages stay permanently
disabled across cold boots (com.apps.usbmediaplayer, com.apps.mk.wd, android.autoinstalls.config.scbc.device,
com.android.tv.feedbackconsent, com.realtek.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer, com.mxtech.videoplayer.television,
com.apps.wifihotspot). The remaining packages stay disabled across warm reboots and sleep/wake, but are
re-enabled by the firmware if the TV undergoes a full cold boot.

Kept on purpose: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (stock home, needed for boot safety),
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (owns Wi-Fi network), com.apps.passthrough (HDMI / inputs),
com.apps.smartmenu (picture/display menu), key handlers (com.apps.smartkey, com.apps.virtualkey,
com.mk.tv.fivekey, com.realtek.keyinterceptserver, com.apps.bluetoothremote), com.apps.sys,
com.mk.service.tvmidware, Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), and user streaming apps
(YouTube, Netflix, Prime Video, Hotstar, Aha, Crunchyroll, Zee5, Airtel Xstream).

Firmware updaters: com.apps.ota, com.apps.authota, com.realsil.ota, and com.google.android.tv.dfuservice
are kept enabled by default (commented out below). They are turned off by choice on the author's TV.

mau.header:
Acer AR55AR2851UDPRO 55" (SCBC device R4, Realtek rtd2851m), India, Android TV 14, firmware UKR1.260308
Build UKR1.260308, incremental 3272 (the R4G 50" note's set is 5597)

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/acer-ar55ar2851udpro/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/acer-ar55ar2851udpro/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (Android TV, not Google TV: launcherx is not installed).
HDMI and AV inputs: com.apps.passthrough. Live TV: com.apps.livetv with com.apps.atv / com.apps.dtv.

Not the same as the Acer R4G 50" in docs/devices/acer-r4g.md (MOKA R4_GTV, Google TV 14), although the
build is the same. Boot runs Acer's own com.apps.tvsettings/.ui.FallbackHome, and nothing came back:
after three cold boots (power cable out for 30 s) all 28 packages below stayed disabled, including ten that
the R4G firmware re-enables at every boot (play.games, feedback, gdpr, esticker, tvmanager, meeting.service,
timeclock, audiolink, scast, fastscreen). No RecoveryActivity in logcat.

setupwraith owns the saved Wi-Fi network on this set (dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'): leave it enabled.
Port 5555 opened with `adb tcpip 5555` after Wireless debugging pairing stayed open across all three cold boots.

The remote's YouTube button never reaches Android: com.realtek.keyinterceptserver takes it (keycode 2030) and
starts com.google.android.youtube.tv by package, so app_keys cannot remap it. With YouTube disabled, every press
crashes that persistent service (ActivityNotFoundException); Android restarts it at once and nothing else
breaks. Comment out the YouTube line below if you want the button to work.

New launcher: see README.md and config.json here. Home stays on tvlauncher with set-home-activity, so the
launcher takes the Home button through HOME_KEY_SERVICE with stock_home_redirect (tvlauncher stays enabled).

Kept on purpose: com.realtek.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer (supplies the Inputs button on tvlauncher,
as on the Compac ATV R2), com.apps.passthrough, com.apps.smartmenu (picture menu), the key handlers
(com.apps.smartkey, com.apps.virtualkey, com.mk.tv.fivekey, com.realtek.keyinterceptserver,
com.realtek.android.globalkeyhandler, com.apps.bluetoothremote), com.apps.sys, com.mk.service.tvmidware,
firmware updates (com.apps.ota, com.apps.authota), Assistant, Chromecast, Netflix, Prime Video, Backdrop.
Not touched: com.apps.factory.ui and com.realtek.factorytools (never started), com.apps.biz.ds and
com.apps.biz.mt (unclear), com.seraphic.hbbtv.app, com.apps.usbmediaplayer.

Tested on one set on 2026-10-24, in three batches with a Home screenshot after each, then a cold boot:
Home, HDMI input, Prime Video, Assistant mic, casting, Home/Back/volume/Settings keys work. Then five more
packages (Play Movies, speed test, partner setup, basic screensaver, TalkBack) and two more
cold boots, with the new launcher on Home. AdGuard Private DNS validates and Prime Video plays with it.
Fresh, not yet lived with for days; update it if something breaks.

AiPro2K (Expressluck, device dongnae), Android TV 14, firmware UKN6.260116.085
Same Changhong "AI PONT" family as examples/rca-ai-pont and examples/chiq-gtvu65, but vendor apps are
Expressluck / CVTE instead of Homwee. 1 GB RAM (MemTotal about 930 MB), UI 1280x720 at 213 dpi.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it as STOCK_LAUNCHER)

Tested on one set (the same day it was applied, not a multi-day soak): after applying the list, installing
launcher/ and rebooting, Home opens the new launcher, HDMI 1-3 switch from the dock and the Inputs menu,
Netflix launches, the microphone button and the phone remote work, and logcat shows no FATAL or ANR.
The IP did not change across the reboot, but a DHCP reservation is still a good idea.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/aipro2k/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx

Already disabled from the factory (do not re-enable them on restore): com.cltv.hybrid,

- com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter(.plus), com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard: Live TV and the Inputs menu.
- com.google.android.apps.mediashell: Chromecast.
- com.google.android.katniss: microphone button and voice search.
- com.google.android.tv.remote.service: controlling the TV from the phone.
- com.epl.hotkey (HotKeyDispatcher, runs as system, has INJECT_EVENTS): probably handles the remote's

- Factory packages (com.cvte.tv.at, com.at.factory.*, com.express.at.factory.factorymanager,
com.expressluck.facmenu, mediatek.factorymenu.ui).
- com.google.android.tv.dfuservice, googletvremotepairer, com.google.android.tv.inputplayer.

The apex packages below (adservices, ondevicepersonalization, federatedcompute) accepted `pm disable-user`.

- With launcherx disabled, Home falls to com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity, so

- com.google.android.gms shows a Google sign-in dialog when an app is started from the command line; it
is Play Services, not something on this list.

mau.header:
AIWA AI PONT SA (Changhong, brand AIWA, device osaka, product ISDB86AW)
Google TV 14 (API 34), firmware UKNV.260603.001, security patch 2026-06-01,
MediaTek mt5867. About 1.4 GB RAM (MemTotal 1448260 kB).
Same "AI PONT" family as examples/rca-ai-pont (device redwood, stock tvlauncher)
and examples/benq-e55-735 (launcherx), but this board is osaka.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/aiwa-ai-pont-sa/debloat.txt
Dock:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/theme.sh examples/aiwa-ai-pont-sa
config.json is the layout that was on the test set. The dock is 4 columns:
TV ao vivo, Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video. Globoplay is the 5th favourite,
so it is the first tile of the row below. Edit dock_apps before pushing.
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/aiwa-ai-pont-sa/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
The remote's source button is not KEYCODE_TV (it sends KEY_G), so INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1
alone doesn't bring it back yet; see the quirks below.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Live TV: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter
Pass launcherx to restore.sh. Its default stock launcher is
com.google.android.tvlauncher, which this firmware does not have.

Tested the same day on one set, not a multi-day soak. Packages marked
"already disabled" shipped that way. The others were disabled in this session
and were still disabled after a power cycle, before the new launcher was
installed. launcher/build-and-install.sh with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 then set
com.gathin.tvhome as Home.

Checked on that home, by screenshot and by the window in front:
- D-pad moves focus across the dock and down into the grid.
- With config.json applied, the focused hero is "TV ao vivo" and the dock is
TV ao vivo, Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video. Globoplay is the first tile below.
- Inputs lists HDMI 1, HDMI 2, composite ("No device") and Live TV.
- HDMI opens com.google.android.tv.inputplayer/.player.PassthroughPlayerActivity.
- Live TV in that menu, and the TV ao vivo tile, both open
com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter/.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity. The system input player
on the tuner URI stays black on this set, so the menu must not use it.
- com.netflix.ninja/.MainActivity starts, and Home returns to the new launcher.
- Streaming apps left enabled: Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Globoplay,
Disney+, Max, Apple TV, Claro tv+, Paramount+, Spotify.
- The remote's source button was captured with getevent on
"MStar Smart TV IR Receiver": MSC_SCAN 0040bf5b and linux KEY_G (scan 34),
19 times across 6 presses because the IR code repeats. It is not KEYCODE_TV,
which is why the button did nothing at first. On the author's branch (a separate
launcher change, not on main yet), treating KEYCODE_G / scan 34 from that IR
device as the Inputs button made one press on the home screen open the Inputs menu. Confirmed by the person
holding the remote. Not rechecked from inside another app. A keyboard G is
not consumed. sendevent on the IR device is denied to the shell, so the
press could not be injected.

KEEP, even though some names look like bloat:
- com.homwee.dmt.upgrade: firmware updates. com.homwee.upgrade below is the
vendor app updater; the Play Store still updates apps.
- com.homwee.factory, com.homwee.synckey, com.homwee.dynamicbacklight (picture).
- com.homwee.mmp.fileexplorer, com.homwee.mmp.imageplayer.
- com.mediatek.* (Live TV, inputs, remote pairing), including
com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.autopair and
com.mediatek.androidbox.
- com.mediatek.android.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer. Left enabled. On the
Android 11 CHiQ list, disabling it crash-loops com.mediatek.tv.service after
a reboot, and this set was not reboot-tested with it off.
- com.google.android.gms, com.android.vending, and the streaming apps.

Quirks on this firmware:
- USB debugging alone opens network ADB on port 5555. There is no separate
wireless-debugging pairing step.
- Standby can drop the TV off Wi-Fi. After a power cycle, check port 5555
before assuming the old address.
- Home claimants, in order: launcherx/.home.HomeActivity (priority 2),
setupwraith/.MainActivity and setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity (priority 1),
then com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome. Disable setupwraith
before launcherx, or Home lands on the setup wizard. The launcher package
is commented out below so disable.sh does not remove Home first;
launcher/build-and-install.sh disables it after the new home is set.
- The stock screensaver was com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx/.service.Backdrop.
After dreamx is disabled, com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors is the fallback
until the launcher Clock dream is selected.
- The launcher's Wi-Fi pill shows the network name only while Location is on.
On the test set location_mode was 0, so the pill read "Wi-Fi".
- Two hardware tuners are registered: AnalogInputService/HW7 and
TunerInputService/HW0. Alphabetical order picks the analog one. Live TV in
the menu still launches the app above, not a passthrough URI.
- Inputs on this remote: see the getevent note above. The source button isn't mapped
on main yet. input_key_keycodes [35] (KEYCODE_G) with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 would
catch it, but also every G typed on a keyboard.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/disable.sh examples/alwtniet-hy320-mini/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/restore.sh examples/alwtniet-hy320-mini/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Applied 2026-10-21 and lived with since: Wi-Fi, the
remote, YouTube and Spotify keep working, and the launcher (STOCK_LAUNCHER=none) owns Home.

Getting ADB: Settings > About > press OK on "Build number" seven times. This firmware says
"Setup mode turned on" rather than "You are now a developer". Developer options is then under
System; USB debugging opens port 5555. ro.adb.secure=1 (the Allow prompt appears).

Kept on purpose:
- com.htc.htcsettings: the projector's own settings (keystone, focus, picture).
- com.htc.closedialog: the power-button menu (it holds REBOOT and SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW).
- com.hotack.writesn: factory serial/MAC writer that starts at boot. Left alone here, as
disabling it while connected over Wi-Fi risks losing the connection.
- com.android.nfx (NFXAccessibility, v1.1.3, updated in /data): left on here; the Portronics list
disables it without issues.
- com.htc.htclauncherhighenglishd08: the stock Home. build-and-install.sh does not recognise it, so
run it with STOCK_LAUNCHER=none; set-home-activity takes Home and the stock one stays as fallback.

Firmware notes:
- The panel is 1280x720 but ships at density 240, which gives apps an 853x480dp screen. TV apps and
the launcher are laid out for 960x540dp: `wm density 213` (undo: `wm density reset`) fixes the
cramped layout.
- Low-RAM device (about 30 MB free with apps running), yet Android still allowed a notification
listener (`cmd notification allow_listener`).
- The unit arrived with unofficial streaming apps in the user partition, not the system image
(HDO Box, a "Cinema HD" build as com.yoku.marumovie.analytics, Sports Zone, UKTurks, StreamFire,
Drama Player). A factory reset removes them; they are not listed here because this list only
disables. com.hotack.silentsdk (the dropper on some H713 units) is not present on this build.

stack trace once per run (reported on Fire OS 8), which the batch carries on past:
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, 'Fire TV (Fire OS)'.)
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
ADB on Fire OS 6: Settings > My Fire TV > Developer options > ADB debugging. If Developer options is hidden,
Settings > My Fire TV > About > highlight the first entry and press select 7 times. Port 5555, no pairing.

Lived with since 2026-10-18 on one stick (the group dated 2026-10-19 for one day less). Nothing had to be re-enabled.
Protected by Fire OS 6 (pm disable-user is refused without root), so commented out below: com.amazon.client.metrics,
com.amazon.device.metrics, com.amazon.minerva.client.api, com.amazon.device.logmanager, com.amazon.device.crashmanager,
com.amazon.diode, com.fireos.usagestats.proxy, com.amazon.ftvads.deeplinking, com.amazon.tv.csapp, com.amazon.tv.oobe.
No com.amazon.tv.acr on a stick (ACR is a TV-set thing).

Second unit, same model and build (AFTMM, NS6711/5908), Europe, 2026-10-22: the list above applied cleanly.
Three more packages are protected on this build: com.amazon.tcomm, com.amazon.securitysyncclient and
com.amazon.whisperlink.core.android ("Cannot disable a protected package"). With com.amazon.vizzini disabled, Fire OS
re-enables it at every boot (all other disabled packages stay off), so dropping voice search means re-running
disable.sh after each reboot. Disabling the casting group at the end closed ports 8009, 55442 and 60000 on the LAN.
With Fire OS parental controls on ("PIN protect app launches"), any start of another app over Amazon's home,
including a Home-watcher launcher from SHOWCASE.md, opens the Prime Video PIN prompt every time.
After 10 days two disabled third-party apps (Disney+, RaiPlay) were enabled again, both updated meanwhile, most likely
by Appstore auto-update; the Amazon packages all stayed off. Check `pm list packages -d` now and then.

Kept on purpose: com.amazon.tv.launcher, com.amazon.tv.settings.*, com.amazon.venezia (Appstore),
com.amazon.tigris (Appstore UI), OTA updates, remote/Bluetooth services, com.amazon.tv.ime (keyboard),
com.amazon.vizzini (Alexa voice search for the remote mic) with com.amazon.aria/cardinal (its screens),
Prime Video (com.amazon.firebat, com.amazon.tv.support), display mirroring and DIAL casting
(com.amazon.cast.sink, dialservice, ssdpservice, whisperlink/whisperplay, awvflingreceiver),
screensaver, profile picker, accessibility (com.amazon.logan) and TTS. The streaming apps this owner uses
(Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, Apple TV, DirecTV, Crunchyroll, YouTube) are not listed; the rest are, by choice.

What the list cannot remove: the "Sponsored" hero banner and sponsored app row are fetched by the launcher itself
from amazon-adsystem.com. Private DNS needs Android 9, so on Fire OS 6 set an ad-blocking DNS (AdGuard 94.140.14.14 /
94.140.15.15) through a static IP in the Wi-Fi advanced settings, or block *.amazon-adsystem.com on the router.
Also turn off Settings > Preferences > Featured Content autoplay and the three Privacy Settings toggles.
Gotchas: a reboot resets the favourites bar to Amazon's defaults; OTA updates may re-enable packages, re-run
disable.sh afterwards; Netflix is DRM-black in screenshots.

mau.header:
Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K, 2nd gen 2023 (AFTKM, codename karat), Fire OS 8.1.8.5 (RS8185.3891N, build 0033018557316),
Android 11 (SDK 30), Brazil. The first Fire OS 8 list here: it starts from amazon-fire-tv-stick-lite-2020/ and
amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2018/, and every package new in Fire OS 8 was checked with `dumpsys package` before listing.

FIRE OS: DEBLOAT ONLY. Home is com.amazon.tv.launcher/.ui.HomeActivity_vNext (priority 950); launcher/ does not apply.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<stick ip> tools/disable.sh examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<stick ip> tools/restore.sh examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/debloat.txt com.amazon.tv.launcher
For the whole list, put HANDLERS_ALLOW=1 in front of the Apply line ($env:HANDLERS_ALLOW=1 for disable.ps1). Since
2026-10-23 disable.sh keeps the app that answers VIEW vnd.android.cursor.item/channel, read as the HDMI input
handler, and here that is com.amazon.tv.livetv/.TvChannelsPlayerActivityAlias: a stick has no tuner or HDMI input.
Seen 2026-10-25 on a Fire TV Stick 4K Plus (AFTMA08C15, karat, RS8185.3891N): livetv was the only listed package
the check held back; the Settings handlers (com.amazon.tv.launcher, com.amazon.tv.settings.v2) are not listed.
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
ADB on Fire OS 8: Settings > My Fire TV > About > press select 7 times on the device name, back > Developer Options >
ADB Debugging. Port 5555, accept the prompt on the TV (ro.adb.secure=1).
The stick's USB port carries ADB too, over a data cable rather than a charge-only one: on Fire OS 8.1.8.5 an AFTKM
listed as "product:karat model:AFTKM" in `adb devices`, and its owner replayed this restore's `pm enable` lines
through the stock `adb -d shell` when network ADB was not answering (#2950). tools/tv.py, disable.sh and restore.sh
talk AdbDeviceTcp and never USB, so that cable is the stock adb by hand: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md's Connecting
section has the network routes.

Applied 2026-10-20 in four batches with a screenshot after each, then rebooted: all 57 stayed disabled, Home, Prime
Video, Netflix, Globoplay and Disney+ open, Wi-Fi validates.
Protected on this build (pm disable-user: "Cannot disable a protected package"), so commented out below, the same set
as Fire OS 7 plus the help app: com.amazon.device.metrics, com.amazon.device.logmanager, com.amazon.device.crashmanager,
com.amazon.diode, com.fireos.usagestats.proxy, com.amazon.ftvads.deeplinking, com.amazon.tv.csapp.

Kept on purpose: com.amazon.tv.launcher, com.amazon.firehomestarter, com.amazon.tv.settings.*, com.amazon.venezia and
com.amazon.tigris (Appstore), com.amazon.tv.ime, remote/Bluetooth services, OTA updates (device.software.ota*,
tv.forcedotaupdater.v2), Alexa voice search, Prime Video (com.amazon.firebat, com.amazon.tv.support), casting and
mirroring (cast.sink, dialservice, awvflingreceiver, whisperplay, whisperlink, com.amazon.tv.matter for Matter
casting), Amazon sign-in for apps (com.amazon.tv.ottssocompanionapp, com.amazon.imp), profiles, com.amazon.tv.oobe
(needed for a factory reset), the screensaver, accessibility (com.amazon.logan), notification center.
com.amazon.imp confirmed load-bearing on a second AFTKRT unit (same karat board, Fire OS 8.1.8.5): disabling it
together with shoptv.client, shoptv.firetv.client, media.recommendations, sneakpeek, systemnotices, tv.earlyaccess
and tv.acr left HomeActivity_vNext resumed and the remote fully responsive, but painted nothing -- confirmed black
on the physical TV. Re-enabling just those eight (imp included) fixed it within seconds, no reboot needed; the
other seven were not re-tested standalone, so this list's existing success with them already disabled stands.
Fire OS 8 packages looked at and left alone: com.amazon.adep (package verification / security events),
com.amazon.platform.fdra (package allowlisting), com.amazon.tv.turnstile (PIN sign-in), com.amazon.tv.consents,
com.amazon.ssm / ssmsys (captive portal, error codes), com.amazon.tiramisubootsupport, com.amazon.d3 (has a demo
content provider but also OOBE and provisioning receivers).

What the list cannot remove: the hero banner, the "Patrocinados" (Sponsored) row and the Luna tile in "Your apps"
come from the launcher's own feed. Point the stick's DNS at a blocker for those (Pi-hole, or Private DNS
dns.adguard-dns.com on Android 11). Also turn off Settings > Preferences > Privacy Settings (Device Usage Data,
Collect App Usage Data, Interest-based Ads) and Featured Content autoplay in the menus: those values sync with the
Amazon account, so the menu is the place to change them, not `settings put`.
Prime Video registers only LEANBACK_LAUNCHER, so `monkey -p com.amazon.firebat 1` does nothing; start
com.amazon.firebat/com.amazon.pyrocore.IgnitionActivity with `am start -n` to test it.
Leave the animation scales at 1.0 on this build. At 0.5 (window, transition and animator) every entry in the
side menu (☰: Settings, Appstore, My Stuff...) closes the menu and goes back to Home without opening anything:
NavigationActivity logs "onStop with slideoutState=false, finishing to prevent stuck menu" before the navigation
request is sent. Back at 1.0, Settings opens again with all 57 packages still disabled.

mau.header:
Amazon Fire TV Stick Lite, 1st gen 2020 (AFTSS, codename sheldon), Fire OS 7.7.1.7 (PS7717/5741, build PS7717.5741N), Android 9 (SDK 28), 1 GB RAM, India
Same Fire OS build as toshiba-fire-tv-aftha004/. Based on amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2018/ (same keep choices: voice search,
Prime Video, casting, OTA) with the telemetry additions from the Toshiba list.

FIRE OS: DEBLOAT ONLY. com.amazon.tv.launcher is a protected package and keeps Home; launcher/ does not apply.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<stick ip> tools/disable.sh examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-lite-2020/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<stick ip> tools/restore.sh examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-lite-2020/debloat.txt com.amazon.tv.launcher
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
ADB on Fire OS 7: Settings > My Fire TV > Developer Options > ADB Debugging. Port 5555, accept the prompt on the TV.
Switch it off again afterwards (`settings put global adb_enabled 0` from the shell does it and closes 5555).

Protected on this build (pm disable-user: "Cannot disable a protected package"), so commented out below:
com.amazon.minerva.client.api, com.amazon.device.logmanager, com.amazon.device.crashmanager, com.amazon.diode,
com.fireos.usagestats.proxy. Not on this stick: com.amazon.client.metrics, com.amazon.whisperjoin.wss.wifiprovisioner.
Rebooted after applying: everything stayed disabled, Home, Prime Video and Netflix open, Wi-Fi validates.

Kept on purpose: com.amazon.tv.launcher, com.amazon.tv.settings.*, com.amazon.venezia (Appstore), com.amazon.tv.ime,
remote/Bluetooth services, OTA updates, Alexa voice search (com.amazon.vizzini, aria, cardinal, ivona TTS, tcomm),
Prime Video (com.amazon.firebat, com.amazon.tv.support), miniTV (com.amazon.minitv.android.app), casting
(cast.sink, dialservice, awvflingreceiver, whisperplay, whisperlink), profiles (com.amazon.prism.android.service),
com.amazon.tv.oobe (must stay enabled for a factory reset), screensaver, accessibility (com.amazon.logan).

Not packages, but worth doing on a 1 GB stick (Settings > Preferences): Privacy Settings > Device Usage Data,
Collect App Usage Data and Interest-based Ads OFF; Featured Content > Allow Video Autoplay and Allow Audio Autoplay OFF.
The privacy intent (com.amazon.device.settings.action.PRIVACY_SETTINGS) is refused from the shell, so drive the menus
with input keyevent. Developer animation scales at 0.5 also help.

What the list cannot remove: the hero rotator and the Prime Video promo strips come from the launcher's own content
feed. Router-wide AdGuard DNS did not remove them on this stick either.
Gotchas on this build: the shell cannot disable single components of third-party apps (boot receivers):
"Shell cannot change component state". `exec-out screencap` can return a truncated PNG over a weak Wi-Fi link;
`screencap -p /sdcard/s.png` then `pull` is reliable. Netflix screenshots come back empty (DRM).

mau.header:
Anker Nebula Mars 3 Air projector, model D2325 (build name Nebula_Mars_2_V2, device taihang,
ANKER board, MediaTek m7332), Google TV 14 / Android 14 (SDK 34), build UKNV.260210.001.
No tuner: live_tv_package stays "" and the Inputs menu lists HDMI 1 / HDMI 2 only.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/disable.sh examples/anker-nebula-mars-3-air/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/restore.sh examples/anker-nebula-mars-3-air/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Google TV 14 Home quirk (the important one): while the setup wizard (setupwraith) is enabled,
cmd package set-home-activity prints Success but Home still resolves to setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity,
so the new launcher never comes up (the same behaviour as xiaomi-tv-a-pro-2026). Disable it before
build-and-install.sh disables the stock home; the wizard is only used for first-time setup, and
restore.sh brings it back. Re-enable it before a factory reset. Unlike the D2426 Capsule
(anker-nebula-d2426, where setupwraith owns the Wi-Fi but never claims Home), here it owned only
one old hidden network that was no longer connected; the network in use belongs to android.uid.system
and kept working after the disable, verified live before proceeding. Phone casting kept working too.
On other Google TV units the Cast receiver loses its credentials with setupwraith gone and phone
casting fails with "Untrusted device" (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) - re-enable setupwraith if your phone
refuses to cast.

Re-enabled by the firmware at every boot (checked with one reboot on 2026-10-22):
com.google.android.katniss (Assistant) comes back enabled, the same behaviour as anker-nebula-d2426.
This owner keeps it on, so the mic button works and nobody re-disables it after each boot.
To keep it off instead, uncomment com.google.android.katniss and com.google.android.tv.assistant
below and run Apply again (disable.sh records them first, so Undo brings them back); after each
boot, tools/check.py --fix <this file> re-disables what came back.

Already disabled at the factory: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.google.android.marvin.talkback.

Remote buttons on this firmware (dumpsys window policy, mKeyMapping): the gear button's
KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION (83) is consumed by GlobalKeyManager for the stock launcherx, and the Netflix
button's KEYCODE_BUTTON_4 by com.mediatek.tv.service's NetflixKeyReceiver - both mapped by the
static overlay com.mediatek.android.tv.globalkeyoverlay, which no shell command can turn off
(cmd overlay disable throws a SecurityException, and disabling the package changes nothing: static
overlays ignore package state). Neither key ever reaches an app, so com.netflix.ninja stays ENABLED
for the Netflix button (it is in the launcher's dock instead), and Settings is the gear pill in
the launcher's top bar (top_menu in the config.json here). Keep the launcher's key-filtering
services off (key_filter false, no INPUT_KEY_SERVICE / HOME_KEY_SERVICE build flags): on this
firmware any bound key service turns ramping volume into one step per press.

DO NOT DISABLE on this model (projector hardware, inputs, remote):
com.mediatek.tvinput                       # HDMI input service
com.mediatek.tv.service                    # TV service, global keys, Netflix key receiver
com.google.android.tv.inputplayer          # HDMI passthrough player
com.mediatek.tv.inputplayeroverlay         # HDMI overlay
com.oceanwing.receiver                     # remote control, Nebula IME, accessibility, screen control
com.zhixin.nebulasmart                     # remote events, accessibility service
com.zhixin.remoteautopair                  # Bluetooth remote auto-pairing
com.oceanwing.nebulalinker                 # device info, custom shutdown, firmware update dispatch
com.zhixin.apphelper                       # package install helper, HTML viewer
com.zhixin.projector.settings              # picture / focus / keystone / battery / update UI
com.zhixin.nebulasetupwizard               # Nebula first-run wizard (not Google's setupwraith)
com.mediatek.wwtv.mediaplayer              # USB media player
com.mediatek.wwtv.webview                  # webview the settings apps use
com.dolby.android.audio.service            # Dolby audio processing
com.google.android.inputmethod.latin       # the on-screen keyboard
com.google.android.tv.remote.service, Play Store and Play Services

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (.home.HomeActivity); the install script disables it.
Live TV: com.cltv.hybrid (Anoki "LiveTV", AnokiTvInputService). HDMI 1-4 = com.mediatek.tis/.HdmiInputService/HW2-HW5,
AV = com.mediatek.tis/.CompositeInputService/HW6, DVB tuner = com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.dvbtuner/.DvbTvInputService/HW0.

(cmd wifi forget-network) before setupwraith was disabled. The network in use belonged to android.uid.system.

Tested on 24 October 2026 on one set, including two reboots, with the real remote. Same-day test, not a
multi-day soak. Order used: this whole list (setupwraith included) while launcherx still owned Home, then
launcher/build-and-install.sh, which disables launcherx once the new launcher is running.
The home screen was launcher/ from this repo; config.json beside this list has its dock and the gear key.
Network ADB on 5555 survived a reboot on this set (service.adb.tcp.port=5555), Wireless debugging was on too.
com.haier.gamingbar comes back enabled at every boot (seen on the first reboot), so it is commented out below.

Remote ("SmartTV-RC Consumer Control", BLE HID): Netflix, YouTube, Input and Mic keep working with no helper
(com.mediatek.tv.agent and Haier global-key receivers). The YouTube Music button opens YouTube Music, which
forwards into YouTube on this build. The Prime Video button goes to Prime Video (disabled here, so nothing).

mau.header:
Bell Fibe TV (ARRIS VIP7802, codename vip7802_bell), Android TV 11 (SDK 30),
firmware RTT4.240509.001 (build 11.02.02.02.160-RC.149, release-keys).
This is Bell Canada's IPTV set-top box, not a TV: Bell's launcher and remote key handling
stay, and this list leaves the HDMI/CEC and Netflix-key packages alone (see below).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<box ip> tools/disable.sh examples/bell-fibe-tv-vip7802/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<box ip> tools/restore.sh examples/bell-fibe-tv-vip7802/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.custom.tvlauncher (Bell/ARRIS, not AOSP's com.google.android.tvlauncher).
There is no separate Live TV package: Fibe content plays through ca.bell.chiclet.fibehelper,
a real content app (see "Not disabled" below), and this box registers no
android.media.tv.TvInputService at all.

This box does not carry much ARRIS/CommScope bloat once content apps are left alone: the default
list below is 12 packages - telemetry, two stub apps with no logic at all, and five Google TV
services most owners would not miss (Play Games, Play Movies & TV, YouTube Music, Android TV's
own feedback reporter, and the stock recommendation-row service, which this box's own launcher
doesn't even read). Each of those five is still a real, separate thing, not telemetry; comment
out any line below if you want it back - that's the convention this repo's other lists use for a
package that's genuinely a personal call (see examples/anker-nebula-d2140, examples/asus-m1g for
the same pattern: disabled by default with a comment, not held back as opt-in).

It does not touch content apps, including the ones Bell preloaded (CTV, TSN, Noovo, TOU.TV, the
Weather Network, iHeartRadio, Tubi, the Fibe player itself): those are free, ad-supported services
real people use, the same way Fire TV lists in this repo keep Prime Video, Amazon Music and Luna
by default and only flag them as the owner's own choice to remove.

A separate, opt-in block lower down holds mainstream streaming apps (Netflix, Prime Video,
YouTube) and three ARRIS features with a minor, skippable function (UPnP/DLNA, the customizer's
resource overlay, Play Auto Install) - the streaming apps the same way examples/acer-ar3-r3 and
examples/dexp-a651 in this repo offer Netflix and Prime Video as removable, for an owner who
genuinely doesn't use one. Assistant voice search, Chromecast casting and the phone-as-remote app
are NOT in that block: unlike UPnP or Play Auto Install, those are mainstream features most owners
would reach for and miss immediately, so they're not offered at all - see "Kept deliberately" at
the end. Seven other ARRIS/CommScope packages this list also looked at are not in this file at
all, in any form either: six declare a real feature (factory reset, diagnostics, find-my-remote,
network setup, remote-key/power-button/HDMI-CEC handling), and the seventh (com.arris.oemdata)
looks like telemetry but breaks another package if disabled - a debloat list is for bloat, and
none of these seven qualify - see "Kept deliberately" for what each one does and why it's
excluded, not just held back.

"AI PONT" platform is sold as CHiQ (see the CHiQ DVB93CQ example in PR #10).

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/benq-e55-735/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it as STOCK_LAUNCHER).
Already disabled from the factory: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.google.android.marvin.talkback.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- USB debugging alone does NOT open port 5555 until the first reboot. Pair once with Wireless
debugging instead: `adb mdns services` shows the random pairing and connect ports, then
`adb pair <ip>:<pairing port> <code>` and `adb connect <ip>:<connect port>`. After a reboot,
with USB debugging still on, plain port 5555 answers.
- Home keeps going to com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity after the stock
launcher is disabled: setupwraith must be disabled too (listed below).
- Standby is MediaTek suspend-to-RAM: once the CPU suspends (seconds after the screen goes off,
when no wakelock is held), Bluetooth and Wi-Fi stop. A Chromecast voice remote (Bluetooth only)
then cannot turn the TV on; the BenQ IR remote and the power button can. Holding a wakelock
to prevent it confuses the vendor standby (panel off, system awake, ARC broken). Wake-on-LAN
does work from deep standby: a magic packet to the Wi-Fi MAC brings the TV up in about 5 s.
- The Chromecast remote's Input button sends KEYCODE_TV, which the stock launcher handled. Its
YouTube and Netflix buttons have no key layout on this TV (HID usages 0x0c0077 / 0x0c0078
both arrive as KEYCODE_UNKNOWN), so they do nothing once the stock launcher is gone.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- There is NO Wireless debugging toggle while the set is on Ethernet, and USB debugging alone never
opens port 5555 (it answers "Connection refused" even after a reboot). The TV's only open ports are
6465-6467, 8008-8010, 8443 and 9000. Move the TV to Wi-Fi: Wireless debugging then becomes tappable
and pairing works. Its connect port is random and changes on every reconnect, so resolve it with
`adb mdns services` instead of hard-coding one. A reboot switches Wireless debugging off again.
- The TV's USB ports are host-only. "Select USB configuration" offers MTP/PTP/RNDIS in developer
options, but a cable to a computer enumerates nothing, so there is no ADB over USB.
- The saved Wi-Fi network is owned by setupwraith (`dumpsys wifi | grep cname=`). Forget the network
and re-join it from Settings before disabling setupwraith, or the TV drops off Wi-Fi and ADB with it.
- Home keeps going to com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity after the stock
launcher is disabled: setupwraith must be disabled too (listed below). build-and-install.sh stops
with that exact message and re-enables the stock launcher, so run the list first, then the script.
- com.gdch.wwtv.mediaplayer asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE and HDMI_CEC, so tools/disable.sh skips it, but
it is a false positive: `pm query-services -a android.media.tv.TvInputService` answers only
com.mediatek.tis (HDMI/Composite/Component), com.mediatek.tv.agent and com.mediatek.autopair. HDMI
was checked on the set after a reboot with it disabled. It needs TVINPUT_ALLOW=1.
- The remote's gear button sends HID consumer usage 0x000c009f, which evdev reports as KEY_UNKNOWN,
so the stock launcher was the only thing answering it and it does nothing once launcherx is
disabled. settings_key_scancodes 786591 (the MSC_SCAN value) did NOT catch it; what the framework
reports is keyCode 83 / scanCode 240, as on the PEAQ AI PONT unit in #853. Its Netflix and YouTube
buttons emit no input event at all, with or without a helper. The Input button is 0x000c0097 /
KEY_TV2 and keeps working.
- HOME_KEY_SERVICE with key_filter TRUE costs key repeats here, as on the TCL G09 build: holding
volume up steps once per press instead of ramping. The final setup below keeps the helper bound
with key_filter FALSE, which is what gets the ramp back; see the two bullets after this one.
- power_on_home is not needed on this set: the firmware already resumes com.gathin.tvhome at
power-on by itself (wm_set_resumed_activity in `logcat -b events`).
- The gear button is a global key: `dumpsys window policy` routes KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION to
com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx/.remotecontrol.GlobalKeyListener_Receiver (NOT to
com.homwee.factory, which takes SOFT_LEFT/CALL/CAMERA/AT/PLUS here, so #853's factory-menu
caveat does not apply to this unit). A temporary Log.w at the top of MainActivity's
dispatchKeyEvent showed the gear never reaches the focused window at all, while DPAD_DOWN does
(keyCode=20 scanCode=108) - so an Activity-level route is impossible and only a bound helper,
or launcherx itself, can answer it.
- Held volume with HomeKeyService bound and key_filter true: the same Log.w in the helper's
onKeyEvent logged the gear (keyCode=83 scanCode=240) twice and **no volume event of any kind**,
down or repeat. That is the onKeyEvent evidence docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md asks
for ("a future report that logs the repeat event arriving at a helper"): on this set the helper
never receives the volume key, so the launcher cannot be the one dropping the repeats, which
matches the AOSP reading in that note. Android 14 / SDK 34, a sixth vendor.
- key_filter false then gives the ramp back while the helper stays bound for the home redirect,
and the gear keeps working because launcherx answers it, not the helper (the Sony BRAVIA VU3
arrangement). Measured working on this set.
- Assistant content search ("大谷翔平") is drawn inside launcherx's own home screen: katniss sends
VIEW https://tv.google.com/... to .gateway.LauncherDeepLink, launcherx then starts
.home.HomeActivity with the results. With stock_home_redirect set, HomeKeyService bounces that
screen to this launcher about 240 ms later and the results are gone - no error, just nothing.
So stock_home_redirect and Assistant content search cannot both work here; voice app commands
("open Netflix") are unaffected. With launcherx disabled entirely the same search fails with an
on-screen error, as docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md describes for the onn 4K box.
- Re-enabling launcherx takes Home back immediately: `cmd package set-home-activity` prints
Success and changes nothing (priority=2 outranks this launcher), as on the Hisense set.
- This firmware does not re-enable anything at boot: the disabled list was identical after a reboot.
- There is a second, dormant user (10, "new_user"). `pm disable-user --user 0` does not touch it.

- Inputs menu: nothing on this TV answers ACTION_VIEW on a passthrough input URI. com.toptech.tvmenu/.MainActivity

by asking its provider. A launcher intent that carries the type never matches; an explicit component does.

cast/AirPlay/DLNA (com.ecloud.*), the USB media browser (com.rtk.mediabrowser, com.hitv.explore), the Aptoide

- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to android.uid.system, not to a setup wizard, so nothing here deletes it.

asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE and the guard reads that as the HDMI/AV/tuner layer. On this set
that is a false positive: the permission is requested, nothing implements a TvInputService.
What settles it is which packages actually serve that service:

Here that lists only com.mediatek.tvinput (tuner, HDMI, VGA, composite, component, SCART) and
com.mediatek.tv.service, both kept. Disabled by hand and reboot-tested: all seven inputs and
the source panel still work. Use TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 to disable it, and check your own inputs
after a reboot before trusting this on another model.

com.vestel.tv.eib (the E-User Manual app).

all stay enabled. The Coocaa AirPlay app is off by choice. io.github.jqssun.airplay (the repo
README's AirPlay answer) installs and runs correctly on this hardware: it registers
_airplay._tcp and _raop._tcp through NsdManager and listens on 7000. It is useless on a managed
network that isolates clients, though, because mDNS never reaches the other devices. Check with
`arp -n <tv ip>`: a placeholder MAC means proxy ARP and no AirPlay discovery, whatever you install.
Toshiba owner's choices: Netflix, Prime Video, Disney+, YouTube, Chromecast and the aerial
screensaver (com.google.android.backdrop, kept) stay; Assistant (katniss) off as below, which
leaves that remote's microphone button doing nothing; RiksTV off (commented line below).

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- With USB debugging on, network ADB answered on port 5555 straight away.
- Home goes to com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity (priority 1) once launcherx is
disabled. It logs "Reenabling disabled home activity", fails, and only then falls through to the new
home, adding a delay on every Home press. A third-party HOME filter is capped at priority 0, and
`pm disable-user` on the RecoveryActivity component alone is refused for the shell
(SecurityException), so the whole setupwraith package has to be disabled (listed below).
- Inputs switch through com.google.android.tv.inputplayer/.player.PassthroughPlayerActivity
(ACTION_VIEW on TvContract.buildChannelUriForPassthroughInput). Input IDs look like
com.mediatek.tvinput/.hdmi.HDMIInputService/HW5 (HDMI 1-3 = HW5-HW7, AV = composite HW2).
- HDMI and Live TV screenshots come out black (protected video layer).
- The Wi-Fi pill shows the network name once ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION is granted; Location is on by default.

mau.header:
Skyworth Coocaa K3 Pro 90P3D Max (system board 8R145_P3DM, Realtek RTD2885N),
Android 11 (SDK 30), build eng.www-da.20231205.132148, China-market Coocaa OS.
First China-market Coocaa (Realtek) list in this repo. The export Skyworth lists in
this folder (com.skyworth.* Google TV builds) share nothing with this firmware: here
the namespace is com.coocaa.* / com.tianci.* and the stock launcher is
com.tianci.movieplatform.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/coocaa-k3-pro-90p3d-max/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/coocaa-k3-pro-90p3d-max/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED (pm disable-user --user 0), not uninstalled. Comment out any
line you want to keep.

⚠ CRITICAL: NEVER disable com.tianci.movieplatform (the Coocaa launcher). The 8R145
boot flow hard-depends on it: disabling it hangs the TV on the COOCAA logo, the remote
becomes unresponsive, and the only recovery is a factory reset from recovery mode
(verified the hard way). It is deliberately absent from the list below.

ADB: this firmware hides Developer options. ADB is toggled from the Coocaa factory
menu (a secret key sequence), not from stock Settings, and ro.adb.secure is set, so
the TV still shows the "Allow USB debugging?" prompt. The ADB toggle resets on every
reboot - re-enable it from the factory menu after rebooting.

Launcher notes (for anyone porting cleanyourtv to this set):
1. Almost no app declares a leanback entry on this firmware: the Home grid starts
nearly empty (only the app store resolves LEANBACK_LAUNCHER). The TV app
(com.skyworth.tv), local media (com.tianci.localmedia), TV manager
(com.coocaa.tvmanager) and settings (com.coocaa.os.softsettings) only resolve the
plain LAUNCHER category - they need the app-library mechanism to appear on
Home/dock.
2. The launcher needs a plain CATEGORY_LAUNCHER intent-filter on MainActivity so it
shows up in the Coocaa launcher's "My Apps" list (that list only queries LAUNCHER).
3. The Home key is hard-coded by the firmware to bring up com.tianci.movieplatform;
the accessibility HomeKeyService cannot intercept a standard Home key press
(Android platform limitation), so no launcher can own the Home button here. The
launcher is set as the default Home (cmd package set-home-activity) and reached
from the stock "My Apps" list.
4. The firmware never broadcasts standard boot events (BOOT_COMPLETED,
QUICKBOOT_POWERON) to third-party apps, so auto-start on boot is not possible
without root.
5. "Boot source" is also hard-coded: "Signal source" on boot launches
com.skyworth.tv (TV app) via firmware logic - there is no app-selection option.

Verified: 23 packages disabled with pm disable-user --user 0, then a full reboot.
Home, the source panel, local media, TV manager, app store, casting, settings and the
remote all still work. Fully reversible with restore.sh.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (Android TV home with Search/Home/Live/Shop/Apps tabs, not
Google TV's launcherx). HOME claimants on stock: tvlauncher and com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome.

KEEP, the Android side drives the projector itself:
- com.epson: projector control (auto focus, auto keystone, cinema/picture modes, Bluetooth speaker mode).
- com.epson.droidsettings (projector menu), com.epson.flexiblepicture, com.epson.installation,
com.epson.visualization, com.epson.warningui (lamp/temperature warnings), com.epson.bizmodeui.
- com.epson.logcollection: it collects operation logs, but it also owns the Information screen
(com.epson.intent.action.INFORMATION). Disabled, Projector Settings > Information crashes Projector
Settings with ActivityNotFoundException. Opt out of operation logs on that screen instead.
- com.droidlogic.tv.extras: input-source screen (com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS) and sleep timer.
- com.droidlogic.tvinput, com.droidlogic.android.tv, com.droidlogic.tv.settings: HDMI inputs and settings.
- Firmware updates kept by choice: com.epson.fwupdate, com.droidlogic.updater, com.askey.autousbota.

Notes from this unit (verified with screenshots, 21 October 2026):
- Only Wireless debugging (TLS) is offered; pair once with `adb pair`, then `adb tcpip 5555`. Port 5555
came back by itself after a reboot.
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to setupwraith (cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith), but
setupwraith does not claim HOME here, so it stays enabled and is not in this list.
- Launcher: install and HOME takeover work (mFocusedApp = com.gathin.tvhome after Home and after a reboot).
Inputs lists HDMI 1-3 (droidlogic HW5-HW7, HDMI 1 also as a CEC device); HDMI opens in
com.droidlogic.android.tv, so keep that enabled and only hide its tile. No tuner, no Live TV row.
- Remote ("EPSON PJ REMOTE", BT, Vendor_005d_Product_0001.kl): Home, Input (opens droidlogic's source
screen), Settings, projector menu and mic all keep working without the stock launcher.
The YouTube button is usage 0x0c008d -> KEYCODE_MACRO_3, and Epson's PhoneWindowManager.startCustomApp
hard-codes it to com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic (Play Store page if that is missing), which forwards
to YouTube. It runs in interceptKeyBeforeQueueing, so app_keys cannot remap it; keep YouTube Music enabled.
The Apps button (ALL_APPS) goes dead once tvlauncher is disabled: Android 14 consumes it before
accessibility services and sends it only to a system launcher, so HomeKeyService cannot catch it either.
- Reboot-checked: everything listed stays disabled. Left out on purpose:
com.google.android.tvrecommendations. Disabled, it is back to enabled=1 within minutes, with
`dumpsys package` naming com.droidlogic (Amlogic's system package) as lastDisabledCaller. It only feeds
the stock launcher's rows, so with that launcher gone it is harmless; don't keep disabling it.

Notes from a second unit (same HA90 module and firmware, sold as an Epson HA90, 25 October 2026):
- com.google.android.katniss (Assistant) gets the same treatment as tvrecommendations: disabled, it is back
within minutes with lastDisabledCaller com.droidlogic. Disabling it doesn't stick; leave it.
- Amlogic's TV extras app carries a hidden "Startup Setting" (Settings.System tv_start_up_enter_app, 0 =
launcher, 1 = TV app) and a "Power on behavior" slice; set over adb and reboot-checked, the key changes
nothing on this firmware: Home still comes up. To start on an HDMI port, use the launcher instead
(boot_to_live_tv opens com.droidlogic.android.tv, which returns to the last source).
- Android 14 names the foreground activity topResumedActivity in `dumpsys activity activities`; HDMI on
screen gives a 0-byte screencap.
- Disabling com.epson.fwupdate, com.droidlogic.updater and com.askey.autousbota (updates off by choice) and
com.epson.onlinemeetings, com.epson.logcollection kept as above: Projector Settings > Picture, Sound,
Installation, Information and Bluetooth Speaker Mode all still open.

fronted by fr.freebox.fbxdtvkit) and IPTV through OQEE (net.oqee.androidtv), which is the Live TV app.

(live_tv_package net.oqee.androidtv), or put OQEE in the dock.

the TV app then stops at "Vérifiez votre connexion réseau". Worse, a session refreshed while it was
blocked stayed broken after the DNS went back: the app logged "invalid access token" until
`pm clear com.spotify.tv.android` and a new login. With Spotify, use a personal NextDNS / AdGuard
DNS profile that allowlists pixel.spotify.com, or no ad-blocking DNS at all.
Standby is not a reboot (uptime keeps counting), and ADB stays reachable through it.

Wi-Fi/setupwraith gotcha confirmed again on this unit, same as wanbo-x5-pro and byintek-t5-max:
dumpsys wifi showed cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (the network saved at first
setup), so disabling it or launcherx first drops Home to setupwraith's RecoveryActivity, which

android.uid.system. Only then disable setupwraith and launcherx and set the new launcher's Home.

Wireless debugging (stock `adb pair`/`adb connect`), then `adb tcpip 5555` got a plaintext port
tools/tv.py can use (adb_shell has no STLS/TLS support, and this firmware answers wireless
debugging's port in TLS only). `adb tcpip 5555` and the Wireless debugging toggle both reset on
every reboot; re-pair (or re-connect if still trusted) each time, then re-run `adb tcpip 5555`.

(confirmed on wanbo-x5-pro too); not attempted here.

mau.ten: Chromecast with Google TV 4K (2020, device sabrina, product sabrina_prod_stable), 2 GB RAM
mau.header:
Chromecast with Google TV 4K (2020, device sabrina, product sabrina_prod_stable), 2 GB RAM
Google TV 14 (SDK 34), build UTTC.250917.004 (14193937)
Second unit: Canada, same build, one day of use (2026-10-22). Notes under "Second unit" below.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<ip> tools/disable.sh examples/google-chromecast-gtv-4k/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<ip> tools/restore.sh examples/google-chromecast-gtv-4k/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
To keep phone casting and the stock home (no new launcher), use debloat-keep-cast.txt in this folder instead.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. No Live TV app and no HDMI inputs (it's a dongle):
leave live_tv_package empty in config.xml.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- ADB on port 5555 is closed (connection refused) until you pair once through Wireless debugging with
the stock adb: Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code, `adb pair
<ip:pairport> <code>`, `adb connect <ip:connectport>` (`adb mdns services` lists both ports), then
`adb tcpip 5555`. After that tools/tv.py works on 5555
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "USB debugging never opens port 5555").
- `cmd package set-home-activity com.gathin.tvhome` returns Success but launcherx stays the default.
Disable BOTH com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx and com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
(setupwraith re-enables launcherx), only after the new launcher is installed.
- WARNING: setupwraith can own a saved Wi-Fi network on this model too, as on the HD. On the second
unit `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` named com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith as the
creator of one of its two saved networks; the network it was on when checked was created by
android.uid.system:1000. Android deletes an app's saved networks when the app is disabled, so
disabling setupwraith deletes that network, and if the stick is on it, Wi-Fi and ADB go with it.
Before disabling setupwraith, forget that network and join it again in Settings > Network &
Internet until every cname reads android.uid.system:1000 (the HD list, same build, also removes it
under Wi-Fi > App preferences). tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith while it owns a network, and
FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 overrides that (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "The TV drops off Wi-Fi for good").
- Disabling setupwraith also breaks casting from phones, reported on the Chromecast HD on the same
build (#361). The Cast receiver (com.google.android.apps.mediashell) reads its factory device
credentials from a provider inside setupwraith
(com.google.android.libraries.tv.setupwraith.libs.castinfo.CastInfoProvider), so once the wizard
is gone and the device has rebooted, YouTube on the phone answers "Untrusted device ... couldn't
be verified" and the receiver logs "No private key, hence empty signature" every minute. Keeping
the provider while taking Home away does not work: pm disable-user on
setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity is refused with a SecurityException. Either debloat only (keep
launcherx and setupwraith enabled), or re-enable setupwraith after each boot, wait a minute for
"Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner" in logcat, then disable it again - the receiver
holds the credentials in memory, so casting works until the next reboot
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Casting fails with Untrusted device").
Seen again after a reboot: re-enabling setupwraith brought no ClientAuthSigner line within 3 minutes
and phones did not list the device at all. Restart the receiver while setupwraith is enabled:
pm enable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
logcat -c
am crash com.google.android.apps.mediashell
The system starts it again with a new pid, and "Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner"
follows within seconds. Check that pid (pidof com.google.android.apps.mediashell) is still the same
30 s later, then: pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
Not am force-stop plus am start-foreground-service: started that way the receiver never calls
startForeground(), Android kills it after 30 s, and the copy that comes back with setupwraith
already off has no credentials (the signer line came from the killed process) (#2615).
- Turning USB debugging off leaves Wireless debugging listening on its own port. Switch both off when
you are done. tools/adb-closed.py checks 5555 unless it is given that port: note the port from
`adb mdns services` first, and check it with tools/adb-closed.py <ip> <port> before the reboot.
- With launcherx disabled the YouTube button on the remote does nothing. It sends BUTTON_3
(keycode 190). Button Mapper only remaps added buttons in its paid Pro version; Key Mapper
(open source, keymapperorg/KeyMapper) does it for free. Play Store lists Key Mapper as incompatible
with this device, so install the -foss APK from its GitHub releases, then over ADB:
pm grant io.github.sds100.keymapper android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services io.github.sds100.keymapper/io.github.sds100.keymapper.system.accessibility.MyAccessibilityService
Map trigger "Button 3" (short press) to action "Launch app > YouTube". Record the trigger with the
physical remote: keys injected with `input keyevent 190` don't reach Key Mapper, and D-pad presses
made while recording get added to the trigger.
- com.google.android.tvrecommendations and com.google.android.apps.education.cast2class ship
disabled at the factory; `pm disable-user` on them fails with "Shell cannot change component
state". Don't add them to a restore list either.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Point it at the launcher's clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
- Animation scales already ship at 0.5x on this build.
- Disable in small batches, and wait before walking away. A run that disabled 21 packages in one
batch had every one report "new state", then the device rebooted: 19 of the 21 were back
afterwards. PackageManager writes package-restrictions.xml asynchronously, so a package disabled
seconds before a reboot is lost while ones disabled minutes earlier (launcherx, setupwraith)
survive. Four batches of 4/4/4/7 with a 20-second pause after each, checking the device is still
up between them, went through with no reboot.
- If the device does reboot, check the uptime before assuming a crash loop:
GET http://<ip>:8008/setup/eureka_info reports it, and one reboot with a steadily climbing
uptime afterwards is not a loop.

Second unit. The list's telemetry and preloaded-app groups were applied (the screensaver pair and
setupwraith were kept), plus a few apps by choice;
after a reboot the disabled list was unchanged. Private DNS validated, and YouTube and Plex loaded
their profiles. Power and Ethernet came through one USB-C hub.
- On Ethernet the Wireless debugging toggle flipped straight back off: unplug the cable, join Wi-Fi
and pair as above. Wireless debugging also went off at every reboot (Wi-Fi drops during boot) and
had to be switched on again by hand; the pairing was kept and the stock adb reconnected on its own.
Port 5555 from `adb tcpip` lasted until the next reboot.
- The hub stayed powered with USB debugging on: `ip link` still listed eth0 (NO-CARRIER only because
the cable was out), while `dumpsys usb` printed host_connected=false and sys.usb.config was "none",
so host_connected=false was no proof the hub was gone. With USB debugging still on, plugging the
Ethernet cable back in brought the Chromecast up on Ethernet, and tools/adb-closed.py then reported
5555 refused (not checked whether that came from a restart or from Wireless debugging going off).
- The remote ("Chromecast Remote", 18d1:9450; /odm/usr/keylayout/Vendor_18d1_Product_9450.kl is not
readable from the shell) shows YouTube and Netflix as KEY_UNKNOWN in `getevent -lt`, with MSC_SCAN
000c0077 and 000c0078: the usages the Google TV Streamer list maps to BUTTON_3 (190) and
BUTTON_4 (191).
- Home by redirect: launcherx and setupwraith left enabled for casting, stock_home_redirect set to
com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx, HomeKeyService enabled by hand. launcher/build-and-install.sh
with STOCK_LAUNCHER=none installs, then stops at its Home check, as expected while launcherx is
Home. Home pressed in an app landed on the new launcher. After a reboot the TV stayed on the Google
TV home: it is drawn before Android binds HomeKeyService, so no window change reaches the redirect
(#698 and #1024 work on this). With launcherx kept as Home, tools/check.py needs it as the second
argument, or every run reports Home as drift: the Check line in debloat-keep-cast.txt, which is the
list this setup matches.
- With the redirect on, the YouTube button did nothing although launcherx was enabled. The redirect
opens the launcher with ACTION_MAIN + CATEGORY_HOME, so this is consistent with #698's explanation
(this launcher becomes the Home process and launcherx loses its Android 14 exemption for background
activity starts, BAL_BLOCK), but no BAL_BLOCK line was captured in logcat. app_keys
"190:com.google.android.youtube.tv" and "191:<package>" in a theme, handled by HomeKeyService,
worked with both buttons on the real remote. (Seen on a build with a local boot check added to
HomeKeyService; the redirect's intent was main's.)
- Holding Volume Up on the real remote still ramped with HomeKeyService filtering keys (key_filter at
its default) and Button Mapper's accessibility service enabled as well. Not checked with
HomeKeyService alone.

Kept on purpose: Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), Cast receiver
(com.google.android.apps.mediashell), phone remote (com.google.android.tv.remote.service), Play Store /
Play Services, Gboard, Bluetooth, com.google.android.tv.dfuservice (remote firmware updates).
The receiver itself stays enabled, but casting still needs setupwraith for its credentials
(see the setupwraith quirks above).

mau.ten: Chromecast with Google TV HD (2022, device boreal, product boreal, Amlogic S805X2), 1.4 GB RAM
mau.header:
Chromecast with Google TV HD (2022, device boreal, product boreal, Amlogic S805X2), 1.4 GB RAM
Google TV 14 (SDK 34), build UTTC.250917.004 (14193937), security patch 2025-10-01

Apply:   TV_HOST=<ip> tools/disable.sh examples/google-chromecast-gtv-hd/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<ip> tools/restore.sh examples/google-chromecast-gtv-hd/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Same firmware build as the 4K model, so examples/google-chromecast-gtv-4k applies almost as is; this
list is that one minus com.google.android.apps.tv.netoscope, which the HD doesn't ship, plus the Play
Auto Installs config stub.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. No Live TV app and no HDMI inputs (it's a dongle):
leave live_tv_package empty (a theme with "live_tv_package": "" does it without a rebuild).

Known quirks on this firmware:
- ADB: the same one-time pairing as the 4K (Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with
pairing code, `adb pair`, then `adb tcpip 5555` on the device `adb devices` lists). Port 5555 closes
again on every reboot and Wireless debugging switches itself off; turn it back on (no new pairing
code needed, stock adb reconnects by mDNS) and run `adb tcpip 5555` again.
`adb mdns services` lists the stick's current address on the _adb._tcp port; the unit takes a new
DHCP address after a re-join or reboot (this one alternated between two), so read the address there
before reconnecting.
- WARNING: Wi-Fi joined during the first-run setup belongs to setupwraith (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o
'cname=[^ ]*'` printed com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith), and Android deletes such a network
when setupwraith is disabled (see examples/sony-bravia-9-ii). The HD has no Ethernet, so that drops
ADB too. Before disabling setupwraith: Settings > Network & Internet > your network > Forget, then
join it again. The owner then reads android.uid.system:1000, and disabling setupwraith kept Wi-Fi.
tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith while it still owns the network.
Google TV 14 also shows the wizard's saved network under Settings > Network & Internet > Wi-Fi >
App preferences; removing it there, then joining the network in Settings, leaves every owner
android.uid.system. Joining the router's other band's SSID (the 2.4 name of the same router) creates
the system-owned entry, so FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 then deletes only the wizard's unused copy. Verified
on a second boreal unit, 2026-10-23.
- setupwraith has to go before the launcher can own Home, as on the 4K: launcherx is HOME priority 2,
setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity priority 1. launcher/build-and-install.ps1 then switched Home on the
first try.
- WARNING: disabling setupwraith breaks casting from phones ("Untrusted device ... couldn't be
verified"). setupwraith hosts the CastInfoProvider the Cast receiver (mediashell) loads its factory
device credentials from; without it logcat shows `cast_ClientAuthCredsFactoryProvisioned: Cannot get
device credentials` once a minute and auth replies go out unsigned. adb can't disable RecoveryActivity
alone ("Shell cannot change component state"). Either keep setupwraith and launcherx (debloat only),
or enable setupwraith until mediashell logs `Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner` and then
disable it again: the receiver keeps the credentials until it restarts, so that is needed after every
reboot and whenever the receiver restarts (crash, force-stop, update). Cast Fix (SHOWCASE.md) does it
at boot; it ran on every reboot during the trial and phone casting worked each time. Details in
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md ("Casting from a phone fails with Untrusted device", issue #361).
Cast Fix 1.0 (thayford/castfix) was verified on a second boreal unit, 2026-10-23: paired with the
PairReceiver broadcast, `adb_allowed_connection_time` set to 0, and the boot run logged
"Cast credentials loaded" -> "Casting ready."; the cast log showed
"Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner", and phone casting, HOME and the mic button
worked after the reboot.
- With launcherx disabled the remote's YouTube button does nothing (the Netflix button still works).
Same fix as the 4K: Key Mapper's -foss APK from GitHub (4.6.1 here), `pm install` from
/data/local/tmp, then the `pm grant` / `settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services` lines
from the 4K list, and `dumpsys deviceidle whitelist +io.github.sds100.keymapper` to clear its
battery warning. Don't `am force-stop` Key Mapper over ADB: that unbinds its accessibility service
until the setting is cleared and set again. Record the "Button 3" trigger with the physical remote.
The -foss APK from its GitHub releases, version 4.6.2, is what the second unit (2026-10-23) runs.
- The "type on your phone" prompt that never works: default_input_method was
com.google.android.tv.remote.service/.ImeBridgeService before anything here was changed. Gboard is
installed and enabled, so the on-screen keyboard comes back with
`ime set com.google.android.inputmethod.latin/com.android.inputmethod.latin.LatinIME`.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Point it at the launcher's clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
`cmd dreams start-dreaming` needs root here; to see the screensaver, set screen_off_timeout to
60000 for a minute and put it back (600000 by default).
- Location is off by default, so the launcher's Wi-Fi pill shows "Wi-Fi" instead of the network name.
- Only 1.4 GB RAM (about 480 MB available with Home idle) and a 4.3 GB /data partition that was 82%
full before anything was installed; the launcher's 270 KB APK fits, larger sideloads may not.
- com.google.android.tvrecommendations and com.google.android.apps.education.cast2class ship
disabled at the factory, as on the 4K. Don't add them to a restore list.
- AdGuard Private DNS (README) validated; Spotify loads and Tubi plays with it on.

Lived with from 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-21 (several reboots and a full power cycle), nothing re-enabled.
The new launcher comes back as Home with Wi-Fi connected; the Assistant mic button, the remote's TV
volume buttons, Home from inside an app, PBS Kids, Tubi and Spotify playback, casting from a phone
(YouTube) and a tablet (Disney+) with Cast Fix, and Play Store app updates (com.wbd.stream updated
on 2026-10-21) all work.

Kept on purpose: Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), Cast receiver
(com.google.android.apps.mediashell), phone remote (com.google.android.tv.remote.service), remote
pairing and TV control setup (com.google.android.tv.axel), Play Store /
Play Services, Gboard, Bluetooth, com.google.android.tv.dfuservice (remote firmware updates),
com.netflix.tokenmanager.
