mau.ten: Google TV Streamer (2024, device kirkwood, model "Google TV Streamer" / GZRNL), 4 GB RAM
mau.header:
Google TV Streamer (2024, device kirkwood, model "Google TV Streamer" / GZRNL), 4 GB RAM
Google TV 14 (SDK 34), build UTTK.260317.003

Cast-preserving five-package alternative, tested on a second unit: see README.md and debloat-keep-cast.txt.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<ip> tools/disable.sh examples/google-tv-streamer-4k-kirkwood/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<ip> tools/restore.sh examples/google-tv-streamer-4k-kirkwood/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

This is a dongle: no Live TV app and no HDMI inputs, so leave live_tv_package empty in config.xml.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- ADB on port 5555 is closed (connection refused) until you pair once through Wireless debugging with
the stock adb: Developer options > Wireless debugging > Pair device with pairing code, `adb pair
<ip:pairport> <code>`, `adb connect <ip:connectport>` (`adb mdns services` lists both ports), then
`adb tcpip 5555`. After that tools/tv.py works on 5555
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "USB debugging never opens port 5555").
- The Cast receiver (com.google.android.apps.mediashell) reads its factory device credentials from a
provider hosted INSIDE the setup wizard package:
Provider{com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/com.google.android.libraries.tv.setupwraith.libs.castinfo.CastInfoProvider}
There is no separate com.google.android.tvsetup package; the com.google.android.tvsetup.* classes
ship inside the setupwraith APK. Disabling setupwraith therefore takes the credentials out of
scope and casting dies with "No private key, hence empty signature" (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md,
"Casting fails with Untrusted device"). This is NOT limited to Google's own Chromecast hardware:
it reproduces on the Google TV Streamer too (#361).
- The credentials only live in the receiver PROCESS. Re-enabling setupwraith and waiting for
"Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner" in logcat (about 7 s here) brings them back, but
`am force-stop com.google.android.apps.mediashell` loses them again ("Retry loading factory
credentials"), so the ritual has to be redone whenever the receiver is restarted.
- The manifest android:priority does NOT work on this build. Giving the replacement launcher
android:priority="3" on its HOME intent-filter was tried, the attribute IS in the installed APK
(aapt2 shows android:priority=3) and the PackageManager still reports priority 0, even after a
reboot. `cmd package set-home-activity` returns Success and does not change the dispatch either,
and the HOME role holder is ignored. The HOME can only be taken by DISABLING setupwraith
(package level).
- pm hide is not an alternative: `pm hide com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith` fails with
"SecurityException: Neither user 2000 nor current process has android.permission.MANAGE_USERS".
- Consequence for the Cast: with setupwraith disabled the receiver keeps the credentials in MEMORY
only, so after every reboot (or every receiver restart) the Cast has to be restored by briefly
re-enabling setupwraith and waiting for the signer:
logcat -c
pm enable --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
# wait ~30 s, then check logcat -d -s cast_shell for "Created singleton instance of ClientAuthSigner"
pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
Do not press HOME while setupwraith is enabled: RecoveryActivity may claim it (see below).
- If setupwraith is enabled and it wins HOME, RecoveryActivity runs as a DETACHED root task and
the first home transition kills the system, roughly every 47 s:
FATAL EXCEPTION IN SYSTEM PROCESS: android.display
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: positionChildAt:
container=Task=20383 is not a child of container=Task=1 current parent=null
at com.android.server.wm.WindowContainer.positionChildAt(WindowContainer.java:903)
at com.android.server.wm.Task.moveToBack(Task.java:4768)
at com.android.server.wm.TransitionController.tryStartCollectFromQueue
followed by DeadSystemException in setupwraith and com.android.systemui. The way out is to
disable the whole package, not the component:
pm disable-user --user 0 com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
(`pm disable-user com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity` is refused with a
SecurityException, same as the stock launcher.)
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to the setup wizard on this device, so disabling setupwraith can
drop the device off Wi-Fi: `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`. tools/disable.sh skips
setupwraith when it sees that. Re-join the network from Settings > Network afterwards, and check
again: the network then belongs to android.uid.system:1000 instead.
If the guard skips setupwraith, re-join the Wi-Fi FIRST (so the network belongs to
android.uid.system:1000) and re-run, or force it with FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1. On Ethernet the risk of
losing connectivity is nil, but the guard is about the saved network, not about the live link.
- With launcherx disabled the YouTube button on the remote does nothing. It sends BUTTON_3
(keycode 190). The launcher maps it itself: set app_keys to "190:com.google.android.youtube.tv"
in config.xml (or a theme's config.json) and enable InputKeyService:
settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.gathin.tvhome/.InputKeyService
settings put secure accessibility_enabled 1
Record the trigger with the physical remote: keys injected with `input keyevent 190` don't reach
the accessibility service. Key Mapper (keymapperorg/KeyMapper) does the same job if you prefer it;
the Play Store lists it as incompatible with this device, so install the -foss APK from its
GitHub releases, then over ADB:
pm grant io.github.sds100.keymapper android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS
settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services io.github.sds100.keymapper/io.github.sds100.keymapper.system.accessibility.MyAccessibilityService
Map trigger "Button 3" (short press) to action "Launch app > YouTube".
- The other two app buttons go silent with launcherx too. The remote's layout file
(/system/usr/keylayout/Vendor_18d1_Product_9451.kl, named by `dumpsys input`) maps them by HID usage:
usage 0x000c0077 -> BUTTON_3 (190)  YouTube
usage 0x000c0078 -> BUTTON_4 (191)  Netflix
usage 0x000c0186 -> MACRO_1  (313)  Star (launcherx opens the Google Home panel with it)
so app_keys "191:com.netflix.ninja" and "313:<package>" bring them back, with InputKeyService on.
`getevent -lt` prints the Star button as KEY_SPREADSHEET and the other two as KEY_UNKNOWN, which is
why the layout file is the place to read them. All three checked with the real remote on
UTTK.260317.003.
- Both helpers cost the remote's key auto-repeat on this build: with HomeKeyService or InputKeyService
bound, holding Volume Up/Down stops after about six steps. The YouTube button can also be taken
without an accessibility service, which keeps the ramp: a shell-owned process watches the remote's
input device ("Google TV Remote Keyboard", found by name with `getevent -pl`, never by a fixed
number) and starts the app itself. It cannot consume the press, so the button's own action still runs
as well - see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Remapping the remote's app buttons without a key helper"
(#796).
A second unit (same build, 2026-10-28) kept the YouTube button and the ramp together without a script, the
Sony VU3 way from that same TROUBLESHOOTING section: launcherx re-enabled after the install
(`pm enable com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx`), the theme's config.json setting
"stock_home_redirect": "com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx" and "key_filter": false, and HomeKeyService
enabled. YouTube then goes to launcherx's GlobalKeyListener_Receiver as stock, Home flashes launcherx and
lands on this launcher, and held volume ramps. It survived a reboot; the price is launcherx running again.
setupwraith stays disabled, so this does not bring casting back.
- com.google.android.tvrecommendations and com.google.android.apps.education.cast2class ship
disabled at the factory; `pm disable-user` on them fails with "Shell cannot change component
state". Don't add them to a restore list either.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Point it at the launcher's clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
- Animation scales already ship at 0.5x on this build.

Kept on purpose: Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), Cast receiver
(com.google.android.apps.mediashell), phone remote (com.google.android.tv.remote.service), Play Store /
Play Services, Gboard, Bluetooth, com.google.android.tv.dfuservice and
com.google.android.tv.overlay.dfuservice (remote firmware updates). The setup wizard
(com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith) is disabled, but the Cast credentials it hosts are restored
with the enable/wait/disable ritual described above.

Android TV 11 (API 30), build RTO1.251027.001. ro.product.manufacturer = ARCELIK, ro.adb.secure = 1.
USB debugging alone opens port 5555 (tested over Wi-Fi and Ethernet), no pairing.

Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV home, not Google TV launcherx).
Live TV, HDMI and the source menu: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, as on examples/grundig-kunyang.
Also claiming HOME: com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome. Make the new launcher Home before the stock one goes.

KEEP, even though some names look like bloat (same Arcelik/MediaTek family as examples/grundig-kunyang and beko-b43b880b):
- fusion.android.tv.demo: the remote's Input key (answers android.intent.action.TV_INPUT_BUTTON).
- com.arcelik.tv.arcelikbacklight: backlight control service (keeps picture settings working).
- com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter: Live TV, HDMI, source menu.
- com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith: Wi-Fi setup and saved network credentials.
- com.arcelik.ChannelEditor: TV channel management.
- Factory packages, never opened: arcelik.factorymenu.hatone, com.mediatek.tv.factory, mediatek.factorymenu.ui.

every remote button (Home, Input, Settings, app keys) works without extra key services. Screensaver set to
com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream before backdrop goes.

Inputs & HDMI-CEC:
Android TV Settings > Device Preferences > Inputs pre-assigns generic labels ("Game console", "Blu-ray")
to HDMI ports, which hides real device names. Clearing them via `settings put secure tv_input_custom_labels '""'`
lets CleanYourTV show HDMI-CEC devices natively (e.g. "PlayStation 5", "BD HTS") under the Inputs menu.

Owner's choices: Chromecast kept; voice assistant, YouTube Music, Play Games, and TTS off.
Self-installed streaming apps untouched.

Android TV 11 (API 30), build RTO1.240312.001, 1.4 GB RAM, UI 1920x1080, density 320.
ro.product.manufacturer = ARCELIK, ro.adb.secure = 1. USB debugging alone opens port 5555 (tested over Wi-Fi).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/grundig-50vlx22ldlbv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/grundig-50vlx22ldlbv/debloat.txt
Windows: tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost <tv ip> examples\grundig-50vlx22ldlbv\debloat.txt (restore.ps1 to undo)
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Same Arcelik "sinchon" platform as examples/beko-b43b880b, older build. This firmware has no Anoki ACR,
FAST channels or brand channel app, so those Beko entries are absent here.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV home). Only it and
com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome claim HOME.
Live TV, HDMI and the source menu: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter (input panel .nav.inputpanel.InputsPanelActivity).
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith claims no HOME but owns the saved Wi-Fi network: left enabled.

KEEP, even though some names look like bloat (same family as examples/beko-b43b880b):
- fusion.android.tv.demo, com.arcelik.smartremoteservice: Input key and remote keys, as on the Beko.
- com.arcelik.tv.arcelikbacklight, com.arcelik.ChannelEditor, com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer.
- com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter: Live TV, HDMI, source menu.
- Checked with dumpsys package and kept, all system plumbing: com.mediatek.network (persistent network
monitor), com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard (setup hooks), com.mediatek.wwtv.webview,
com.google.android.boot.appsplashscreen, com.google.android.sss.authbridge,
com.google.android.tv.frameworkpackagestubs.
- Factory packages, never opened: arcelik.factorymenu.hatone, com.mediatek.tv.factory,
mediatek.factorymenu.ui, com.arcelik.tv.rctest.
No separate firmware-updater package on this build.

Reboot-checked: pm list packages -d identical before and after; nothing is re-enabled at boot.
Launcher works: installs over pm install, owns Home (mFocusedApp) also after a reboot; every remote button
(Home, Input, Settings, app keys) works without the key services, pressed on the real remote.
HOME_KEY_SERVICE costs key repeat here, as in docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md:
with it bound, holding Volume Up gives one step per press; repeat returns once it is off.
Screensaver set to com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream before backdrop goes.

Owner's choices: YouTube, Prime Video, Chromecast, Play Movies and Play Games kept; Netflix, YouTube Music,
voice assistant and the phone-remote service off. Self-installed streaming apps untouched.

mau.ten: Haier Android TV DVB2K (ro.product.model, device broadway, product HaierATVT56DVB),
mau.header:
Haier Android TV DVB2K (ro.product.model, device broadway, product HaierATVT56DVB),
Android TV 11 (API 30), firmware RTMA.250416.179, armeabi-v7a, 1280x720 at 213 dpi, about 934 MB RAM.
Also sold as the CANDY Android TV DVB2K (product CANDYATVT56): identical broadway board and the same
RTMA.250416.179 firmware build (ro.build.flavor and ro.build.description still read HaierATVT56DVB on
this unit; only the retail branding differs). See the Candy variant notes below.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/haier-android-tv-dvb2k/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/haier-android-tv-dvb2k/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (.MainActivity). The install script disables it
after the new launcher is running; it is not in this list.
Live TV: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter (.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity).
Saved Wi-Fi networks on the test set were owned by android.uid.system, not setupwraith.
setupwraith is installed and its RecoveryActivity claims HOME, but it was not an active Home
candidate. Disabling only com.google.android.tvlauncher was enough for Home to land on the new launcher.
Same-day test, not a multi-day soak.

Already disabled before this list, so they are not repeated here:
com.google.android.marvin.talkback, com.cltv.fast, com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic,
com.haier.apps.evoSmart, ru.haier.evo (also claims HOME), com.google.android.play.games.

KEEP, even though the names look like bloat (components checked with dumpsys package):
- com.haier.tv.hmagicboard, com.cvte.tv.hkcfac: GlobalKeyReceiver, remote hot keys.
- com.example.bt_pair_tips, com.mediatek.autopair: Bluetooth remote pairing.
- com.telink.lt.ota: remote (Telink BLE) firmware.
- com.at.factory.*, com.cvte.tv.at, com.cvte.tv.fac.menu, com.cvte.tv.fac.aging, mediatek.factorymenu.ui: factory.
Never launch these either, not just keep them enabled: on this Haier/CVTE board family, opening one is
reported to flip a factory-mode flag and disable Play Services, Netflix and Chromecast on the next boot
with no way back from the shell. Not deliberately reproduced on either unit; treat it as a real risk.
- com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard,
com.mediatek.wwtv.mediaplayer (USB media), com.mediatek.androidbox (HaiCast / Miracast).
- com.google.android.katniss (Assistant), com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast).
- Streaming apps left installed: Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube, Hotstar, Sun NXT, Zee5 (com.graymatrix.did).

CANDY Android TV DVB2K variant (one set, disabled in one batch on 2026-10-27, checked with screenshots and
a reboot the same day; same-day only, not yet a multi-day soak):
- List differences, by the owner's choice: com.mediatek.androidbox (HaiCast / Miracast, kept above) was also
disabled, since the owner doesn't cast. Also disabled: com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic,
com.google.android.syncadapters.calendar and miada.tv.webbrowser (a bundled browser not mentioned above).
Owner uses Live TV, YouTube, Play Store and the bundled Multi Media (USB) player; Netflix and Prime Video
are kept installed for later. Nothing else on this TV.
- com.haier.launcher.haiermatrix and com.google.android.tvrecommendations, both disabled above, came back on
by themselves at the next boot on this unit regardless of pm disable-user; so did
com.google.android.apps.mediashell and com.google.android.katniss, which are on the KEEP list above anyway.
Worth re-checking on the original test set, since the firmware build string matches. Hidden in the
launcher's hidden_apps instead of fought at the package level; with app_library on, the stock library
screen ignored hidden_apps and offered the factory-menu packages above as "Add to Home" entries. Fixed
with the launcher's library_excluded_apps key (#2174), since it isn't specific to
this TV and changes App Library behaviour for every set with app_library on.
- The Live TV dock tile needed a small launcher fix to land on HDMI1: a plain tap just reopened
com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter to whatever input it last remembered (Composite, on this unit), since
live_tv_input_id only matches TYPE_TUNER inputs, never TYPE_HDMI. Fixed with launch_actions' "input:<id>"
prefix (#2159): com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter=input:com.mediatek.tvinput/.hdmi.HDMIInputService/HW5 here.

mau.header:
Haier H32S80EFX (ro.product.model "Haier MatrixTV CE", product HRT56EU, device deto), Google TV 14 (API 34),
firmware UKNV.260302.001, MediaTek (CVTE board), armeabi-v7a, Thailand.
1.4 GB RAM (MemTotal about 1.38 GB). 1920x1080 panel, UI rendered at 1280x720 (wm size override), 213 dpi.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/haier-h32s80efx/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/haier-h32s80efx/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it as STOCK_LAUNCHER).
Live TV: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter (.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity).
Already disabled from the factory: com.google.android.marvin.talkback, it.hon.onboarding.

Tested the same day on one set, with the real remote: Home opens the new launcher, Netflix / YouTube
launch, HDMI 1 and Live TV switch from the launcher's Inputs menu, voice button works.
The home screen on the test set was a small custom launcher built from PROMPT.md, not launcher/ from
this repo; the package list does not depend on which launcher replaces Home.
Not a multi-day soak.

KEEP, even though the names look like bloat (components checked with dumpsys package):
- com.haier.appmanager.dispatcher: GlobalKeyReceiver + HotKeyService (BIND_TV_INPUT), remote hot keys.
- com.haier.hkcfac, com.haier.tv.hmagicboard: global key receivers (hmagicboard also sound settings).
- com.mediatek.autopair, com.haier.bt_pair_tips: Bluetooth remote pairing.
- com.telink.lt.ota: remote (Telink BLE) firmware.
- com.cvte.tv.at, com.cvte.autobacklight, com.at.factory.*: factory / backlight, not checked further.
- com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard,
com.google.android.tv.inputplayer, com.mediatek.wwtv.mediaplayer (USB media).

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- USB debugging on: network ADB answered on port 5555 straight away; ro.adb.secure=1 (authorisation prompt).
- pm install of a debug-signed APK declaring HOME works (pushed + pm install -r, adb install not needed).
- Home goes to launcherx (priority 2), then setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity (priority 1); a third-party HOME
filter is priority 0, so set-home-activity alone does nothing. Disabling only the RecoveryActivity
component is refused for the shell (SecurityException), so the whole setupwraith package goes.
The test set was on Ethernet; on Wi-Fi, check `cmd wifi list-networks` first, setupwraith owns a
network saved during setup and disabling it deletes that network.
- Three tuner inputs: TunerInputService/HW0 (digital, DVB-T2), CableInputService/HW0, AnalogInputService/HW1.
A launcher that picks the first tuner by label lands on analog and shows no channels; prefer the
digital one. HDMI 1-3 = com.mediatek.tvinput/.hdmi.HDMIInputService/HW5-HW7, AV = composite HW2.
- Open inputs with an explicit component (com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter/.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity, ACTION_VIEW
on TvContract.buildChannelUriForPassthroughInput): a preloaded TrueID app also claims channel VIEW intents.
- HDMI and Live TV screenshots come out black (protected video layer).

mau.header:
Haier MatrixTV GE (ro.product.model "Haier MatrixTV GE", product HR9216EU, device haeundae),
Google TV 14 (API 34), firmware UKN6.260116.152, MediaTek (CVTE-family board: com.cvte.tv.at,
com.cvte.autobacklight present), 1920x1080 panel, UI rendered at 1280x720 (wm size override), 213 dpi.
Tested on 23 October 2026 on one set, including two reboots.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/haier-hr9216eu/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/haier-hr9216eu/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (.home.HomeActivity).
Live TV: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter (.nav.TurnkeyUiMainActivity).
Already disabled from the factory on the test set: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter.plus, com.wbd.stream,
in.startv.hotstar.dplus.tv, com.iqiyi.i18n.tv, com.truedmp.idtv, com.tencent.qqlivei18n,
com.netflix.ninja, com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom. Netflix was re-enabled by owner choice; the
other streaming apps stayed off.

setupwraith owns the saved Wi-Fi on a freshly set-up unit: the network's creator was
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (dumpsys wifi cname=), so disabling it deletes the network
and takes the TV off Wi-Fi and ADB. Forget and re-join the network first (then cname=android.uid.system);
`cmd wifi forget-network 0` from the shell works when the TV's own Forget menu does not take.
disable.sh refuses setupwraith until that is done.

This firmware re-enables two of its own packages at every boot (seen on two reboots):
com.haier.oemtabprovider and com.haier.launcher.haiermatrix. Both are inert with the stock home
disabled (the Haier tab they feed is launcherx's), so leave them or disable them again after a boot.

The remote's gear button sends KEY_UNKNOWN, scancode 240 on /dev/input/event3 ("HaierTV-RC Keyboard");
put 240 in settings_key_scancodes in launcher config.xml before building, HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 on the install
line. That service costs the volume ramp on this set too (one step per press while bound) - the same
all-or-nothing key-filter trade as docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md, here on Google TV 14.
Netflix / YouTube / Input / Live TV / voice buttons all work with no helper (Haier's own
GlobalKeyReceiver services answer them).

Port 5555 opens with `adb tcpip 5555` but does not survive a reboot (setprop persist.adb.tcp.port is
refused). Wireless debugging (_adb-tls-connect._tcp) survives and re-advertises on mDNS; reopen 5555
through it when the repo's tools (tv.py over 5555) are needed again.

KEEP, even though the names look like bloat (components checked with dumpsys package):
- com.haier.appmanager.dispatcher, com.haier.hkcfac, com.haier.tv.hmagicboard: global key receivers
(remote hot keys; hmagicboard also sound settings).
- com.mediatek.autopair, com.haier.bt_pair_tips: Bluetooth remote pairing.
- com.google.android.tv.googletvremotepairer (+ its mediatek overlay): remote pairing activities.
- com.telink.lt: remote (Telink BLE) firmware, also claims HOME at priority 0.
- com.cvte.tv.at, com.cvte.autobacklight, com.at.factory.androidtvaidlservice, mediatek.factorymenu.ui:
factory / backlight - never disable, never open.
- com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard,
com.mediatek.wwtv.setup.customization, com.google.android.tv.inputplayer, com.mediatek.wwtv.mediaplayer,
com.mediatek.androidbox (HaiCast / Miracast), com.mstar.android.tv.disclaimercustomization.
- com.cltv.hybrid: iwedia channel-list UI (claims generic VIEW channel intents alongside tvcenter).
- com.google.android.katniss (Assistant), com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast): kept by
owner choice; disable if you use neither.

mau.header:
Haier HRA962X2_2G_ALI6G_A (Ali6G board), Android TV 9 (SDK 28), firmware PPR1.180610.011.20220314 test-keys
A China-market set on the Aliyun YunOS stack: the stock Home is Youku's launcher, and the
firmware's own packages are com.yunos.* / com.haier.*. Works as a starting point for other
Haier sets on Ali6G with the same package set.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/haier-hra962x2/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

The updater is disabled here on purpose: on this set com.yunos.osupdate pushed a new preload
(com.haier.aitv, an Aligenie content app) to /data/app while it was enabled. Re-enable it to
check for firmware updates (remove the whole line to let check.py --fix re-disable it).
Firmware updates arrive only while it is enabled.

See README.md in this folder before installing the launcher: this firmware intercepts the
remote's Home key in YunOSTVPolicy and sends a private intent instead of the standard HOME
broadcast, so a stock launcher build does not receive the Home key without a manifest filter.

mau.ten: Haier MatrixTV BE, Google TV 14, firmware UKNV.260313.001.
mau.header:
Haier MatrixTV BE, Google TV 14, firmware UKNV.260313.001.
Tested on one set from 31 October to 1 November 2026, including one reboot and real remote checks.
Short trial, not a multi-day soak. Re-check this list against your own firmware and app choices.

Apply:   TV_HOST=YOUR_TV_IP tools/disable.sh examples/haier-matrixtv-be/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=YOUR_TV_IP tools/restore.sh examples/haier-matrixtv-be/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Every active line disables one package for user 0; nothing is uninstalled.

Stock Home: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (.home.HomeActivity).
The launcher install script disables stock Home only after the new Home starts; it is not in this list.
Live TV: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter.

Check saved Wi-Fi ownership before disabling setupwraith. On the tested set, the connected

Notes from this TV:
- Sideloading works: pm install of an APK declaring category HOME succeeds (no verifier block).
- The TV is a userdebug build with ro.adb.secure unset: port 5555 gives a shell to anyone on the
LAN while ADB is on, with no "Allow" prompt. Turn debugging off when done.
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to android.uid.system, not to a setup wizard, so disabling
setupwraith does not take the TV off Wi-Fi.
- Screencap returns a 0-byte file on this firmware in every app (Live TV, Home, dialogs), so
verify steps with `dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus` instead of screenshots.
- disable.sh skips com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.recommendations on this firmware: its
dumpsys prints no permission block for the input-driver check. After a reboot with the inputs
verified, run the list again with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 to take that one line.
- Settings on this set is com.hikeen.settings (CATEGORY_LAUNCHER, no leanback entry); the Android
TV settings app (com.android.tv.settings) has no launcher entry at all. The folder's config.json
seeds the Hikeen settings app with library_apps and pins it in the dock.
- Kept in use: the USB media browser and quick menus (com.hikeen.mediabrowser, Quickmenu,
scrollhelper, menu, settings), MX Player, Live TV and the TV inputs (com.android.tv carries the
AV/HDMI/VGA TV input services), all com.realtek.* (tuner, providers, passthrough), the on-screen
keyboard, Play Store and Play Services.

Same platform and build as examples/vidda-mt9653/ and examples/hisense-e5q-pro/ (device MT9653,
build RP1A.200720.011, package namespace com.jamdeo.* / com.hisense.*). This list was derived from

Packages those lists name that are NOT installed here are left out rather than copied over.

ADB: turning USB debugging on opens port 5555 directly. ro.adb.secure=0 means the TV does not show
the "Allow USB debugging?" dialog: ANY device on the LAN gets a shell with no prompt. Close the
debugging switches when you are done and check the port really refuses connections
(tools/adb-closed.py <tv ip>).

State at the time this list was written (2026-10-22):
pm list packages -d        -> empty: nothing is disabled at the factory on this build, so the
AOSP leftovers in BATCH 5 below are all running here.
dumpsys tv_input           -> empty: no TvInputManager inputs at all. The launcher's Inputs pill
therefore has nothing to list and must use the vendor source panel
(config.json in this folder: source_panel_service =
com.hisense.tv.inputs/com.hisense.tv.InputsUIService,
source_panel_action = com.hisense.tv.start_inputs).

Applied on the real set on 2026-10-22: five batches, each followed by a cold reboot, with the input
panel switching HDMI, the remote, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth pairing and the IME checked after every one.
26 packages stick. com.android.calendar / .deskclock / .music do not: the firmware re-enables them
at every boot (see BATCH 5). Nothing else came back.

Read before applying:
* This list does NOT change how Home looks. The sponsored rows, the VIP banner and the promo
tiles are fetched by com.jamdeo.tv.vod itself, not by the ad sidecars below. Only swapping the
launcher removes them. What this list buys is the telemetry, the push channel, the persistent
network poller, the ad SDK processes and the leftover preloads.
* Everything is DISABLED (pm disable-user --user 0), never uninstalled. tools\disable.ps1 records
each package's original state under %USERPROFILE%\.cleanyourtv\ before touching it, so
tools\restore.ps1 with this same file puts it all back.
* Apply in batches, reboot after each one, and confirm the TV boots, the remote works, the input
panel switches to HDMI and Wi-Fi is still up. A batch can take something load-bearing with it
and you cannot tell which without the reboot.

Undo:    tools\restore.ps1 -TvHost <tv ip> examples\hisense-65d62qh\debloat.txt
Reboot:  & tools\venv\Scripts\python.exe -I tools\tv.py --reboot   # returns once ADB accepts it; wait for the TV to come back

Applied 2026-10-24 in four batches with a screenshot of Home after each (the Alexa group on 2026-10-25), then
rebooted three times: Home, Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Apple TV, Spotify, Settings, the Appstore, AirPlay
mirroring from an iPhone and HDMI-CEC (a PS5 switching the TV to its input when it wakes) all work. Lived with for
about a day so far. Free memory after a reboot (MemAvailable): 463 MB before, about 740 MB after.

Fire OS 8 notes on this set:
- com.amazon.vizzini (Alexa voice) comes back ENABLED AT EVERY BOOT, as on hisense-fire-tv-aftcibfbd1/; the rest of
the Alexa group stays off. Re-run the list after a reboot if you don't use Alexa.
- Third-party apps preinstalled by the retailer or Hisense (Bell Fibe TV / Crave, VIDAA, a YouTube player, Twitch)
came back ENABLED after a reboot when disabled. They are ordinary user apps, so they are not in this list;
remove them in Settings > Applications if you don't want them.
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to com.amazon.tv.oobe (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`): never disable it.
- No package in this list was refused; the protected ones are the same as on hisense-fire-tv-aftcibfbd1/.
- AdGuard Private DNS works (mads.amazon-adsystem.com resolves to 127.0.0.1) and removes the third-party ads from the
hero banner; Amazon's own promotions stay (they come from the protected launcher's feed).
- Animation scales at 0.5 make the ☰ side menu open nothing, as on amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/.
- ADB Debugging switched itself off after one of the three reboots: check Developer Options before running a script.

For launcher authors (what Fire OS 8 reserves to Amazon here, read from the APKs' manifests):
- Switching to an HDMI input: com.amazon.tv.inputpreference.service's PassthroughPlayerActivity needs
com.amazon.tv.permission.TUNE_INPUT, InputTabActivity and StartAmazonInputActivity LAUNCH_INPUTS,
GameBoardInputSwitchActivity SET_UPDATE_INPUT_STATE; the standard passthrough request opens Live TV. The remote's
Input button and HDMI-CEC still work.
- The Home key never reaches an accessibility service's key filter, and the CLOSE_SYSTEM_DIALOGS "homekey" broadcast
requires com.amazon.permission.ENABLE_KEYGUARD_FLAGS (signature|privileged|amazon).
- ACTION_SETTINGS goes through Amazon's Home; the settings grid itself, com.amazon.tv.launcher/.ui.MainSettingsActivity
(action amazon.intent.action.MAINSETTINGS), is exported without a permission.
- The Appstore (com.amazon.venezia/.grid.AppsGridLauncherActivity) has no screen of its own: it opens Amazon's Home on
its Apps page.
- An accessibility service that opens another home screen over HomeActivity_vNext works as a replacement Home.

Kept on purpose: Live TV and the TV inputs, settings, the Appstore, Silk, OTA updates, the keyboard, remote and
Bluetooth services, casting (DIAL, Matter casting), AirPlay (personal choice: mirroring from an iPhone or a Mac),
com.amazon.tv.oobe, com.amazon.imp, the screensaver.

firmware RS8180.3734N, US. The first Fire OS 8 TV (Fire TV Edition) here. amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/ (Fire OS 8.1)
goes further on packages and its notes apply here too; this list adds what is TV-specific: Alexa voice coming back at
every boot, and HDMI input switching being reserved to Amazon.

FIRE OS: DEBLOAT ONLY. As on Fire OS 7, com.amazon.tv.launcher and com.amazon.firehomestarter are protected
(pm disable-user and am force-stop are refused) and keep Home. Live TV app: com.amazon.tv.livetv.

Apply:  TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/hisense-fire-tv-aftcibfbd1/debloat.txt
Undo:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/hisense-fire-tv-aftcibfbd1/debloat.txt com.amazon.tv.launcher
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Lived with since 2026-10-19, through several reboots: Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Spotify, Settings, the Network
page, Live TV settings and HDMI inputs (via the remote's Input button) all work.

Fire OS 8 notes:
- com.amazon.vizzini (Alexa voice) comes back ENABLED AT EVERY BOOT. Neither pm disable-user, pm suspend,
`appops set ... RECORD_AUDIO ignore` (not even applied) nor pm uninstall -k --user 0
(DELETE_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR) survives a reboot; re-run this list after one. Everything else stays off.
- Two packages are protected (pm disable-user is refused), so they are commented out below:
com.amazon.ftvads.deeplinking and com.amazon.device.crashmanager.
- AdGuard Private DNS works (mads.amazon-adsystem.com stops resolving) and removes the third-party ad
in the hero banner; Amazon's own promotions stay, they come from the protected launcher.
- Input switching is Amazon-only: its player needs com.amazon.tv.permission.TUNE_INPUT (signature|amazon) and
its picker com.amazon.tv.inputpreference.permission.LAUNCH_INPUTS (signature|privileged). The standard
passthrough URI opens Live TV's settings instead of the input, so a launcher's Inputs button can't switch here.
- Leave the animation scales at 1.0, as on amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2023/: at 0.5 every entry in the ☰ side menu
(Inputs, Settings, profile) closes the menu and opens nothing. Confirmed on a second set (65U68QF, Canada) by
toggling 1.0 / 0.5 with the list applied.
- Screensavers: Amazon's AmbientManagerService (in system_server) replaces any DreamService with Ambient
Experience ("Stopping Ambient, reason=starting new dream", then "Starting Ambient"), and with
com.amazon.tv.ftvambient disabled it ends the dream at once ("No AmbientService implementations found"). A
third-party screensaver set through screensaver_components never shows. With ambient_turn_off_in_darkroom=1
the light sensor sends the set straight to sleep from Ambient in a dark room.
- Live TV screens and a sleeping panel both screenshot as plain black; check `dumpsys power | grep mWakefulness`.
Amazon's screens expose no text to uiautomator, so verify the UI with screenshots.
- Owners who use Alexa voice, casting and Ambient: comment out the Alexa and Casting groups and ftvambient. The
65U68QF set ran that way (vizzini, Alexa extras, cast.sink, AirPlay, Photos and Ambient kept) with the rest of
this list plus kso.blackbird, client.metrics.api and hedwig, and with Amazon Kids (tahoe) off as well, which
this list keeps on purpose: free memory after a cold boot went from about 1.0 GB to 1.6 GB and swap from
98 % full to empty.
- Second unit: 65U65SFC (U65 Pro series, US), firmware RS8180.3749N, 3.8 GB of RAM. Applied 2026-10-26 in four
batches with a screenshot of Home after each, then rebooted twice: only vizzini came back, everything else stayed
off, and ADB Debugging stayed on. It ran this list (Tubi was not installed) plus the entries marked "tested on
65U65SFC", with AirPlay kept and Amazon Kids (tahoe) off as well. MemAvailable went from about 1.6 GB before to
2.0 GB after a reboot. The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to com.amazon.tv.oobe here too.
- On that unit, router-level AdGuard Home blocking amazon-adsystem.com (checked from the TV) did not remove the
Sponsored tile or the hero and bottom banners: they changed after a reboot, so there they come with the
launcher's own feed.

Kept on purpose: Amazon Kids (com.amazon.tahoe), OTA updates, Live TV, settings, Silk, Appstore, the stock launcher.

mau.ten: Hisense HG9 (HiSmart 4K A4FFM, device laohushan, MediaTek), Android TV 9 (API 28),
mau.header:
Hisense HG9 (HiSmart 4K A4FFM, device laohushan, MediaTek), Android TV 9 (API 28),
build PTMR.190127.037, security patch 2021-02-05, kernel 4.9.118. 2 GB RAM class.
Tested on a set used as an Apple TV display over HDMI.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (pass it to restore.sh; replaced
here by FLauncher from the Play Store, not launcher/, set as default with
`cmd package set-home-activity me.efesser.flauncher/.MainActivity`).
Live TV app: stock Live TV was left alone; HDMI input is com.hisense.tv.hitvinput.

Second and third units (two more sets, same product, same build PTMR.190127.037 and
2021-02-05 patch, MStar MSD6886, 1.8 GB RAM, US; one on Wi-Fi, one on Ethernet),
both with launcher/ as Home for several days, October 2026:
- Developer options > USB debugging alone opened port 5555 on both, within seconds and
without a reboot; the Network debugging toggle was never touched. The first unit's
note above still stands for it; expect either.
- The smartsense trio (smartsense, smartsense.ui, smartservice) was disabled on both and
both rebooted normally, confirming the first unit's reboot test on this build.
- com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith is the creator of the saved Wi-Fi network on
both (tools/disable.sh refuses it for that reason), so it was KEPT; the launcher/
handover held across reboots with it enabled, so it does not need disabling here.
- The remote's Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube and Google Play buttons kept working under
launcher/ with no app_keys mapping. Live TV for the launcher's Inputs menu is
live_tv_package com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter.
- Kept by choice on both: Backdrop and TTS (voice search still wanted), Chromecast,
Alexa, RemoteNOW, Media Center, the OTA updaters, and com.mstar.netflixobserver (not
tried without it; it may serve the remote's Netflix button). Also disabled on both,
beyond the list: com.google.android.leanbacklauncher (the old launcher; not a Home
claimant on this build), com.google.android.partnersetup, the calendar and contacts
sync adapters, and com.seraphic.browser (Hisense's browser). Nothing was re-enabled.
- On this firmware `screencap -p` over `adb exec-out` prints a log line before the PNG
bytes; tools/tv.py --screenshot (a file on the TV, then a pull) is unaffected.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/hisense-hg9/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/hisense-hg9/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Reboot-tested: the TV boots normally with this full list applied, including
com.hisense.tv.smartsense, com.vt.tv.smartsense.ui and
com.hisense.tv.smartservice all disabled (verified after a settings-reset
reboot, followed by a full evening of use: streaming, Store, launcher).
This differs from the #45 SmartTV 4K FFM (Android TV 10) report where the
smartsense pair sent that set to Recovery — model/firmware difference, HG9
on Android TV 9 is unaffected.

Notes from this firmware:
- USB debugging alone does NOT open network ADB; the TV needs its explicit
Network/Wireless debugging toggle too, plus a reboot before port 5555 opens.
(On the two later units below it opened at once; see their notes.)
- The Beryl/GL.iNet "block client" toggle deauths the TV entirely (no join at
all), it is not a WAN-only block. Debloat over an isolated offline LAN instead.
- com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith re-enables the stock launcher, so it
is listed (per the FLauncher README method).
- Play Store showed "Something went wrong" with AuthFailureError even after
re-signing in; `pm clear com.google.android.gsf` + reboot + fresh sign-in
fixed it. The tvrecommendations prefetch errors in Finsky logs are a red
herring (they persist with the services enabled and are non-fatal).
- Kept deliberately: hitvinput + mtktvapi_agent + tvcenter (HDMI/tuner),
tv.settings/providers.tv, Play Store + Play Services, remote keys (kpad,
hotkey dispatcher, autopair), Bluetooth, latin IME, system UI, Alexa,
Chromecast, DLNA service, OTA updater, phone-remote service (lost-remote
fallback), and the MStar disclaimer customizer (first-boot legal text).
- Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube, Apple TV, Pluto, Vudu, Hulu apps kept and
updated through the Play Store. Pandora, Peacock, Kids, Play Games, Max,
Paramount+, MediaCenter removed by owner choice (Apple TV is the streamer).

mau.header:
Hisense HiSmart 2K ATV4 (ro.product.model "HiSmart 2K ATV4", device hamamatsucho, CVTE board), India.
Android TV 11 (SDK 30), firmware RTO6.250817.001, 924 MB RAM, ro.adb.secure=1. Same device and firmware as
docs/devices/hisense-hismart-2k-atv4-hamamatsucho.md; the Android 9 sibling on this board is
examples/vu-premium-fhd-43-hamamatsucho/.
Live TV app: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter. Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (not in this list:
launcher/build-and-install.sh disables it after the new launcher is Home). setupwraith does not claim HOME
on this firmware and the saved Wi-Fi belongs to android.uid.system, so it is left alone.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/hisense-hismart-2k-atv4-hamamatsucho/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/hisense-hismart-2k-atv4-hamamatsucho/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Status: applied 2026-10-30 in five batches with a screenshot after each, then two cold reboots (one before and
one after the launcher handover). Normal boot (~35 s) every time, nothing re-enabled at boot. Working: Home, the
Input key's own panel (DTV, ATV, HDMI 1, HDMI 2), all seven TvInputService providers, HDMI-CEC with a Sony
soundbar on ARC and a set-top box on HDMI 2, YouTube. One session so far, not yet lived with for days; the
physical remote's app buttons and held volume were not tested.

Note: with com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer off, the stock launcher loses its Inputs,
Wi-Fi and notification icons in its top bar. The Input key and Settings > Inputs still work, and the new
launcher has its own Inputs pill, so this only matters if you keep the stock Home.
Note: after a reboot the TV can ask the ARC soundbar for System Audio Mode before the soundbar is awake, give
up, and play through its own speakers (mSystemAudioActivated: false in dumpsys hdmi_control). Settings > Device
Preferences > Sound > ARC off, then on, brings the sound back to the soundbar. Not caused by this list.
At boot com.at.factory.factorymanager shows for about a second by itself; that is the firmware. Keep the
com.at.factory.*, com.cvte.*fac*, mediatek.factorymenu.ui and com.hisensefac.daemon packages, and never open them.

Keep: com.mediatek.* (Live TV, inputs, TV service), com.cvte.autobacklight, com.airoha.android.btd (Bluetooth
audio), com.google.android.tv.remote.service, Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), Play Store and
Play services, Gboard.
Already disabled when the set arrived (owner history, not in this list): TalkBack, com.cltv.fast.

mau.ten: Hisense HiSmartTV A4 (device xiaoyushan, MStar/MediaTek m7322), Android TV 11, firmware RTT2.221108.001
mau.header:
Hisense HiSmartTV A4 (device xiaoyushan, MStar/MediaTek m7322), Android TV 11, firmware RTT2.221108.001
(build 00.00.00.18), security patch 2023-12-05. 1.8 GB RAM, 32-bit userspace (armeabi-v7a only:
sideload armeabi-v7a or universal APKs). Same set as hisense-hismarttv-a4 after its Android 11 update.
Second unit: 75A53FUA, US market, same build and security patch, incremental 00.00.01.18. Groups 1, 2
and 4 applied there with Netflix and Prime Video kept; its differences are noted below where they apply.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/hisense-hismarttv-a4-android11/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/hisense-hismarttv-a4-android11/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

ADB: turning USB debugging on opens network ADB on port 5555 directly (service.adb.tcp.port=5555,
adb_wifi_enabled=0); no Wireless debugging pairing needed. ro.adb.secure=1, so the TV asks
"Allow USB debugging?" on first connect.
Applied in three batches (group 1, group 2, then groups 3 and 4 together), ~15 s wait and a reboot
after each: normal boot every time, all 7 TV inputs still registered (HDMI 1-4, composite, two
tuners), and switching to HDMI 1 from the launcher's Inputs menu works. The wait is not optional: on
the second unit a reboot sent straight after a batch came before Android wrote the package state, and
every package in that batch was enabled again at boot.

This firmware mixes the package namespaces of the Android 9 A4 list (com.mstar.*, the xiaoyushan
autoinstalls) and of hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm (com.hisense.evservice, service.message, b2b, alexa,
VIDAA). Most of the Android 9 list is gone here: com.hisense.app.logreport, com.hisense.storemode,
fusion.android.tv.demo, com.seraphic.browser, com.google.android.leanbacklauncher(.recommendations),
com.google.android.music, com.hisense.myapplication, com.google.android.apps.nbu.smartconnect.tv.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (the default in restore.sh), with Shop and Discover
tabs and a full-width sponsored hero banner that only the launcher swap removes. setupwraith is
installed but does not claim HOME on this firmware, and the Wi-Fi saved at setup belongs to
android.uid.system, so it is not in this list. On the second unit `dumpsys wifi` names setupwraith as
the network's owner instead; setupwraith still does not claim HOME there, so it stays enabled and the
network is never at risk. launcher/build-and-install.sh worked unchanged and Home survives a reboot.
Input key: the remote's Input button sends KEYCODE_TV_INPUT (scancode 184). The framework routes it
as a global key to com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, which starts com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS, and
the only handler of that action is tvlauncher's InputsPanelActivity. With the stock launcher
disabled the key does nothing (ActivityNotFoundException in logcat); use the launcher's Inputs pill.
Or set "handle_view_inputs": true (config.xml or a theme): the launcher then answers VIEW_INPUTS and
the Input button opens its Inputs menu, with no key helper. Checked on the real remote, second unit.

Do NOT disable: com.hisense.tv.smartsense, com.vt.tv.smartsense.ui (the smartsense family sent the
Hisense FFM set to Android Recovery), com.mediatek.* (wwtv.tvcenter is Live TV and HDMI; autopair,
hotkey.dispatcher, tv.agent), com.hisense.tv.hitvinput (HDMI/AV/tuner inputs), com.hisense.kpad and
com.hisense.favkey (remote keys), com.mstar.netflixobserver (Netflix key), com.vidaa.persistent.service,
com.hisense.tv.smartservice, com.hisense.tv.customerlauncher, com.hisense.uifac,
com.hisense.audio_update_service, com.vt.eula. Left alone as well: com.hisense.tv.protector
("Device Assistant" cleaner) and com.hisense.mixbar.
Kept here and optional: firmware updates (com.hisense.tv.ota, com.hisense.remoteupgrade), YouTube,
Chromecast (mediashell), Assistant (katniss), Screen Sharing / Miracast (com.mediatek.androidbox),
RemoteNOW (hisremotenow, hisremotenowserver), DLNA (com.hisense.tv.dlna), USB media player
(com.jamdeo.tv.mediacenter), Ambient screensaver (com.google.android.backdrop).
Already disabled at the factory: com.google.android.videos, com.google.android.play.games,
com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic, net.vidaatv.android.tv, air.com.vudu.air.DownloaderTablet.
The second unit shipped with all five enabled.

mau.header:
Hisense SmartTV 4K FFM (device huangshan, MediaTek), Android TV 10, firmware QTG3.200902.001
Security patch 2023-02-05. Sold in Latin America; the Android model string is "SmartTV 4K FFM".
The same device and build ships in the USA as the Hisense U9DG (75" Dual-Cell ULED, 2021), with a
US preload set: the "US (U9DG)" groups below. 2 GB RAM, armeabi-v7a (32-bit userspace), 7.7 GB /data.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

WARNING, read before applying: a first version of this list that also disabled
com.hisense.tv.smartsense, com.vt.tv.smartsense.ui and com.vt.tv.aiot sent the TV to Android
Recovery on the next boot ("Can't load Android system. Your data may be corrupt"). "Try again"
booted normally and tools/restore.sh undid everything. Which of the three was the cause is not
confirmed, so all three are left out below. Never pick "Factory data reset" on that screen
before trying "Try again".
This list was then applied in seven groups with a reboot after each: no crashes, normal boot.
If you experiment with more packages, reboot after each small group, and wait ~15 s after

mau.header:
Hisense SmartTV 4K FFM (device songshan, product songshan_emH_FFM, board m7632, MediaTek),
Android 11 / SDK 30, firmware RTT2.220118.001 / 01.00.05.04. The Android model string is
"SmartTV 4K FFM".
Also sold as the Hisense 50A6H4 (US), Hisense 65U6G and Hisense 65A6H: the third, fourth and fifth units
below.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm-android11/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm-android11/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED with pm disable-user, never uninstalled.

Android 11 sibling of examples/hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm/ (Android TV 10, device huangshan): same model
string, different board and firmware and a different package set (no evservice, no hotel mode, no
tvrecommendations here). Applied in two batches with a reboot after; no crashes, normal boot.

WARNING, shared with the huangshan FFM list: never disable com.hisense.tv.smartsense,
com.vt.tv.smartsense.ui or com.vt.tv.aiot. A version of the huangshan list that did sent the set to
Android Recovery on the next boot ("Can't load Android system"). They are kept out below.

Keep: com.mediatek.* (including com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, the Live TV and HDMI app),
com.hisense.tv.hitvinput and com.mediatek.tv.service (they serve TvInputService and ask for
TV_INPUT_HARDWARE, so the HDMI/AV/tuner inputs depend on them), com.hisense.tv.smartservice,
com.hisense.tv.customerlauncher, com.vt.tv.input, com.hisense.tv.protector.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (the Google TV home). It is disabled by the
launcher install, not by this list; pass it to tools/restore.sh as the stock launcher.
Already disabled at the factory on this set: YouTube Music, Google TV Movies, Feedback, Play Games,
HiBrowser, TalkBack, TTS, mediashell, basic dreams, calendar/contacts providers, Kika keyboard.
Left ON by choice here (deliberately not in this list): all streaming apps, voice assistant
(katniss / tv.assistant / hisense.alexa), casting and mirroring, and the firmware updaters
(hisense.tv.ota, hisense.remoteupgrade, vt.tv.usbota).

Second unit (US, same device songshan and build RTT2.220118.001, one session plus standby and reboot
tests): com.hisense.storemode is not installed, com.hisense.evservice is (see the commented entry at the
end), and nothing on it came disabled from the factory. The owner also disabled katniss,
tv.assistant and hisense.alexa (no voice use); nothing else broke in that session. Notes from it:
- Standby (com.hisense.STR_SUSPEND) kills every third-party app except the one on screen
("PowerVtImp: kill 3rd app" in logcat), the launcher included, which takes its key helpers off. Install
with restore_key_services on and -RestoreKeyServices / RESTORE_KEY_SERVICES=1 (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md,
"Accessibility helper enabled but the remote button does nothing").
- Its remote differs from the SmartRC below: Disney+ is keycode 607 (scancode 418) and Peacock 608
(scancode 421); YouTube 293, Prime Video 295 and the gear 83 (scancode 598) match. The firmware logs
every press as "WindowManager: interceptKeyTq keycode=... scancode=...".
- HomeKeyService did not bind in the first session (it stayed under "Binding services" in dumpsys
accessibility, with nothing in logcat), so settings_key_keycodes did nothing; in a later session it bound
normally, cause unknown. Mapping the gear through InputKeyService works either way:
app_keys 83:com.android.tv.settings.
- With InputKeyService bound, holding volume moves it one step
(docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md).

Third unit: the Hisense 50A6H4 (US retail model; same device songshan and build RTT2.220118.001,
incremental 00.00.00.53, security patch 2025-06-01, Android model string "SmartTV 4K"). One session on
2026-10-24 with three reboots: this list plus the commented entries at the end marked "third unit",
applied in batches, then the launcher. Nothing came disabled from the factory; storemode is not
installed, evservice is. Notes from it:
- setupwraith passed disable.sh's Wi-Fi guard without FORCE_SETUPWRAITH: every saved network belonged to
android.uid.system.
- With launcherx disabled and no key helper enabled, every button on its remote kept working when
pressed for real: Input, the gear, YouTube, Netflix, Prime Video and the other app buttons.
- The owner also disabled katniss, hisense.alexa and mediashell (no voice or Chromecast use), Play Games,
Google TV Movies, both VIDAA apps (net.vidaatv.*), HiBrowser, and some apps installed through the Play
Store (Tubi, Pluto TV, Haystack News, YouTube TV, MX Player, the TCL browser); nothing broke.
- com.hisense.tv.dlna, Hisense's DLNA renderer, listens on ports 38400 and 39500. Disabled, it closed
them only after a reboot; until then the port stayed open, even after am force-stop. AirPlay (7000)
and the Google TV remote service (6466/6467) are separate and kept working.
- With setupwraith and launcherx disabled, Settings > Privacy > Usage & diagnostics opens nothing (focus
goes to frameworkpackagestubs' SettingsPrivacyStub). The page is setupwraith's, not the Google TV
home's: on a Chromecast with Google TV 4K (Google TV 14) only setupwraith answers it
(README, "Are there switches in the TV's own Settings worth flipping too?"); not checked on this set. Set it before
this list disables setupwraith.
- Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) works; YouTube and the streaming apps still play.

Fourth unit: the Hisense 65U6G (retail model; same device songshan and build RTT2.220118.001,
Android model string "SmartTV 4K FFM", Android 11 / SDK 30). One session on 2026-10-27 with reboots:
- setupwraith passed the Wi-Fi guard without FORCE_SETUPWRAITH (active network owned by com.android.tv.settings).
- Applied debloat (setupwraith, mediashell, YouTube Music, Google TV Movies) and clean launcher swap.
- Remote keycodes match the SmartRC layout: YouTube 293, Prime Video 295, Disney+ 607 (scancode 484),
Tubi 606, and gear 83.
- Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) verified persistent across reboots; streaming apps play normally.

Fifth unit: the Hisense 65A6H (same device songshan, build RTT2.220118.001, incremental 00.00.00.53,
security patch 2025-06-01, Android model string "SmartTV 4K"). One session on 2026-10-28 with two reboots:
this list plus the three commented entries marked "third unit" at the end, applied in batches, then the
launcher. Nothing came disabled from the factory; storemode is not installed, evservice is. Notes from it:
- tools/disable.sh held back gtvpai and disclaimercustomization at first: this firmware's dumpsys prints no
permission block for either, so the input-driver check cannot read them. With HDMI confirmed working
after a reboot, TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 disabled them, as the script's message says.
- setupwraith passed the Wi-Fi guard without FORCE_SETUPWRAITH: every saved network belonged to
android.uid.system. Usage & diagnostics was switched off in Settings before it was disabled.
- Unlike the third unit, with launcherx disabled and no key helper enabled only Netflix, Input and Home
worked when pressed for real; the gear, YouTube, Prime Video and Disney+ buttons did nothing. The owner
kept them unmapped rather than enable InputKeyService and lose the volume ramp (held Volume Up repeats
about every 115 ms with no helper bound). Their codes were not captured on this unit.
- The owner also disabled katniss, hisense.alexa, dreamx, AirPlay (com.mediatek.AirplayAPK and
com.mediatek.partner.airplay; AirplayAPK serves a TvInputService, so it too needs TVINPUT_ALLOW=1),
com.vt.miracast and com.hisense.tv.dlna, plus unused streaming apps and preloads; mediashell (Chromecast)
and the firmware updaters stayed on. Nothing broke, and every package stayed disabled across both reboots.

Sixth and seventh units: two sets in one home (same device songshan, build RTT2.220118.001, incremental
00.00.00.53, security patch 2025-06-01, Android model string "SmartTV 4K"; retail model not checked). One
session on 2026-10-29 with two reboots each: this list plus the three commented entries marked "third unit"
and com.hisense.evservice, applied in batches with a screenshot between them, then the launcher. Nothing came
disabled from the factory; storemode is not installed, evservice is. Notes from them:
- As on the fifth unit, tools/disable.sh held back gtvpai and disclaimercustomization (no permission block in
dumpsys); with every input still registered after a reboot (AV, three HDMI, the tuner, AirPlay), TVINPUT_ALLOW=1
disabled them.
- On both, setupwraith owned one saved Wi-Fi network that the TV was not using, and the active one belonged to
android.uid.system, so disable.sh's guard held it back; FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 disabled it, that one saved network
was deleted and the TV stayed on Wi-Fi and ADB. Usage & diagnostics was switched off in Settings first.
- As on the third unit, with launcherx disabled and no key helper enabled, Home, Back, Input and the gear worked
when pressed for real, and a held Volume Up still ramped.
- Power-on goes FallbackHome, then the new launcher; the firmware does not put Live TV in front by itself.
- The owner also disabled katniss, hisense.alexa, mediashell, com.vt.miracast, com.hisense.tv.dlna,
com.vt.tv.homekitproxy, dreamx, HiBrowser, Play Games, Google TV Movies, YouTube Music, both VIDAA apps
(net.vidaatv.*) and every unused streaming app (the seventh unit also had YouTube TV and Haystack News);
AirPlay and the firmware updaters stayed on. Every package stayed disabled across both reboots.
- After "Revoke USB debugging authorizations", a detached `settings put global adb_enabled 0; reboot` started
from the same ADB shell never ran (port 5555 stayed open); switching USB debugging off with the remote closed it.

Status: applied 2026-10-29 in batches with a screenshot after each, then rebooted twice and power cycled once
(unplugged). Normal boot every time and nothing came back on. Working: Home, the remote, Input, held volume,
Kodi, YouTube, Netflix, Disney+, Home Assistant's Cast link. Not working: native AirPlay (see below).
Not tested yet: casting from a phone (other Google TV lists say it can stop without setupwraith).

AirPlay: the TV's own AirPlay stops working with this list, because of setupwraith. AirPlaySystemService reads
content://com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/setup_provider when it starts, and with setupwraith disabled it
sets show_airplay_setting_ui to 0, stops advertising _airplay._tcp, and the AirPlay and HomeKit page comes up
empty. setupwraith has to go for the launcher to keep Home, so this list trades native AirPlay for the launcher.
If you need AirPlay, keep setupwraith and Google TV's home (comment out the last line, skip the launcher).

ADB: USB debugging alone leaves port 5555 closed on this set. Use Wireless debugging with a pairing code
(tools/native-adb.md). It turns itself off on every reboot or Wi-Fi drop and comes back on a new port.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. launcher/build-and-install.sh disables it.

first, check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` shows android.uid.system:1000, then apply with
FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1.

packages (com.mediatek.airplay*, com.vt.tv.airplaykeycheck; idle without setupwraith), screen mirroring

Known quirks on this firmware:
- screencap -p on stdout is corrupted by MediaTek log lines ("Init wrapper sys mutex successful").
Save to /sdcard and pull the file instead.
- Screenshots are empty while Netflix, an HDMI input or the ttvs update screen is shown.
- Storage: /data was 93% full (190 MB free) and sys_storage_threshold_percentage is 10, so about 270 MB
is reserved and pm install failed with "Requested internal only, but not enough space".
`pm trim-caches 4G` freed about 100 MB, not enough. Uninstalling user-installed apps the owner did not
want (Crossy Road, Max, Crunchyroll, DirecTV GO) freed about 470 MB. Those are not in this list.
- INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE is not a firmware sideload block here:
1) with this little RAM, the com.tcl.guard memory manager (TGuard) kills com.android.vending in the
middle of verification (logcat "tguard-kill-systemApp"), which fails the install. Force-stop
apps / `am kill-all`, or install right after a reboot.
2) installing only base.apk of a split app is rejected by Play Protect for the missing splits; that
is not a valid sideload test. The 272 KB launcher APK installed fine.
- com.tcl.guard runs as a persistent system process (*PERS*, uid 1000). `pm disable-user` succeeds but
the process still starts at boot, so the disable does not stop the memory manager. It stays in the
list for the UI/cleaner parts.
- Opening Settings' About page directly (am start -a android.settings.DEVICE_INFO_SETTINGS) and then
Software update crashes TvSettings (ClassCastException AboutActivity -> MainSettings in
com.tcl.android.tv.settings.update.SoftwareUpdateFragment). Enter through the main Settings menu.
Not caused by the debloat.
- com.tcl.ttvs is the firmware updater (also BI and Alexa), not text-to-speech. Keep it.
com.tcl.messagebox carries an org.tcl.ttvs receiver; it was disabled here and the updater still
opened and showed the check screen.

mau.header:
Home+ (中嘉寬頻, Taiwan) STB-6252C, Inspur "Homeplustv", MediaTek MT5221, 1.85 GB RAM, 32-bit (armeabi-v7a)
Android TV 11 (API 30), Operator Tier. Tested on build Homeplustv/STB6252C/STB6252C:11/MAIN/2.22.12 (2024-09-05 patch).

Apply:   tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost <box ip> examples\homeplus-stb-6252c\debloat.txt
Undo:    tools\restore.ps1 -TvHost <box ip> examples\homeplus-stb-6252c\debloat.txt -Stock com.inspur.isoc.launcher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Connecting: Developer options > USB debugging. service.adb.tcp.port=5555 is baked into the firmware,
so port 5555 is open whenever USB debugging is on. ro.adb.secure=1: accept the prompt on screen once.
No device owner / MDM. Sideloading is allowed (install_non_market_apps=1).

Quirks: `screencap` returns a 0-byte file on this box, so verify Home with
`dumpsys window | grep mCurrentFocus` instead of screenshots.

Stock launcher: com.inspur.isoc.launcher (CNS_Launcher, HOME priority 2). There is NO Google launcher
on this box; the only other HOME claimant is com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome. The
launcher rotates friDay 影音 promo posters every 5 s (RecommendPosterRotationFrameView). Its embedded
TvInputService is not a registered TV input (dumpsys tv_input lists only the DVB-C tuner
com.inspur.tang.mwtvinput/.MWTvInputService/HW28), so disabling the launcher does not touch cable TV.
It is NOT in this list: launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -StockLauncher com.inspur.isoc.launcher disables
it once com.gathin.tvhome owns Home. While it stays enabled, HOME priority 2 beats the new launcher's 0
and `cmd package set-home-activity` to com.gathin.tvhome is ignored.

Live TV: com.android.tv (operator build LiveTv_CNS) on the tuner above. It cannot parse the passthrough
channel URI the launcher's Inputs menu sends on a cold start (ContentUriUtils.safeParseId), and its window
closes again, which looks like a crash. Set "live_tv_input_id": "none" in a theme so the Live TV row starts
the app normally, and "input_sources": ["HW28=-"] to drop the tuner's own row, which sends the same URI.

Firmware updater: com.inspur.httpupgrade (the operator's OTA client, a PERSISTENT priv-app) stays ON:
its line at the end is commented out. The tested unit had it disabled, because its owner chose to freeze
the firmware so that an operator update cannot re-enable the packages below or hand Home back to the
stock launcher. Uncomment the line to do the same. Then no firmware, security-patch or channel-table
updates arrive while it is off, and being PERSISTENT an empty process still starts at boot (no services,
about 5 MB). To take an update later: `pm enable com.inspur.httpupgrade`, let it run, then re-apply the
list with tools\check.py --fix.

Watchdog: com.inspur.android.daemon is left enabled. From its APK: LightsService (front LED),
ProcessMonitorService (force-stops cached processes not on the allow list in assets/processes.json),
GlobalKeyReceiver (remote keys such as YouTube), and boot-time sleep/dream/animation/HDMI-CEC settings.
Nothing in it re-enables packages or resets Home, and it did not kill com.gathin.tvhome in the
background (Android protects the Home process). Disabling it would lose the LED and the YouTube key.

Wi-Fi: disabling a uid 1000 com.inspur.* package logs "Remove all networks for app"; the saved networks
survived because their creator is android.uid.system. Check `cmd wifi list-networks` before and after.

Leave alone: com.inspur.tang.mwtvinput (DVB-C cable tuner, TIF input), com.android.tv (Live TV),
com.inspur.cns.settings (channel and time settings), com.atv.keymanage (remote keys), com.atv.setupwizard,
com.actions.* (Bluetooth remote firmware, pairing, volume), com.omni.simplesetup (remote's TV/AVR IR setup),
com.omni.modeswitch, com.omni.sci, com.mstar.* and com.mtk.systemcontrol (SoC services),
com.google.android.tv.remote.service (BT remote), com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith,
Play Store / Play services, the keyboard. Never start com.inspur.factory (factory test).

Kept on by the owner's choice (disable them if you do not use them): com.google.android.katniss
(voice search, 110-196 MB resident), com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast built-in, about 137 MB),
com.google.android.youtube.tv, com.disney.disneyplus, tw.com.app.watchtv, com.inspur.member.center,
com.omni.otademo (ODM OTA), com.inspur.cnsvbm (VbmService + AreaLimitationService; purpose unknown,
may be tied to the cable entitlement, untested).

Netflix: the box is not Netflix certified (no ro.netflix.* properties); Play Store answers
"your device isn't compatible with this version".

Status: applied 2026-10-20 and used daily for three days. Nothing broke. Used and working: Home, the Inputs
list, YouTube, MagentaTV, Jellyfin, Prime Video, Bluetooth, HDMI playback (picture and sound),
every remote button listed below, USB storage (a stick mounts, shows in Files and ES File Explorer
and the remote's USB button opens the Whale file browser; a 1080p H.264 MP4 plays with picture and

See also examples/sankey-smart2ktvse (another WhaleOS set: stock launcher com.whaletv.launcher, different
package set); both agree that com.zeasn.livetv must stay.

Live TV: com.zeasn.livetv is the stock Android TV app. With no tuner source it opens to "Kein Signal", but it
also hosts HDMI playback, so keep it (and live_tv_package pointing at it).

HDMI: with a source plugged in, the Inputs menu shows it as one row ("Playback_1 . HDMI3", the CEC device name
plus the port) and switching works. Two things must be right for that: the TV app has to be named in config.xml
(live_tv_package = com.zeasn.livetv), and the launcher has to send the input intent to it (#1297). Without that,
Android shows its chooser (com.zeasn.livetv, MagentaTV and ES File Explorer all claim the channel URI) instead
of switching. Older launcher builds also listed the port and the CEC device as two rows.

Connecting: Settings > Developer options > USB debugging; ADB answers on 5555 (Wireless debugging also
works, port shown in its screen). Turn both off afterwards; port 5555 is plaintext.

Launcher half works: sideloaded APKs install and a launcher with the HOME category is accepted.

No Google Play Store and no Google setup wizard: nothing else claims Home (only Android's FallbackHome).

APP STORE: com.zeasn.whaleos.appgallery ("Apps" tile) is the ONLY store, and the installer of record for
apps added through it (Downloader, Jellyfin, ZDF, ...). It is left ENABLED below. Disabling it leaves no
way to install or update apps except sideloading (Downloader, or `pm install -r` over ADB).

Remote (IR remote "ir_keypad", layout /vendor/usr/keylayout/RS1U-GL-RY.kl). With the stock launcher gone:
Input    scancode 79  = TV_INPUT. Nothing on this firmware answers com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS, so the
button needs INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 and handle_view_inputs = true in config.xml (the launcher then
answers the request with its Inputs menu, also from inside an app).
Gear     scancode 141 = SETTINGS, handled by the firmware (opens Whale settings).
Netflix  scancode 60  = KEYCODE_F2   -> app_keys "KEYCODE_F2:<package>" (useless once Netflix is off).
Disney+  scancode 897 = keycode 312  -> app_keys "312:<package>"; stock behaviour is a "please try again" toast.
YouTube and Prime Video buttons keep working through the firmware.
Find other codes: `getevent -lt` while pressing, then grep the scancode in the .kl file above.

mau.header:
Impex evoQ 4K (Changhong, product GTVU64IP, board alimos), Google TV 14 (SDK 34), firmware UKN3.250415.053,
MediaTek mt5896 (platform merak), India. MemTotal about 1.8 GB. ro.product.manufacturer Changhong.
Same Changhong board ("alimos") as examples/benq-e55-760 (GTVU64BQ) on an older UKN3 build, and the same
UKN3 platform as examples/kogan-gtvu65kg.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip>:<port> TV_ADB_BINARY=adb tools/disable.sh examples/impex-evoq-4k/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip>:<port> TV_ADB_BINARY=adb tools/restore.sh examples/impex-evoq-4k/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Install: TV_HOST=<tv ip>:<port> TV_ADB_BINARY=adb launcher/build-and-install.sh   (after this list)
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (build-and-install.sh disables it; pass it to restore.sh).
Live TV: com.cltv.hybrid (iWedia TV app, enabled here; set live_tv_package to it).
Already disabled from the factory: com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.isdbtuner, com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.atsctuner,
com.mediatek.opapp, com.mediatek.tv.oneworld.tvcenter.

Tested on one set the same day, not a multi-day soak: after each batch Home opens and the Input menu still
lists Live TV, AV and HDMI 1-4; HDMI 1 switches and Home returns; YouTube and JioHotstar launch and play.
After a reboot with the whole list and the launcher: the disabled list is identical (no package re-enabled at
boot), Home is com.gathin.tvhome at power-on (no Live TV autostart, so neither power_on_home nor
boot_to_live_tv), the crash buffer is empty. AdGuard Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) validates.

KEEP, even though the names look like bloat:
- com.cltv.hybrid, com.cltv.mal, com.mediatek.tis, com.mediatek.tv.agent, com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.dvbtuner:
Live TV and the inputs.
- com.mediatek.extservice (CEC, Bluetooth mic), com.mediatek.autopair (remote pairing),
com.mediatek.tv.oneworld.wizardkt (its BluetoothActivityVoice is the "pair your remote" screen the mic opens).
- com.homwee.factory (not started, not disabled), com.homwee.dynamicbacklight, com.gdch.gameoptimiser.
- com.homwee.mmp.screenshare and com.homwee.multiscreenshare: the AirPlay receiver, kept by choice here.
- com.gdch.wwtv.mediaplayer: the USB media player. tools/disable.sh skips it (it asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE);
examples/benq-e55-760 found that a false positive on the same board, not re-checked on this set.
- com.homwee.upgrade, com.homwee.dmt.upgrade, com.mediatek.tv.systemupdater: firmware and app updates.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- Port 5555 is closed with USB debugging on; Wireless debugging (on Wi-Fi) pairs and works, with
TV_ADB_BINARY=adb (tools/native-adb.md). Its port changes at every reboot: read it with `adb mdns services`.
- The saved Wi-Fi network is owned by setupwraith (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`): forget and re-join
it in Settings, switch Wireless debugging on again, then apply the list. Without setupwraith disabled its
.RecoveryActivity (HOME priority 1) takes Home once launcherx is off, as on examples/chiq-gtvu65.
- The remote here is IR (MTK Smart TV IR Receiver, vendor 0x3697). Its gear button arrives as evdev code 498
(0x1F2), with no Android keycode, so it does nothing once launcherx is disabled. The kernel logs every IR key
(`logcat | grep MIRC_Keydown`), which is how 498 was read; getevent showed nothing. settings_key_scancodes 498
with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 makes it open Settings, but a bound helper then drops the volume key repeats (one
step per press while held, as in docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md). The owner kept the ramp and no
helper; Settings is the pill on Home. The mic button (evdev 0x242) opens the wizard's "pair your remote"
screen while no Bluetooth remote is bonded.
- Injected `input keyevent` presses sometimes moved focus two rows (a synthesized repeat); the real remote
moves one row. Check navigation with the remote.

Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (disabled by launcher/build-and-install.sh once the new
launcher is Home). With launcherx and setupwraith both enabled, set-home-activity printed Success and Home
stayed on launcherx.
setupwraith: the active Wi-Fi had been created by setupwraith during first setup. It was forgotten and re-joined
in Settings first (then owned by com.android.tv.settings), so disable.sh's guard passed without
FORCE_SETUPWRAITH. CastInfoProvider lives in setupwraith here and logcat reports "Failed to find provider
info" after the disable, yet casting from an iPhone (YouTube) still worked after a reboot.
Live TV / input switcher: com.realtek.tv (.SelectInputActivity); set live_tv_package to com.realtek.tv.
Remote (RC-37, Bluetooth + IR): the gear sends keycode 83 over Bluetooth -> settings_key_keycodes [83] with
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1. The Netflix and YouTube buttons go out over IR as KTC keycodes 3001/3003 and are consumed
by com.realtek.keyintercept, which on Google TV only broadcasts com.google.global_button.ACTION_LAUNCH_APP to
launcherx: with launcherx disabled they do nothing, and no key helper sees them.
With HomeKeyService bound, a held volume key stops repeating (one step per press), as on the TCL G09.
Kept: all com.realtek.* TV/input packages; com.realsil.ota (remote firmware updater, RcuUpdate); KTC factory
packages com.kgzn.serialport and com.kgzn.tvfactory (global key receivers, never launched); Chromecast;
voice (katniss, tv.remote.service); YouTube Music, karaoke, the ambient screensaver, TalkBack by choice.
No manufacturer firmware updater was found on this build.
Tested on one unit for ONE DAY only, not yet lived with for several days: HDMI game consoles, voice, casting and
the gear button checked with the real remote, one reboot.
