Built from examples/amazon-fire-tv-stick-4k-2018/debloat.txt (same Fire OS 6 build family), cut down to the packages
that exist on this TV and with the Live TV packages left alone: this is a TV set, and com.amazon.tv.livetv,
com.amazon.franktvinput and com.amazon.hedwig sit under its Live tab and inputs.

FIRE OS: DEBLOAT ONLY with the stock repo. Amazon's launcher is a protected package and keeps Home. To replace what
Home looks like on this set, see https://github.com/jeanbuntu/cleanyourtv/tree/fire-tv-launcher (a launcher plus a
Home watcher, kept in its own fork).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/insignia-ns42f201na22/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/insignia-ns42f201na22/debloat.txt com.amazon.tv.launcher
(restore.sh re-enables every package the record holds as on, the stock launcher included, since it is what owned
Home. On Fire OS it was never off, and Fire OS refuses the attempt with a `Cannot disable a protected package`
stack trace once per run (reported on Fire OS 8), which the batch carries on past:
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, 'Fire TV (Fire OS)'.)
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
ADB on Fire OS 6: Settings > My Fire TV > Developer options > ADB debugging. If Developer options is hidden,
Settings > My Fire TV > About > highlight the first entry and press select 7 times. Port 5555, no pairing.

Applied in three batches with the TV checked in between, then one reboot: all 43 stayed disabled. Lived with for three
days; the packages left enabled below are the ones used every day.
disable.sh skipped com.amazon.bueller.photos, com.amazon.cloud9 and com.amazon.tahoe on its input-handler check (they
accept any video link, they do not run an input); with HANDLERS_ALLOW=1 they disabled cleanly and nothing broke.

Kept on purpose (personal choices, comment them back in to drop them): Alexa voice search (com.amazon.vizzini and its
helpers), Prime Video (com.amazon.firebat), casting and mirroring (com.amazon.cast.sink, dialservice, whisperplay),
Hulu, Live TV, OTA updates and the Appstore. The streaming apps this list names are the ones this set did not use.

does not claim HOME on this build. `set-home-activity` prints Success but Home stays on tvlauncher until it

Notes from this TV (all batches verified with screenshots, a reboot and YouTube playback):
- The stock adb binary connects on Windows; port 5555 opens with USB debugging alone.
- If you keep the stock home: disabling tvrecommendations removes its notifications icon, the "Sponsored" hero
and "Sponsored by ..." rows stay (Google serves them to tvlauncher itself), and the Apps tab keeps a
"Google Play Movies & TV" promo tile after com.google.android.videos is gone.
- Screenshots come out black on Live TV, HDMI and DRM video. The Input key opens tvcenter's
TurnkeyUiMainActivity, which switches to the TV source after a few seconds. The launcher's Inputs menu
lists HDMI 1-4, Composite and Live TV.
- After a reboot com.mediatek.tv.service logs "Failed to find provider info for tv.anoki.acr.controller.support"
twice and carries on (same PID afterwards), as on the Hitachi.
- Used RAM 150 s after boot: 938 MB stock, 820 MB with every line below disabled, 703 MB with the launcher
as Home (free RAM 474 -> 561 -> 657 MB). Before, TED, Spotify, tvrecommendations and Google TV were
running in the background after boot (about 150 MB resident); none of them starts any more.
- /data is only 4.3 GB and was 86% full with a few streaming apps. Disabling frees no storage.
- Removing an updated system app's Play Store update (`pm uninstall <package>` without --user) re-enabled it
on this firmware; disable it again afterwards.

Kalley R10G (device R10G, product ACER_FFM, made by MOKA), Google TV on Android 14, firmware UKR1.260612.001
Realtek RTD2875P SoC, RTD6748 platform, 2 GB RAM. The remote reports as "RC860G Consumer Control".
Same hardware family as examples/prismplus-q65-ultra-r10g/, but a different brand build
(ACER_FFM) with its own preloads: Claro, Kick, JioTV, CBS, Apple TV and Prime Video.
Second unit (#1807), Colombia: same device and firmware, but product KALLEY_FFM
(fingerprint KALLEY/KALLEY_FFM/R10G:14/UKR1.260612.001); the boot loop and re-enable notes below are from it.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/kalley-r10g/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/kalley-r10g/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it to restore.sh).
Live TV and inputs: keep com.realtek.dtv and com.realtek.tv.atv (HDMI and the other inputs use them).
OTA: keep com.apps.ota and com.apps.authota. Keep com.realsil.ota too: it updates the remote.

Input button: the RC860G remote sends KEYCODE_TV_INPUT (kernel scan code 225), not KEYCODE_TV.
Enable the launcher's InputKeyService (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1) so the new launcher answers it.
com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS resolves to com.realtek.tv/.SelectInputActivity.

KEEP launcherx AND setupwraith ENABLED on this set (#1807). With both disabled, system_server crashed
35-75 s into every boot (sys.boot.reason watchdog; IllegalArgumentException: positionChildAt ... in
Task.moveToBack) and the TV restarted in a loop until both were enabled again over ADB in the boot window.
The setup that works here, from the #1807 report:
- set stock_home_redirect to com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (config.xml or a theme), so the
stock home is sent straight back to the new launcher;
- install with the key helpers and without disabling the stock launcher:
STOCK_LAUNCHER=none INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh
(Windows: launcher\build-and-install.ps1 -StockLauncher none -InputKeyService -HomeKeyService)
The installer stops at its Home check in this mode, since Home still resolves to launcherx: enable
HomeKeyService and InputKeyService by hand afterwards (Settings > Accessibility). Without the helpers
Home goes back to launcherx; set-home-activity does not hold on this build.
- With both helpers bound, holding volume steps once instead of ramping (the trade in
docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md).

The firmware turns most preloads back on at boot, as on the MOKA Acer R4G (docs/devices/acer-r4g.md):
after one reboot only com.cbs.ca, com.seraphic.media.tv.interactive.app, com.realtek.kara and
com.realtek.karaoke.userguide stayed disabled on the first #1807 set pass.
On the second pass, the privacy, telemetry, hotspot, partner and regional streaming packages
(com.android.adservices.api, com.android.ondevicepersonalization.services,
com.android.federatedcompute.services, com.android.tv.feedbackconsent,
com.realtek.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer, com.apps.wifihotspot,
com.mercadolibre.android.mplay_tv, com.iqiyi.i18n.tv) also stayed disabled across reboots.
config.json in this folder sets the 4-column dock with frosted glass and stock_home_redirect.

Tested on one set on 2026-10-19/20 with the reference launcher: the apps kept (Netflix, Disney+,
Max, Spotify, YouTube, Twitch, GeForce NOW, Stremio) still launch, and HDMI input, Home and the
Input button work. This list is fresh, not yet lived with for days; update it if something breaks.

mau.header:
Karbonn SWTV-20AE (Skyworth OEM, SW4H, MediaTek), Android TV 10, firmware QTG3.200617.002
Unit 2: Motorola SWTV-20AE (India), product SW4_TG, device SW4H, MediaTek m7332, the same build
QTG3.200617.002 (security patch 2022-04-05). Its notes are under "Unit 2" below.
ro.product.manufacturer=skyworth, device SW4H, API 29, armeabi-v7a, ~1.68 GB RAM.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV home, not Google TV launcherx).
Live TV: com.smartdevice.livetv / com.mediatek.tvinput.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/karbonn-swtv-20ae/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/karbonn-swtv-20ae/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Tested on the day of debloat and confirmed working. Same Skyworth SW4H platform as the
Panasonic 4KTV-0SU and OnePlus Y1. com.sky.market is a protected package: the firmware
refuses pm disable-user for it (SecurityException); it stays on.

Performance tweaks for 1.68 GB RAM (32-bit armeabi-v7a, MediaTek):
settings put global window_animation_scale 0.5
settings put global transition_animation_scale 0.5
settings put global animator_duration_scale 0.5
settings put global background_process_limit 2
Set reduced_motion: true in your theme's config.json for the CleanYourTV launcher.

Unit 2 (Motorola SWTV-20AE), applied 2026-10-23 in batches with a screenshot after each, then the
CleanYourTV launcher with HomeKeyService; Home, helpers and every disable held over two reboots.
Seen on that unit:
- com.google.android.tvrecommendations froze system_server's main thread for 2 s every 32 s
(logcat: "Slow dispatch took 2002ms ... AlarmManager", just before its ForegroundActivityTrackerJobService).
While HomeKeyService filters keys, a key release that lands in that freeze makes Android auto-repeat, so
the D-pad "keeps moving". Disabling it (already in this list) made the freezes rare.
- The firmware puts the screensaver back to Google Backdrop at boot (ScreenSaverSetDefTimeReceiver). To keep
the launcher's clock, set both `settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream`
and `screensaver_default_component` to the same value.
- With HomeKeyService filtering keys, a held volume key steps only once: Android 10 applies the step before
the helper sees the key. key_filter false brings hold-to-ramp back, at the cost of the remote buttons.
- Remote buttons handled by HomeKeyService ignore keys sent with `input keyevent`; test them with the remote.
- Granting usage access with appops is lost if the TV reboots before Android saves it: run
`cmd appops write-settings` straight after.
- A saved Wi-Fi network joined in the first-run wizard belongs to setupwraith and is forgotten when it is
disabled (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`). The home network there was android.uid.system.

mau.ten: Kogan G7 Google TV (model "Kogan G7", manufacturer Expressluck, device cottongreen, Realtek), Australia
mau.header:
Kogan G7 Google TV (model "Kogan G7", manufacturer Expressluck, device cottongreen, Realtek), Australia
Google TV (Android 11, SDK 30), firmware RTK5.250429.042, 1.7 GB RAM

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/kogan-g7/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/kogan-g7/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.realtek.tv (HDMI inputs are
com.realtek.tv.passthrough). Lived with for six days with the launcher installed, on Wi-Fi.
This firmware is lean: no ACR or analytics package was found.

Keep: com.realtek.tv*, com.realtek.dtv, com.realtek.menu, com.realtek.slices (settings slices, restarts the
TV input service), com.realtek.keyintercept* (remote keys), com.realtek.statusbar, com.realtek.secservice,
com.realtek.display.monitor, com.seraphic.hbbtv.app (HbbTV / Freeview Plus), com.realsil.ota (firmware
updates), com.rtk.mediabrowser (USB media player), com.realtek.kara (karaoke mic).

Known quirks on this firmware:
- With launcherx disabled, setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1, so it goes too.
Disabling it did not drop the TV off Wi-Fi here.
- The remote's app buttons die with launcherx. Netflix (IR keycode 3001), YouTube (IR 3003) and Prime Video
(Bluetooth usage 0x0c0076) are consumed by Realtek's key service (com.realtek.keyintercept) before Android
sees them. Because the TV has the com.google.android.feature.AMATI_EXPERIENCE feature, it only hands them
to launcherx/.globalbutton.GlobalButtonLaunch_Receiver as an explicit broadcast, so they cannot be
remapped (same as the IR keys on inclo-google-tv-4k). Disney+ arrives as KEYCODE_BUTTON_6 (193) through
Google's GlobalKeyReceiver, and app_keys "193:com.disney.disneyplus" with InputKeyService brings it back
(checked with the real remote). Shell cannot disable launcherx's HomeActivity on its own
(SecurityException), and with launcherx enabled it takes HOME back, so the other three stay dead.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Point it at the launcher's clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (disabled by launcher/build-and-install.sh after the
new launcher is confirmed Home). On this build setupwraith re-claims Home (.RecoveryActivity/.MainActivity)
the moment launcherx is off, and the shell cannot disable that component alone (SecurityException), so
setupwraith has to be disabled too (listed below). The active Wi-Fi here was system-owned (OwnerUid 1000),
so disabling setupwraith did NOT drop Wi-Fi - but setupwraith owned another saved network, so disable.sh's
guard skipped it and this unit needed FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1. Check yours first with the README's
"Currently Connected" check (the cname list alone does not say which network is in use): if setupwraith
owns the network in use, forget and re-join it in Settings. Disabling setupwraith may break Chromecast
(mediashell reads device info from it); re-enable setupwraith to get casting back.
With launcherx disabled, Assistant/Gemini results no longer open (Google shows them inside launcherx, #2812):
see docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Voice search for a song or video", and `stock_home_redirect` in themes/README.md.
Live TV / tuner app: com.realtek.tv (set as live_tv_package in config.xml, and hidden from the grid).
Netflix (com.netflix.ninja) shipped already disabled on this unit.
Remote app buttons (for config.xml app_keys): YouTube 190, Netflix 191, Prime Video 195, TL;DR 200.

installed app verified by screenshot; rebooted and the fork launcher came back as Home.

Status: applied 2026-10-27 on one projector and used daily through 2026-10-28, reboot-checked several
times. Nothing broke. Used and working: Home, Settings (Android's settings, #2101), Inputs (HDMI1),
YouTube, the launcher's Open on start.

ADB: the firmware's "ADB debug" switch (Other settings > Developer mode) turns on TLS Wireless debugging
on 5555, and the firmware has no pairing screen of its own. Pair through com.android.tv.settings (open its
Wireless debugging page with Activity Launcher), then `adb tcpip 5555` and Wireless debugging off. 5555
closes again at every reboot.

Home: with the stock launcher left enabled (STOCK_LAUNCHER=none) the firmware opens com.htc.magcubicos at
every boot whatever the default Home, and stock_home_redirect does not help: something with the system uid
clears enabled_accessibility_services within seconds, so HomeKeyService never stays bound. Disabling the
stock launcher (install line above) makes the projector boot into this launcher. The cost: the tile
Settings go with it, so there is no keystone or projection-mode screen and the remote's Settings key does
nothing; auto keystone and autofocus (com.hysd.vafocus) stay on. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are in Android's
settings (the Settings pill).

Inputs: com.softwinner.vis lists HDMI1-3 and CVBS1-2, but nothing on this firmware handles the
passthrough URI as a TV app (ACTION_VIEW on it resolves to OfficeSuite), so config.json sends the Inputs
pill to Allwinner's own source picker, com.softwinner.awsource.

Status: disabled in batches on one TV on 2026-10-21 with a Home screenshot after each, then launcher/ installed
as Home, a reboot, Live TV/HDMI switching and the real remote's buttons checked. Still working after a day of use, not days yet.

RE-ENABLED AT EVERY BOOT: com.at.factory.factorymanager (CommonManager.enableApp, on BOOT_COMPLETED) turns
com.google.android.katniss and com.google.android.tvrecommendations back on, and Android then rebinds katniss
as the voice interaction service and tvrecommendations as a notification listener (~63 MB PSS together).
Cleared voice settings, a revoked listener, RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND ignore and the restricted bucket are all
reset at boot, and shell may not disable single components on Android 11, so both stay commented out below.
Without them MemAvailable after boot would be ~349 MB instead of ~315 MB.
com.google.android.marvin.talkback also comes back enabled after a reboot but never runs.
The screen sleeps after 5 minutes idle (screen_off_timeout=300000, factory value) and Wi-Fi drops with it:
a TV that "vanishes" a few minutes after a reboot is asleep, not broken; press Power.

"Allow USB debugging?" on first connect. Sideloading works (pm install over the shell).

tv.service dispatches the YouTube/Prime keys; tvinput is the HDMI/tuner inputs), com.cvte.hotkey.receiver
(Disney+ key), com.cvte.tv.infoprovider (device serial), com.cvte.autobacklight, com.airoha.android.btd
(Bluetooth). Never open com.cvte.tv.fac.*, com.cvte.tv.hisensefac, com.cvte.tv.at, com.at.factory.* or
mediatek.factorymenu.ui, even to look: on Hisense/CVTE boards that flips a factory-mode flag.

not the stock launcher, so they keep working with launcher/ as Home; no InputKeyService needed. The remote
has no Settings button. The mic button (KEY_F13) opens Bluetooth pairing until the remote is paired.
setupwraith does not claim HOME here and is left on; on the tested set it owned one saved Wi-Fi network.
Inputs: HDMI 1, HDMI 2, two tuner inputs; no composite AV is registered.

Inputs, YouTube, casting and the clock screensaver checked, and everything held over several reboots.

Setup wizard:     com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (claims HOME)

HDMI/AV inputs:   com.mediatek.tis
Remote:           the Settings (gear) button sends keycode 83 (KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION); it needs HomeKeyService
(settings_key_keycodes 83). With the helper on, a held volume key steps only once.

Quirks on this firmware, all seen on the TV:
- com.netflix.ninja is turned back on by the firmware at every boot. Disabling it only lasts until the
next restart; block it from running in the background instead if you never use it:
`cmd appops set com.netflix.ninja RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND ignore`, the same for RUN_IN_BACKGROUND, then
`cmd appops write-settings` (undo: set both back to `default`). That freed about 50 MB of RAM.
- Wi-Fi joined in the first-run wizard belongs to setupwraith, and Android forgets it the moment setupwraith
is disabled. Check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`: if it is not android.uid.system, forget the
network and join it again in Settings before setupwraith goes.
- The ambient glow costs about 22 ms a frame on this GPU (~45 fps). reduced_motion true with
focus_overshoot false keeps the glow at 11 ms a frame (60 fps).
- A second Google TV profile is a second Android user, and this board's key service
(com.smartdevice.global.service, kept) then takes a provider client for launcherx's LiveTvContentProvider
on every gear/Input hotkey: with launcherx disabled it throws, and RescueParty climbs to the level that
switches the launcher's accessibility helpers off. Seen on a Coocaa Y74 Pro 65" (SW10_TG, Google TV 14,
UKN4.250714.140). Run `pm list users` first, and see
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#app-buttons-crash-the-tvs-own-key-service-on-a-set-with-a-second-user-skyworthcoocaa

com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.atsctuner, com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.isdbtuner and five jp.co.sharp.* demo apps.

Kept on purpose: com.mediatek.tis (HDMI/AV), com.tianci.localmedia (USB media), com.mediatek.extservice
and com.dolby.android.audio.service (HDMI-CEC/ARC and audio), com.smartdevice.global.service,
com.mediatek.autopair and com.mediatek.tv.agent (remote, pairing, hot keys), com.smartdevice.dailyshortcut
(quick menu), com.mediatek.tv.systemupdater (firmware updates), Play Store, Play Services, keyboards.

code), `adb pair <ip:pairport> <code>`, `adb connect <ip:port>`, then `adb tcpip 5555`. persist.adb.tcp.port
stays 5555, and port 5555 answered after later reboots. ro.adb.secure=1, so each computer is accepted on screen.

Setup wizard (com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith):
- With launcherx disabled and Projectivy as Home, setupwraith's RecoveryActivity took HOME and system_server
crashed in a loop (FATAL EXCEPTION IN SYSTEM PROCESS: android.display, positionChildAt ... is not a child),
as described in docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md. Disabling setupwraith stopped it.
- The box then dropped off Wi-Fi: the network had been saved during setup, so it belonged to setupwraith.
Re-joining it in Settings fixed it (owner now android.uid.system). tools/disable.sh checks this for you.
- The Cast credentials provider lives in setupwraith here too (CastInfoProvider), yet casting YouTube from a
phone still worked four days and several reboots after disabling it, unlike on the Google TV Streamer list.

AUDIO (Realtek Dolby MS12, soundbar over HDMI). See README.md in this folder for the logs.
- With Settings > Display & Sound > Advanced sound settings > Surround sound = Always
(settings global encoded_surround_output=2), ExoPlayer apps (Stremio, Nuvio) open a DIRECT E-AC3 track and
the sound stutters about once a second on a Samsung HW-Q990C. Never (=1) stops the stutter, but the
soundbar then reports 2-channel PCM.
- Fix: keep Surround sound on Never and set Realtek's hidden "Preferred MS12 output" page to
"Dolby Digital Plus/Dolby Atmos" (2nd entry; the list is MAT, DD+/Atmos, PCM, DD/AC3):
adb shell am start -n com.android.tv.settings/.slice.SliceActivity \
-d content://com.realtek.slices.sliceprovider/ms12 --es slice_uri content://com.realtek.slices.sliceprovider/ms12
adb shell input keyevent DPAD_DOWN; adb shell input keyevent DPAD_CENTER
logcat then reads `GetAudioMs12OutputMode ... mode=2`. It survives reboots (checked twice). Result: no
stutter and the Q990C shows Dolby Atmos for an E-AC3 Atmos stream in Stremio.
- The box ships with HDMI-CEC auto wake/standby off; left that way.

Kept on purpose: com.dolby.android.audio.service, com.realtek.slices (hidden audio/video pages),
com.rtk.partnerinterface, every com.sdt.* service (front panel LED, global keys, remote pairing
com.sdt.mecoolrcupair, OTA com.sdt.ota, device info, customization, backup manager), com.oemservice,
com.google.android.tv.remote.service and com.google.android.tv.dfuservice (remote), Play Store and Play
Services, Gboard, the Assistant (com.google.android.katniss), Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell),
Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:

Max, YouTube and Play Store start on their own. This list plus launcher/ took MemAvailable from about
230 MB to about 300 MB; `cmd appops set <pkg> RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND ignore` on the streaming apps took
it to about 330-360 MB. The apps still open normally; `... allow` undoes it, restore.sh does not.
- The load average reads ~95 at idle with the CPU 80% idle: about 98 MStar driver threads (DMX_Filt_Task,
VMon_Task...) sit in D state. Not real load.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV, not Google TV launcherx), with
Shop and Discover tabs. Only it and Settings' FallbackHome claim HOME; setupwraith does not.
No HDMI inputs (it's a box); a DTVKit tuner input (org.dtvkit.inputsource) is registered, and

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Port 5555 opens as soon as USB debugging is on; no pairing. The box also advertises
_adb._tcp over mDNS, which is the quickest way to find it when DHCP moves it.
- The saved Wi-Fi belongs to com.google.uid.shared (GMS), not setupwraith.
- Network debugging does not survive a reboot: port 5555 refuses connections afterwards until it
is switched on again in Developer options (USB debugging itself stays on).

launcher has HOME priority 2, so this list is suspended instead (README.md here) and the
stock launcher cannot be replaced yet.

Not the 8000: the Nokia Streaming Box 8000 (SEI600NK4, PR #326) refuses every `pm disable*`. This

and launcher/build-and-install.sh work and no suspend or Home redirect is needed. Check

Connecting: Developer options > USB debugging and Network debugging. Port 5555 opens without pairing,
but ro.adb.secure=1, so the computer has to be accepted on screen once. The box advertises _adb._tcp
over mDNS. Unlike the 8000, network debugging survives a reboot here: switch it off when done.

claim HOME, and the saved Wi-Fi belongs to Play services (com.google.android.gms), not setupwraith.

RemoteKeyEventActionImpl, LogcatEventProducer and an AccessibilityController. AdGuard DNS does not
block it (hopprtv.com, hoppr.com.au resolve), so disabling it is the only way to stop it.

Private DNS with dns.adguard-dns.com works (Android 14), see PROMPT.md.

rather than this repo's launcher; the stock launcher has to go for either of them to take over.
A Shield has no HDMI inputs and no tuner, so the launcher's Inputs pill has nothing to list.

mau.header:
NVIDIA SHIELD TV Pro (2019, model P2897, codename mdarcy, Tegra X1+, 3 GB RAM), Android TV 11 (API 30)
Tested on SHIELD Experience 9.2.4 (33.2.0.400), build RQ1A.210105.003.7825230_4387.0822,
security patch 2026-01-05. Package names also checked against a unit on 9.2.2.
The 2019 tube (P3430) and the 2015/2017 models run the same 9.x software, so this is a fair
starting point for them too. Check `pm list packages` first.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<shield ip> tools/disable.sh examples/nvidia-shield-tv-pro-2019/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<shield ip> tools/restore.sh examples/nvidia-shield-tv-pro-2019/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Connecting: Developer options -> turn on "Network debugging"; that is what opens ADB on port 5555.
The Pro has only USB-A host ports, so there is no cable route. Ethernet and Wi-Fi get different
addresses and the Shield can come back from a reboot on the other one, so reserve an IP in your router.

Launcher: the stock launcher is com.google.android.tvlauncher, so the defaults in tools/restore.sh
and launcher/build-and-install.sh work. Run build-and-install.sh before this list. The stock
launcher's Home filter has priority 2 and launcher/'s has 0, so `cmd package set-home-activity`
has no effect while the stock launcher is enabled; disabling it (build-and-install.sh does that
last) is what hands Home over. launcher/ stayed the default Home across a reboot. With no
launcher at all, Home falls back to com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome.
Leave com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith alone. It declares Home activities, but after setup
none of them is a Home candidate (its MainActivity is disabled), unlike on some Google TV sets.
A Shield has no HDMI inputs and no tuner, so the launcher's Inputs pill has nothing to list. To
reach a network tuner through Live Channels, set live_tv_package to com.google.android.tv in
config.xml.
The network pill says "Wi-Fi" without the network name, because location is off by default
(location_mode=0) and Android 11 hides the SSID without it. Over Ethernet it says "Ethernet".

Notes:
- The remote's Netflix button is handled in firmware; disabling Netflix doesn't free it.
- The default screensaver is Backdrop (com.google.android.backdrop). Switch to the Clock
screensaver (README) before disabling Backdrop, or nothing is set.
- A SHIELD Experience update can re-enable packages; re-run this list afterwards.
- On a Shield where some of these were already removed with `pm uninstall --user 0`,
disable.sh still reports "disabled-user" for them. That's harmless.
- Leave alone: com.nvidia.blakepairing, com.nvidia.bluetooth.*, com.nvidia.shieldtech.accessoryui,
com.nvidia.ControllerMapper, com.nvidia.remotelocator, com.nvidia.irtuner (remote, controllers,
Bluetooth); com.nvidia.NvCPLSvc, com.nvidia.nvaudiosvc, com.nvidia.avsync,
com.dolby.android.audio.service (AI upscaling, display, audio); com.nvidia.shieldservice,
com.nvidia.packagemanagerservice, com.nvidia.KeyComboOta, com.android.tv.settings,
com.android.providers.tv (Watch Next and Live Channels), com.google.android.tv.remote.service.
- Some guides remove Play Services, keychain or com.android.se on the Shield. People report
soft-bricked units after doing so. Don't.

mau.header:
OnePlus TV (model C00, codename Cebu), Android TV 10 (API 29), firmware QTG3.201207.001
MediaTek m7632, armeabi-v7a, UI at 1920x1080, ~1.8 GB RAM, India. Classic Android TV home, not Google TV.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher. Live TV app: com.heytap.tv.livetv.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/oneplus-tv-cebu/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/oneplus-tv-cebu/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Kept on purpose: the HDMI/tuner stack (com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.agent, com.heytap.tv.support,
com.mediatek.tvinputservice.arbitratorservice, com.heytap.tvapiservice), Live TV (com.heytap.tv.livetv),
the remote service and TV keyboard (com.oneplus.tv.remote), the hot keys (com.mediatek.hotkey.dispatcher,
which handles the Input key), the Netflix key (com.mstar.netflixobserver), Google Assistant
(com.google.android.katniss), firmware updates (com.oneplus.tv.systemupgrade, com.heytap.oprcupgradeservice),
Play Store and Play Services. Left alone and never launched: the factory apps (com.heytap.optvfactory,
com.oneplus.tv.factory). setupwraith does not claim HOME here.
Specifically, keep com.heytap.tv.support enabled: com.heytap.tv.livetv (IPCManager.java#177) binds to
com.heytap.tv.support/.server.TvSupportService before opening a TvInputSession. With it disabled,
dumpsys hdmi_control still detects the connected device (e.g. a PlayStation 5 on HDMI 3), but
com.heytap.tv.livetv leaves mainSessionToken null and times out after 3 seconds with "No Signal, please
check the connection of input source." (#321). Re-enabling com.heytap.tv.support alone restores HDMI
immediately with no reboot.
With launcher/ as Home (live_tv_package com.heytap.tv.livetv), Home, Input, Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video
and the Assistant mic on the remote work without InputKeyService or HomeKeyService.
USB debugging alone opens port 5555, and it stays open across reboots until switched off.
Reboot-checked: nothing came back enabled. AdGuard Private DNS validates.

Second unit: same model on Android TV 11 (API 30), firmware RTM8.240401.135, India.
The telemetry and content groups were applied, plus some extras and preloads by choice;
Chromecast, Miracast, TV Mirror, OnePlus Connect and Bluetooth speaker mode were kept. After a reboot
the disabled list was unchanged.
- Not installed on this firmware: com.google.android.tv.bugreportsender, net.oneplus.odm(.provider),
com.heytap.tv.imagewall and the streaming preloads below except YouTube Music and Play Movies.
The USB gallery, music and video players are activities of com.heytap.tv.filebrowser here, so
disabling that one package takes all four.
- Not installed either: com.mstar.netflixobserver and com.mediatek.tvinputservice.arbitratorservice. The
remote's Home, Input, Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video and mic buttons still worked with launcher/ as Home
and no key services.
- setupwraith does not claim HOME here either: only the stock launcher and Settings' FallbackHome did.
- The remote's Settings (gear) button sends KEY_MENU, which arrives as keycode 82. With
"settings_key_keycodes": [82] and "settings_key_panel": true in a theme, it opens the quick settings
panel on Home without HomeKeyService; inside apps it stays their Menu key.
- com.heytap.tv.btspeaker is only the screen that makes the TV discoverable as a Bluetooth speaker; the
A2DP sink is in com.android.bluetooth. Keep it if a phone or laptop plays through the TV.
- The kernel reports a MemAvailable far above MemTotal (about 309 GB), so RAM readings that use it
(launcher show_stats, addons/capacity-stats) show 0 MB used. Storage readings are right.
- Private DNS (Control D) validates.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- USB debugging opens port 5555 straight away; no Wireless debugging pairing needed.
- KEEP com.google.android.tv.remote.service. Besides the phone remote it carries the Bluetooth remote's
mic: with it disabled the mic button does nothing at all (no key event, no voice UI). Re-enabling it
brings the mic back. It holds the android.app.role.SYSTEM_TELEVISION_REMOTE_SERVICE role.
- The Wi-Fi network saved during first setup belongs to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi: OwnerUid = setupwraith's
uid). Forget and re-join it in Settings > Network & Internet before disabling setupwraith; afterwards it
shows cname=android.uid.system:1000. tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith until then.

- Voice search (Gemini / com.google.android.katniss) keeps working with launcherx disabled.
- Remote buttons (/vendor/usr/keylayout/Vendor_0957_Product_0031.kl):
YouTube = KEYCODE_BUTTON_3 and Free TV = KEYCODE_FEATURED_APP_1, both routed to launcherx, so they do
nothing once it is disabled. Netflix = KEYCODE_BUTTON_4; the Disney+ and Paramount+ buttons send
BUTTON_9 / BUTTON_10. Those three go to com.droidlogic's GlobalKeyReceiver ("oneTouchPlay"), which opens
the app, and for a disabled or missing app logs "Cannot find intent" or opens its Play Store page.
InputKeyService (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh) with app_keys remaps them, checked
with the physical remote, e.g. in a theme's config.json:

"KEYCODE_FEATURED_APP_1:com.amarullz.androidtv.animetvjmto"]

- Google TV / Play Movies (com.google.android.videos) is not preinstalled on this box.
- Disabling dreamx leaves no screensaver set (screensaver_components was null; the default was dreamx).
Point it at the launcher's clock: settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Unlike the Chromecast on Google TV 14, port 5555 is open as soon as USB debugging is on; no pairing.
- If a VPN app is connected, Settings > Network shows the VPN tunnel address, not the LAN one.
Find the box with `nc -z <lan>.x 5555` or `dns-sd -B _adb-tls-connect._tcp local.`.
- The Wi-Fi network saved during first setup belongs to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi: cname=...setupwraith).
Forget and re-join it in Settings before disabling setupwraith, or the network is deleted.
Second unit: this applies to every network saved during setup, not only the one in use - a second,
out-of-range network saved at setup was still owned by setupwraith after the first was re-joined, and
was deleted with it (`cmd wifi list-networks` lists them; check each one's cname in `dumpsys wifi`).
- As on the Chromecast, setupwraith's RecoveryActivity takes Home until setupwraith is disabled.
- Unlike the Chromecast, the remote's app buttons and mic keep working with launcherx disabled
(com.gretzky.GlobalKey handles them; keep it). No key-mapper workaround needed.
Second unit: not with its remote. Its YouTube button (KEYCODE_BUTTON_3, usage 0x0c0077), profile button
(KEYCODE_PROFILE_SWITCH, 0x0c019c) and MACRO_1 (0x0c0186) are global keys routed to launcherx, and its
Settings button (KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION 83, 0x0c009f) goes to com.droidlogic's receiver, which opens
launcherx's quick settings: all four do nothing once launcherx is disabled (`dumpsys window policy` lists
the routing). HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with settings_key_keycodes [83] and app_keys
["KEYCODE_BUTTON_3:com.google.android.youtube.tv", "KEYCODE_PROFILE_SWITCH:<app>"] brings them back, but
the bound helper costs held-key repeat on this box (Volume Up moves one step per press), as on the TCL G09.
The mic itself keeps working.
- The gear does nothing once launcherx is disabled, on the first unit's remote as well. The same
recipe as the second unit brings it back: HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, settings_key_panel on, and 83 in
settings_key_keycodes. That opens the launcher's quick settings panel, and the helper was still
bound after a reboot. Holding volume may step only once while it is bound.
- Second unit: voice search for songs and videos needs launcherx. With it disabled, saying a title gives
"Google Assistant is having trouble processing your request" (logcat: provider.OPEN UNKNOWN_ERROR); app
commands ("open YouTube") still work. See docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md. Apps only mode (Settings > Accounts)
is no way out: on this build it switches the Assistant off.
- Second unit: casting with setupwraith disabled was not tested. On the Chromecast with Google TV the Cast
receiver loses its device credentials with setupwraith (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md); check before relying on it.
- Second unit: `com.google.android.videos` is not preinstalled.

QUIRKS ON THIS FIRMWARE:

1. Screensaver. screensaver_components ships as com.google.android.backdrop/.Backdrop with a
5-minute screen_off_timeout. Once backdrop is disabled the screensaver points at a disabled
component, so set another one:

(or com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors without the launcher).
2. Chromecast on a shared network. On this owner's Wi-Fi (a large shared network, ~150 hosts
across 192.168.1-18.x) about 150 devices held connections to the TV's Cast port 8009, and
YouTube kept pausing and then closing a few minutes into a video. The log showed the exit:
ActivityTaskManager: START u0 {act=MAIN cat=[HOME] ...} from uid 10043

50PUS8517 (its quirk 4), mediashell stayed disabled here 45 s after disabling; a reboot
check is still pending. Keep it (comment the line out) if you cast from your phone and your
network is your own.

thrashing"); this is a 1.38 GB low_ram set, so every background service removed helps.

PROMPT.md); they are left alone.

settings list has a switch for it. A normal power-on from standby lands on Home.

Philips 50PUF7099/T3 — China-market set, TPV EBONY_V560 board, Hisilicon platform
Android TV 9 (API 28), build PPR1.180610.011 release-keys, 2 GB RAM, 32 GB storage.
ro.product.model=V560V2_CPFC1_0  ro.product.device=EBONY_V560  ro.product.manufacturer=TPV
No Google services at all on this unit (no com.google.* package is installed).
Stock home is com.bestv.ott (BestV / 百视通). See docs/devices/philips-50puf7099-t3.md
before replacing it: the launcher install needs STOCK_LAUNCHER=com.bestv.ott explicitly,
because com.bestv.ott is not in the repo's KNOWN_STOCK_LAUNCHERS list.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/philips-50puf7099-t3/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/philips-50puf7099-t3/debloat.txt com.bestv.ott
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Live TV / inputs: com.tpv.tvinput, the only TvInputService on this set (tuner, HDMI, VGA,
composite, component, SCART). Keep it, or the inputs go black.

ADB: ro.adb.secure=0, so port 5555 gives a shell to anything on the network with no prompt.
Turn network ADB off again when you are done.

Tested on this unit on 2026-10-26: this whole list applied, then the launcher handover,
then a reboot. Nothing came back, no crash, and the input menu still lists HDMI 1, HDMI 2,
HDMI 3 and composite. It has not been lived with for days yet, and the real remote keys
have not been tried (only injected keys, deviceId=-1), so treat the notes in
docs/devices/philips-50puf7099-t3.md as the limits of what was checked.

QUIRKS ON THIS FIRMWARE:

1. The three upgraders all hold INSTALL_PACKAGES, and tv.fun.tvupgrade is the
installerPackageName of com.bestv.ott itself: while it lives it can put the BestV
launcher back and wipe this list. Disabling it gives up system OTA, and firmware
updates have to be sideloaded by hand from then on.
2. The screensaver shipped pointing at com.google.android.deskclock, which is not
installed, and pm query-services -a android.service.dreams.DreamService answers
"No services found": this set had no screensaver at all. After the launcher install,
point it at the launcher's own clock:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
settings put secure screensaver_default_component com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
3. org.droidtv.usagelogger asks for android.permission.TV_INPUT_HARDWARE, so
tools/disable.sh skips it by default. It is a false positive here:
pm query-services --components -a android.media.tv.TvInputService lists only
com.tpv.tvinput's six services, usagelogger is not among them. Disabling it needs
TVINPUT_ALLOW=1. Same as examples/cecotec-shandao.
4. The screen is 60 Hz 4K on a 2 GB set, so lowmemorykiller is active at idle.
Every background service removed is a net gain.
5. default_input_method is com.android.inputmethod.pinyin/.PinyinIME, which is
installed — not the Xiaomi quirk where it points at a missing com.baidu.input.

mau.ten: Philips 50PUS8517/12 (50" 4K UHD LED, 3-sided Ambilight, P5 Picture Engine, 2022 model)
mau.header:
Philips 50PUS8517/12 (50" 4K UHD LED, 3-sided Ambilight, P5 Picture Engine, 2022 model)
Android TV 11 (ro.build.version.release=11), firmware RTT2.211108.001, board PH1M_EA_9970A
ro.product.model=2021_22_Philips_UHD_Android_TV  ro.product.device=PH1M_EA_9970A
Fingerprint: Philips/PH1M_EA_9970A/PH1M_EA_9970A:11/RTT2.211108.001/21029:user/release-keys
TP Vision build: MediaTek MT5895, 2.67 GB RAM, armeabi-v7a userspace. Vendor packages use the
org.droidtv prefix.

Match on the BOARD and firmware, not on the model number. Philips/TP Vision ships one
org.droidtv layer across a whole generation, so the x PUS85xx / PUS88xx sets of 2021-2022 on
board PH1M_EA_9970A should carry the same package set; a different board or a Google TV
(Android 12+) Philips will not. Check your own `pm list packages` against this file first —
`tools/tv.py --probe` prints model, Android version and build.

NOT the same platform as examples/philips-smart-4k-google-tv, which is a Skyworth-built
India-market set on Google TV 14 with com.smartdevice/com.sky/com.tianci packages and no
org.droidtv at all. Nothing from that file applies here and nothing here applies there.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/philips-50pus8517/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/philips-50pus8517/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (pass it to restore.sh, as above).
Live TV app:    org.droidtv.playtv
App labels below were resolved by pulling each APK and reading it with `aapt dump badging`,
not guessed from the package name. That matters on this firmware: org.droidtv.nettvapp4546 is
MEGOGO, nettvapp4655 is Deezer, nettvapp5512 is Fishing TV, and org.droidtv.candeebug is
labelled "DAC" and is the analytics uploader, not a debug tool.

QUIRKS ON THIS FIRMWARE, in the order they will bite you:

1. pm disable-user persists to /data/system/users/0/package-restrictions.xml with a delay
(~10 s on AOSP). If you run disable.sh and power-cycle the TV straight away, the changes
are silently lost: packages come back as enabled=0 (DEFAULT). Wait, or run
`pm list packages -d` and confirm your packages are listed before pulling the plug.
2. `adb reboot` over TCP hangs holding the dropped connection. Kill the adb server right
after sending it and wait on port 5555 coming back instead of on the adb command.
3. The Android 11 shell cannot disable individual components of another app
("SecurityException: Shell cannot change component state") and cannot `pm hide`
("Neither user 2000 nor current process has android.permission.MANAGE_USERS"). So if a
package refuses to stay disabled, the shell has no second lever. `pm suspend` does work
and survives a reboot, but it does not stop services: an app that starts itself from its
own boot receiver keeps running with suspended=true.
4. com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast built-in) could NOT be kept disabled on this
firmware and is deliberately absent from the list below. It returns to enabled=1 about 35 s
after every boot, reproducibly. pm disable-user, pm suspend, per-component disable and
pm hide were all tried; the first is undone, the second does not stop it, the last two are
refused by the platform. Left enabled, at a cost of about 37 MB.
5. A DISABLED PACKAGE CAN LEAVE A PERSISTENT PROCESS RETRYING FOREVER, AND pidof WILL NOT
SHOW IT. org.droidtv.xtv is the persistent TV engine and has five outbound service
bindings. Two of them, eum and aurora, were on the first version of this list, and
BOTH leave xtv in a permanent retry loop when disabled. Neither is in the list above now;
both are in the DO NOT DISABLE block below.

org.droidtv.eum -- bound via CONTEXTUALHELP. About five retries per second, logged as
xtvContextInterface ... connectCotextService - Service failed to connec i is null
51 of them in 10 seconds of an idle TV. This one also BREAKS A VISIBLE FUNCTION, and not
the one you would guess: the Philips sources drawer opens and vanishes within a second,
so HDMI inputs stop being reachable from the remote's SOURCES key. SourcesService logged
a correct, complete source list every time and the drawer still died.

org.droidtv.aurora -- about five retries per second too, logged as
xtvService: xtvService handleConnectAurora
at a steady 201 ms interval, 59 in 30 seconds of an idle TV. This one breaks nothing
visible and costs little: xtv sits at 0.2% of one core while doing it. It is log noise
plus a retry that can never succeed. Re-enabling it is free in practice -- aurora's
process does not start at idle even when the package is enabled, so xtv only needed the
package to be resolvable.

`pm enable` on either took its counter to zero immediately, with no reboot.

THE METHOD, which is the transferable part: a live PID proves the process exists, not
that it is healthy. xtv held the same PID through all eleven batches while both loops
ran. And do not grep for a string you already know -- that is how I missed the second
loop for a day after fixing the first. Clear the log, wait 30 seconds on an idle TV,
then group EVERYTHING by frequency and look at what repeats:
adb shell logcat -c; sleep 30; adb shell logcat -d > idle.txt
# then collapse digits and count: anything repeating several times a second is a loop
On this set that takes an idle log from 130 lines per 30 s down to 50, and the 50 that
remain are the firmware's own heartbeats.
6. The replacement launcher takes over on its own. Projectivy declares
android.intent.category.HOME, so the moment com.google.android.tvlauncher is disabled the
system resolves HOME to it — immediately, without a reboot and without enabling any
accessibility service. Check with
`cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME`
BEFORE disabling the stock launcher, and make sure your replacement is listed by
`cmd package query-activities` for that intent. If it is not, you will be left without a
home screen (see issue #90).

Philips 55OLED707/12 (55" 4K OLED with Ambilight), UK
Android TV 11, firmware RTT2.211108.001 build 21029, security patch 2025-10-01, board PH1M_EA_9970A
ro.product.model=2021/22 Philips UHD Android TV  ro.product.device=PH1M_EA_9970A
Fingerprint: Philips/PH1M_EA_9970A/PH1M_EA_9970A:11/RTT2.211108.001/21029:user/release-keys
MediaTek MT5895, 2.67 GB RAM. Connected over Ethernet.

This is the same board AND the same firmware build as examples/philips-50pus8517, on an OLED
panel instead of an LED one. That file's quirks and its DO NOT DISABLE block apply here as
written; read them first. Nothing in its DO NOT DISABLE block is disabled below: eum, aurora,
xtv, playtv, contentexplorer, homeintentresolver and the browser engine all stay on.
This file lists what this unit disabled on top of, or instead of, that list.

Second unit: Philips 48OLED707/96 (48" OLED with Ambilight), Taiwan, on Wi-Fi.
Same board, same RTT2.211108.001 firmware, but an older build: 2769, security patch 2023-08-05.
Fingerprint: Philips/PH1M_EA_9970A/PH1M_EA_9970A:11/RTT2.211108.001/2769:user/release-keys
ro.boot.device_name and the global device_name read 48OLED707/96; 2.67 GB RAM as above.
- Out of the box, org.droidtv.freeviewplayers and 15 uk.co.freeview.* apps were already disabled,
so they are not something to add here.
- Wi-Fi: com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith was KEPT on this unit, as this list advises.
com.google.android.tvrecommendations was kept too, so the notification panel stays.
- Everything else in this file that is installed on the set was disabled, and on top of it these
entries from examples/philips-50pus8517: partnersetup, onetimeinitializer, sss.authbridge,
syncadapters.calendar, nettvapp4655 (Deezer), m7opapp, marvin.talkback, Prime Video
(com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom), dlna and ipcontrol. CHILI, Singa, Pluto TV, Rakuten TV and
nettvapp4546/4932/5527 are not installed on this unit.
- All of them were still disabled after a restart, and the replacement launcher stayed Home.
Idle-loop check after the debloat (50PUS8517 quirk 5 method, 30 s): 186 lines, no line repeating
more than 10 times; the top repeater was WifiVendorHal's link-layer stats poll.
- Screensaver on an OLED: the firmware does not let Android's screensaver start on a timer. At every
boot org.droidtv.tv.tptvservice (TPTvServiceReceiver) puts screen_off_timeout and sleep_timeout back
to 604800000 ms, "Never", logging "screensaver put when to start is not never". A shorter "When to
start", from the TV's settings or `settings put system screen_off_timeout`, works until the next
boot and is then reset. Read from the receiver's code; the same strings are in the Android 9 build
of tptvservice on PH9M_EA_5599 (examples/philips-tpm191e). What survives a reboot is the launcher's
own idle clock: "home_idle_clock_minutes": 3 in a theme. It drifts the clock to spare the panel and
starts only on Home, never over an app or Live TV. Checked here: the clock came up after 3 minutes
on Home.

Third unit: Philips 55OLED887/12 (55" OLED with Ambilight), Poland, on Wi-Fi. Same board and the same
RTT2.211108.001 build 21029 as the first unit (fingerprint above), security patch 2025-10-01, 2.7 GB RAM.
Applied in six batches with tools/disable.sh on one day with two reboots; not yet lived with for days,
so nothing below changes the list.
- Disabled there from this file: candeebug, gel, usagelogger, nettvrecommender, recommendation,
nettv.market, demome, amazonalexa, feedback, setupwraith, katniss, play.games, videos,
youtube.tvmusic, Rakuten TV, and tvrecommendations after the replacement launcher was Home. On top of
it (owner's choice): org.droidtv.tv.frameworklogger, nettv_launcherapp, leanbackcustomizer (Philips
partner rows for the stock launcher), m7opapp, astrahdplus, dropboxprovider, partnersetup,
onetimeinitializer, sss.authbridge, syncadapters.calendar, marvin.talkback and
com.google.android.backdrop. Not installed on that unit: nettvapps and the nettvapp* web apps, Fitness
Buddy, CHILI, Singa, TED, WhaleLive, Pluto TV and Boosteroid.
- Kept there (owner's choice): everything Ambilight and Hue, the picture and sound settings and the audio
path, Play-Fi soft AP included, Chromecast, DLNA, IP control, the Philips side menu, the firmware
updaters, and Netflix, Prime Video, Apple TV, YouTube, MEGOGO and Sweet TV. The owner syncs Ambilight
with Hue bulbs: AmbilightService, HueService, AmbiAirControllerService and the ambihue LinkService stayed
bound after every batch, and Ambilight + Hue sync worked on screen after the list.
- Wi-Fi: the saved network belongs to android.uid.system (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`), not to
setupwraith, so disabling setupwraith kept the TV on Wi-Fi. This answers the Wi-Fi question above for
this firmware, on one unit.
- disable.sh's TV-input guard held back usagelogger and demome. Neither serves a TvInputService
(`pm query-services --components -a android.media.tv.TvInputService`), so both were disabled with
TVINPUT_ALLOW=1, as on the 65PUS9206 in examples/philips-50pus8517. HDMI 2 still had a picture after
a reboot, and the SOURCES drawer listed HDMI 1-4.
- After both reboots `pm list packages -d` was identical: nothing re-enabled itself. Idle log after the
last batch (50PUS8517 quirk 5 method, 30 s): about 400 lines, almost all of them adbd's USB retry; no
handleConnectAurora or connectCotextService loop.
- Launcher: build-and-install.sh ran through. The firmware opens org.droidtv.playtv at every power-on.
power_on_home with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 did NOT send it to Home on this unit: Live TV came back after the
boot probe and stayed. power_on_home_always did, after a reboot and after waking from standby with the
real remote. With HomeKeyService bound, a held Volume + steps once per press, as measured on the
65OLED804 in docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md; the owner kept the helper for Home at power-on.
- The board reports Composite (HW1), Component (HW2), SCART (HW3) and VGA (HW4) inputs that this model
does not have; `input_sources` HW1=- to HW4=- leaves them out of the Inputs menu.
- Home, SOURCES, Netflix, Ambilight and Quick menu worked on the real remote afterwards; this remote has
no Settings or YouTube button. Private DNS (AdGuard) works.

Fourth unit: Philips 77OLED806/12 (77" OLED with Ambilight), Germany, on Ethernet. Same board and the same
RTT2.211108.001 build 21029 as the first unit (fingerprint byte-identical), security patch 2025-10-01.

list on the board and the build, not the model name. MemTotal 2,958,184 kB (2.82 GiB).

tvrecommendations last, then rebooted; nothing below changes the list.
- Disabled there from this file: candeebug, gel, usagelogger, nettvrecommender, recommendation,
nettv.market, nettvapps, amazonalexa, demome, playfi.softap, feedback, setupwraith, play.games, videos,
youtube.tvmusic, and tvrecommendations after the replacement launcher was Home. On top of it (owner's
choice): partnersetup, onetimeinitializer, sss.authbridge, syncadapters.calendar, YouTube
(com.google.android.youtube.tv), Apple TV (com.apple.atve.androidtv.appletv), Disney+
(com.disney.disneyplus) and Twitch (tv.twitch.android.app). Not installed on that unit: the nettvapp* web
apps other than ARTE, Fitness Buddy, CHILI, Singa, TED, WhaleLive, Pluto TV, Rakuten TV and Boosteroid.
- Kept there (owner's choice): katniss (Assistant), Chromecast, ARTE (nettvapp1814), Netflix, Prime Video,
Spotify, Tidal, ARD, Joyn, DLNA, IP control, the Philips side menu, the firmware updaters, and Play-Fi
(note 2). This remote has no YouTube button, so disabling YouTube cost no key.
- Out of the box org.droidtv.aurora, org.droidtv.freeviewplayers and 15 uk.co.freeview.* apps were already
disabled, as on the second unit. With aurora off from the factory, the 50PUS8517 quirk 5 check on an idle

android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME` answered only com.google.android.tvlauncher
and com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome. The saved network belongs to android.uid.system
(`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`), so disabling setupwraith kept the TV on the network.
- After the reboot `pm list packages -d` was unchanged: nothing re-enabled itself. Twice `pm disable-user`
printed success for a package (usagelogger, demome) that `pm list packages -d` did not list a few seconds
later; disabling it again held, through the reboot too (50PUS8517 quirk 1).
- Screensaver: "When to start" is `system screen_off_timeout`, which read 604800000 ("Never") out of the box.
Writing `secure sleep_timeout` over ADB took the value and changed nothing. With "When to start" at 5
minutes from the TV's settings, the system screensaver started after 5 min 40 s idle
(`dumpsys power`: mWakefulness=Dreaming). Not re-read after a reboot on this unit; see the second unit
above for tptvservice putting it back at boot, and home_idle_clock_minutes for what survives.
- Switching off: Android's screensaver menu has no "Put device to sleep" here. The TV switches itself off
from Eco settings > Switch off timer, which is Philips firmware (org.droidtv.tv.inactivityservice, kept).
Every `input keyevent` sent over ADB counts as a key press and restarts that timer, so a TV being driven
over ADB will not switch itself off.

(philips_js) integration, over the JointSpace API that org.droidtv.xtv serves (50PUS8517 DO NOT

certificate, so `curl -k`): api_version 6.1.0, pairing_type digest_auth_pairing, Ambilight features
LoungeLight, Hue, Ambilight and HueStreaming. Port 1925, which older guides name, is open on this unit but
answers nothing. For the TV to stay reachable in standby, Eco settings > Quick start has to be on.

`tools/b64push.py` sent the same file in about a second. theme.sh and build-and-install.sh push with
b64push, so themes and the launcher went through; use b64push for anything else.

board and the same RTT2.211108.001 build 21029 as the first unit, security patch 2025-10-01,
ro.product.first_api_level 29. Applied 2026-10-29 in seven batches with tools/disable.sh, the launcher from
launcher/ before the last batch, two reboots that day; lived with for three days since. Nothing below changes
the list.
- Developer options had USB debugging only, no Network debugging entry; with it on, port 5555 answered on the
LAN, as on the 43PUS7304 in examples/philips-tpm191e.
- Disabled there from this file: candeebug, gel, usagelogger, nettvrecommender, recommendation, nettv.market,
nettvapps, nettvapp4546, 5326, 5512 and 20004410, amazonalexa, demome, playfi.softap, feedback, setupwraith,
katniss, videos, TED, Rakuten TV, and tvrecommendations after the replacement launcher was Home. On top of it
(owner's choice): partnersetup, onetimeinitializer, sss.authbridge, syncadapters.calendar, marvin.talkback,
m7opapp, dlna, ipcontrol, Netflix and Prime Video. Kept: YouTube Music, play.games, Chromecast, the firmware
updaters, everything Ambilight and Hue. Not installed on this unit: CHILI, Singa, WhaleLive, Pluto TV,
Boosteroid, Fitness Buddy and the nettvapp1814, 4932 and 5527 web apps.
- disable.sh's TV-input guard held back usagelogger and demome; neither serves a TvInputService, so both were
disabled with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1, as on the third unit. The Inputs menu still listed HDMI 1-4 afterwards.
- Wi-Fi: the saved network belongs to android.uid.system, not setupwraith, as on the third unit.
- After both reboots, and again after 2.5 days of uptime, `pm list packages -d` still held every package
disabled here and the stock launcher; nothing re-enabled itself.
- Launcher: HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with power_on_home_always and input_sources HW1=- to HW4=-, as on the third
unit. At power-on the TV shows the last HDMI input or Live TV for a moment, then Home.
- Screensaver: screensaver_enabled read 0 out of the box and screen_off_timeout 604800000, so nothing started
on Home while YouTube still showed its own screensaver. "home_idle_clock_minutes": 3 in a theme brought the
launcher's clock up after 3 minutes on Home, as on the second unit.
- AirPlay: this firmware's userland is 32-bit (ro.product.cpu.abilist armeabi-v7a,armeabi). The Play Store
called jqssun/android-airplay-server (the receiver the README's AirPlay answer names) not compatible; the
GitHub release APK carries armeabi-v7a code, installed with `pm install`, and played from an iPhone. It
holds a PARTIAL_WAKE_LOCK 'airplay:server' for as long as it runs (`dumpsys power`).

What this unit adds to the 50PUS8517 notes:

1. org.droidtv.nettvbrowser is needed on a UK set. With it disabled, ITVX (a Freeview Play
app) hung while BBC iPlayer still worked. It is re-enabled here, as the browser-engine
entry in the 50PUS8517 DO NOT DISABLE block says it should be.
2. com.phorus.playfi.tv (Play-Fi) could NOT be kept disabled and is commented out below, like
mediashell in 50PUS8517 quirk 4. It came back after both full restarts, with enabled=1
(ENABLED), not 0 (DEFAULT): something re-enables it on purpose, so this is not the ~10 s
persistence delay (50PUS8517 quirk 1). Every other package stayed disabled. The likely
source is org.droidtv.tv.tptvservice, which must stay and which posts a notification on a
PlayFi_ChannelID channel at every boot. That link is not proven.
3. org.droidtv.homeintentresolver ships with its HomeActivity component already disabled
(`pm dump` lists it under disabledComponents), so it does not compete for Home. While
com.google.android.tvlauncher is enabled it wins Home at priority 2 and
`cmd package set-home-activity` does not stick; once it is disabled, the replacement
launcher takes Home immediately (50PUS8517 quirk 6).
4. uk.co.freeview.mdsclient (Freeview Play metadata) crash-loops in the background, several
times in a few minutes. It did this before anything was disabled, so it is the firmware,
not this list. Each crash logs DeadSystemException, which looks alarming and is not.
5. Idle-loop check (50PUS8517 quirk 5 method, 30 s, TV in standby): 163 lines, no line
repeating more than 15 times, and nothing tied to a disabled package. The top repeaters
were cast_shell (a phone probing Chromecast) and the tuner's signal-level poll.

Verified after a full restart (off at the wall): the replacement launcher stays Home, ITVX
plays, channel changes and the TV guide work with Alexa disabled, the SOURCES drawer stays
open and lists HDMI 1-4, and the red button opens HbbTV.

This list + a new launcher: 1,389 MB used PSS,  831 MB free,  80 MB in swap
In a 30-minute Netflix session afterwards, free memory stayed between 814 and 939 MB with no
low-memory kills.

Applied in small batches on 2026-10-21 with a screenshot and a 30 s idle-log check (50PUS8517 quirk 5
method) after each. No retry loop appeared; the idle log went from 865 to ~690 lines per 30 s.
Home, inputs (HDMI 2 with a PS5), Live TV, Settings, YouTube playback and every remote button were
checked the same day; not yet lived with for days. If something breaks, `pm enable <package>` and report it.
After a reboot `pm list packages -d` was identical: nothing re-enabled itself on this firmware, Play-Fi
and Chromecast included (unlike the 55OLED707 and 50PUS8517). Checked again 8.5 min after boot.

Stock:                      1,755 MB used PSS (launcherx 182 MB across two processes)
This list + launcher/:      1,582 MB used PSS (com.gathin.tvhome 159 MB)

Quirks on this firmware:
1. org.droidtv.demome asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE here, so tools/disable.sh refuses it (#321). Kept.
2. Remote buttons go through org.droidtv.GlobalKey, which hard-codes two of them to the stock launcher:
the gear button (scancode 141, KEY_SETUP) starts launcherx/.dashboard.DashboardActivity and the
Apps button (scancode 779, keycode 813) sends ALL_APPS. With launcherx disabled both do nothing.
Fixed with the launcher's HomeKeyService (HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1): settings_key_scancodes 141 and
app_keys 813:com.gathin.tvhome. Matching the gear button by keycode (327) did NOT work, by
scancode it does; checked with the real remote. SOURCES (768), Netflix (772), YouTube (776), TV
(170, last source) and Quick menu (765) are handled by GlobalKey itself and keep working.
TV Guide (172) does nothing on a set with no channels tuned, before and after.
3. The org.droidtv.candeebug CollectionService is bound by 22 TV processes; none retried after it was
disabled. tv.samba.ssm is bound by org.droidtv.tv.tptvservice:SambaService, also no retries.
4. Settings references io.mimi.tvapp and tpvaudiomanager sends Mimi a broadcast; with both Mimi
packages disabled the sound menus still open.

Kept on purpose: AirPlay (com.mediatek.partner.airplay_sys, AirplayAPK, airplaydaemon), Google
Assistant (katniss), firmware updates (org.droidtv.upgradeapp, com.mediatek.tv.systemupdater), DLNA
(org.droidtv.dlna, bound by the Media app), org.droidtv.tv.playFiAudioService (bound by Settings,
audiocalibration and tpvaudiomanager), com.mediatek.browservice (bound by the DVB tuner), Multi View,
IP control, Ambilight, BrowseHere and the Vewd browser, and the streaming apps this household uses
(Netflix, YouTube, YouTube Music, Prime Video, HBO Max, Apple TV).

inputs and Live TV, and switching to an HDMI input opens it in playtv)

What this unit adds to the 50PUS8517 / 55OLED707 notes:

1. Already disabled at the factory on this French unit: the UK Freeview apps (uk.co.freeview.*,
org.droidtv.freeviewplayers), Apple TV, YouTube Music AND org.droidtv.aurora. The 50PUS8517 notes say a
disabled aurora leaves xtv retrying every 201 ms; on this unit an idle 30 s log shows 0 handleConnectAurora
and 0 connectCotextService lines, so aurora was left as the factory set it.
2. Packages the earlier lists do not have, checked with `dumpsys package` (none launched):
org.droidtv.astrahdplus (HD+ German satellite info pages), io.mimi.tvapp + io.mimi.sdk.service (Mimi
hearing-personalised sound), org.droidtv.dropboxprovider (Dropbox in Media). All three disabled cleanly;
sound, Media and live TV unaffected. Not touched: org.droidtv.fastip (IP channel installer; the 75PUS8505
notes say SOURCES dies without it), org.droidtv.sam / csm (service menus), dukservice, usbbreakin, factory.
3. tools/tv.py (adb_shell) gets no answer until it is accepted at the TV's own "Allow USB debugging?" prompt,
even with the same key the stock adb already uses; tools/theme.sh hangs on it until then. The stock adb works.
4. OLED screensaver: tvsystemui draws a moving Philips logo over everything after about 5 minutes of a still
picture, and once it is up it stays on top of the launcher's own idle clock. home_idle_clock_minutes must
therefore be 4 or less here; with the clock already up (it moves every minute) the logo did not come back
in more than 7 minutes. Injected keys over adb do not dismiss the logo, and the shell cannot write to the
remote's input device on this firmware (sendevent: Permission denied), so test it with the real remote.
5. The TV powers on to the last source in use: switched off from Home it comes back on Home, switched off on
an HDMI input it comes back on that input. It only resumes the PlayTvActivity it left, which sends its
window event once the input has a picture (about 5 s), if at all, so power_on_home alone is late or
misses it. power_on_home_always (with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1) brings Home up about 1 s after wake, from an
HDMI input or an app. After installing the launcher and after a theme push (which force-stops it),
switch enabled_accessibility_services off and on again, or the helper stays in "Crashed services".
6. Chromecast (mediashell) re-enables itself, as on the 50PUS8517: left out.
7. show_stats and the CPU figure: apps cannot read the CPU load here. /proc/stat and /proc/loadavg are
denied to apps on this Android 11 build, and the kernel has no cpuidle (no
/sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu0/cpuidle). The load average read over adb sits around 36 on 4 cores at
idle, so it would not be a usable stand-in anyway. Memory and storage read fine; the CPU part is left out.

Verified with the real remote after the list and the launcher: channel change, TV guide, SOURCES drawer and
HDMI switching, sound and Ambilight all work; Home opens the replacement launcher. After a reboot, waiting
15 s first (quirk 1), all 26 packages were still disabled and nothing came back. Free memory at idle on Home:
about 780 MB stock, about 1.1 GB with this list and the launcher.

Kept on purpose (owner's choice): Google Assistant (katniss), Play-Fi, IP control, DLNA, YouTube, Prime Video.

Philips quirks seen on the 55OLED907:
* The screensaver ships off and the firmware puts its delay back to "never" at every boot: on an OLED, set it
again after each boot.
* With "Ambilight+hue" enabled in the TV's Ambilight settings, the TV turns the Hue lamps back on at every
power-on, whatever was chosen before standby.
* The JointSPACE API (port 1926) works from another computer, but called from an app on the TV itself it drives
org.droidtv.xtv to 100 % CPU with connections that never close, until the TV is restarted.
* Also keep there: org.droidtv.philipstvdrawer (the OPTIONS key), org.droidtv.xtvsystem,
org.droidtv.homeintentresolver, org.droidtv.channels, org.droidtv.alhuewizard and org.droidtv.sunrise
(Ambilight + Hue) and com.easy.oad (USB firmware updates).

A TAILORED list, not a copy of another owner's. The board and firmware match
examples/philips-50pus8517, examples/philips-55oled707 and examples/philips-65oled706 exactly, so their
DO NOT DISABLE block and firmware quirks apply here as written. Read the 50PUS8517 file first.

What this list deliberately does NOT do, and why:
* com.google.android.tvlauncher is NOT listed. launcher/build-and-install.sh disabled the stock
launcher as part of the Home handover, and recorded its own restore snippet
(~/cleanyourtv-handover-<host>.txt). Adding it here would make tools/restore.sh record it as
"already disabled" and refuse to bring it back.
* The streaming apps stay: com.netflix.ninja, com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom,
com.google.android.youtube.tv and com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic. The 50PUS8517 and 65OLED706
lists disable Netflix and Prime Video because those owners did not use them. That is taste, not bloat.
* com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith is NOT listed. This TV is on Wi-Fi, and the 55OLED707 file
says to keep it on a Wi-Fi set. Checked on this unit anyway: the saved network cname= is
android.uid.system:1000, not setupwraith, so disabling it would be safe here -- it is simply not
worth the risk for 24 MB. tools/disable.sh re-checks this at runtime regardless.
* Kept on purpose, all user-visible: org.droidtv.ambiair/ambihuecommon/calmancalibrator (Ambilight),
org.droidtv.xtv (the SOURCES drawer and the JointSpace API on 1925/1926), org.droidtv.eum,
org.droidtv.aurora, org.droidtv.playtv, hdmiservice, GlobalKey, tvsystemui, org.droidtv.oad,

Launcher handover, two things that differ from the script's assumptions on this TV:
1. The first cold start of the freshly installed, not yet compiled launcher takes longer than the
10 s `am start -W` waits on this 32-bit MT5887, so build-and-install.sh stops with
"Status: timeout" although the launcher came up fine (it was the resumed activity and drew its
first screen). The remaining steps (pm grant, cmd package compile -m speed, set-home-activity)
were run by hand. Updating the already installed launcher later started in 2.2 s and the
script ran through on its own.
2. The stock launcher's HOME filter has priority=2, a third-party launcher's always 0, and Android
picks the higher priority before it looks at the preferred activity. So with the stock launcher
still enabled, set-home-activity succeeds and the HOME role moves to com.gathin.tvhome, yet the
Home key still opens com.google.android.tvlauncher. The new launcher only takes over once the
stock one is disabled, as note 3 in examples/philips-55oled707 found on the Android 11 board.

After each batch: logcat -c, 30 s of an idle TV, logcat -d, then group lines by shape and look
for anything repeating several times a second (see quirk 5 in examples/philips-50pus8517). The
only loop on this TV before and after is adbd retrying the USB gadget about once a second while
USB debugging is on; it is not caused by the debloat.
A soundbar on HDMI ARC that goes to standby on its own silence timer sends <Set System Audio Mode>
off and <Terminate ARC>, and the TV shows "TV reproduktory aktivní" (TV speakers active). With
Home on screen and nothing playing that happens during testing too; it is the soundbar, not the
debloat.

Notes from this unit:
- setupwraith holds the Cast receiver's credentials here too (CastInfoProvider in `dumpsys package`), so with
it disabled, casting from a phone fails (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Untrusted device"). This owner uses
AirPlay instead (native on this set: com.mediatek.partner.airplay_sys, com.mediatek.AirplayAPK,
com.mediatek.airplaydaemon, all kept). If you cast from phones, leave setupwraith and launcherx on.
- tools/disable.sh skipped setupwraith ("could not check which app owns the saved Wi-Fi networks"): the set
had no saved network at all and is on Ethernet, the case its message names, so it went with
FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1.
- Remote: the Sources key keeps working (org.droidtv.GlobalKey). The gear key sends KEY_SETUP (scancode 141)
and GlobalKey hands it to launcherx, so it does nothing once launcherx is off. HomeKeyService with
settings_key_scancodes 141 in config.xml brings it back, but with it bound, holding volume up or down moves
one step per press (as in docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md and the TA5 notes in
examples/philips-google-tv-ta1/README.md). This owner kept the gear key.
- org.droidtv.demome is refused by tools/disable.sh (TV_INPUT_HARDWARE, #321); hide its tile with hidden_apps.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- Port 5555 was already open and the PC already authorised; ro.adb.secure=1.
- `screencap -p` prints "Init wrapper sys mutex successful. Pid:..." before the PNG on stdout:
strip everything before the \x89PNG signature.
- The remote's Settings (gear) button is scancode 357 (KEY_OPTION) -> KEYCODE_SETTINGS (176), a
global key routed to com.mediatek.tv.service's HotKey GlobalKeyReceiver, which forwarded it to the
stock dashboard. With launcherx disabled it does nothing until HomeKeyService is on
(HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, no config needed for KEYCODE_SETTINGS). Input and app buttons keep working.
- KEYCODE_GUIDE and KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION are global keys of launcherx; this remote does not send them.
- setupwraith owned one old saved network (not the one in use), and only that entry was deleted.
Third unit: the same. Forgetting that network first (`cmd wifi list-networks`, then
`cmd wifi forget-network <id>`) lets tools/disable.sh's Wi-Fi check pass without FORCE_SETUPWRAITH.
- Third unit: with HomeKeyService bound, holding volume up moves one step; with the accessibility list
empty it ramps again (tested both ways on the real remote). Same trade as
docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md: the gear button or the volume ramp, not both. That owner
kept the ramp and installed without HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1; the gear button then does nothing, and

TPM237L_R.101.000.072.000, security patch 2026-03-05). Debloated on 2026-10-20 with the core of this

panel still open.
- Live TV: tvcenter ignores TvContract.buildChannelsUriForInput(<tuner>) and stays on the last HDMI
source, but switches to the tuner with TvContract.buildChannelUriForPassthroughInput(<tuner input id>)
(TunerInputService/HW0 or HW8; it picks the right one itself). HDMI 1-4 are HDMIInputService/HW4..HW7.
- Location: Play Services re-applies the Google account's location consent at every boot
(LocationConsentTransfer), so `cmd location set-location-enabled true` does not survive a reboot and
apps read the Wi-Fi name as "<unknown ssid>" unless Location is turned on in Settings.

the real remote (`input keyevent` bypasses accessibility filters).

Not the same board as examples/philips-50pus8517 (PH1M_EA_9970A, Android 11) or
examples/philips-55pus7503 (TPM171E, Android 8); entries shared with those lists were checked

Same board AND firmware build (identical fingerprint), each with another owner's choices:
examples/philips-75pus8505 (keeps org.droidtv.fastip, the SOURCES drawer dies without it) and

Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher
The uk.co.freeview.* packages and org.droidtv.freeviewplayers are disabled from the factory on
this unit, so they are not listed (restore.sh would turn them ON).

Kept on purpose: org.droidtv.amazonalexa (Alexa power on/off), com.google.android.apps.mediashell
(Chromecast), org.droidtv.oad and com.easy.oad (firmware updates), org.droidtv.eum (see the
