unit below disabled org.droidtv.nettvbrowser, org.droidtv.menudataapp and
org.droidtv.nettvregistration too, then re-enabled all three without confirming a failure first:
they are in the philips-50pus8517 DO-NOT-DISABLE block (written for board PH1M_EA_9970A, a
different board), and re-enabling cost nothing, so the same caution was applied here on
PH9M_EA_5599 rather than testing whether it actually needed it.

Second unit (same model, firmware STT2.230526.001, Norway, on Ethernet): the whole list applied, with
Prime Video, Assistant and Alexa off by choice. After one reboot every entry stayed disabled except
com.google.android.tvrecommendations, which came back enabled (batch 4). Left as is rather than disabled
again after each boot.

Third unit: Philips 75PUH8265/96, Taiwan, on Ethernet, still on the ANDROID 9 firmware the 2020 sets
shipped with: PTT1.181130.001 build 200260, security patch 2021-11-05. Same device PH9M_EA_5599,
model TPM191E, MediaTek mt5887, about 2 GB RAM.
Fingerprint: Philips/PH9M_EA_5599/PH9M_EA_5599:9/PTT1.181130.001/200260:user/release-keys
- The same 15 Freeview packages were disabled from the factory, on a Taiwanese set too.
- Not installed on this firmware: com.google.android.music, com.phorus.playfi.softap,
org.droidtv.fastip and org.droidtv.aurora (so the 8505 note on fastip does not apply here).
- Disabled from this list: batch 1, batch 2, and batch 3 except dlna. org.droidtv.dlna was KEPT,
following examples/philips-75pus8505 (contentexplorer, "Media", binds it on this board).
tvrecommendations (batch 4) was kept, so the notification panel stays.
- Also disabled on this unit: org.droidtv.amazonalexa (kept above, unused here),
com.google.android.sss.authbridge, org.droidtv.nettvapps, org.droidtv.sticker, and the preloaded
web-app tiles nettvapp1814 (ARTE), 4655 (Deezer), 4771 (Divan.TV), 5326 (Toon Goggles),
5512 (Fishing TV) and 20004410 (Couchplay Games). Labels read with `aapt2 dump badging`.
- launcher/build-and-install.sh ran through on its own on Android 9: the first cold start answered
`am start -W` with Status ok in 2.6 s, unlike the Android 12 timeout in the 8505 notes.
- Idle-loop check after the debloat (philips-50pus8517 quirk 5 method, 30 s): 306 lines, nothing tied
to a disabled package. Most of it was org.droidtv.ambihue driving paired Hue lights, plus
tptvservice's ApplicationSwitchService about once a second.
- Checked the same day; the set has not been restarted since, so persistence across a reboot is
not confirmed for this unit.

Fourth unit: Philips 55OLED854/12 (OLED, not LED like the other three units here), Poland, on
Ethernet. Same firmware as the lead unit above: STT2.230526.001, security patch 2025-11-01,
fingerprint Philips/PH9M_EA_5599/PH9M_EA_5599:12/STT2.230526.001/4215:user/release-keys. A
single session, not a several-day test. Like the lead unit, only an owner-selected subset of the
list below was applied, not all of it: from batch 1, usagelogger, candeebug, demome, feedback
and syncadapters.calendar, but not gel, partnersetup or onetimeinitializer (not tested, not
chosen either way); all of batch 2; from batch 3, only katniss and playfi.softap, since the
owner's own choice of apps meant amazonvideo.livingroom, videos, music, youtube.tvmusic,
play.games, marvin.talkback and dlna were left enabled (Prime Video is this owner's own dock
pick; the rest were simply not chosen, not confirmed safe or unsafe here); batch 4 after the
launcher took Home, as written. Checked after one reboot and a 30 s idle-log check (the
philips-50pus8517 quirk 5 method), both run before the launcher install and its batch-4 disables:
no line tied to a disabled package repeated, the Sources drawer and every HDMI input listed
correctly, and `pm list packages -d` still showed every one of the 25 disables below (10 from
the list below plus the 15 new ones noted next) after the reboot. com.google.android.tvrecommendations
and the stock launcher (batch 4) were disabled afterward, once the launcher install had Home;
neither has been through a reboot yet on this unit.
- The same 15 Freeview packages (plus org.droidtv.freeviewplayers) were disabled from the
factory here too, on a Polish unit.
- com.phorus.playfi.tv matched the lead unit's note: re-enabled itself after the reboot
(AudioOutService, "PlayFi Enabled"). softap stayed off.
- tvrecommendations (batch 4) was disabled only after the launcher took Home, so after this
unit's one reboot, not before it; whether it stays disabled through a reboot on this unit, as
it did not on the second unit, is not yet confirmed.
- Disabled on top of the list below, none of them used by the owner, all confirmed through the
reboot and idle-log check: org.droidtv.tv.frameworklogger, com.mediatek.backgrounddetection
(MediaTek's own background-app heuristic, not an org.droidtv package), org.droidtv.dukservice,
org.droidtv.usbbreakin, org.droidtv.nettv_launcherapp, org.droidtv.nettvapps, and the preloaded
web-app tiles nettvapp1814 (ARTE), 4508, 4609, 4655 (Deezer), 5225, 5326 (Toon Goggles),
5512 (Fishing TV) and 20004410 (Couchplay Games) -- the same numbered-tile pattern as the
third unit's list, on this unit's own `pm list packages`. Also dk.logisoft.snipergame, a
preloaded demo game present on this unit but not mentioned on the other three.
- org.droidtv.philipstvdrawer was disabled by mistake, then re-enabled: it is the Philips side
menu (TV guide, channel list, sources, Media, quick settings), not a content tile, matching the
philips-50pus8517 list's own note on it.
- Settings button, launcher/build-and-install.ps1 -HomeKeyService: this remote's Settings button
sends Linux scancode 357 (KEY_OPTION, no MSC_SCAN), read with `tools/tv.py 'getevent -lt'`, so
config.xml settings_key_scancodes = 357 fixes it. Costs the same trade-off as the TCL G09 in
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md: HomeKeyService's key filtering also stopped Volume Up/Down from
repeating on hold. The owner chose to keep volume repeat, so key_filter is false on this unit
and the remote's Settings button does nothing (Settings stays reachable from the launcher's own
on-screen button).
- OLED screensaver: org.droidtv.tvsystemui's GFXCaptureService (bound from com.android.systemui)
draws a moving Philips logo over everything after a few minutes of a still picture, as on the
65OLED706 (a different board, PH1M_EA_9970A) -- so this is not board-specific, likely whichever
OLED panel is fitted. Confirmed here too: injected keys over ADB do not dismiss it; a real
remote key does.

Fifth unit: Philips 65OLED804/12 (OLED, 2019 model), Germany, on Ethernet. It shipped with Android
TV 9 and now runs the same Android 12 firmware as the lead unit: STT2.230526.001, security patch
2025-11-01, fingerprint Philips/PH9M_EA_5599/PH9M_EA_5599:12/STT2.230526.001/4215:user/release-keys.
Applied in five batches on 22 Oct 2026, each followed by a check of `dumpsys tv_input`, the TV
processes and a 30 s idle log (the philips-50pus8517 quirk 5 method), and lived with until 25 Oct
through three restarts, one of them a cold start. The only repeating idle lines before and after
were xtv's JointSpace REST server (org.restlet ... InboundWay) answering a client on the LAN.
- From the list below: all of batch 1 except usagelogger and demome, which tools/disable.ps1 skips
because both ask for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE (the 65PUS9435 list explains why that is a false positive
here); all of batch 2; from batch 3 katniss, videos and playfi.softap, with Prime Video, TalkBack
and DLNA kept by choice; batch 4 after the launcher took Home. youtube.tvmusic and play.games were
disabled from the factory, with the same 15 Freeview packages and org.droidtv.freeviewplayers.
com.google.android.music and org.droidtv.android.fitness are not installed on this unit.
- Also disabled, none used here: org.droidtv.sticker, org.droidtv.amazonalexa (no other process
held a connection to it in `dumpsys activity services`; channel changes and the TV guide work
without it), and the preloaded Apple TV, MUBI, Twitch, Paramount+ (com.cbs.ca) and WWE apps.
- Every entry stayed disabled through all three restarts, com.google.android.tvrecommendations
included, unlike the second unit. `tools/check.py` reported nothing drifted after the last one.
- Checked with the remote afterwards: Live TV and channel changes, the TV guide, the SOURCES drawer
with HDMI 1-4, Ambilight, picture settings, and casting from a phone. The third-party remote in use
has no Settings button; its gear-like button opens the Philips options menu, before and after the
debloat, so the fourth unit's Settings-button finding was not testable here.
- The household uses a slow third-party remote whose presses last 430-550 ms. With the stock
launcher disabled, a Home press held past 400 ms did nothing: Android sends its long-press action,
ALL_APPS, to the system-image Home, which is com.android.tv.settings' FallbackHome and answers
nothing (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "Home works when tapped but does nothing when pressed firmly").
`settings put secure long_press_timeout 800` did not change that, not even after a reboot. The
launcher's home_long_press_home switch, installed with -HomeKeyService, fixed it; as on the fourth
unit, the key filter ends Volume Up/Down repeat on hold, which this household preferred anyway.
- An injected KEYCODE_TV is ignored here too; test Live TV and SOURCES with the real remote.

STT2.230526.001, fingerprint Philips/PH9M_EA_5599/PH9M_EA_5599:12/STT2.230526.001/4215:user/release-keys.
One session on 27 Oct 2026 with two restarts, not a several-day test. Launcher notes are in README.md.

talkback and playfi.softap, with katniss (Assistant) and dlna kept by choice; com.google.android.music is not

--components -a android.media.tv.TvInputService` lists only com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.agent,
org.droidtv.fastip and com.google.android.videos, so both were disabled with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 set for those two
alone. `dumpsys tv_input` still listed HDMI 1-4 after each batch.

org.droidtv.nettv_launcherapp and org.droidtv.sticker (as on the fourth unit), com.netflix.ninja,

(casting from a phone needs it), Alexa, Chromecast and both firmware updaters.

compared before and after). com.phorus.playfi.tv was left enabled, per the note in batch 3.

- usagelogger and demome: TV_INPUT_HARDWARE false positives again (`pm query-services` lists only

- Also disabled, as on the sixth unit: org.droidtv.tv.frameworklogger, org.droidtv.nettvapps,
org.droidtv.nettv_launcherapp, org.droidtv.sticker, org.droidtv.dropboxprovider, com.netflix.ninja,
com.apple.atve.androidtv.appletv; plus de.telekom.magentatv.tv (a Play Store install, unused).
Kept: YouTube, Chromecast, both firmware updaters, com.phorus.playfi.tv.

and favourites. `pm clear` on the disabled streaming apps and com.google.android.tts, plus `pm trim-caches`,
freed about 450 MB.

through the three restarts; tools/check.py reported no drift. The 30 s idle log after batch 3 (the
philips-50pus8517 quirk 5 method) had nothing tied to a disabled package; most of it was xtv's JointSpace
REST server answering a client on the LAN, as on the fifth unit.
- The remote's App Gallery button (a butterfly icon) opens org.droidtv.nettv.market (batch 2) and nothing else,
so it does nothing once this list is applied; README.md has its scancode and the remap.

Ninth unit: Philips 65PUS7354/12 (LED), Portugal, on Ethernet. Same firmware as the lead unit: STT2.230526.001,

The firmware reports the generic Allwinner "ADT-3" / "adt3" identity, so match on the build
string rather than ro.product.model.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/restore.sh examples/portronics-beem-470/debloat.txt com.htc.htclauncherhighenglishd08
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out anything you use.

checking for firmware updates. Casting/EShare packages (com.ecloud.*, com.eshare.*,

com.htc.htcsettings/com.htc.activity.HomeActivity to settings_fallback_components in config.xml,
and com.htc.htcsettings to the <queries> in AndroidManifest.xml (a <package> line).
- The stock launcher is com.htc.htclauncherhighenglishd08; re-enable it if you remove launcher/.

mau.ten: PPTV p34a4p (Suning PPTV, Amlogic board), Android 5.1.1, build LMY47V.20251117, 1 GB RAM.
mau.header:
PPTV p34a4p (Suning PPTV, Amlogic board), Android 5.1.1, build LMY47V.20251117, 1 GB RAM.
Tested 2026-10-24. First PPTV list.
ADB: 5555, no auth (ro.adb.secure=0); the owner re-opens network debugging after a power cycle.
Stock launcher: com.pptv.launcher (locked in, see below). Live TV: com.pptv.tv.

Apply:   NOT tools/disable.sh — it uses pm disable-user, which this firmware DENIES (see
the blocker below). Hide each package instead, one pm command per shell call:
grep -vE '^\s*(#|$)' examples/pptv-p34a4p/debloat.txt | sed -E 's/\s+#.*$//' \
| awk '{print "pm hide " $1}' | TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/venv/bin/python -I tools/tv.py --batch
Undo:    NOT tools/restore.sh — its pm enable cannot undo a hide on this firmware.
Same as Apply, but `pm unhide`.

The blocker: pm disable-user is denied for every package with a SecurityException
(attempt to change component state — the same wall the FFalcon r34a0 and Whaley WTV55K1
sets hit on Android 5.x). pm hide instead: the hidden state persists across reboots on 5.1
and pm unhide restores. Check: dumpsys package <pkg> | grep "User 0"  (hidden=true).

SDK 22, below the bundled launcher's minSdk 26: debloat only, the stock launcher stays —
and it cannot be replaced either (its HOME intent filter carries a custom
android.intent.category.HOME.pptv, no chooser ever appears, and hiding it kills the HOME
key after the next reboot). The full story is in docs/devices/pptv-p34a4p.md.

Ads on this set come in three layers; the list below is layer 1. Layer 2 is the Amlogic
bootanimation video ad, killed with properties (these survive reboots; persist.sys.advert
gets flipped back to 1 by an app after boot, the ad stays gone with videoadvert=0):
setprop persist.sys.videoadvert 0; setprop persist.sys.picadvert 0
setprop persist.sys.advert 0; setprop persist.sys.advert_enable 0
setprop persist.sys.advert_status 0
Layer 3 is network-layer ads — the launcher's hifuntv.com/huan.tv feed and the hpplay cast
promos — which no package list can reach. The device note names the domains that must stay
reachable if you block them elsewhere.

Watchdog: com.pptv.search, com.pptv.usercenter and the launcher embed a MyInstallReceiver
(PACKAGE_REMOVED, then download + reinstall of the package). It needs INSTALL_PACKAGES,
so once snisupdate / push.service / newtvad are hidden the chain is dead — nothing came
back across a day of reboots.

Kept on purpose: com.pptv.launcher (the only HOME handler), com.pptv.snisservice (SNIS
service bus, the framework's core), com.pptv.tv (live TV), com.pplive.tvplayer (local
player, DLNA/AirPlay receiver), com.pptv.lisenceauth (CIBN licence check), and — after a
failed experiment — com.pptv.search, com.pptv.usercenter, com.pptv.tvhousekeeper,
com.pptv.terminalmanager, com.pptv.microhelper, com.nanosic.www.remoteota,
com.example.upgrad, com.bajintech.karaok: hiding those eight crashed the launcher in a
boot loop until all were unhidden, and the culprit was never isolated. If you experiment,
hide one at a time with a reboot in between.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- USB debugging alone opens network ADB on port 5555. On realme firmware UKNV.260514.001,
Developer options also offers Wireless debugging with pairing.
- After a reboot the TV may take a new DHCP address.
- com.cltv.fast is automatically re-enabled by the Changhong vendor firmware at every boot.

launcher's poster rows. Those go away only after launcher/ replaces Home.

- com.cltv.fast ("Live TVx", FAST channels) is re-enabled by the firmware at every boot. config.json hides it,
with Settings (the top-bar pill covers it) and the Live TV app.
- A cold boot came up in com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter instead of Home; waking from standby goes to Home.
Settings has no "Power on behavior" entry.
- Besides 5555, Wireless debugging offers a random port (37683); the stock adb binary got "No route to host" on it.
- Play Movies & TV shows as a stock-launcher tile but com.google.android.videos is not installed.
- Private DNS dns.adguard-dns.com validates and survives a reboot.

ERGO DVB92YC variant (one set, Android TV 14, UKNV.260514.001, 1 GB, low_ram=true, 1280x720; 20-24 Oct 2026,

- Differences in the list: setupwraith kept, because here it owned the Wi-Fi network the TV was on (it was saved

- The remote is Bluetooth LE ("TVC0GWBT"): keep com.android.bluetooth and com.mediatek.autopair.

Disabled on 2026-10-21 in two batches; the owner checked Home and the voice remote after each batch,
and Xiaomi settings and a streaming app after the first. Package states were read back after a
standby cycle (all still disabled). After a full reboot (not standby) the owner reported the
replacement launcher still Home and no startup ad; ADB closes at reboot, so package states were not
read again after it. Not yet lived with for several days.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/redmi-mitv-mftp0/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Notes from this firmware:
- ADB: Settings -> About -> press OK on 产品型号 (product model) 7 times to unlock developer mode,
then Settings -> 账号与安全 (Account & Security) -> ADB 调试 -> 允许. Network ADB (port 5555) closes
on every reboot; turn it on again there after each power cycle. Standby is not a reboot.
- `pm disable-user --user 0` is accepted for the shell user (unlike MiTV-ANTL0, which needs `pm hide`).
- Home: the framework filters third-party HOME candidates by a package-name allowlist, the same
mechanism as MiTV-AETP0 (services.vdex has isThirdpartyHomeAllowed and
APP_WHITELIST_ALLOW_THIRDPARTY_HOME; the list is /data/system/mitv_security_center.xml, not readable
from the shell). The standard com.gathin.tvhome build installed and opened, and
`cmd package set-home-activity` printed Success, but HOME still resolved to com.mitv.tvhome.
The opt-in application-ID build from docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-aetp0-dofus.md
(`./gradlew assembleRelease -PlauncherApplicationId=com.ts.launcher`) became Home with
com.mitv.tvhome still enabled, and stayed Home after a full reboot. Do not run
launcher/build-and-install.sh with its defaults here: it would disable com.mitv.tvhome, and
disabling the stock launcher leaves no allowed Home. Use the manual commands in that doc.
- Settings: android.settings.SETTINGS and android.settings.WIFI_SETTINGS resolve to nothing; the
launcher's Settings pill falls back to com.xiaomi.mitv.settings/.entry.MainActivity, which opened.
- App grid: the streaming apps declare LEANBACK_LAUNCHER and show up; Xiaomi settings, weather and
TV Manager are LAUNCHER-only. com.mitv.alarmcenter declares LEANBACK_LAUNCHER (hide it with
hidden_apps if you don't want a 定时提醒 tile).

Tested on a real SEMP TCL 50P8M unit running V728 (Android 11, build AR05):
Lived with this list in daily use since 2026-10-19 (10+ days) across multiple cold reboots
(adb reboot and full AC power-cycles) and daily Quick Start (Suspend-to-RAM) cycles. It survived
all reboots cleanly: Wi-Fi and Ethernet stayed up, D-pad, short-press Power, TCL's source menu,
the launcher's Inputs menu (HDMI via TvInputManager works, no source_panel fallback needed),
Bluetooth audio/remote, Settings and Home from HDMI all worked without issues.

Quirks on this firmware (verified on 50P8M V728 / Android 11):
- Bluetooth & Quick Start (STR) bug fixed on Android 11 (V728): Unlike older Android 9 builds
where Quick Start (Suspend-to-RAM) caused Bluetooth remote/audio drops or ALSA DMA lockups,
the newer Android TV 11 release (V728 / AR05) does NOT exhibit the Bluetooth bug and resumes
cleanly with quick_start_mode=1 enabled.
- TclAppBoot blocks third-party launcher autostart unless granted via appops:
cmd appops set com.gathin.tvhome AUTO_START allow && cmd appops set com.gathin.tvhome APP_AUTO_START allow && appops write-settings
- OOBE Wi-Fi ownership (setupwraith): If Wi-Fi was configured during initial setup, the saved
network carries cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith; keep setupwraith enabled (or
forget and reconnect Wi-Fi via Settings so android.uid.system owns it).
- Intelligent Volume (AVL/DRC) audio drop: TCL's "Intelligent Volume" saturates when switching
between stereo PCM and multichannel Dolby (AC3/E-AC3), muting audio until toggled. Turning off
Intelligent Volume in Sound -> Advanced Settings resolves it completely.
- input keyevent KEYCODE_TV_INPUT is an "Unhandled key"; the remote's Source button goes through
TCL's own path (com.tcl.sourcemananger/com.tcl.insrc.ShowWindowService -a com.tcl.insrc.SHOW_WINDOW).
- The voice processes (voice_ap, katniss:interactor) used ~45% of one core continuously until
Group 6 disabled katniss; voice_ap is a native daemon and stays running without root.

Firmware build: MTK9612PA-userdebug 11 RTM9.241015.013 59. EU set, German UI.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (Google TV).
Setup wizard: com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (claims HOME with .RecoveryActivity).
Live TV app: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter; HDMI/tuner inputs: com.mediatek.tvinput.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/sharp-55gp6260e/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Tested on one unit in a single session, not over several days: screenshots after each batch, one reboot
(all packages stayed disabled, Home stayed the new launcher, the TV did not open Live TV by itself),
the Inputs menu listing HDMI 1-4, and the real remote's gear and YouTube buttons. Live TV and HDMI
playback were not opened. Treat it as a starting point and report anything that broke.

ro.adb.secure is unset on this build, so port 5555 was open to the whole LAN while debugging was on:
switch USB debugging off afterwards and reboot (it stayed closed after the reboot).

WARNING: the Wi-Fi network saved during first setup belonged to setupwraith
(`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`). Forget it and re-join it in Settings before disabling
setupwraith, or Android deletes the network and the TV drops off Wi-Fi and ADB. Done here: it then
belonged to com.android.tv.settings and stayed connected.

Home: set-home-activity alone resolved to setupwraith's RecoveryActivity while it was enabled; the
handover only held once setupwraith and then launcherx were disabled (not a CVTE board).

Remote (Bluetooth/IR remote): the gear sends KEYCODE_FOCUS (80, scancode 204) and the YouTube button
KEYCODE_TV_INPUT_COMPOSITE_1 (scancode 74), both through the MediaTek hotkey dispatcher, which asked the
stock launcher and the YouTube app. With them gone the buttons did nothing. Mapped with the launcher's
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1: settings_key_keycodes 80 and app_keys KEYCODE_TV_INPUT_COMPOSITE_1:org.smarttube.stable.
Both worked on the real remote; the price was that a held volume key moves one step per press.
Input and Home needed no helper. Two more buttons break the same way and were mapped the same way:
Prime Video  KEYCODE_TV_INPUT_COMPONENT_2 (183): the firmware starts com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom
directly (AMAZON_BUTTON), so with Prime Video disabled it does nothing. Re-enable the app to get
the stock behaviour back, or map it: app_keys KEYCODE_TV_INPUT_COMPONENT_2:<package>.
FAV APP      KEYCODE_BUTTON_11: com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard's FavKeyReceiver opens com.mtc.emanual
(hardcoded, no setting), so with the e-manual disabled it does nothing. Re-enable
com.mtc.emanual to restore it, or map it: app_keys KEYCODE_BUTTON_11:<package>.
Here they open Spotify and LocalSend through HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1; both checked on the real remote.
Netflix      KEYCODE_STEM_1 (scancode 104): firmware opens com.netflix.ninja, so with Netflix disabled it does
nothing; app_keys KEYCODE_STEM_1:<package> maps it (Jellyfin here, checked on the real remote).

Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) validated on this set; not part of the list.

Re-enabled along the way: only the stock launcher, once and automatically, when launcher/build-and-install.sh
rolled the first handover back because setupwraith took Home. Nothing else was re-enabled.

Already disabled before this list, left as they were: com.android.tv.settings.mtc.overlay,
com.google.android.marvin.talkback, com.mtc.emanual.overlay.ok (also listed below, harmless).

Kept on purpose: Play Store + Play Services, Gboard, Dolby audio, com.mediatek.tvinput / com.mediatek.tv.service /
com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter (Live TV and HDMI), com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard (channel scan),
com.mediatek.wwtv.mediaplayer (USB media player; tools/disable.sh skips it because it holds
TV_INPUT_HARDWARE, but `cmd package query-services --components -a android.media.tv.TvInputService` does not list
it here, only com.mediatek.tvinput and the TV agent, so it is probably a false positive. Not tried: no input check), com.mediatek.autopair (remote pairing), com.mediatek.mtc.factory and
mediatek.factorymenu.ui (factory tools, never launched), com.mediatek.androidbox (Wi-Fi Display Sink test app),
com.google.android.katniss + com.google.android.tv.remote.service (voice), com.google.android.apps.mediashell
(Chromecast), com.google.android.tts, com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx, the user-installed browser and file managers.

(GLOBAL_BUTTON extras), since the vendor .kl is not readable from the shell:
Input   usage 0x0c0091 -> handled by the firmware (Google's input switcher), works with no helper
Netflix usage 0x0c0078 -> KEYCODE_STEM_1, firmware opens Netflix, works with no helper

mau.header:
Skyworth 65A3F (7T641_A3F, MediaTek MT9633), China, Android 13 (API 33), build 10.01.250328
Chinese Coocaa/CCOS firmware, no GMS. Stock home is com.coocaa.aigc.home
(com.coocaa.aigc.home.home.rootpage.HomeActivity): it is launched at boot and it also takes the
remote's HOME key, although the only HOME-category activity is the third-party launcher.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/skyworth-65a3f/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/skyworth-65a3f/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

com.coocaa.aigc.home must stay ENABLED. Tried on the TV 2026-10-21:
- `pm disable-user` restarts the framework and the package comes back enabled by itself.
- `pm suspend` brings up com.coocaa.os.control/.ui.QrActivity, a WeChat QR unlock screen.
- `pm hide`, component-level disables and `su` are all refused; with no root /system/xbin/su
fails with "setgid failed: Operation not permitted".
- Disabling it and rebooting leaves the TV with no home: it hangs on the SKYWORTH logo, the
network stack never starts and 5555 disappears. Recovery was a factory reset from Recovery
(power off, hold the hidden touch button under the logo while plugging the set back in,
wipe data/factory reset).

Ads on this firmware: com.tianci.ad BootService draws the boot ad, its PowerOffActivity the
shutdown ad, and the same package hosts the ad landing pages. Disabling it removed both;
checked across a reboot with zero logcat hits for the package.

Quirks, all checked on the TV:
- 5555 opens without pairing (ro.adb.secure=0), so any host on the LAN gets a shell.
- adbd's stdout wrapper corrupts `exec-out screencap -p` here as well; screencap to a file on
the TV and pull it.
- `tools/tv.py --push` is for small files. b64push.py needed roughly 20 minutes for a 17 MB
APK. Faster: hold an adb shell running `toybox nc -l -p 9999 > /data/local/tmp/x.apk` and
send from the computer with `nc <tv ip> 9999 < x.apk` (about 100 s; verify with md5sum, the
adb_shell read timeout can fire at 120 s even when the file arrived intact).

A third-party launcher cannot own the boot screen:
- boot_start_tv_source only picks the input source (DEFAULT/REMEMBER, HOME, CHANNEL); there is
no "launch an app" value, and HOME changes nothing.
- Two one-press routes work. (1) The remote's colour key:
com.skyworth.setting/.module.device.shortcutkey.ShortcutKeySetActivity lists the installed
launcher and the binding sticks — press the colour key, the launcher opens. (2) The stock
home's dock: com.coocaa.aigc.home/.dockedit.DockEditActivity, after a reboot the launcher sits
in the left rail. `cmd package set-home-activity` also succeeds and the launcher does become
the default HOME, but the boot screen and the HOME key still go to aigc.home.

Kept on purpose: com.coocaa.aigc.home, com.skyworth.setting, com.tianci.system, com.coocaa.os.*
(including com.coocaa.os.control and com.coocaa.os.softsettings), com.coocaa.safelauncher,
com.tianci.movieplatform, input methods, voice/mic, casting and audio/PQ packages.
com.overseas.store.appstore is absent after a factory reset; the line is harmless there.

CRITICAL SAFETY NOTE:
Do NOT disable com.skyworth.officehomepage or com.tianci.movieplatform directly.
Coocaa OS boot chain hardcodes dependencies on these stock home launchers. Disabling
either package causes the system to hang indefinitely at the boot logo (network stack
does not initialize, ADB drops). Recovery requires a hardware factory reset.

RECOMMENDED BEST PRACTICE (ZERO DEBLOAT):
On this model, switching the television to "Office Mode" (办公模式) in the native settings
natively shuts off all video streaming feeds, banner advertisements, and background cloud
preloading from the source.
Leaving all packages enabled (zero debloat) is the safest approach, ensuring 100% firmware
stability, OTA upgrade safety, and eliminating any risk of boot hangs.
Only com.skyworth.device is active by default; the rest are commented out. Uncomment only what you want to disable.
For replacing the home screen safely, see docs/devices/skyworth-7t861-a23.md.

Quirks on this firmware, checked on the TV 2026-10-27:
- Port 5555 is open when USB debugging is on; stock adb (platform-tools 37.0.1) authenticates after the
"Allow USB debugging?" prompt. `adb exec-out screencap -p` is corrupted by an adbd stdout banner
("Init wrapper sys mutex successful"), so screencap to a file and `adb pull` it.
- disable.sh skips com.Smartdevice.emanual and com.mstar.android.tv.disclaimercustomization here: this
firmware's dumpsys gives no permission block for the input-driver check (#321), so they stay enabled
and are commented out below. Both are harmless.
- Launcher handover works (launcher/build-and-install.sh, INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1). The first run rolled back
because com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith claimed Home once launcherx was disabled; the saved Wi-Fi
network in use was owned by android.uid.system, so FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 was safe, and a second run kept

Lived on for a few days on a 2019 box with 2 GB RAM: the aim was a box that lands in a clean
launcher and starts live TV by itself, for someone who only wants to press the power button.

Two things about this firmware, worth knowing before you disable anything:
- Home is filtered by package-name PREFIX. logcat says "PackageManager: block home apk <pkg>"
or "allow home apk <pkg>"; the whitelist is prefix-matched and includes com.ktcp.launcher,
so a sideloaded launcher only becomes selectable when its applicationId starts with one of
those prefixes. `settings put global enable_launcher_components` and
`setprop sys.launcherlist.enable 0` are both reset on boot - do not spend time on them.
- Every third-party boot receiver is blocked: "BroadcastQueue: Block auto start app from
broadcast: <pkg>". BOOT_COMPLETED never reaches a sideloaded app, and neither does a
foreground-service self-restart. The only thing that worked was the launcher itself calling
startForegroundService for our own service on its first start after boot.
- The screensaver is rewritten to the Skyworth ad component on every boot, so setting it back
is not a one-off either.

Miracast is off here because nobody casts to this box; comment it back in if you do.
The stock launcher is last, and only because a replacement was confirmed as Home first.

which stay optional here because only that unit tried them: uncomment any you want off too.

TVX tuner and the remote's buttons (owner, real remote) worked with the stock launcher off. The PA firmware
ships neither com.sony.dtv.promos nor any of the preloaded apps below. Its hotel-mode packages are named
com.sony.dtv.b2b.adminpassword and com.sony.dtv.b2b.deviceadminsettings and were left enabled: the second
answers ADD_DEVICE_ADMIN (DeviceAdminAdd, ProfileOwnerAdd). com.sony.dtv.livingfit and com.sony.dtv.kenhchonloc
were already disabled at the factory on it.

Live TV / tuner app: com.sony.dtv.tvx (set it as live_tv_package in the launcher's config.xml and hide it).

com.sony.dtv.sonysystemservice, imeproxy, settingsprovider, systemupdate/update (firmware), the Sony
settings apps and all com.mediatek.*: they drive HDMI, the tuner, Bravia Sync, updates and the remote.

com.sony.dtv.promos, com.sony.dtv.b2b.vendorprotocol, com.sony.dtv.seeds.iot, com.sonypicturescore.
The recovery record disable.sh writes keeps them disabled on undo; with no record, restore.sh
enables every listed package, these four included.

Live TV in the launcher: set live_tv_package to com.sony.dtv.tvx and hide it; Inputs lists HDMI 1-4 and
AV from the TV input framework. Launcher installed with the Input-button service (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1).
Applied one afternoon on a KD-55X80J with the dock set to Stremio, Netflix, SmartTube, OTT Navigator.
Not yet lived with for weeks; if something breaks, re-enable it with `pm enable <package>` and please
report it. launcherx was left enabled, since Home already resolved to the new launcher once the setup
wizard was disabled.

Second unit, North American firmware: build BRAVIA_VH2_M_UC-user 12 STT2.230505.001.S136 682241,
same board and the same build number as the EU unit above. Every package in this list is present and
every one disabled cleanly, but two things differ:

- Home handover needs the stock launcher disabled. On this firmware launcherx registers its HOME
intent filter at priority=2, which outranks the preference `cmd package set-home-activity` writes:
it prints Success while `resolve-activity` keeps naming launcherx. Disabling setupwraith alone did
not hand Home over either, so the note above about leaving launcherx enabled does not hold here.
Disabling it (the commented line at the end of this list) handed Home over at once, and the TV has
booted to the new launcher since. Check with `dumpsys activity activities | grep mFocusedApp`, not
with the "Success" from set-home-activity.
- promos, seeds.iot and b2b.vendorprotocol ship ENABLED here, where the EU unit has them off at the
factory; sonyselect and seeds.iot.remotestart are enabled too and were not named either way above.
They are in the list below, so one file covers both regions: on an EU set they are already disabled
and recovery.py records that, so undo leaves them alone.

The Input-button service was NOT needed on this unit: with launcherx disabled, the remote's Input,
gear and app buttons were all still answered by Sony's own firmware (checked on the real remote, not
with injected keys), so INPUT_KEY_SERVICE was left off and key auto-repeat kept. On Ethernet, so the
setupwraith Wi-Fi check did not apply. Applied over one evening, not lived with for days.

Third unit, Asia-Pacific firmware, bought in India: KD-55X80J, build
BRAVIA_VH2_PA-user 12 STT2.230505.001.S136 682241, the same build number again. It behaves like the UC
unit, not the EU one:

- launcherx registers HOME at priority=2 here as well, so it was disabled once the new launcher was
installed, together with its Sony companion com.sony.dtv.launcherxcustomizer (commented lines at
the end). Home has stayed on the new launcher since.
- Factory-disabled on this unit: only com.sony.dtv.b2b.vendorprotocol, com.sony.dtv.b2b.softap and
com.sony.dtv.kenhchonloc. promos and sonyselect ship enabled and were disabled.
- It carries extra preloads the list above didn't cover: Sony's tab, partner auto-installs, usage
agents and India-market streaming apps. They are in the "Asia-Pacific unit" groups below; on a set
that doesn't have them the line just fails and the rest of the list carries on.
- Left enabled and untested here: seeds.iot, seeds.iot.remotestart, youtube.tvmusic.
- Kept by the owner's choice: Assistant, Chromecast built-in, firmware updates.
- On Wi-Fi: the TV stayed on its network after setupwraith was disabled.

Lived with since 19 October 2026 with a custom launcher (its own app, not this repo's); nothing has
broken in daily use (owner's report).
The commented "one day" group at the end was disabled four days later and has only had a day so far.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (Google TV). Pass it to restore.sh as above.
Live TV / tuner app: com.sony.dtv.tvx (set it as live_tv_package in the launcher's config.xml and hide it).
Keep the com.sony.dtv.tvinput.* services, com.sony.dtv.braviasync*, tvapi, sonysystemservice, imeproxy,
settingsprovider, systemupdate/update, the Sony settings apps and all com.mediatek.*: they drive HDMI,
the tuner, Bravia Sync, updates and the remote.
Kept by owner's choice: Chromecast built-in (mediashell), AirPlay/HomeKit (airplayapp, homekit),
firmware updates, HbbTV / Freeview Plus (interactivetvutil), DLNA, Sony IP control (webapi.core).

First unit (Australia, Ethernet, disabled-launcher route):
The launcher must target SDK 30+ or Play Protect blocks the install on this firmware as "built for an older
version of Android". Inputs lists the PS5 on HDMI 1 twice (the port and its CEC device input). Memory was
the bottleneck (~480 MB available); window/transition/animator scales at 0.5 and pm trim-caches helped.
On Ethernet, setupwraith owned no saved Wi-Fi network and was disabled along with launcherx.
Unit 1 route: uncomment com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith at the end (Ethernet only, costs casting).

Second unit (India, Wi-Fi & Ethernet, redirect route):
Same model KD-65X85K and MediaTek MT5895 board, Asia-Pacific build
BRAVIA_VH21_M_PA-user 12 STT2.230505.001.S136 682241 release-keys.
Tested with the reference launcher via the REDIRECT route (see config.json):
- launcherx and setupwraith stay ENABLED: on Wi-Fi, dumpsys wifi confirms setupwraith owns the saved Wi-Fi
credentials (cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith). Disabling it disconnects Wi-Fi and ADB.
Keeping launcherx on prevents setupwraith's RecoveryActivity (HOME priority 1) from taking Home and
preserves remote app hotkeys.
- Home redirection: config.json sets stock_home_redirect to com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx, handled
by HomeKeyService (Settings > Accessibility). Home pressed anywhere bounces straight back to CleanYourTV.
- Remote keys: Settings button sends scancode 646 ("scan:646:settings" in app_keys). Remote app keys:
scan:485 (YouTube) and scan:490 (Prime Video) in app_keys.
- Additional bloat discovered and disabled: BRAVIA CAM services (camerafwupdate, settings, distancealert,
livingfit), Sony seeds IoT auth and remotestart, Sony help and eco dashboard.
- screensaver: dreamx is commented out below because disabling it requires setting screensaver_components
first (e.g. com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream or com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors).

Third unit (New Zealand, Wi-Fi, redirect route):
Same model line and the same PA build. Applied in three batches with a screenshot between, then the
reference launcher via the redirect route, as the second unit: launcherx and setupwraith stay enabled
(setupwraith owns the saved Wi-Fi network here too), config.json's stock_home_redirect, and only
HomeKeyService bound. Differences from the second unit:
- key_filter left on (true) and no app_keys: launcherx answers the remote's YouTube, Settings and Input
buttons itself, and with the helper filtering keys a Home press opens the launcher even while Google
home is already on screen. Checked on the real remote: a held Volume Up still ramps on this build.
- Cold boot: 3 of 5 restarts landed on the new Home by themselves; on 2 the launcher's ProbeActivity ran
but no window event for launcherx followed, and Google home stayed up until one Home press (the #1116
race). A standby wake is not a cold boot, so it only shows after a restart or a firmware update.
- com.qterics.da.product was back on (enabled state "default") after the first reboot; disabled again by
hand it stayed off through five more restarts.
- The screensaver shipped pointing at com.sony.dtv.livingfit (BRAVIA CAM Living Fit), which this list
disables: screensaver_components was moved to com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream, then dreamx disabled.
- Off by choice on this unit: Netflix, Prime Video, Spotify, HbbTV, the Sony bug report service and the
customer support tile. The remote's Netflix and Prime Video buttons then open the app's Play Store
page, which has an Enable button. Kept: QuickSet, Chromecast, AirPlay/HomeKit, DLNA, updates;
seeds.iot was already off at the factory on this unit.

Applied 19-20 Oct 2026 (Unit 1), 26 Oct 2026 (Unit 2) and 29 Oct 2026 (Unit 3); reboot-checked.

range, US firmware. Same device BRAVIA_VH21, same product BRAVIA_VH21_M_UC, same build

so it belongs here and not in a folder of its own. 230 packages, not 250; the one line of this list
it could not use is com.sony.dtv.sonyselect, which is not installed on it. Everything else applied,
and Home came back on the new launcher over two reboots, with nothing re-enabled by the firmware.
One sitting, not a week: the 65" entry above is the lived-with one.
- Wired Ethernet, no Wi-Fi network ever saved. `dumpsys wifi` then prints no cname= line at all,
and tools/disable.sh and tools/disable.ps1 fail closed on that rather than reading it as "nobody
owns it", so setupwraith was skipped with a warning until FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 was passed - the
case that warning names.
- Installed with NO key helper, unlike the 65" above, and the remote is better for it: with nothing
bound, the Input, Settings, Home and Back buttons all still work, and holding volume ramps again.
With INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 bound, volume moved one step per press instead. On this set the helper
costs the ramp and buys nothing: docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md has the two rows.
- The owner also disabled the streaming apps, voice search, AirPlay/HomeKit and the BRAVIA CAM
packages. Those are preferences, not findings, so they are not lines in this list, which stays
the privacy and ads core it says it is above.

Applied 19 Oct 2026 in two batches with a screenshot between; launcher 2.3 installed with the
Input-button service (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1). Reboot-checked twice:
Home came back on the new launcher both times. Lived with for a week; nothing re-enabled.
One incident, not the debloat: on 20 Oct the Widevine L1 HAL died mid-stream and would not re-initialize
(GetProvisioningMethod failed, usage table status 340), so DRM-protected apps crashed on launch or would
not play. Network, packages and Home were fine. A reboot (`tools/tv.py --reboot`) cleared it. If DRM apps
stop at once on this firmware, reboot before you suspect the list.

History: the same set was first removed with `pm uninstall --user 0` on 2026-10-18 and lived with for seven
days (several reboots; Home, Inputs, Settings, Netflix and YouTube fine; no crashes seen apart from the one below).
On 2026-10-25 the packages were re-enabled and this file was applied with tools/disable.sh:
all 19 stayed disabled after a reboot, `tools/check.py` reported "nothing drifted", Home, Settings and the
21 HDMI/AV input entries were fine. One boot earlier in the run logged a crash in two Realtek vendor
services (exTv HAL, com.realtek.tv.atv); both respawned and nothing was visibly wrong.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV; recommendations rows with sponsored
tiles). cmd package set-home-activity printed Success and changed nothing: the stock launcher outranks any
other HOME app, so it has to be disabled for a new launcher to get Home (FLauncher, me.efesser.flauncher, was
used). The run above removed it with uninstall rather than disable-user; the second unit below disabled it with
disable-user. It is the last line: disable it last, after the new launcher answers HOME.
Tuner / inputs on this Realtek set are com.realtek.dtv, com.realtek.tv.atv and com.android.tv (Live
Channels): keep them, plus the com.sony.dtv.* services (sonysystemservice, smartui = Input menu, ipcontrol,
remotecontrolsettings, timers) and all com.realtek.* overlays.

Kept on purpose: Chromecast built-in (com.google.android.apps.mediashell). Measured on this set after a fresh
boot and 2 minutes idle: about 31 MB PSS (109 MB RSS, mostly shared pages), +16 MB used RAM, and
`am force-stop` leaves it stopped (no respawn after 65 s) until the next boot.

Gotchas from the run:
- Wait at least 15 s after the last `pm` command, and run `adb shell sync`, before rebooting. Eight changes
made right before a reboot were lost (package state is written lazily).
- Before disabling setupwraith check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`. Here the saved networks belong
to android.uid.system and com.google.uid.shared, so Wi-Fi and ADB stayed up.
- While setupwraith is enabled its .MainActivity answers HOME; it takes Home from a third-party launcher
until it is disabled.
- Not tested: the remote's mic button after katniss goes (it also needs com.google.android.tv.remote.service,
kept), and Google Home Mini voice control of the TV.

Second unit (same product BRAVIA_VU1_UC and build 366.60436, 2026-10-26): every line applied unchanged with
tools/disable.sh in three batches, tvrecommendations before the launcher. Then launcher/build-and-install.sh
installed com.gathin.tvhome and disabled the stock launcher with `pm disable-user` (not uninstall):
Home resolved to the new launcher, and after a reboot all packages were still disabled and the TV started
straight into it (not Live TV). So the last line is now active.
- setupwraith was left ENABLED on this unit, and it did not claim HOME once tvlauncher was disabled
(query-activities listed only com.gathin.tvhome and the two FallbackHome activities), and phone casting still
worked after two days. Owners who cast from a phone can comment its line out; see README.md in this folder.
- Live TV: com.android.tv has no leanback launch entry here, so the launcher's Inputs menu needs
live_tv_package com.realtek.tv.atv (the stock "TV" tile); config.json in this folder sets it.
- Remote: Input and the settings button are vendor keys (EV_KEY 0x225, 0x254) handled by the firmware. They
kept working with the stock launcher disabled and no key helper enabled, and holding Volume still ramps.

Third unit (KD-65X750H, US/Canada, same product BRAVIA_VU1_UC and build 366.60436, on Ethernet, 2026-10-22):
a subset of this list plus four more, applied with tools/disable.sh in three batches with a screenshot and
crash-log check after each, then launcher/build-and-install.sh, then a reboot. Lived with for 8 days, nothing
re-enabled. It kept Assistant (katniss), the Ambient screensaver (backdrop), TTS, tvrecommendations,
setupwraith, providers.calendar, gallery3d, htmlviewer and livepicker, and added play.games and the Sony
auto-installs config (below) plus YouTube Music and Disney+ (commented out, owner's choice).
- setupwraith again claimed no HOME with tvlauncher disabled; it owns one saved Wi-Fi network on this unit, so
check the cname before disabling it on a set that uses Wi-Fi.
- Remote: Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Input and the mic button were pressed on the real remote with the
stock launcher disabled and katniss kept: all work, no key helper. `dumpsys window policy` routes no key to
tvlauncher. The Help key goes to com.sony.dtv.smarthelp, so it does nothing once that line is applied.
- HDMI rows in the launcher's Inputs menu open an "Open with: TV / TV" chooser: com.android.tv and
com.realtek.tv.atv both answer the passthrough URI, and "Always" is never applied. Either choice plays the
input; the Input key goes through smartui and has no chooser.

HDMI/AV inputs continued to work. This list is for the recorded product/build; verify your own TV.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. The custom launcher was installed and confirmed
as Home before this package was disabled; restore.sh takes the stock launcher package above.
Second unit (same product and build, India, 25 October 2026): with launcherx disabled the remote's Netflix,
YouTube, Prime Video and YouTube Music buttons do nothing, because Realtek's GlobalKeyReceiver hands them to
launcherx. Keeping launcherx with stock_home_redirect and key_filter false kept both the buttons and the
volume ramp; see README.md in this folder.
Live TV: com.android.tv. Keep the Realtek input/tuner packages com.realtek.dtv, com.realtek.tv.atv,
com.realtek.tv.passthrough and Sony's com.sony.dtv.smartui (the input menu).
Kept during the session: streaming apps, Assistant, Chromecast, AirPlay, Play Store/Services, and
the TV's core, remote, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth services. Two packages were already disabled in the initial
backup and are not part of this list: com.sony.dtv.b2b.vendorprotocol and com.android.camera2.

Second unit: KD-55X75K, India, same build (UKR1.240726.001). Every line applied unchanged, in three
batches (setupwraith before launcherx); the same packages were still disabled after a reboot, and power-on
goes through com.realtek.advancesetting/.FallbackHome to the new launcher, not to Live TV. Only
com.sony.dtv.b2b.vendorprotocol was disabled at the factory here. Port 5555 was closed: Wireless debugging
pairing, then `adb tcpip 5555`. The saved Wi-Fi belonged to android.uid.system, so setupwraith was safe to
disable. Once launcherx is off, the remote's Netflix, YouTube, YouTube Music and Prime Video buttons do
nothing; Input, the settings button, the mic and Home keep working without a helper. Those four buttons are
vendor keys told apart by scancode (getevent EV_KEY 0x2f6, 0x239, 0x28d, 0x28c), so config.json maps them as
scan:758, scan:569, scan:653 and scan:652 (INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1). With that helper bound, holding volume
moves one step per press (docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md); leave the helper off to keep the ramp.

mau.header:
Sony BRAVIA VU31 4K (device BRAVIA_VU31_4K, Realtek SoC), India firmware, 2 GB RAM
Google TV 14 (API 34), build UKR1.240726.001

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/sony-bravia-vu31/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/sony-bravia-vu31/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (Google TV); pass it to restore.sh as above.
Launcher: done on a second VU31 (see the last group). setupwraith also claims HOME (priority 1), so it
goes before launcherx; build-and-install.sh disables launcherx itself.
Tuner / inputs on this Realtek set are com.realtek.dtv, com.realtek.tv.atv and com.android.tv (Live
Channels): keep them, plus com.sony.dtv.tvapi-style services (sonysystemservice, smartui = Input menu,
m2.devicecontrolservice, ipcontrol) and all com.realtek.* overlays.
Unlike the MediaTek Sony sets, this firmware ships no Samba TV, Qterics or IDD agents, so there is
nothing of that kind to disable. com.sony.dtv.b2b.vendorprotocol was already disabled from the factory.
ADB: USB debugging alone opens port 5555 (no wireless-debugging pairing needed); the "Allow USB
debugging?" prompt appears on first connect. On macOS the terminal app needs Local Network permission
or every LAN host answers "No route to host".
Applied 2026-10-20 in two batches with a screenshot and crash-log check after each, then reboot-checked:
all 18 stayed disabled, no crashes, Home, Inputs and the kept apps fine. Not lived with for days yet.
With 2 GB of RAM the set still swaps after this; the stock home screen (~170 MB over two processes)
is the next thing to replace.

Second VU31, same build, 2026-10-20: the extra lines marked (2nd) disabled in batches with a screenshot and
crash-log check after each, then the launcher installed and Home switched, reboot-checked. Notes from it:
- Live TV and every HDMI/AV input play in com.android.tv; the inputs come from com.realtek.tv.passthrough
(HDMI 1-3, a CEC soundbar on HDMI 3, Video). In the launcher set live_tv_package to com.android.tv and
hide it. The Input key opens smartui's menu system-wide, so no INPUT_KEY_SERVICE is needed.
- Before disabling setupwraith check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`: here the network belonged to
android.uid.system, so Wi-Fi and ADB stayed up.
- com.sony.dtv.applicationdisabler re-enables com.sony.dtv.ecodashboard at every boot (as on the BF1), so
it is not listed; hide its tile in the launcher (hidden_apps) instead.
- Sony's Timers & Clock declares two leanback activities with one label, which showed as two tiles
(launcher fix in #298).
- Real remote checked after the switch: Home, Input, the mic and the app buttons all work.

Third VU31, same build, 2026-10-21: the list above plus the launcher, reboot-checked. On this set the remote's
app buttons did NOT work once launcherx was off:
- Realtek's com.realtek.advancesetting owns the app buttons (`dumpsys window policy`: KEYCODE_BUTTON_2/4/14/15
go to its GlobalKeyReceiver), but on Google TV it does not open the app itself: Utils.startApp hands every
launch to launcherx's globalbutton.GlobalButtonLaunch_Receiver whenever the
com.google.android.feature.AMATI_EXPERIENCE feature is present. With launcherx disabled that broadcast has no
receiver and the press does nothing; logcat shows "Failed to find provider info for
...launcherx.coreservices.DeviceModeContentProvider".
- Fix for four of them: app_keys in the launcher with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1, which catches the keycode first:
201:com.google.android.youtube.tv, 202:com.google.android.youtube.tv (second YouTube button),
191:com.netflix.ninja, 189:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom. Checked with the real remote.
- SonyLIV (3004) and JioHotstar (3006) cannot be fixed this way: Realtek's KeyEventManager delivers those Sony
codes to advancesetting only, they never reach Android's input pipeline, so no accessibility service sees
them. Only re-enabling launcherx brings those two buttons back.
- InputKeyService also takes the Input key, but com.android.tv.action.VIEW_INPUTS resolves to
com.sony.dtv.smartui/.select.SmartSelectActivity here, the same menu the button opened before.
- The Ambient screensaver (dreamx) keeps working with launcherx disabled, for owners who want to keep it.
- com.android.camera2 is installed and crashes on open (the set has no camera); safe to disable.

Fourth VU31, same build, 2026-10-25/26: most of the list above (Google TV, Apple TV and dreamx kept; Alexa and
camera2 off by choice), four batches with a screenshot and crash-log check after each, then the launcher; several
reboots. Lived with for 2 days so far. Remote: SONY TV VRC 001 (Bluetooth, mic). Notes from it:
- com.sony.dtv.m2.seeds.iot and com.sony.dtv.m2.seeds.iot.remotestart (Alexa) were enabled again after every
reboot, like Eco Dashboard (applicationdisabler presumably; not confirmed). Left alone: harmless while Alexa is
not linked to an account.
- The gear (Settings) button sends keycode 83 to advancesetting, which hands it to launcherx like the app buttons
(same DeviceModeContentProvider error), so it does nothing once launcherx is off. 83:settings in app_keys
(INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1) brings it back. Checked with the real remote.
- Holding volume up or down moves one step per press while InputKeyService is bound: the key-repeat trade in
docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md. consume_volume_keys did not help; empty-service control not run.
- The mic button did nothing because Android's microphone privacy toggle was on (dumpsys sensor_privacy, sensor 1;
AtvRemote logged "katniss doesn't have access to the on-remote mic"), not because of a disabled package.
Settings > Privacy > Microphone on (or cmd sensor_privacy disable 0 microphone) fixed it. Whether it was on
before the debloat is not known.
- With launcherx off, Down in the Ambient screensaver no longer opens its Screensaver settings panel
(dreamx/.settingsv2.TwoPanelActivity); the same panel is under Settings > System > Ambient screensaver > Settings.
- The stock screensaver delay was 10 minutes (screen_off_timeout 600000); Google TV has no on-screen setting for it.

com.google.android.tvlauncher as Home. Applied in six batches with tools/disable.sh, checking Home, Live TV
and Netflix after each one: 35 of the 38 lines above. inputmethod.japanese and music are not installed on
it, and disable.sh skipped smarthomesettings (enabled from the factory on this unit), which was left on.
By the owner's choice it also disabled the DLNA trio and com.google.android.tv.remote.service from the
"Left enabled" block below, with no crash and no change to Home, Live TV, Netflix or the remote's buttons.
Rebooted twice: everything stayed disabled, MemAvailable up from about 230 MB to about 770 MB after boot.
A Projectivy Launcher the owner had installed also answered HOME and was disabled before the launcher went
in. Same day only, not lived with for days.
Notes from this firmware:
- Android 9 has no topResumedActivity line: check apps and inputs with
`dumpsys activity activities | grep mResumedActivity`, and the input with
`dumpsys tv_input | sed -n '/sessionStateMap/,$p' | grep inputId` (HDMI 1 = ExternalTvInputService/HW2).
Netflix screencaps come back empty too, like HDMI and Live TV.
- disable.sh skips com.sony.dtv.smarthomesettings: it asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE. It was already off from
the factory/owner and `pm query-services -a android.media.tv.TvInputService` does not list it, so it is a
false positive here; no TVINPUT_ALLOW needed while it stays off.
- Launcher works: built from launcher/ and installed with build-and-install.sh, which disables tvlauncher
(HOME priority 2) before set-home-activity. Home confirmed with `dumpsys window | grep mFocusedApp`
(on Android 9 it is in dumpsys window, not dumpsys activity) before and after a reboot; Netflix,
YouTube, Input, Settings and Home on the real remote all work without the accessibility services.
config.xml: hidden_apps com.sony.dtv.tvx and com.sony.dtv.tvxlauncher.programguide,
live_tv_package com.sony.dtv.tvx. The UI stays at 1920x1080 / 320 dpi, no zoom.
- With katniss and backdrop off, voice_interaction_service and screensaver_components still name them;
Android ignores disabled components, and leaving them means restore.sh brings both back untouched.

reboots. Re-enable it before a factory reset (restore.sh does).
- /data is 4 GB and was 99% full with a handful of streaming apps: the first launcher install failed with
"Requested internal only, but not enough space". `tools/tv.py 'pm trim-caches 1G'` freed ~450 MB.
- `svc power reboot` is killed on this firmware; use `adb reboot` (and check `uptime`).
- A key remapper (Button Mapper) was sending Home to another launcher; turn its accessibility service off.
- The Sony tab on the Google TV home stays as a label after sonytab is disabled; it only goes with launcherx.
- Applied in batches on one evening with reboots and checks after each (Home, Settings, inputs, Media Player,
no crashes). Not yet lived with for weeks; if something breaks, `pm enable <package>` and please report it.

mau.header:
Sony BRAVIA KD-65X82L (2023, device BRAVIA_VH22, MediaTek), India
Google TV 12 (API 31), build BRAVIA_VH22_M_PA-user 12 STT2.230505.001.S136 682241
Also Sony BRAVIA XR-65X90L (2023, BRAVIA_VH22, MediaTek MT5835), US/Canada, build
BRAVIA_VH22_M_UC-user 12 STT2.230505.001.S136 682241: every package below exists on it except
com.vewd.core.integration.dia. Applied there on 2026-10-26 in three batches: batch 1, batch 2 without
YouTube Music and Play Games (kept by choice), and batch 3. The TV was on Ethernet and setupwraith owned
only the Wi-Fi network saved during setup, which is deleted when it is disabled (FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 with
the owner's agreement). The launcher went in on the first try with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1; the US remote's gear
button is scancode 646 too. Reboot-checked: everything stayed disabled, Home stayed on the launcher, and Home,
gear, app buttons, Input, the mic button and a power cycle checked on the real remote.
Also Sony BRAVIA KD-55X82L (2023, BRAVIA_VH22), India, the same BRAVIA_VH22_M_PA build: every package below
exists on it. Applied on 2026-10-27 in three batches, batch 2 without YouTube Music (kept by choice) and with
the two commented-out apps there. The TV was on 5 GHz Wi-Fi and setupwraith owned that very network: it was
forgotten and re-joined in Settings first, after which the network had a new ID and belonged to
com.android.tv.settings, so batch 3 ran without FORCE_SETUPWRAITH. Re-joining without "Forget network" keeps
the old ID and owner; check the cname again. com.qterics.da.product was still enabled after the first run of
batch 1 and disabled on a second try. Launcher with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 on the first try; gear is scancode 646.
Reboot-checked (tools/check.py: nothing drifted, Home on the launcher; power-on lands on Home); Home, gear,
app buttons, Input, the mic button and volume hold-to-repeat checked on the real remote. Not lived with for
days yet.
Also Sony BRAVIA 4K VH22 (2023, BRAVIA_VH22, MediaTek MT5895; product code not read), Australia, the same
BRAVIA_VH22_M_PA build: every package below exists on it. Applied on 2026-11-01 in three batches with a
screenshot between, without YouTube Music and the seeds.* phone link (kept by choice), without batch 3, and
with the commented-out Australian-unit lines at the end of batch 2. On Wi-Fi the saved network belonged to
android.uid.system, not setupwraith, but setupwraith's RecoveryActivity still claims HOME, so launcherx and
setupwraith both stayed enabled and the launcher took Home by the redirect route (as on the second and third
examples/sony-bravia-4k-vh21 units): cmd package set-home-activity prints Success and changes nothing on this
unit, so launcher/build-and-install.sh with STOCK_LAUNCHER=none HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 (on Windows
launcher/build-and-install.ps1 -StockLauncher none -HomeKeyService: parameters, not environment variables)
ends on its Home check before it enables the helper; HomeKeyService was then enabled by hand, the same
settings the script writes, with stock_home_redirect com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx in config.xml. The
screensaver ships as dreamx's Backdrop, so livingfit went with no screensaver change. Reboot-checked twice:
nothing came back on, power-on lands on the new Home with the helper bound, and the real remote's Home button
opens it from inside an app. Same-day test, not lived with for days yet.

ADB: the TV shows only "ADB debugging" (no separate USB toggle); it opens port 5555, and the "Allow USB
debugging?" prompt appears on first connect. ro.adb.secure=1.

once setupwraith (batch 3) was off. Set live_tv_package and hidden_apps to com.sony.dtv.tvx. The remote's
gear button stops working with launcherx off: it is scancode 646 (0x286, HID 0x0c0586, device "SONY TV VRC
001"), so settings_key_scancodes [646] with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 brings it back.
The display runs a 1920x1080 override on the 3840x2160 panel at density 320; that is the factory state.
Applied 2026-10-21 in three batches with a screenshot and crash-log check after each, then reboot-checked: all
disabled packages stayed disabled, Home stayed on the launcher. At that boot com.sony.dtv.sonysystemservice

and the saved Wi-Fi belongs to android.uid.system, so it is left alone.

home's top bar; the remote's Input button still works through com.sony.dtv.tvx.

and Live TV; HDMI 1 opens in com.sony.dtv.tvx. Hide com.sony.dtv.tvx and set live_tv_package to it.
- Home, Input, Netflix, Back and Action Menu all work on the real remote with no key services.
- Used RAM went from 1,119 MB to 1,003 MB after this list, the launcher and a reboot. Boots straight
into the new launcher. com.sony.dtv.systembootmonitor crashes once at boot (Android 8 background
service limit); it is not in this list.

com.google.android.tvlauncher is disabled; disable it, then `cmd package set-home-activity
com.gathin.tvhome/.MainActivity`. Home key from inside apps returns to the new launcher.
- Inputs works: HDMI 1-4 (HDMI 3/ARC), Video and Live TV listed via com.sony.dtv.tvx. This firmware
reports real per-port status ("No device" / "Connected"), not every port as connected.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/sony-xr-65x90j-cn/debloat.txt com.dangbei.TVHomeLauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

First VH2 list on Android 10 (the other BRAVIA_VH2 / VH21 lists are Android 12) and the first
China-market VH2 build, so the package set differs from all of them: this firmware has no
tv.samba.ssm, no com.sony.dtv.promos / sonyselect / sonytab, no com.google.android.feedback and no
Play Store, so there is no Sony ACR or recommendation row to remove here. The ad surfaces on a
China set are the Dangbei home and store and the preinstalled content apps.

Stock Home on this firmware is com.dangbei.TVHomeLauncher (ChinaHome). It is left enabled as the
fallback, which is why restore.sh is given it rather than com.google.android.tvlauncher. Pass the
owner's own launcher instead if that is what owns HOME on your unit. Live TV / player:
com.sony.dtv.tvx.
Keep the com.sony.dtv.tvinput.* services, tvapi, sonysystemservice, sonyvendorservice,
settingsprovider, systemupdate/update, partnerkeycn (DRM), braviasync*, imeproxy, webapi.core,
irbservice, devicecontrolservice, homenetwork, searchapp, notificationcenter, HappyCast
(com.hpplay.happyplay.aw, the only casting path on a set without Google Cast), the Dangbei store
(com.sony.dangbeimarket) and every com.mediatek.* package: they drive HDMI, the tuner, DRM, CEC,
the remote, OTA and casting. None of them is in this list.

Checked on the TV over wired Ethernet with network ADB on 5555:
- 47 packages are disabled on this set in total. The 13 that were already disabled at the factory
or by an earlier session (setupwraith, mysony, iot, livingfit, smarthelp, eulaviewer, braviashow,
smartmediaapp, b2b.softap, b2b.vendorprotocol, screnmirroring.com, dreams.basic,
providers.contacts) are not in this list, so restore.sh leaves them as they were.
- All 34 below survived `adb reboot` (pm list packages -d still showed them) and none had a process
again afterwards, including the PERSISTENT com.sony.dtv.b2b.hotelmode: unlike the X9000H Android
12 report, system_server did not start it again on this build.
- MemAvailable went from 1,053,752 kB to 1,092,224 kB without a reboot, and SwapFree from 49,404 kB
(53 MB already swapped out) to 102,396 kB after the reboot. The processes below measured about
103 MB of PSS together while they were still running. Most of the RAM on this set belongs to user
apps, not to anything in this list, so expect a smaller win than on a 1.5 GB set.
- After the reboot HOME still resolved to the owner's launcher, the Home key returned to it, HDMI
1-4 still enumerated, tvinput / sonysystemservice / tvx / webapi.core / systemupdate were still
running, `logcat -b crash` had no new FATAL entry and a screenshot was a normal 1920x1080 frame.
- `svc power reboot` is refused on this firmware (PowerManagerService.reboot, SecurityException);
`adb reboot` works.
- Applied and reboot-checked on 22 October 2026, not yet lived with for days. If something breaks,
re-enable it with `pm enable <package>` and please report it.

back if anything breaks). The first pass also disabled com.tcl.system.server, com.tcl.autopair,
com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.messagebox and com.tcl.dashboard; after comparing with tcl-40s5400a they
are not in this list, because the first three are remote/pairing/picture-sound plumbing. If an
earlier guide disabled them on your set, re-enable them:
for p in com.tcl.system.server com.tcl.autopair com.tcl.settings com.tcl.messagebox com.tcl.dashboard; do
TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/tv.py "pm enable $p"; done
(pm enable takes one package at a time.)
Checked after the full list: a custom HOME app comes up after a reboot, YouTube opens, HDMI 1/2,
AV and Live TV switch, Wi-Fi and Settings open, Play Store and Play Services stay enabled.
Not tested: casting from a phone (the Cast receiver is kept), the physical remote's Input key,
TCL picture/sound settings and Bluetooth re-pairing.

Quirks on this firmware:
- Stock tvlauncher declares HOME priority 2, so `cmd package set-home-activity` alone does not
take Home while it is enabled. Disable it after the replacement is running.
- com.tcl.ttvs is the firmware updater, not text-to-speech. It is disabled below to stay on
V8-T221T05-LF1V005; comment it out if you want OTA updates.
- screencap writes an empty file while an HDMI input is on screen. Press Home first.
- com.tcl.usercenter can be switched back on by the system at boot on some C06 units; it stays
idle, so it is left in the list. Re-check `pm list packages -d` after a reboot.
- Storage reserve (second unit): the storage monitor keeps a fixed 500 MB free
(`dumpsys devicestoragemonitor` shows lowBytes=524288000) on a 2.7 GB /data, and every install fails
below it with "Requested internal only, but not enough space" - launcher/build-and-install.sh included.
`tools/tv.py 'pm trim-caches 4G'` frees the app caches and was enough to get past it; check that
devicestoragemonitor says level=NORMAL before installing. TGuard's "TV storage Low" popup comes from the
same check and still showed once with com.tcl.guard disabled.
- `pm uninstall-updates` does not exist on this Android 11 build ("Unknown command").

Same platform and build family as examples/tcl-40s5400a (that unit: LF1V325). This list is that

none missing, none already disabled.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-32s5k/debloat.txt

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher. Live TV app: com.tcl.tv (also plays HDMI).
Inputs come from com.tcl.tvinput.

TESTING, honestly: applied in three rounds on 2026-10-20 and used for a few hours only, which is
shorter than CONTRIBUTING.md asks. What was actually checked, each after a reboot: Netflix and
YouTube open and play, HDMI input switching works, the Live TV source picker works, Wi-Fi survives,
picture/sound settings open, the firmware update check still runs, the screensaver still starts.
The full list was also restored (tools/restore.sh) and re-applied once, so the undo path is tested
on this unit. I will report back if something breaks.

Measured effect on this unit, idle, settled, after reboot:
MemAvailable 307 MB -> 363 MB with the stock launcher (+56 MB), 391 MB with launcher/ (+84 MB).
This TV is RAM-bound, not I/O-bound: 0% iowait, ~88% idle CPU, but ~330 MB of zram swap in use.
Every MB freed here is a MB less swapped, which is why debloating helps this set noticeably.

Unit-specific notes (these differ from the 40S5400A list, check yours before copying):
- The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to com.android.tv.settings, NOT setupwraith, so setupwraith is
safe to disable here and the network survives. disable.sh checks this for you; do not force it.
- The photo screensaver (com.google.android.backdrop) must be swapped before it is disabled:
tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors'
(restore: com.google.android.backdrop/com.google.android.backdrop.Backdrop)
- com.tcl.usercenter does NOT stay disabled. com.tcl.ttvs contains a service logging as
"OverSeasAppShow" which reads /tclconfig/software/param/apps/app_EU_4K.json and re-enables it,
at every boot and again whenever ttvs itself restarts. Disabling com.tcl.ttvs does not help:
it is re-enabled too. /tclconfig is mounted ro and is not even readable from an adb shell.
The entry is left in the list because it does get disabled; it just does not stay that way.
- On this set "standby" from the remote is a full power-down: the TV leaves the network entirely
and cold-boots on the next power-on. There is no network wake, and nothing applied with adb that
the firmware re-asserts at boot will survive being switched off.

PRE-EXISTING FIRMWARE BUG, not caused by debloating (verified by restoring every package to stock,
rebooting, and reproducing it again):
com.android.tv.settings crashes every single time you leave the Settings app.
java.lang.IllegalArgumentException: Service not registered:
com.tcl.android.tv.settings.accounts.TCLAccountManager$1
at TCLAccountManager.destroyManager -> MainSettings.onDestroy
In TvSettings 1.3.0, destroyManager() calls unbindService() on the Activity context while
bindRemoteServiceIfNeverBind() binds on the Application context, and it guards on mInstall
("is the TCL User Center activity installed") instead of isConnection, so it also double-unbinds.
The correctly written sibling method unbindRemoteServiceIfHasBind() is right there in the class.
Workaround while the TV stays on: disabling com.tcl.usercenter makes mInstall false and the bad
branch is skipped (verified, 0 crashes over repeated open/exit cycles). It does not survive a
power cycle, see the note above. Mentioned here so nobody files it against this project.

DO NOT DISABLE on this TV (kept and working):
com.tcl.tv                           # Live TV app, plays HDMI, source picker on the Input key
com.tcl.tvinput                      # TV input services for HDMI, AV and the tuner
com.tcl.ttvs                         # firmware updater; also hosts the BI telemetry and the
# OverSeasAppShow service described above
com.tcl.messagebox                   # carries a ttvs receiver; kept to be safe
com.tcl.system.server                # remote-key plumbing
com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service           # Bluetooth remote
com.tcl.autopair                     # Bluetooth remote auto-pairing
com.tcl.settings                     # picture/sound settings
com.tcl.dashboard                    # "TCL HOME" tile
com.tcl.suspension                   # Quick Panel
com.tcl.providers.config             # reported to drop Wi-Fi on the 65C725; not tried here
com.tcl.keyhelp                      # remote-key help/virtual keys

amazon-fire-tv-afttiff43, amazon-fire-tv-stick-lite-2020, insignia-ns55f301na25 and amazon-fire-tv-afteu014
were the starting point, filtered to the packages this set actually ships.

FIRE OS: DEBLOAT ONLY. Fire OS will not let a third-party launcher take over Home: com.amazon.tv.launcher
claims HOME at priority 950 (com.amazon.firehomestarter at 1), both are protected packages, and
`cmd package set-home-activity` prints Success but changes nothing. This list removes Amazon's telemetry,
ads, preloads and voice assistant around the stock home screen. Live TV app: com.amazon.tv.livetv.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-32sf560-fire-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-32sf560-fire-tv/debloat.txt com.amazon.tv.launcher
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Applied on 2026-10-24 in four batches with a screenshot after each, then rebooted: all 83 stayed disabled
across that reboot, and HDMI, Live TV, Settings and the sideloaded streaming apps were confirmed on the set
afterwards. Lived with since that day; re-check after a firmware update, Fire OS resets some packages.

Not listed because pm disable-user refuses it ("Cannot disable a protected package") on this build:
com.amazon.device.software.ota, com.amazon.device.software.ota.override (firmware and security updates keep
running - Amazon enforces them here), com.amazon.device.sync, com.amazon.device.sync.sdk.internal,
com.amazon.sync.service, com.amazon.diode, com.amazon.platform.fdrw, com.amazon.securitysyncclient,
com.amazon.tcomm, com.amazon.tcomm.client. Also not listed: com.amazon.vizzini (Alexa voice), which Fire OS
re-enables at every boot on 7 and 8, so the microphone button comes and goes; com.amazon.vizzini.ftvcds below
does stay off.

Kept on purpose: the stock launcher, Live TV and the whole tuner and input stack (channelscan,
conditionalaccess, franktvinput, com.vewd.*, com.droidlogic.*, inputpreference.service), Settings and Quick
Settings, the on-screen keyboard, remote and Bluetooth pairing, profiles and parental controls, the Appstore,
Prime Video, AirPlay, the screensaver, OTA, and every app the owner sideloaded (Netflix, Disney+, Prime,
HBO Max, Apple TV, YouTube, Kodi, ZDF, ARD, MagentaTV, 7TV, JustWatch, Downloader). Miracast and DIAL
receivers are off by choice - casting *to* this TV is not used; nothing here touches casting *from* it.
