mau.ten: TCL 40S5400A (40" FHD, S5400 series), EU unit: device C06, product C06_2K_GB, model "Smart TV".
mau.header:
TCL 40S5400A (40" FHD, S5400 series), EU unit: device C06, product C06_2K_GB, model "Smart TV".
Android TV 11 (SDK 30), build AR2101, TCL software V8-T221T05-LF1V325, security patch 2025-03-05.
MediaTek MT9221 (ro.board.platform mt5867), 4x Cortex-A55, about 1 GB RAM (low_ram=true).
Likely a good starting point for other TCL S-series Android TV 11 sets on MT9221.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-40s5400a/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-40s5400a/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (the restore.sh / build-and-install.sh default).
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv. It also plays HDMI: it is the only handler of the passthrough-input
VIEW intent the Inputs menu sends, and the remote's Input key opens its source picker.
Inputs come from com.tcl.tvinput (2x HDMI, AV, tuner).

Applied in three rounds on 2026-10-18 and lived with for one day so far (shorter than
CONTRIBUTING.md asks; I'll report back if anything breaks). Rebooted after each round.
Checked after the full list: launcher/ comes up as Home after a reboot, YouTube and Netflix open,
switching to HDMI 2 (PS5) works, the remote's Input key opens the source picker.
Checked after the first two rounds: Disney+, picture settings, the firmware update check.
Not tested: casting from a phone (the Cast receiver is kept).
Memory, PSS: stock tvlauncher 64 MB + 15 MB swapped vs 41 to 46 MB for my build of launcher/
(a few local changes); tvrecommendations about 20 MB, katniss about 52 MB (two processes).

Second unit: Asia-Pacific (persist.tcl.client_type TCL-AP-MT9221-01), same product C06_2K_GB and
build AR2101, security patch 2024-02-05. The firmware update check reports "up to date" on this
region's server, so AP units may stay behind the EU unit above. Remote: BT_RC833_M4 (Bluetooth LE,
with mic). Applied on 2026-10-23 with the list below, except where noted; lived with until 2026-10-26.
- Voice from the Bluetooth remote needs com.google.android.tv.remote.service as well as katniss.
With remote.service disabled the mic button does nothing and logs nothing. Both re-enabled here.
- After katniss is re-enabled, the mic first opens the Assistant setup screen once; "Use
Assistant without signing in" is enough for voice search in YouTube.
- Here the saved Wi-Fi network belonged to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi | grep cname=), so it was
left enabled; disabling it would have dropped Wi-Fi and ADB.

Vietnam unit, 2026-10-27 (@d0nj): same model "Smart TV", product C06_2K_GB and build
AR2101 / AR14, Android TV 11 (SDK 30), security patch 2022-01-05, mt5867, about 918 MB RAM.
One session, not a several-day test. Kept setupwraith: dumpsys wifi showed four saved-network
entries with cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith; disabling it would delete those
networks and disconnect Wi-Fi and ADB. Chromecast (mediashell), ttvs firmware updates, YouTube,
TV360 and VTVgo were kept. Google TTS was left enabled. Stan, Rakuten TV and TCL Alexa were
already disabled. The photo screensaver was switched to AOSP Colors before disabling backdrop
(command and undo below).
- Off by owner choice: voice (katniss), the remote-mic bridge (tv.remote.service), TalkBack and
all four TCL USB media apps, as in the labelled block below. The mic button is unused.
- Additional packages disabled on this unit are listed as commented choices at the end; they
do not change the EU/AP list's defaults. Remote buttons were not physically tested afterwards.
- After sync, a wait and one reboot, usercenter alone returned among the disabled packages.
Left enabled after that, rather than disabling it again at every boot.
- YouTube, Live TV and SmartTube opened; the TV input framework created an HDMI 1 session
(HW1413744128). HDMI screenshots were empty. Hardware inventory reported more HDMI IDs than
the registered input map, so those IDs are not evidence of extra physical ports.
- launcher/ became Home with stock tvlauncher disabled (mFocusedApp confirmed). The final
launcher configuration was not reboot-tested, and physical remote buttons remain unverified.
- Dock note: four columns, YouTube (com.google.android.youtube.tv), TV360 (com.viettel.tv360.tv),
VTVgo (vn.vtv.vtvgotv), SmartTube (org.smarttube.stable), left to right; live_tv_package=com.tcl.tv.
These are per-unit config.json/theme values, not shared launcher defaults.

Brazil unit, 2026-10-28: same model "Smart TV", product C06_2K_GB and build AR2101 / AR13,
Android TV 11 (SDK 30), TCL software V8-T221T01-LF1V014 (persist.tcl.client_type TCL-LA-MT9221-01),
1280x720 panel, about 922 MB RAM (low_ram=true). The settings menu calls the TCL layer "TV+ OS"; it is
this Android TV 11 build. One session of about an hour, not a several-day test.
- Applied the list above in three batches, with plain `pm disable-user --user 0`, plus TCL Alexa and
the Assistant stub (labelled block at the end). Kept by choice: Chromecast (mediashell), Prime Video,
ttvs. Voice, TalkBack/TTS, the photo screensaver and the four TCL USB players are off by choice.
- setupwraith was safe here: dumpsys wifi showed the saved networks under com.google.uid.shared, not
setupwraith, and Wi-Fi and ADB stayed up after disabling it.
- Reboot too soon and the state is lost: `adb reboot` a few seconds after the last batch brought that
whole batch back enabled. Disabled again, waited 60 s, rebooted: all of it stayed disabled.
- com.tcl.usercenter and com.tcl.smartalexa are switched back on at every boot, as on the
32ES570F; both stay idle.
- MemAvailable: about 250 MB on the stock setup (TV running), about 320 MB after a reboot with the
list, about 370-380 MB after a reboot with launcher/ as Home.
- launcher/ became Home with stock tvlauncher disabled (resolve-activity and mFocusedApp) and stayed
Home after a reboot. Config: live_tv_package and hidden_apps com.tcl.tv, reduced_motion true (as on
the L40S66E, same MT9221).
- Checked by the owner: the physical remote on Home and switching to an HDMI input. Not tested yet:
streaming playback and casting from a phone.
- `adb exec-out screencap -p` wrote the firmware's "Init wrapper sys mutex successful" line into the
file instead of a PNG; `screencap -p /data/local/tmp/s.png` followed by `adb pull` works.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The stock launcher declares HOME priority 2, so `cmd package set-home-activity` alone does not
take Home while it is enabled (Home still opens it). Disabling it, as build-and-install.sh
does, is required.
- com.tcl.usercenter (TCL account) is switched back on by the system at every boot. It stays
idle, so it is left in the list.
- com.tcl.ttvs is NOT text-to-speech: its activities are versionUpdateApp SystemUpdateActivity and
NetworkUpdateActivity, i.e. the firmware updater. Keep it for OTA updates.
- After a reboot the system can switch to the last HDMI source on its own (com.tcl.tv started by
uid 1000 about 2 s after Home). Seen once; a PS5 on HDMI-CEC may be the trigger. Home brings
the launcher back.
- The photo screensaver (com.google.android.backdrop) used about 105 MB while running. Before
disabling it, switch to the AOSP one:
tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors'
(restore: com.google.android.backdrop/com.google.android.backdrop.Backdrop)
- screencap writes an empty file while an HDMI input is on screen. Press Home first.

DO NOT DISABLE on this TV (kept and working):
com.tcl.tv                           # Live TV app, plays HDMI, source picker on the Input key
com.tcl.tvinput                      # TV input services for HDMI, AV and the tuner
com.tcl.ttvs                         # firmware updater (see quirks)
com.tcl.messagebox                   # carries a ttvs receiver (org.tcl.ttvs); kept to be safe
com.tcl.system.server                # remote-key plumbing
com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service           # Bluetooth remote
com.tcl.autopair                     # Bluetooth remote auto-pairing
com.tcl.settings                     # picture/sound settings
com.tcl.dashboard                    # "TCL HOME" tile; kept, only hidden in the launcher config
com.tcl.suspension                   # Quick Panel; kept, not tested without it
com.android.location.fused           # boot-looped a 43S5400A into recovery on V325 (#2803)
com.tcl.providers.config             # reported to drop Wi-Fi on the 65C725; not tried here
com.tcl.keyhelp                      # remote-key help/virtual keys; kept

mau.header:
TCL G03 / BeyondTV4 firmware V8-R51MT05-LF1V652 (AR11), reports as "Smart TV Pro", Android TV 11 (SDK 30),
Google TV launcher (com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx). Same firmware as docs/devices/tcl-75c63b.md.
Tested models:
TCL 43C645, Realtek RTD2851 / R51MT05, Ethernet. Groups 1-3, tested 2026-10-19.
TCL 60C635 (product G03_4K_GB, device BeyondTV4), Realtek rtd288o, 2 GB, security patch 2024-12-05,
Spain, Wi-Fi. Every group except 3, com.tcl.android.webview and com.tcl.keyhelp, plus launcherx,
tested 2026-10-20.
TCL 50C635 (product G03_4K_GB, device BeyondTV4), Realtek rtd288o, 2 GB, build RP1A.200622.001 (AR11),
Spain, Ethernet. Groups 1, 1b, 2 except webview/keyhelp, 4, launcherx, AdGuard Private DNS,
tested 2026-10-24.
TCL 55C645 (product G03_4K_GB, device BeyondTV4), Realtek rtd288o / RTD2851M, security patch 2024-12-05,
Ethernet. Groups 1, 1b, 2 except webview/keyhelp, 4, 5, plus launcherx, tested 2026-10-29. Remote
buttons worked without the launcher's key helpers on this unit (README.md).
List derived from examples/tcl-65c725 (same Android 11 TCL platform), checked against both units' packages.

43C645: applied in three batches with a screenshot after each: Ethernet stayed up, Home and the D-pad, the
launcher's Sources menu (HDMI via TvInputManager), Netflix, and Home from Netflix all worked, also after a
reboot. Private DNS (AdGuard) kept working. tools/b64push.py failed its md5 check here, plain `adb push` +
`pm install -r` worked.
60C635: batch by batch with a screenshot after each: Home, the Input key (Quick panel), Live TV, HDMI and
YouTube kept working, also after a cold reboot with launcherx off. The remote's app buttons need the
launcher's key services: see README.md, config.json and build-and-install.sh.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-43c645/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-43c645/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. HOME fallback com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
takes over once it is disabled, so it is disabled too (group 1b). Home then resolves to the new launcher.
build-and-install.sh disables launcherx itself once the new launcher is Home.
Live TV / HDMI: com.tcl.tv (TVActivity) + com.tcl.tvinput (tuner and passthrough input services).
Never disable: com.tcl.providers.config com.tcl.initsetup com.tcl.factory.view com.tcl.system.server
com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service com.tcl.autopair com.tcl.tvinput com.tcl.tv com.tcl.tvpassthrough com.tcl.settings
com.tcl.inputmethod.international com.tcl.sourcemananger com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice
com.tcl.suspension (Input key / Quick panel) com.google.android.inputmethod.latin com.google.android.gms
com.google.android.gsf com.android.vending
Kept by choice on both: Cast receiver (mediashell), Live TV (com.tcl.tv), screensaver (dreamx).

mau.ten: TCL 43EP660, Europe (Croatia) (ro.product.model BeyondTV, board rtd285o, software V8-R851T02-LF1V378 / AP04),
mau.header:
TCL 43EP660, Europe (Croatia) (ro.product.model BeyondTV, board rtd285o, software V8-R851T02-LF1V378 / AP04),
Android TV 9 (API 28), build PPR1.180610.011, security patch 2020-06-05, 2 GB RAM.
Same platform family as examples/tcl-beyondtv-rt2851/ (older AP04 software); that list's notes apply too.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-43ep660/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-43ep660/debloat.txt
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (restore.sh default). It declares HOME with priority 2,
so a sideloaded launcher only becomes Home once it is disabled. Other HOME claimants are fallbacks:
com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice/.FallbackHome and com.android.tv.settings FallbackHome.
setupwraith does not claim HOME here, but it owns one saved Wi-Fi network: leave it enabled.
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv. HDMI/AV inputs: com.tcl.tvpassthrough. Tuner: com.tcl.tvinput.

Tested 2026-10-20 on a real unit, in the groups below with a screenshot after each, then two reboots:
Wi-Fi stayed up, TCL's source menu, the launcher's Inputs menu (HDMI1, HDMI2 and Live TV switch via
TvInputManager), Netflix, YouTube playback with AdGuard Private DNS, Settings and Home all worked.
Not yet lived with for days.
Quirks on this firmware:
- Sideloading works with `pm install`; Play Protect rejects a reinstall of a split APK copied as
base.apk only ("missing splits"), which looks like INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE but is not
the China-firmware signature check.
- `input keyevent KEYCODE_TV_INPUT` does nothing; TCL's source menu opens with
am start -n com.tcl.sourcemananger/com.tcl.sourcemanager.MainActivity
- screencap is 0 bytes over HDMI and Netflix (secure surface).
- The remote is IR (rtk_keypad); nothing on USB.

Already disabled at the factory, left alone: the 14 uk.co.freeview.* apps, com.tcl.bootadservice,
com.tcl.common.terminalmanagerplus, com.tcl.smartalexa, com.tcl.notereminder, com.tcl.gallery,
Prime Video, Stan, ZEE5, Eros Now, LINE TV, Rakuten TV, Play Music, Play Movies.

DO NOT DISABLE (load-bearing on this firmware):
com.tcl.tv com.tcl.tvinput com.tcl.tvpassthrough  # Live TV, tuner, HDMI

mau.header:
TCL 43S5K and 32V5C, India (device G13, product G13_2K_GB, model "Smart TV"), Google TV 14 (SDK 34),
build UKN2.241110.001 AU10, security patch 2025-12-01. The 43S5K reports MediaTek MT9221 and the
32V5C reports MT5867 (both ro.board.platform mt5867); about 1 GB RAM (954 MB, low_ram=true), 32-bit
only (armeabi-v7a).
Unlike the G08 TCL Google TVs, Live TV and HDMI are MediaTek's com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, not com.tcl.tv.

A TCL 40" 2K QHD Google TV (V5C series), same device/product on a newer firmware sub-build
(UKN2.241110.001 AU13, security patch 2026-06-01): the debloat packages below all applied cleanly and reboot-checked (storage 66%->53%
after also running `cmd package trim-caches`). com.mediatek.MtkDemo (MediaTek's demo app, not in
this unit's build) was also disabled there with no issue.

The launcher half now works on the AU13 unit too, confirming it was never an AU13-specific
regression: the first two attempts skipped Batch 3 (setupwraith stayed enabled) and both landed on
its RecoveryActivity, exactly as this list's own Batch 3 note predicts. Redone with setupwraith
disabled first (Wi-Fi forgotten/re-joined, as below), then the same build-and-install.sh sequence -
reboot-checked, Home came back on launcher/ cleanly (home splash to usable Home in ~10s, vs. hanging
indefinitely on the attempts that skipped setupwraith).

On the AU13 unit, settings_key_keycodes=[83] (the known quirk below) restored the gear/Settings
button as expected. But fixing it costs the same thing noted for the G09 unit elsewhere in this repo:
once HomeKeyService is bound at all (HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1), long-pressing volume steps once instead of
ramping - confirmed here too, and confirmed by logcat to be unfixable from app code on this firmware:
`interceptKeyBeforeQueueing`/`interceptKeyBeforeDispatching` (WindowManager) handle volume directly,
with zero trace of AccessibilityInputFilter or this app anywhere near the event. Volume keys never
reach any accessibility service's onKeyEvent on this unit, so no app-side remap or synthesized repeat
can restore ramping without root. All-or-nothing, same as the G09 case; this one chose the gear button.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-43s5k/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-43s5k/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter.
Keep: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.service, com.tcl.partnercustomizer, com.tcl.suspension
(source panel / Input button), com.tcl.keyhelp (virtual keys), com.tcl.useragreement, com.tcl.factory.view,
mediatek.factorymenu.ui, com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard, com.google.android.tv.remote.service.
Live TV/HDMI safety (both models): keep com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter; it also plays HDMI, so disabling it
breaks both. Keep com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.tv.service and com.tcl.suspension as well.
On G13/AU10, com.tcl.partnercustomizer owns the tvlauncher.widget provider used by the persistent
com.mediatek.tv.service. Keep it enabled: a related MediaTek build repeatedly crashed the service after
that provider was removed (#2138). The G13 provider owner was verified, but the crash was not reproduced
on this TV; the rest of the list was applied and reboot-checked with partnercustomizer still enabled.
Earlier 43S5K, AU07 and AU13 reports disabled it without a reported crash; those historical runs do not
establish that removing this provider is safe on every G13 build after a reboot.

com.tcl.ttvs on this firmware is BOTH TCL's analytics (bi.core.BIService, identifier, trackdata) AND
TCL's firmware/app updater (versionUpdateApp.core.SystemUpdateService). Disabling it stops TCL
firmware updates until it is enabled again, so it is commented out below; uncomment it to trade
updates for less tracking.

The saved Wi-Fi network was created by com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith on the 43S5K (cname= in
dumpsys wifi), so forget and re-join it in Settings before setupwraith is disabled there. On the 32V5C
the saved network survived disabling setupwraith without forgetting and re-joining; check dumpsys wifi /
the network owner on another unit before copying that step.

Applied in four batches on 2026-10-20 with a screenshot after each and lived with for an afternoon so far
(shorter than CONTRIBUTING.md asks; I'll report back if anything breaks). Since then: two power cuts and a
reboot, Home came back on launcher/ each time; Wi-Fi, the remote's Input key (TCL's source panel), the
launcher's Inputs menu (HDMI 1, HDMI 2, Composite, Live TV), YouTube, Netflix and JioHotstar (with AdGuard
Private DNS) all fine. launcherx was disabled by launcher/build-and-install.sh after the new Home ran.

Another G13 unit on AU10 (G13_2K_GB, UKN2.241110.001 AU10, mt5867, 954 MB). Status: applied 2026-10-27
with tools/disable.sh in four batches, reboot-checked the same day, in use for two days so far.
- Disabled: messagebox, logkit, partnersetup, browser, feedback, feedbackconsent, dreamx, setupwraith,
then launcherx through launcher/build-and-install.sh. gtvpai came last: disable.sh skips it
(no readable permission block), so it was disabled with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 after HDMI and Live TV were
checked after the reboot. com.tcl.ttvs was also disabled by the owner's choice (it stays commented
out here).
- Kept: com.tcl.partnercustomizer (#2138), katniss, Play Games and Cast. After the reboot the TV booted
straight into the new Home, every disabled package stayed disabled, com.mediatek.tv.service kept one
PID and `logcat -b crash` was empty.
- com.mediatek.MtkDemo is installed on this AU10 unit as well. disable.sh skips it because it holds
TV_INPUT_HARDWARE, and it was left enabled.
- The saved Wi-Fi network belonged to setupwraith (cname= in dumpsys wifi). After forgetting and
re-joining it in Settings, dumpsys wifi still showed the same network id with cname=setupwraith, and
that happened twice. The way through was switching to another saved network that already belonged
to android.uid.system, then FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1. That deleted only the setupwraith-owned entry, and
the TV stayed online. Check cname= again after re-joining before you disable setupwraith.
- The owner reports that the remote's Input key, app buttons, settings (gear) button and mic all
worked after launcherx was off, with no key helper enabled. HDMI and Live TV through Inputs also
worked.

Brazilian unit (G13, G13_2K_GB, MediaTek MT9221, 954 MB, build UKN2.241110.001 AU07, security patch
2025-06-01, locale pt-BR; the commercial model was not read): every active entry below was applied in four
batches on 2026-10-24, with a screenshot after each, and checked after a reboot. The two Brazilian partner
apps at the end were disabled too; they stay commented here because the Indian units do not ship them. Live
TV and HDMI are com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter here as well; no Ginga package is installed. The network in use belonged to android.uid.system, but an unused
network saved during setup belonged to setupwraith, so tools/disable.sh skipped setupwraith; it was
disabled with FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 after checking the owners, which deleted only the unused network. Home
on this unit is the CleanYourTV UI fork from SHOWCASE.md, not launcher/, and its install script disabled
launcherx. After the reboot: Home came back on it, Wi-Fi reconnected, and MemAvailable was 385 MB
(295 MB before the list). `input keyevent 83` did nothing once launcherx was off (simulated, not a press
on the remote).

Indonesian unit: TCL 32V51C, 32" (G13, G13_2K_GB, MediaTek mt5867, 954 MB, build UKN2.241110.001 AU13,
security patch 2026-06-01, bought in Indonesia). Applied in five batches on 2026-10-27 with a screenshot after
each, and checked after two reboots. Home came back on launcher/ both times, Wi-Fi reconnected, and YouTube
and Netflix played. Three findings on this unit:
- tools/disable.sh skips two active entries of this list here, so the Apply line alone leaves them enabled.
com.mediatek.MtkDemo requests TV_INPUT_HARDWARE, which the input-driver check (#321) refuses, although
`pm query-services --components -a android.media.tv.TvInputService` does not list it. It was kept enabled
here because no HDMI device was at hand to check the inputs afterwards. And
android.autoinstalls.config.google.gtvpai shows no permission block in dumpsys (it is a stub with one
DummyReceiver), so the same check cannot read it; it went with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 on a one-line list.
- The network in use belonged to android.uid.system, and an unused network saved during setup belonged to
setupwraith, as on the Brazilian unit: FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 deleted only the unused one.
- TGuard (com.tcl.guard) and a store demo (fusion.android.tv.demo) ship enabled here and were disabled;
they are listed, commented, at the end.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The remote's gear button sends keycode 83 (KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION, scancode 561), which only launcherx
handled: set settings_key_keycodes to [83] (config.xml or a theme) so it opens Settings again.
- On both models, launcherx is disabled only after CleanYourTV owns Home; build-and-install does it,
and restore.sh needs launcherx as its argument.
- HomeKeyService, used for the gear button, can stop volume long-press from repeating on some TCL
Google TV builds: holding volume then steps once. Set key_filter=false to restore the repeat and
lose the remapped keys, or leave HomeKeyService off. Not measured on the 32V5C; see
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md.
- With katniss off the mic button does nothing; leave it enabled if you use voice.
- Usage statistics restart empty after a power cut (they are written to disk only now and then).
- Without HomeKeyService the gear does nothing, so Settings is reached through Home, and on this 1 GB set
that costs the app: on the 32V51C, YouTube was killed in the background (am_proc_died at oom_adj 900)
between Home and Settings and started cold afterwards. Opened over the app (the gear with
settings_key_keycodes [83]), Settings left YouTube's process alive, and Back returned to it. One test each.
The 32V51C took the gear and lost the volume ramp, as the AU13 unit above did.
- With setupwraith disabled, Settings > Privacy > Usage & diagnostics spins for ever: setupwraith serves
that page (com.google.android.settings.USAGE_AND_DIAGNOSTICS_SETTING). On the 32V51C it was enabled for
a minute to switch the toggle off, then disabled again with tools/disable.sh; Home stayed on launcher/.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv. Nothing was disabled

Left enabled on purpose: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.suspension (the input menu), com.tcl.initsetup,
com.tcl.useragreement, com.tcl.factory.view, com.tcl.gamebar, com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service (the remote),

Store and Play Services, all com.mediatek.*, and the owner's streaming apps (Prime Video kept by choice).

Wi-Fi: the network the TV was using had been saved by setupwraith during first setup. It was forgotten and
joined again in Settings > Network & Internet before batch 3; `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` then
named only com.android.tv.settings, and tools/disable.sh disabled setupwraith without FORCE_SETUPWRAITH.

Launcher: launcher/build-and-install.sh with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 and the app_keys in config.json. The remote
here is the white TCL one with Netflix and YouTube buttons. Netflix and Settings send the same codes as the
55Q77K's in examples/tcl-g08-us-google-tv/README.md (4062, 83), but YouTube sends 4065 (scancode 245, taken by
TCL's TclShortCutKeyManager), not 190, so it needs "4065:com.google.android.youtube.tv". Its TV button (the screen icon right of
Home) sends keycode 4001, scancode 365: com.tcl.tv's GlobalKeyService turns it into KEYCODE_GUIDE for launcherx
while the TV app is not running, so with launcherx off it did nothing. "4001:guide:com.tcl.tv" opens the
program guide again (com.tcl.tv/.epg.EpgProActivity), as before; "4001:input:com.tcl.tvinput/.TunerInputService/HW2"
switches to the antenna without the guide. All checked on the real remote. A held volume button now steps once
per press (the key-helper trade in that README); the owner accepted it.

Second unit: TCL 55C718 (Finland), same build: ro.product.model BeyondTV2, fingerprint TCL/BeyondTV2/BeyondTV:9/PPR1.180610.011/AP06,
software V8-R851T02-LF1V606, client type TCL-EU-RT2851-S1, 2 GB RAM, armeabi-v7a, stock Home com.google.android.tvlauncher 7.7.15.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-55c715/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-55c715/debloat.txt
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (Android TV Home 7.x, Play-updated). Live TV app: com.tcl.tv
(launcher config: live_tv_package com.tcl.tv). The launcher's Inputs menu lists HDMI 1-3, AV and Live TV through
TvInputManager; no source_panel fallback needed. Network ADB (port 5555) was open as soon as USB debugging was on.

Tested 2026-10-20 on a real unit: applied in the groups below with a screenshot after each, then rebooted three times.
Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Play Store, Play Movies, Live TV, HDMI through TCL's source menu and the launcher's
Inputs menu, Settings, Chromecast and the Bluetooth remote all kept working. MemAvailable went from 557 MB to
about 780 MB with the same apps; voice_ap dropped from ~27% of one core to ~3% once group 6 was off.
In daily family use since then (streaming apps, live TV through the set-top box on HDMI 1, casting); nothing beyond
the notes below had to be re-enabled.

Quirks on this firmware:
- com.tcl.usercenter comes back enabled at every boot, even with its Play update removed (TCL's boot-time list;
TV Settings also binds to it). Listed anyway: it stays off until the next reboot. Rakuten TV (tv.wuaki.apptv)
does the same, see group 3.
- com.tcl.partnercustomizer also supplies the stock Android TV Home's Inputs icon (and the TCL Channel tile and a
TV Guard shortcut). Disabling it removes the icon; the remote's Source button still works. No effect with a
custom launcher.
- Disabling com.google.android.katniss (group 6) also disables search on the stock home screen, typed search too.
- Settings > Applications opens TCL "TV Guard" (com.tcl.tvweishi), and still does while it is disabled.
- Re-enable com.tcl.tvweishi and com.tcl.appmarket2 (group 7) while installing the launcher, as on the RT2851 list.
- 55C718: disable.sh skipped android.autoinstalls.config.tcl.device and com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.recommendations
(the input-driver check found no permission block in dumpsys for them), so they stayed enabled; nothing else on the list
needed an override. pm disable-user on com.tcl.usercenter is refused for the shell (SecurityException), as noted above.

Status: 2026-10-27, 55C718 (Finland): groups 1 to 6 and 8 applied (com.tcl.versionUpdateApp and Chromecast left on), launcher
installed, then group 7 and com.google.android.backdrop disabled. Netflix, YouTube, Yle Areena, Live TV, HDMI through the
Inputs menu and the source key, and the remote worked after each step and after restarts; in daily use for 4 days since.
Re-enabled afterwards: none.

- Same as the other G10 sets: setupwraith claims Home once launcherx is disabled, so it goes too.

an accessibility service; test remaps with the real remote.
- Android's screen_brightness does nothing (TCL drives the backlight). TCL's own Audio Only mode turns
the panel off with sound playing: `am startservice -a com.tcl.settings.SHOW_WINDOW -p
com.android.tv.settings --es Type AudioOnly`.
- App log lines rarely show up in logcat (64K buffer); write diagnostics to a file instead.

Tested on a live unit in Germany and lived with. Verified across reboots: CleanYourTV reference launcher is the default
Home on boot and Home key press; HDMI inputs 1-3 switch normally; DVB Live TV / tuner works; TV Picture and
Sound settings open; screensaver and sleep timers start; casting (AirPlay, Chromecast, Miracast) works.

- The active Wi-Fi network belongs to android.uid.system:1000, NOT setupwraith (verified with dumpsys wifi).
Setupwraith can be safely disabled without dropping Wi-Fi or ADB.
- The stock screensaver (com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx) is disabled in favor of ClockDream:
tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream'
Sleep timer set to 20 minutes (settings put system screen_off_timeout 1200000) to protect the panel.
- Remote key helpers and volume repeat (TCL G08 Android 12 firmware limitation):
On this firmware, binding ANY key-filtering accessibility service causes the platform input dispatcher
to suppress continuous hardware auto-repeat when holding the volume buttons (steps once instead of ramping;
see docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md). Leaving accessibility helpers unbound
(enabled_accessibility_services '' and accessibility_enabled 0) preserves full volume ramping.
On Home, the launcher's Settings button (keycode 83) works directly without any helper.

TCL 65C735 (reports as "Smart TV Pro", device G05, product G05_4K_GB), Google TV 11 (SDK 30),
firmware AR2101, 2.7 GB RAM. France, wired through a USB Ethernet adapter (eth1).
Same platform as examples/tcl-g05-google-tv; this list is a little more conservative.

Also used on a TCL 55C728, Turkey (same product G05_4K_GB, build AR2101, software V8-T615T03-LF1V618,
security patch 2024-11-05, wired Ethernet), with these differences:
- com.tcl.ttvs stays enabled there, because the system updater lives in it (versionUpdateApp
SystemUpdateActivity): disabling it also stops OTA updates. Kept, it logs every remote key press for
TCL's BI (KeyDownBehaviorReceiver-BI) and turns com.tcl.usercenter and com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV
(T-Cast) back on at every boot, even after `pm uninstall --user 0`, so those two stay enabled as well.
- Eleven preloads came disabled from the factory on that unit (Abema, U-NEXT, Hulu JP, FOD, Stan,
Rakuten TV, both AirPlay packages, the game bar, notes, Alexa); com.tcl.assistant was left enabled.
- It also disabled the lines marked "55C728" below (commented out, so this list is unchanged).
Two days of use with several reboots; tools/check.py reported no drift. setupwraith stayed
disabled across reboots.
- config.json in this folder maps its remote: gear 4077 to Settings, Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065 and Prime
Video 4099 (install with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1). The TCL Channel button never reaches the accessibility
helpers, so it cannot be mapped. Firmware logs each press as `TclPhoneWindowManager:
handleKeyBeforeQueueing, key = <code>`; the main logcat buffer is 1 MiB, so read it right away.

Also used on a TCL 65C935, France (same product G05_4K_GB, build AR2101, incremental AR25, software
V8-T615T03-LF1V614, Wi-Fi only, MediaTek MT9615), with these notes:
- Applied in five batches with a screenshot between each; Home, the TCL Quick panel (Input key), HDMI,
Wi-Fi, Play Store and YouTube worked after every batch and after a reboot. One evening of use.
- com.tcl.ttvs kept (updater), as on the 55C728. It re-enables com.tcl.esticker within minutes and
com.tcl.usercenter, com.tcl.notereminder and com.tcl.smartalexa at every boot; tools/check.py reports
those four as drift. The 55C728 lines marked below were disabled on this unit too (logkit, channelplus,
useragreement, gtvpai, ocean.instructions, browser, miracast); Assistant and Chromecast kept.
- setupwraith owned TWO saved Wi-Fi networks: the one in use and an old SSID from a previous ISP.
Forgetting and re-joining the current one in Settings moved it to com.android.tv.settings, but
disable.sh still refused setupwraith because of the old one, which Settings offered no way to forget.
`cmd wifi list-networks` showed its id and `cmd wifi forget-network <id>` removed it. Disabling
setupwraith then survived a reboot (third AR2101 report; only tcl-g05-google-tv saw it come back).
- Remote: the same keycodes as the 55C728 (gear 4077, Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065, Prime Video 4099),
plus Input 178, which opens the TCL Quick panel with no helper. config.json applies unchanged;
settings_key_panel: true gives the gear the launcher's quick settings panel. Holding Volume+ still
auto-repeats with HomeKeyService bound (repeatCount climbed normally), so key_filter costs nothing here.
- After tools/theme.sh restarted Home, HomeKeyService was left enabled but UNBOUND (dumpsys
accessibility: "Bound services:{}") and the gear did nothing (#994). Clearing the list, toggling
accessibility_enabled off, waiting 2 s and writing it back bound it again; `appops set
com.gathin.tvhome AUTO_START allow; appops write-settings` first, and restore_key_services in the theme.
- `tools/tv.py 'reboot'` never returns on this set (#995): run it with a timeout.

Also used on a TCL 65C745 QLED, France (2023; same product G05_4K_GB, build AR2101, incremental AR25, software
V8-T615T03-LF1V614, security patch 2024-03-05, wired Ethernet, 32-bit armeabi-v7a), with these notes:
- Applied in seven batches with a screenshot between each. One day of use; several reboots, two of them checked
with tools/check.py (no drift). The 65C745 also comes as a G08 set on Google TV 14 (examples/tcl-55c745): read
ro.product.name before picking a list.
- Also disabled on this unit: the lines marked "65C745" below (commented out, so this list is unchanged), plus
Netflix, Prime Video, the stock YouTube app, Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), T-Cast
(com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV) and the game bar, by choice. AirPlay kept by choice.
- com.tcl.ttvs disabled: TCL offers nothing past LF1V614 on this set. With it off, com.tcl.usercenter and T-Cast
stayed disabled across both reboots, where the 55C728 and 65C935 saw them come back.
- There is no separate Network/ADB debugging toggle: USB debugging alone opens port 5555.
- Two setup-time SSIDs were saved; with both forgotten and the set on Ethernet, disable.sh could read no network
owner and skipped setupwraith, so it went with FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1. Before that, build-and-install.sh rolled
Home back because setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claimed HOME, as described above.
- Remote (IR, "MStar Smart TV IR Receiver"): no Input 178 button. The source button, marked CH, sends KEY_EPG
(scancode 365), which Android does not map: "scan:365:inputs" in app_keys opens the Inputs menu once #1167 is in the launcher.
Gear 4077, Netflix 4062 and YouTube 4065 as on the 55C728.
- Volume: with a key-filtering helper bound (HomeKeyService or InputKeyService), each press of the remote's
volume key steps the volume twice; an injected KEYCODE_VOLUME_UP steps it once, and consuming the key in the
helper does not stop the double step. key_filter: false brings back one step per press, at the price of every
remote button mapped above.
- The auto-start op is named APP_AUTO_START here (`appops get <package>`): `appops set com.gathin.tvhome AUTO_START
allow` fails (Unknown operation string), APP_AUTO_START is accepted. Allowed and saved with `appops write-settings`,
it let a third-party screensaver (Aerial Views) bind, and it still did after a reboot (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md,
"A third-party screensaver never shows"). After a theme push only one of the two helpers was bound at a time; a
reboot binds the enabled ones again.

only, so forget the network and join it again in Settings (owner moves to com.android.tv.settings)
BEFORE setupwraith is disabled, or the TV drops off Wi-Fi and ADB. setupwraith's HOME components could
not be disabled on their own (shell SecurityException), so the whole package goes.
- With launcherx gone, the Settings, TV-guide and app-shortcut buttons go dead. They are remapped in this
folder's config.json app_keys by Android keycode (all share scancode 240): Settings 83, TV guide 4001,
Netflix 4062, Prime Video 4099, YouTube 190 (the TCL button is 4020, left unmapped). This needs
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1, and on this board the key-filter service stops continuous volume-repeat (hold-to-ramp
becomes one step per press) - a trade, not a fault. Leave the helper off to keep volume repeat.

changes after every reboot or Wi-Fi drop. Windows: `adb connect <tv ip>:<port>` first, then TV_HOST=<tv ip>:<port>
with TV_ADB_BINARY set to adb.exe (tools/native-adb.md), so no `adb tcpip 5555` is needed.

com.tcl.tv.plus, com.tcl.browser, com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter, com.tcl.suspension, com.tcl.t_solo and Play Games
are hidden in the launcher (hidden_apps), not disabled.

Input source panel, Live TV, the four HDMI inputs, YouTube with AdGuard Private DNS and the remapped remote
buttons all kept working. All 24 packages stayed disabled after a reboot; nothing re-enables at boot.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The saved Wi-Fi network belonged to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi: cname=...setupwraith). Forget the network and
join it again in Settings (owner moves to com.android.tv.settings) BEFORE setupwraith is disabled, or the TV
drops off Wi-Fi and ADB. tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith until then.
- With launcherx gone, the Settings, TV-guide and app-shortcut buttons go dead. They are remapped in this
folder's config.json app_keys by Android keycode: Settings 83, TV guide 4001, Netflix 4062, Prime Video 4099,
YouTube 190 (all confirmed on the real remote). This needs INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1, and on this board the
key-filter service stops continuous volume-repeat (hold-to-ramp becomes one step per press): a trade, not a
fault. power_on_home in config.json needs HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 as well.
- Custom HDMI input names (e.g. "Cable" on HDMI 3) live in `settings get secure tv_input_custom_labels`, as
`<input id>,<name>` pairs joined by `:`. The launcher's `inputs_connected_only` hides every port here, because
all four report cable_connection_status=0 even with a CEC device plugged in; leave it off.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Developer options has no separate Wireless/Network debugging toggle, but switching USB debugging ON
opens network ADB on TCP port 5555 over Wi-Fi directly.
- `cmd package set-home-activity` prints Success, but launcherx keeps Home until it is disabled; then
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (`RecoveryActivity`) claims Home until setupwraith is disabled too.
- The Wi-Fi network saved during first-time setup belongs to setupwraith (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`).
Forget the network and re-join it in Settings > Network & Internet BEFORE disabling setupwraith (so the network
is owned by com.android.tv.settings), or Android will delete the saved Wi-Fi network when setupwraith is disabled.
- com.tcl.suspension is TCL's Input/source picker (`VIEW_INPUTS`), not an ad overlay: keep it enabled.
- HDMI 1 is `com.tcl.tvinput/.passthroughinput.TvPassThroughService/HW15` (with HDMI-CEC child inputs under it).
- On the 55" unit the saved Wi-Fi already belonged to android.uid.system, so setupwraith did not own it there.
- tools/disable.sh skips android.autoinstalls.config.google.gtvpai, com.android.wallpaperbackup, waipu.tv and
Joyn here: their dumpsys has no permission block, so the input-driver check cannot read them. Only
com.tcl.tvinput serves TvInputService (`pm query-services --components -a android.media.tv.TvInputService`);
once HDMI works after a reboot, TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 disables them.
- To keep casting, the 55" unit kept setupwraith and launcherx and took Home with stock_home_redirect
(key_filter false, HomeKeyService only, as in tcl-q7c-google-tv/). Remote buttons, HDMI and the volume ramp all
worked, but after a cold boot the TV stays on Google TV's home until Home is pressed once (#1546).

TCL ak30a5 — Chinese-market TCL Android TV 9, Amlogic SoC
Android 9 (PPR1.180610.011), locale zh-CN, NO Google services at all
(0 com.google.* packages, no Play Store — apps come from com.tcl.appmarket2 or a USB stick).
Likely a good starting point for other 2020-2023 Chinese TCL sets on the same Amlogic firmware.

TWO UNITS, TWO FIRMWARE GENERATIONS — read the build date before you use a line:

1) TCL ak30a5, build date 20230208, 1.5 GB RAM. The original list; its entries are unchanged.
2) TCL 雷鸟雀4 55F270C-JN (2025 model), build date 20250610, 2 GB RAM, fingerprint
TCL/ak30a5/ak30a5:9/PPR1.180610.011/20250610:user/dev-keys, China (zh-CN).
Same board, same Android version, newer firmware. Lines marked "20250610" were only
verified on that unit. It ran this list for three days, with the Home handover, the
accessibility guard and the boot behaviour re-checked after several reboots.
3) TCL ak30a5, build date 20250401, fingerprint TCL/ak30a5/ak30a5:9/PPR1.180610.011/20250401,
zh-CN. Status: one evening (2026-10-27) with two reboots — NOT the several days this list
asks for, so treat the 20250401 notes below as unverified for daily use. Nothing in the
package list itself was changed for this unit.
Differences measured on that unit:
- Disabling com.tcl.cyberui has a quirk: its old task can still be brought to the front
once in a while within the same boot (logcat shows am_on_start_called for the disabled
package). It stays dead across a reboot; pressing Home after a re-assert of
set-home-activity fixes the session.

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-ak30a5/debloat.txt com.tcl.cyberui
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.tcl.cyberui. On 20230208 it is a PERSISTENT priv-app; on 20250610 it is a
SYSTEM app with UPDATED_SYSTEM_APP (an update in /data/app over /system/priv-app), versionCode
7748, and WITHOUT the PERSISTENT flag. See the note below before disabling it.
Live TV / HDMI: com.tcl.tv. There is NO standard TvInputManager on this firmware (`service list`
has no tv_input), so the launcher's Inputs menu opens TCL's own source panel instead:
startService(com.tcl.settings/com.tcl.insrc.ShowWindowService, action com.tcl.insrc.SHOW_WINDOW).
Keep com.tcl.settings or that panel is gone. HDMI source ids: TV=2, AV1=3, HDMI1=8, HDMI2=9.
That panel is a service, not an activity: `cmd package resolve-activity -a
com.tcl.insrc.SHOW_WINDOW` answers "No activity found", so use `am start-service`.
Keep com.tcl.tv: it owns DTV/HDMI playback and the remote's source key (KEYCODE_TV_INPUT still
opens the source panel over any launcher, cyberui or not).
Keep com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv: it is the ONLY input method on the TV. Disable it and there is
no on-screen keyboard at all.
Keep com.tcl.guard: 电视卫士 is also the only on-screen APK installer (应用安装, needs a USB stick).
Keep com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter if you play anything from USB.
Keep com.tcl.appmarket2 and com.tcl.versionUpdateApp: on 20250610 the boot package was
com.tcl.appmarket2, and the OTA updater is worth keeping.

Known quirks on the 20230208 firmware:
- `pm install` is patched to refuse shell installs ("install apk has be disabled from pm by
system default"), and PackageInstallerActivity is exported=false with its intent filters removed.
`pm install-commit` is not gated though: an APK can still be installed by creating a
PackageInstaller session from a shell-run app_process and committing that session.
- APKs that declare android.intent.category.HOME are refused at parse time unless they are signed
with TCL's key: "INSTALL_PARSE_FAILED_INCONSISTENT_CERTIFICATES: disable install launcher app not
signature by tcl". A third-party launcher therefore cannot be installed on this model at all;
com.tcl.cyberui stays and only its ad/telemetry packages (this list) can be removed.
- 电视卫士 → 应用安装, the only on-screen installer, stages the APK as a file without the .apk
suffix and fails with INSTALL_PARSE_FAILED_NOT_APK ("Failed to parse .../my_app_session") for
every package. Don't use it.
- Installs also need roughly 600 MB free on /data or they fail with
INSTALL_FAILED_INSUFFICIENT_STORAGE; `pm trim-caches 2000M` is usually enough.
- Installed launcher version here is com.tcl.cyberui 7746 (7.7.46). The 灵控桌面 APKs circulating
for TCL sets are the same package at versionCode 7670 (7.6.70), i.e. a downgrade.
- screensaver_components ships pointing at com.android.deskclock, which is not installed, so the
TV has no working screensaver out of the box (and launcher/'s Clock can't be installed here).
- /data/local/tmp is not writable by the shell user; push to /sdcard instead.
- `screencap` cannot write to /data/local/tmp either, and returns an empty file while Live TV/HDMI
is on screen (same as the G10). Press Home first.
- No com.android.dreams.basic fallback screensaver. Also no TCL equivalent of `pm install`.

What is different on the 20250610 firmware (all measured on that unit, 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-25):
- `pm install` is NOT patched any more. With no argument it answers "Failed to parse APK file:
null" — it reaches PackageManager. What refuses the APK is the verifier in front of `pm
install` (INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE), not the parse-time signing gate above, and
`settings get global verifier_verify_adb_installs` is null.
- /data/local/tmp IS writable by the shell user. The narrower quirk: rename(2) is refused there,
so `mv` answers "bad '/data/local/tmp/x': Permission denied" while `cp` and `> file` work. Use
`cp`, not `mv`, when placing a file for tools/b64push.py, which verifies an md5 before it puts
the file in place.
- The stock launcher is versionCode 7748 (7.7.48) there, not 7746.
- The firmware turns USB debugging back off on every reboot: service.adb.tcp.port is still 5555
but nothing listens and `adb connect` answers "connection refused". It has to be re-enabled by
hand on the TV each time (设置 → 本机信息 → remote-control "上上下下左右", or 信源 → 模拟接收
→ 菜单 → 对比度 → 输入 1950). Any scripted run that spans a reboot needs that manual step.

Install the launcher BEFORE group 5: com.tcl.tvweishi and com.tcl.appmarket2 both carry a
PackageInstallerService, and persist.tcl.whitelistpath points into appmarket2's data.

Tested 2026-10-19 on a real unit, applied in the six groups below with a screenshot after each:
Wi-Fi stayed up, D-pad, TCL's source menu, the launcher's Inputs menu (HDMI via TvInputManager works,
no source_panel fallback needed), Netflix, Settings and Home from HDMI all worked, also after a reboot.
Quirks on this firmware:
- `input keyevent KEYCODE_TV_INPUT` is an "Unhandled key"; the remote's Source button goes through
TCL's own path. TCL's source menu opens with
am startservice -n com.tcl.sourcemananger/com.tcl.insrc.ShowWindowService -a com.tcl.insrc.SHOW_WINDOW
- TvInputManager reports AV as connected (state 0) with nothing plugged in.
- screencap is blank over HDMI and Netflix (secure surface). Press Home first.
- TV 2 Play 6.74.0 (no.tv2.sumo) deadlocks in TV2Application.onCreate and ANRs, from the stock
launcher too (an ANR before any change). App bug; update it from the Play Store.
- The voice processes (voice_ap, katniss:interactor) used ~45% of one core all the time. Group 6
stops katniss (~22%); voice_ap is a native firmware daemon and keeps running without root.
- The clock ran 6 h fast with automatic time on (last NTP success months earlier). Toggling
`settings put global auto_time 0` then `1` forced a fresh sync.

TCL/BeyondTV2/BeyondTV:11/PPR1.180610.011/AR05:user/release-keys.

Also sold re-badged: a Hitachi CDH-LE554KSMART22 (55", Argentina) reports this same fingerprint,
board and preloaded set, so this list applies to it unchanged. See README.md for what that second
unit confirmed and where its factory state differs.

Not the same set as examples/tcl-beyondtv2-latin-america: same product name and build number, but
that unit runs Android 9 (API 28, `AP08`) and ships a different preloaded package set (no
com.tcl.overseasappshow, no com.tcl.usercenter, no MagiConnect, no com.tcl.notereminder).
This firmware is also NOT `ro.product.model BeyondTV` (examples/tcl-beyondtv, Android TV 9).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-beyondtv2-android-11/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-beyondtv2-android-11/debloat.txt
Install the launcher BEFORE disabling the stock launcher.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (priority 2, disabled after the replacement was up).
Other HOME claimants are only fallbacks: com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice and com.android.tv.settings.
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv, with com.tcl.tvinput for the tuner and HDMI 1-3 (this set exposes 3 HDMI
ports through the TV input framework). TvInputManager lists them normally, so the launcher's Inputs
menu needs no source_panel_service on this firmware.
setupwraith does not own the saved Wi-Fi network here (dumpsys wifi shows android.uid.system and
com.google.uid.shared), so it can be disabled without dropping the TV off Wi-Fi.

Tested: applied in four batches with a screenshot after each and a full reboot between batches, on
2026-10-20. Verified after the final reboot: every package still disabled, Wi-Fi up, Home on the
replacement launcher, Inputs menu, Live TV (com.tcl.tv/.TVActivity), Netflix and Prime Video launch,
Home returns from every app, no crash and no ANR in logcat. NOT yet lived with for weeks; this
list is deliberately conservative (telemetry, ads, promos, and the voice/mirroring choices).

Second unit (Hitachi CDH-LE554KSMART22, Argentina), 2026-10-27: same four-batch run, a screenshot
after each batch and two full reboots. Same result - every package stayed disabled, Wi-Fi up, Home
on the replacement launcher, Inputs menu with HDMI 1-3 + AV + Live TV, HDMI 1 switching into
com.tcl.tv/.TVActivity, Netflix / YouTube / Play Store / Settings / Live TV all launching and
returning Home, no crash and no ANR. One session only, NOT days of use; see README.md.

Third unit (TCL 65P615, ro.product.model BeyondTV, client type TCL-ME-RT2851-S1, software
V8-R851T02-LF1V715), 2026-10-28: fingerprint TCL/BeyondTV/BeyondTV:11/PPR1.180610.011/AR05 - product
BeyondTV instead of BeyondTV2, same AR05 build and the same preloaded set. Same four batches, then the
launcher, then one full reboot: every package still disabled, Home on the replacement launcher, Inputs
menu with HDMI 1-3 + AV + Live TV, YouTube and Chromecast (mediashell) running. One session only.

mau.header:
TCL BeyondTV2, Latin America / Brazil market (ro.product.model BeyondTV2, brand TCL), Android TV 9
(API 28), build PPR1.180610.011, security patch 2021-01-05. Realtek RTD2851 family
(ro.board.platform = rtd285o), firmware V8-R851T02-LF1V660, client TCL-LA-RT2851-S1.
Fingerprint: TCL/BeyondTV2/BeyondTV:9/PPR1.180610.011/AP08:user/release-keys
What the launcher's clips, gradients and layers cost on this GPU: docs/devices/tcl-beyondtv2-v660.md
2 GB RAM with 800 MB zRAM, 32-bit userspace, eMMC with 10 GB /data. Latin America set
(TCL app store, no India Jio/Airtel/Hotstar; a set of UK Freeview catch-up apps is preloaded
and was already disabled at the factory).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-beyondtv2-latin-america/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-beyondtv2-latin-america/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (restore.sh / build-and-install.sh defaults work).
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv, with com.tcl.tvinput for the tuner and HDMI 1-3 (3 ports on the second,
55" unit below). launcher/ needs live_tv_package com.tcl.tv AND hidden_apps com.tcl.tv, or it
shows twice: once as a grid tile, once in the Inputs menu's own "Live TV" row.
This is a different set from examples/tcl-beyondtv (India market): same build number
PPR1.180610.011, different product name and different region, so the preloaded app set and the
factory-disabled set differ.

Tested: applied on a real unit on 2026-10-18/19. Each package was disabled on its own, the
device rebooted, and a 24-check smoke test (HDMI input, Live TV session, Netflix, Assistant,
microphone, Bluetooth remote, audio output, no crashes) passed after every change.
I have NOT lived with this list for days yet, and the file header says so.
Measured effect: these two packages removed processes but gave NO measurable overall speed gain
(idle CPU and app-open times stayed within run-to-run noise). They are kept for less telemetry,
not for speed.

Second unit, same fingerprint, tested 2026-10-26: a 55" set, also Wi-Fi, launcher/ installed
(Home confirmed with mResumedActivity), Inputs menu (HDMI 1-3, AV, Live TV), D-pad edges and
YouTube launch checked, applied in nine batches with screenshots between them plus a reboot
check. This unit shipped with several packages the first unit's notes only listed as untested
or did not mention at all (see "Added on the second unit" below), and it had an extra Alexa
integration and a second, TCL-native Miracast app alongside MultiScreenInteraction_TV. Not yet
lived with for days either.

Already disabled at the factory on this firmware: com.tcl.bootadservice, com.tcl.gallery,
au.com.stan.and, com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom, com.linecorp.linetv, tv.wuaki.apptv and
the 14 uk.co.freeview.* catch-up apps. Same set on the second unit.

Four packages cannot be kept disabled on the second unit: com.tcl.notereminder,
com.tcl.smartalexa, com.tcl.tv.tclhome_master and com.tcl.usercenter came back enabled on
their own within minutes, with no reboot needed to trigger it - most likely
com.tcl.appstatecontroller (left alone below, "unclear roles, boot/package/network hooks")
watching and restoring them, the same way com.tcl.overseasappshow is documented to do for
notereminder and tclhome_master on the Android 11 BeyondTV2 (examples/tcl-beyondtv2-android-11).
They are listed below for completeness and because they do disable (just not stay disabled);
do not keep re-running disable.sh on them, per PROMPT.md.

DO NOT DISABLE (load-bearing): com.tcl.tv com.tcl.tvinput com.tcl.sourcemananger (Live TV,
HDMI, tuner, Source menu), com.tcl.autopair com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service
com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice (remote, BT pairing, FallbackHome), com.tcl.framework.custom
com.tcl.keyhelp com.tcl.partnercustomizer (key handling, TKey activity),
com.tcl.inputmethod.international com.tcl.settings com.tcl.initsetup com.tcl.factory.view
(never even opened - the name alone puts it in PROMPT.md's "never start a factory package"
category) com.tcl.common.terminalmanagerplus com.tcl.xian.StartandroidService
com.tcl.appstatecontroller com.android.ListenNetStateService (unclear roles, boot/package/network
hooks; appstatecontroller is also the suspected watchdog above), com.realtek.netflix.setting
(Netflix ESN/config), com.tcl.assistant com.tcl.micmanager (voice - but see "off by choice" and
"second pass" below for the other voice packages), com.tcl.versionUpdateApp com.tcl.rc.ota
(firmware updates).
Also left alone on the second unit, none of them tested: com.tcl.pvr.pvrplayer (USB/tuner PVR
recording playback), com.tcl.showmode (Dolby/DTS/night-mode sound settings, despite the name -
not just a retail demo), com.tcl.UpdatePeripheral (remote firmware update receiver),
com.tcl.android.webview (TCL's own WebView build; some kept apps may render through it),
com.google.android.sss.authbridge and com.tcl.systemuioverlay (both gave dumpsys almost nothing
to go on).

mau.header:
TCL "Smart TV Pro", UK Freeview Play build (device BeyondTV4, product BeyondTV6, board Realtek rtd288o), 2 GB RAM
Android TV 11 (SDK 30), 32-bit userspace, build RP1A.200622.001 / incremental AR05, security patch 2022-04-05.
Fingerprint TCL/BeyondTV6/BeyondTV4:11/RP1A.200622.001/AR05:user/release-keys.

Same platform as examples/tcl-50c725k (BeyondTV4 / BeyondTV6 / rtd288o, 2 GB, RP1A.200622.001) but a different
firmware and preload set: that unit runs AR10, this one AR05 with the UK Freeview Play apps (all 16
uk.co.freeview.* packages and tv.wuaki.apptv already disabled at the factory). Do not apply one list to the
other. In particular this build's com.tcl.gallery, com.tcl.imageplayer, com.tcl.audioplayer,
com.tcl.videoplayer, com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter and com.tcl.t_solo all request
android.permission.TV_INPUT_HARDWARE - they are the software layer under HDMI/AV - so disabling one can leave
that port showing "No Signal" until a full restore and a cold boot (#321). tcl-50c725k disables
com.tcl.gallery; on this firmware that is not safe by the permission scan, and it was left alone.

Notes on this firmware (the TV_INPUT_HARDWARE set, the boot re-enable, the katniss revoke):

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv.
Keep: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.dashboard, com.tcl.suspension, com.tcl.autopair,
com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.useragreement,
com.tcl.globalkeyoverlay, com.tcl.systemui.plugin, com.tcl.factory.view, com.tcl.inputmethod.international
(the keyboard), com.tcl.eva, com.tcl.hearaid (sound/accessibility + TCL wireless speakers),
com.tcl.t_solo, tv.mopa.ginga (broadcast middleware) and all com.mediatek.* except AirPlay.
Firmware updates arrive through Google Play Services (no separate TCL updater on this set).
Also keep com.google.android.tv.remote.service: despite the name ("phone-app remote") it holds
AtvSearchAssistantService, which carries the Bluetooth remote's mic button. Disabled, the mic did nothing.
Keep com.tcl.suspension too: it IS the source panel the remote's Input button opens.

Applied and verified on a real unit on 2026-10-20: Wi-Fi, HDMI switching (Inputs menu), Assistant,
Disney+/Netflix playback with AdGuard Private DNS, and the launcher's clock screensaver all worked.

Second unit, UAE, same firmware (UTT2.250416.001 AU02, G08_4K_GB), applied in one session on 2026-10-27:
the same list, except AirPlay, Miracast, T-Cast and the game bar were kept, and Netflix, Prime Video and
YouTube were disabled too (owner's choice; Stan was not installed). All 33 packages stayed disabled
across two reboots, and power-on lands on the launcher, not Live TV. HDMI switching from the Inputs menu,
the Input button's source panel, the mic, and SmartTube playback with AdGuard Private DNS worked.
- setupwraith owned a saved Wi-Fi network that was out of range, so TV Settings never listed it to
forget; the TV was on a different network saved from Settings. `cmd wifi forget-network <id>` on the
setupwraith-owned ID (`cmd wifi list-networks`, `dumpsys wifi | grep cname=`) cleared it, and
tools/disable.sh then disabled setupwraith with Wi-Fi unaffected.
- This remote's YouTube button is KEYCODE_BUTTON_3 (190, scancode 240, usage 0x000c0057), not 4065;
with launcherx disabled it goes to launcherx's GlobalKeyListener_Receiver and does nothing. The gear
button worked with settings_key_keycodes 83 + 4077 and HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1.
- Key helpers cost the volume ramp on this Android 14 firmware too (docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md):
with HomeKeyService and InputKeyService bound, a held Volume Up moves one step; with the list empty and
accessibility_enabled 0 it ramps. The owner kept the ramp and no helpers.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The remote (BT_RC833_A1) sends KEYCODE_TV_INPUT for Input, and TCL's input policy hands it to
com.tcl.suspension before accessibility services see it, so INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 can't redirect it.
The Input button keeps opening TCL's source panel; the launcher's Inputs pill opens the glass menu.
- With com.tcl.interactive disabled, com.tcl.tv logs "tias_sdk getService failure" ~10x/s for a few
seconds when the TV player starts, then stops. CPU on HDMI measured the same (~23%) with it on or off.
- Disabling dreamx: set screensaver_components to com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream first.

Connection: USB debugging alone opens port 5555 on Ethernet. Wireless debugging switches itself back off

TCL Smart TV Pro (device BeyondTV4, product G03_4K_GB, Realtek rtd288o / R51MT05, software
V8-R51MT05-LF1V620), Google TV on Android 11 (SDK 30), build RP1A.200622.001 AR09, security patch
2024-03-05, 32-bit userspace (armeabi-v7a), client TCL-ME-RTD51M-S1 (Middle East firmware).
Fingerprint: TCL/G03_4K_GB/BeyondTV4:11/RP1A.200622.001/AR09:user/release-keys
Same R51MT05 platform as examples/tcl-43c645 (LF1V652); that list was the starting point.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-g03-google-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g03-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Tested 2026-10-20 on a real unit, applied in the seven batches below with a screenshot after each, then a
reboot: Wi-Fi stayed up, Settings, the remote's Input key (TCL's source panel), Live TV and HDMI from the
launcher's Inputs menu, app launches and playback with AdGuard Private DNS all worked, and every package
stayed disabled after the reboot. Lived with for one day so far. launcher/ installed with the default
build-and-install.sh (b64push.py md5 matched here, unlike the 43C645).

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI: com.tcl.tv (TVActivity) with inputs from
com.tcl.tvinput (tuner, HDMI 1-3, AV). The launcher's default live_tv_package is MediaTek's, so the Inputs menu
has no Live TV row until a theme sets "live_tv_package": "com.tcl.tv". config.json in this folder sets it,
the gear button and the app buttons described under "Second unit" below; push it with:
TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/theme.sh examples/tcl-g03-google-tv
Already disabled at the factory: au.com.stan.and (Stan), tv.wuaki.apptv (Rakuten TV); the second unit below
also had com.tcl.smartalexa off at the factory.

Before batch 6 (setupwraith): on this unit the Wi-Fi saved during first setup belonged to setupwraith
(`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`), so disabling it would have deleted the network. Forgetting the
network and joining it again in Settings moved it to com.android.tv.settings; then disabling setupwraith kept
Wi-Fi. tools/disable.sh skips setupwraith while it owns the network.

Remote (Bluetooth "TCL_RC902V_MM", Generic.kl):
- Input keeps opening TCL's source panel (com.tcl.suspension) without launcherx; no InputKeyService needed.
- Gear is scancode 233 (KEY_FORWARDMAIL, HID 0x0c0055), mapped to TCL_SET, keycode 4077. Only launcherx
answered it, so it does nothing once launcherx is off. HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 at install plus
"settings_key_keycodes": [4077] in the theme brings it back (verified with the real remote); with
"settings_key_panel": true it opens the launcher's quick settings panel over any app.
- `input keyevent SETTINGS` opens Android's version easter egg here; inject 176 instead.

Second unit, 2026-10-21, same AR09 build, applied in the batches below with a screenshot after each and then
rebooted with launcherx off: the list minus Netflix and Prime Video, minus the factory-off smartalexa, plus
launcherx (38 packages) stayed disabled, and HDMI, Netflix playback, the remote and Wi-Fi all worked.
AdGuard's Private DNS (private_dns_mode hostname) changed nothing for playback. Two things differ:
- Its Bluetooth remote is "TCL_RC902V_M1" (also /dev/input/event3, Generic.kl), not the "TCL_RC902V_MM" above.
Netflix (HID 0x0c0051, TCL_NETFLIX), YouTube (0x0c0057, TCL_YOUTUBE) and Prime Video (0x0c005f, keycode
4099) are broadcasts only launcherx answers, so all three do nothing once it is off. `getevent -lt` prints
the HID usage and the Linux key under each button, which is how the two remotes are told apart.
- HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with the app_keys in config.json brings all three back (verified with the real remote;
a button whose app you disabled still opens nothing). Gear is keycode 4077 on this remote too, so
settings_key_keycodes and settings_key_panel above apply unchanged.
setupwraith owned the Wi-Fi on this unit as well, and this order worked: forget and re-join the network,
disable setupwraith while launcherx still owns Home, run launcher/build-and-install.sh, switch the
screensaver, then disable dreamx. Home landed on the new launcher straight away (mFocusedApp checked), with
no RecoveryActivity in between.

US firmware unit, 2026-10-25: TCL Smart TV Pro G03_4K_US (BeyondTV4, Realtek rtd288o / R51MT05,
software V8-R51MT05-LF1V813), Google TV 11, build RP1A.200622.001 GTV93, security patch 2023-10-05, client
TCL-NA-RTD51M-S1. The packages of groups 1-3 still enabled on this unit were disabled one per shell call, then
rebooted: Wi-Fi and internet stayed up, Settings opened and every package stayed disabled. Lived with for a few
days. This unit kept launcherx and setupwraith (setupwraith owned the Wi-Fi here too), so group 6 and the
launcherx line were not applied. Found on this unit:
- com.tcl.xian.StartandroidService is also how TCL's updater gets the device number (dnum). With it disabled,
Settings > About > Software Update > Network Update fails with "Local network or server abnormal, please check
the network and try again" while the network is fine (logcat: "dnum is null!"). If you turned it off, to check for an update enable it,
reboot once, run the check, then disable it again (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md).
- com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx is more than the promo screensaver: it also hosts Google TV's Google Home panel
(SmartHomeMainActivity: lights and other devices in the quick settings). Disabling it removes that panel. It also
loads the panel's account through com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx, so with launcherx off the panel opens and
closes at once: if the household uses Google Home lights, keep launcherx enabled as well and hand Home to the new
launcher with stock_home_redirect (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, #1653).
- Apps only mode (Settings > Accounts & Sign In > account) also hides the Google Home panel on this firmware.

TCL 50C641, EU firmware unit, 2026-10-28: Smart TV Pro G03_4K_GB (BeyondTV4, Realtek rtd288o / R51MT05,
software V8-R51MT05-LF1V652, client TCL-EU-RTD51M-S1), Google TV 11, build RP1A.200622.001 AR11, security patch
2024-12-05. Groups 1-3, part of 4 (YouTube Music, Google TV, USB media player, gallery, game bar, TCL Live) and
part of 5 (katniss, tv.assistant, com.tcl.assistant, micmanager, miracast) were disabled one per shell call in
five batches with a screenshot after each, then group 6 after the Wi-Fi re-join (setupwraith owned it here too),
then launcherx via build-and-install.sh, then dreamx; rebooted twice. Every package stayed disabled, Home came
up on the new launcher with no RecoveryActivity, Wi-Fi stayed up, the tuner, AV and HDMI 1-4 still enumerated
in `dumpsys tv_input` and Live TV opened from the launcher's Inputs menu. Tested the same day, not yet lived with
for days. Differences on this unit:
- com.tcl.partnercustomizer was left enabled: besides its promo receivers it holds TKey activities (TCL's remote
shortcut key), and nothing on this unit showed whether the remote needs them.
- android.autoinstalls.config.google.gtvpai was skipped by tools/disable.sh (no permission block in dumpsys).
- com.tcl.gallery and com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter do not request TV_INPUT_HARDWARE on AR11 (only com.tcl.tv does), and
HDMI kept working with both off.
- dreamx was re-enabled afterwards by the owner: Google Photos ambient mode (Settings > System > Ambient mode)
loaded the account and the album with launcherx still disabled, unlike the Google Home panel above.
- The remote is infrared, read as /dev/input/event0 with Generic.kl (no Bluetooth remote in `dumpsys input`).
`getevent -lt` scancodes, decimal: Netflix 758 (0x2f6, in no key layout, so Android sees KEY_UNKNOWN),
YouTube 569 (KEY_YOUTUBE), Prime Video 752 (KEY_PRIMEVIDEO), BrowseHere/Web 651, TCL Home 204 (KEY_DASHBOARD),
TCL Channel 456 (KEY_QUICK_MENU, opens a TCL "coming soon" page with com.tcl.channelplus off). With launcherx off
none of the app buttons did anything; HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with "scan:758:com.netflix.ninja",
"scan:569:com.google.android.youtube.tv", "scan:752:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom",
"scan:651:com.tcl.browser" and "scan:456:ignore" in app_keys brought them back (verified with the real remote).
These are not in this folder's config.json, whose keycode entries are for the Bluetooth remotes above.
- With HomeKeyService bound, one tap of volume moved two steps (#1100); consume_volume_keys true made it one step,
and a held button kept ramping, a little slower than without the helper.

Latin America firmware unit, 2026-10-28: same G03_4K_GB / AR09 / V8-R51MT05-LF1V620 build, client
TCL-LA-RTD51M-S1, security patch 2024-03-05. Applied groups 1-3, group 4 minus Netflix, Prime Video and
com.google.android.videos, group 5 minus voice (katniss, tv.assistant, tcl.assistant, smartalexa, micmanager) and
Chromecast, then groups 6 and 7 and launcherx, in batches with a screenshot after each and three reboots: every
package stayed disabled, Wi-Fi stayed up, the TV powered on to the new Home (FallbackHome, then the launcher; no
Live TV, no RecoveryActivity), and HDMI 1 opened from the launcher's Inputs menu. One day so far.
- tools/disable.sh skipped android.autoinstalls.config.google.gtvpai in group 2: its dumpsys has no permission
block. After a reboot with all five com.tcl.tvinput inputs still listed it was disabled with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1
(the package is a stub with one DummyReceiver).
- setupwraith owned an older saved network, not the one in use. Forgetting that one let disable.sh through.
- Remote: Bluetooth "TCL_RC902V_M2", with the same HID usages as the M1 above: Netflix 0x0c0051, YouTube
0x0c0057, Prime Video 0x0c005f, gear 0x0c0055 (keycode 4077), Home 0x0c0223. Input is 0x0c0049 (KEY_GAMES,
keycode 178) and opens com.tcl.suspension's source panel with no helper. HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with the app_keys
and settings_key_keycodes of config.json brought back the gear and the three app buttons (real remote).
- With HomeKeyService bound, a held Volume Up stepped once per press instead of ramping, the trade described in
docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md. "consume_volume_keys": true (config.xml or a theme) brought the
ramp back with one step per tap, checked on the real remote, and the helper rebound by itself after a reboot.
It is not in this folder's config.json because the other two units were not measured.
- Voice stayed on with launcherx disabled. The first mic press afterwards answered that the Assistant had trouble
processing; later presses, and presses after a reboot, worked.

TCL 50S546, 2026-10-29: same G03_4K_GB / AR09 / V8-R51MT05-LF1V620 build, client TCL-CA-RTD51M-S1, security
patch 2024-03-05. Applied groups 1-3, group 4 minus Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube Music and the USB player, group 5
minus voice (katniss, tv.assistant, tcl.assistant, micmanager) and Chromecast, then groups 6 and 7 and launcherx, in
batches with a screenshot after each; rebooted twice. Every package stayed disabled, the TV booted to the new Home
(FallbackHome, then the launcher; no RecoveryActivity), Wi-Fi stayed up, and HDMI 1-4, AV and the tuner stayed in
`dumpsys tv_input`. Tested the same day, not yet lived with for days. Differences on this unit:
- com.tcl.gallery, com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter and com.tcl.t_solo all show TV_INPUT_HARDWARE granted in dumpsys on this
AR09 unit (unlike the AR11 50C641 above), so gallery and the USB player were left enabled; tools/disable.sh
would skip them anyway.
- setupwraith did not own the Wi-Fi (android.uid.system and com.android.tv.settings did), so it was disabled
without a re-join.
- gtvpai was skipped by tools/disable.sh (no permission block), then disabled with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 after a reboot

- Remote: Bluetooth "TCL_RC902N_M1" (Generic.kl), same HID usages as the M1/M2 above: Netflix 0x0c0051, YouTube
0x0c0057, Prime Video 0x0c005f, gear 0x0c0055. All four did nothing with launcherx off; HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with

TCL 43P739, Italy, 2026-10-31: Smart TV Pro G03_4K_GB (BeyondTV4, Realtek rtd288o / RTD2851M, software
V8-R51MT05-LF1V652, client TCL-EU-RTD51M-S1), Google TV 11, build RP1A.200622.001 AR11, security patch 2024-12-05:
the same build as the 50C641 above. A subset of this list was applied in three batches with a screenshot after
each: TCL analytics, tracking and promo (overseasappshow, bi, guard, tclhome_passive, waterfall.overseas,
messagebox, esticker, channelplus, smartalexa, t_solo, keyhelp), Google telemetry and unused media apps

- setupwraith owned a hidden saved network that was not in use, while the network in use belonged to
com.android.tv.settings after a forget and re-join. disable.sh still skipped it; FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 let it

five did nothing with launcherx off. HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with "scan:242:com.netflix.ninja",
"scan:245:com.google.android.youtube.tv", "scan:752:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom" and "scan:365:com.tcl.tv"

TCL 65P735, Kuwait, 2026-10-20, status 2026-10-28 (eight days, nothing re-enabled): sold as "Smart TV Pro",
G03_4K_GB / BeyondTV4, Realtek rtd288o / R51MT05, software V8-R51MT05-LF1V652, client TCL-ME-RTD51M-S1 (Middle East),
Google TV 11, build RP1A.200622.001 AR11, security patch 2024-12-05, 32-bit userspace (zygote32, armeabi-v7a only), 2 GB
RAM, wired Ethernet, ro.adb.secure=1. Applied in five batches with a screenshot, a network check and a Home check after
each, then rebooted: launcherx and setupwraith stayed disabled. Wi-Fi was not at risk: the saved network belonged to
android.uid.system (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`) and the TV was on Ethernet. launcher/build-and-install.sh with
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 STOCK_LAUNCHER=none installed the launcher; AdGuard Private DNS changed nothing for
playback. Found on this unit:
- Besides the packages above it also had these off: com.tcl.ttvs (TCL BI/awareness/identifier services and T-Cast),
com.tcl.hearaid, com.tcl.magiconnectfree (TCL phone sharing), com.google.android.apps.nbu.smartconnect.tv,
com.tcl.t_solo (Bluetooth "Listen alone") and TalkBack (all six are commented out in the list below: the shared list
leaves them on). The firmware updater was also turned off here by choice
(not listed: keep it enabled unless you want updates frozen).
- Remote buttons only launcherx answered die with it. Keycodes (logcat -s TclPhoneWindowManager, checked with the real
remote): Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065, Prime Video 4099, the old TCL Guard button 4140, Settings gear 4077 (a gear mapped to
83 did nothing here). app_keys and settings_key_keycodes in config.xml or a theme bring them back. After a reinstall the
two helpers are enabled but not bound until they are switched off and on again.
- Game Master (TCL's game mode: ALLM, low lag) survives Home, input changes and power cycles, and the TV shows a "Game
Master : On/Off" banner at every input start. It is turned off only when the Options bar (or the Picture or Sound page)
opens while the current source is not the console: the log says "game console isn't plugged in, turn off game master".
It is not a setting (`settings put` does nothing; com.tcl.tvmanager's setSpecialModeEnable is ignored for an ordinary app).
- No VRR and no 120 Hz: the P735 board configs under /vendor/hardware use 60 Hz panel files, the SoC is HDMI 2.0, and the
TV logs "not support free sync". A PS5 negotiates 3840x2160@60Hz HDR10.
- A VPN app (WireGuard) was killed in the background on the stock firmware. Two suspects, not isolated: com.tcl.guard (TCL's
memory cleaner, disabled here) and TCL's APP_AUTO_START app-op, "ignore" for it (cmd appops set <package> APP_AUTO_START
allow). Both were changed, then it kept running.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it; set another one before (see group 7).

DO NOT DISABLE: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput (Live TV, tuner, HDMI/AV), com.tcl.suspension (Quick panel and the
Input key's source panel), com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.system.server, com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup,
com.tcl.factory.view, com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service, com.tcl.autopair (remote), com.tcl.inputmethod.international
(keyboard), com.google.android.tv.remote.service. Left alone as unclear or small gain: com.tcl.keyhelp (remote
virtual keys on the G05), com.tcl.useragreement, com.tcl.hearaid, com.tcl.t_solo,
com.google.android.apps.nbu.smartconnect.tv (Google data saver / VPN client).
