mau.header:
TCL Smart TV Pro, US (device G05, product G05_4K_US, board C05, MediaTek MT5889 / MT9615)
Android 11 (Google TV), firmware AR2101, software AR68 (built March 2024) and AR71, 2.7 GB RAM
Also sold as the TCL 55Q750G (AR71, on Wi-Fi), where both halves work: debloat and the launcher as Home.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-g05-google-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g05-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it to restore.sh, the default is wrong here).
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv (.TVActivity; keep it, it also owns HDMI/antenna playback, HDMI through
com.tcl.tvinput's passthrough input). Keep com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.system.server,
com.tcl.keyhelp, com.tcl.autopair, com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service (remote) and com.tcl.providers.config.
Unlike the G10, com.tcl.ttvs ships enabled here. It carries TCL's BI analytics and Samba TV ACR, and on AR71
also the TCL firmware updater (versionUpdateApp ... SystemUpdateActivity): comment it out to keep updates.
The firmware re-enables com.tcl.usercenter and com.tcl.smartalexa at every boot (55Q750G, two reboots);
everything else in the list stayed disabled.

Known quirk, read before replacing the launcher. Whether disabling setupwraith sticks goes by the
incremental build (ro.build.version.incremental), not by the model; all reports share the AR2101 build ID:
- AR68 (US, the unit this list came from): this US build is the exception. With launcherx disabled,
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1 and Home lands on a
black, looping recovery screen. Shell cannot disable that component. Disabling the whole setupwraith
package worked until a reboot, after which this TV had it back in charge, unlike the MOOR2, QM6K and
Chromecast reports where the disable survives. launcher/build-and-install.sh refuses and rolls back
while Home resolves to setupwraith (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "The new launcher still doesn't own Home").
Recover with: pm enable com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx; pm enable com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
- AR71 (US, a TCL 55Q750G, 21 October 2026): the first run of build-and-install.sh on G05 firmware.
setupwraith stayed disabled across a reboot and Home stayed with the new launcher (mFocusedApp =
com.gathin.tvhome). Order: setupwraith first, while launcherx still owns Home, then build-and-install.sh,
which starts the new launcher and only then disables launcherx. On Wi-Fi, run
`tools/tv.py "dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'"` first: the network saved during first setup belonged
to setupwraith, so disable.sh skips it. Forget the network and join it again in Settings, typing the
password, until `cmd wifi list-networks` shows a new network ID (the first forget there did not take); it
then belongs to com.android.tv.settings and Wi-Fi survives the disable. Input, Settings, Netflix, YouTube,
Prime Video and the mic all worked with launcherx off and com.tcl.suspension kept, without
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE or HOME_KEY_SERVICE.
- The G05_4K_GB units (tcl-65c735, and docs/devices/tcl-55c728-g05-4k-gb.md on AR28) kept setupwraith off
across a reboot too. The 55C728 report installed its own launcher, not with build-and-install.sh.
Compare ro.build.version.incremental before promising either outcome.
Contributed by damonearl (PR #73); AR71 findings from a 55Q750G.

half done too. Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. HOME claimants on stock: launcherx,
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity and com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome.
Live TV / HDMI: com.tcl.tv + com.tcl.tvinput (four HDMI ports registered, AV, tuner).

KEEP (left enabled and working on this unit):
- com.tcl.tv com.tcl.tvinput: Live TV, HDMI and the source picker; com.tcl.tv also answers the guide button.
- com.tcl.suspension (Input key / Quick Panel), com.tcl.system.server, com.tcl.keyhelp (remote keys),
com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service, com.tcl.autopair (Bluetooth remote), com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.providers.config,
com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.factory.view (never launch it), com.tcl.common.shortcutmenu (not tried).
- com.tcl.ttvs: firmware updater on AR2101 (it also logs remote key presses); kept by the owner.
- Kept by the owner's choice: Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), the voice assistant
(com.google.android.katniss, com.google.android.tv.assistant, com.tcl.micmanager and
com.google.android.tv.remote.service), Prime Video, YouTube, YouTube Music, the USB media player.
- No com.mediatek.tv.service on this build, so the #2138 reason for keeping com.tcl.partnercustomizer
does not apply here; it is disabled below, as on the Indonesia unit.

Notes from this unit (one session on 2026-10-31, verified with screenshots; one day, shorter than
CONTRIBUTING.md asks):
- No Wireless debugging on this firmware: USB debugging alone opens port 5555 over Wi-Fi. The TV asks to
allow the computer's key once.
- The saved Wi-Fi belonged to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi showed four entries with
cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith). The owner forgot the network and joined it again in Settings
(owner became com.android.tv.settings); setupwraith was then disabled with Wi-Fi and ADB staying up.
- Casting from a phone still worked after a reboot with setupwraith disabled.
- Wait about a minute after the last batch before rebooting, as on the other AR2101 lists.
- com.tcl.smartalexa and com.tcl.usercenter are switched back on at every boot (as on the 40S5400A and
32ES570F); both stay idle, so they are commented out below rather than disabled again at each boot.
- Launcher: launcher/ became Home (mFocusedApp = com.gathin.tvhome after Home and after a reboot). The
YouTube and Prime Video buttons are broadcasts only launcherx answers (as on examples/tcl-g03-google-tv), so
launcherx is enabled again behind "stock_home_redirect" with "key_filter": false; see README.md.
- Reboot-checked twice: everything listed stays disabled, Home and the helper survive, Wi-Fi stays connected.

mau.ten: TCL Smart TV (reports as "Smart TV"; device G07, product G07_4K_GB_NF, Realtek RTD2851A), Google TV on
mau.header:
TCL Smart TV (reports as "Smart TV"; device G07, product G07_4K_GB_NF, Realtek RTD2851A), Google TV on
Android 11 (SDK 30), build RP1A.200622.001 AR20, security patch 2025-12-05, 2 GB RAM. Same package family
as the G05 (Quick Panel, waterfall, ttvs, TCL Live) plus the 43C645 extras (useragreement, TCL webview,
tclhome_passive).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-g07-google-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g07-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Tested 2026-10-20 on a real unit, applied in six batches with screenshots between them: Wi-Fi, Home, the Input
key's source panel, Netflix, YouTube, Live TV and HDMI (from the launcher's Inputs menu) all kept working, and
setupwraith, launcherx and dreamx stayed disabled after a reboot (unlike the G05). Launcher works.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx; setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1
once it is gone. The Wi-Fi saved at setup belonged to android.uid.system, not setupwraith, so disabling
setupwraith kept the network.

Also tested 2026-10-19 on a second unit, UK firmware used in Brazil, build RP1A.200622.001 AR17, with the
launcher as Home and through a reboot. Two things differ from AR20 there:
- The Wi-Fi saved during first setup belonged to setupwraith, so disabling it made Android delete the
network and the TV dropped off Wi-Fi (and ADB). Pick the network again in Settings > Network; Settings
then owns it and it survives reboots. tools/disable.sh now checks the owner first and skips setupwraith
while it owns the network.
- The adb shell may not write Android/data, so tools/theme.sh has to go through the launcher's
ThemeProvider (it falls back to it on its own when the plain copy is refused).
TvInputManager reports AV as connected with nothing plugged in. com.tcl.notereminder was enabled on that
unit, not disabled at the factory, so it is listed below.

Also tested 2026-10-20/21 on a third unit in Brazil (product G07_4K_GB_NF, client TCL-LA-RTD51A-S1,
software V8-R51AT01-LF1V126, incremental AR07, fingerprint TCL/G07_4K_GB_NF/G07:11/RP1A.200622.001/AR17,
security patch 2024-12-05; Discussion #729):
- Stage 1 disabled 9 packages in two conservative batches (waterfall.overseas, esticker, notereminder,
feedback, guard, then dashboard, partnercustomizer, messagebox, tv.tclhome_passive) while keeping the
stock launcherx as Home. Stage 2 disabled 25 more packages, installed the reference launcher
(INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1) with the ClockDream screensaver, and disabled launcherx,
setupwraith (saved Wi-Fi belonged to android.uid.system, uid 1000) and dreamx.
- Kept by choice on that unit: com.tcl.ttvs (firmware updates), voice (com.google.android.katniss,
com.tcl.assistant, com.google.android.tv.assistant), Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell)
and com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic. Physical HDMI/AV playback, OTA update arrival and live
tools/restore.sh rollback were not exercised in that session.
- Only au.com.stan.and and tv.wuaki.apptv came disabled at the factory (com.tcl.smartalexa and
com.iqiyi.i18n.tv were not installed); com.google.android.videos and com.tcl.notereminder shipped
enabled.
- Reboot check (tools/check.py): launcherx, setupwraith, dreamx and the other disabled packages stayed
disabled across a reboot, but AR07 firmware automatically re-enabled com.tcl.notereminder and
com.tcl.usercenter at boot. Adding both to hidden_apps in launcher/app/src/main/res/values/config.xml
hides them from the app grid without fighting the firmware on every boot.

Remote (IR, /dev/input/event0 "mtkinp"; scancodes from getevent with the real remote):
- Input (471, TV_INPUT) goes to TclPhoneWindowManager.startQuickPanelService, so it keeps working without
launcherx and needs no InputKeyService.
- Gear (561, TCL_SET) became launcherx's quick settings panel, so it does nothing once launcherx is off.
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 with settings_key_scancodes 561 in config.xml brings it back.
- Netflix (566, TCL_NETFLIX) and YouTube (569, TCL_YOUTUBE) are broadcasts that only launcherx answers, so
they do nothing once it is off. An accessibility service that matches those scancodes and starts the app
fixes both (verified with the real remote).
Remote (Bluetooth, second AR20 unit, France; /dev/input/event3, vendor 0x0417 product 0x0304, Generic.kl):
- Its buttons send other codes, and settings_key_scancodes 561 does nothing for them. Gear is KEY_FORWARDMAIL
(233, TCL_SET) and arrives as keycode 4077; Prime Video is HID usage 0x000c005f and arrives as keycode 4099.
`getevent -lt` while pressing a button tells the two remotes apart (event0 mtkinp or event3).
- With HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, this config.xml brought back Gear, Netflix, YouTube and Prime Video (verified with
the real remote): settings_key_keycodes 4077, and app_keys KEYCODE_TCL_NETFLIX:com.netflix.ninja,
KEYCODE_TCL_YOUTUBE:com.google.android.youtube.tv, 4099:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom.
tools/b64push.py worked here (md5 match). Screenshots of Live TV and HDMI are 0 bytes; Netflix's are black.

Also tested 2026-10-20 to 10-24 on a fourth unit in Brazil, same software as the third (V8-R51AT01-LF1V126,
incremental AR07, patch 2024-12-05), Bluetooth remote "TCL_RC902V_MG" on event3; launcher as Home through
reboots and four days of use:
- Gear sent KEY_FORWARDMAIL (233) as keycode 4077 here too; settings_key_keycodes 4077 with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1
fixed it (enabled and bound for user 0, then pressed on the real remote). It was SystemUI's
TOGGLE_NOTIFICATION_HANDLER_PANEL, which only launcherx answers.
- Wi-Fi: setupwraith owned one of the five saved networks (an old one, not the network in use) and Android
deleted only that one when setupwraith was disabled. Check the creator of every saved network, not just the
current one: `dumpsys wifi`, then the cname= of each.
- com.tcl.micmanager and com.google.android.apps.nbu.smartconnect.tv were disabled for four days with no effect
noticed (voice was off by choice, so the mic was not used).
- With com.tcl.channelplus off, the "free channels" stay listed with no picture: the Input panel's
"Pressione para Canais gratuitos" row and the TV app's channel list. `pm clear com.tcl.suspension` swaps
the panel's channel row for recent apps. The TV app's list is fetched by com.tcl.tv itself (it runs as
uid 1000) and is not kept in TvProvider, so nothing on the TV removes it short of DNS blocking; the owner
re-enabled channelplus and the channels played at once (streams from amagi.tv).
- ttvs's update screen (Settings > System > About > Software update > Network update > System update) cannot
be started over adb (needs com.tcl.permission.START_CHECK_SYSTEMUPDATE) and blocks screenshots. With ttvs
enabled for the check, V8-R51AT01-LF1V126 was the latest version on 2026-10-20; ttvs was off otherwise.
- Used RAM 150 s after boot: 1294 MB stock, 1004 MB debloated, 1019 MB with the launcher (MemAvailable
683 -> 662 -> 801 MB).

Also tested 2026-10-25 on a fifth unit, a Hitachi CDH-LE554KSMART26 (TCL-built re-badge for Latin America,
client HIT-LA-RTD51A-S1), same software as the third and fourth (V8-R51AT01-LF1V126, incremental AR07),
Bluetooth remote "HI_RC902V_MA" on event2. Tested on one day only, with a reboot; I will report back if
anything breaks.
- Applied in five batches with screenshots; launcher/ installed with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, settings_key_keycodes
4077 and app_keys KEYCODE_TCL_NETFLIX, KEYCODE_TCL_YOUTUBE and 4099 (Prime Video), as on the fourth unit.
With the real remote: Home, Back, Input (source panel), Gear (settings), Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video and
the mic (Assistant) all work, and holding volume up still ramps with the helper on.
- Kept by choice: ttvs (updates), voice, T-Solo, com.tcl.gallery and com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter. Chromecast
(mediashell) was disabled by choice on this unit.
- Already disabled at the factory: com.tcl.dashboard, com.tcl.notereminder, com.tcl.usercenter,
com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV, com.tcl.smartalexa, au.com.stan.and, tv.wuaki.apptv. pm disable-user
answers "Shell cannot change component state" for the first four; that is their factory state, not a refusal.
None of the disabled packages came back after the reboot.
- Wi-Fi: an old saved network belonged to setupwraith (not the one in use), so tools/disable.sh skipped it.
`cmd wifi list-networks` then `cmd wifi forget-network <id>` removed that network over adb, and setupwraith
was disabled with the TV still on Wi-Fi.
- The remote's Guard and Channel buttons open TGuard and TCL Live, so they do nothing once those are off.

DO NOT DISABLE: com.tcl.tv (Live TV, HDMI playback), com.tcl.tvinput (tuner, HDMI and AV inputs),
com.tcl.suspension (Quick Panel, also the Input key's source panel), com.tcl.keyhelp (remote virtual keys),
com.tcl.autopair, com.google.android.tv.remote.service, com.tcl.inputmethod.international (the keyboard),
com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.system.server, com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.factory.view,
com.tvos (framework resources).
Unclear, left enabled: com.tcl.micmanager, com.google.android.apps.nbu.smartconnect.tv.
Kept by choice: Netflix, YouTube, Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell).
Already disabled at the factory: au.com.stan.and, com.google.android.videos, com.tcl.notereminder,
com.tcl.smartalexa, tv.wuaki.apptv.

mau.header:
TCL Smart TV Pro (G08, G08_4K_GB, MediaTek), Australian firmware, Android 12 (Google TV, Basic TV mode)
Model "Smart TV Pro", device G08, fingerprint TCL/G08_4K_GB/G08:12/STT2.221228.001/AS34:user/release-keys,
32-bit userspace (armeabi-v7a), about 2.4 GB RAM.
Same fingerprint as examples/tcl-g08-eu-android12, but the Australian set also ships Stan, AirPlay
(com.tcl.airplay2 + com.mediatek.AirplayAPK), TCL Channel (com.tcl.waterfall.overseas), TCL Live free
channels (com.tcl.channelplus), com.tcl.esticker, com.tcl.hotelmenu and com.tcl.guard, and has no Google
Cast (mediashell) and no voice assistant (katniss). com.tcl.browser, com.tcl.messagebox,
com.tcl.smartalexa and com.google.android.videos from the EU list are not on it.

Tested 22 October 2026 on one set, applied with tools/disable.sh in five batches with screenshots between
them. All 28 packages stayed disabled across a reboot (pm list packages -d compared before and after);
the Source key panel, HDMI 1/2 switching, SmartTube and Plex were checked afterwards (AirPlay and Miracast
sessions were not), and the launcher was installed with launcher/build-and-install.ps1 -HomeKeyService
(HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh on macOS or Linux).

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g08-au-android12/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv.

com.google.android.youtube.tv, au.com.stan.and (the recovery record keeps them disabled on undo).
Left enabled on purpose: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter (USB

is off; hide it with hidden_apps instead), com.tcl.useragreement, tv.mopa.ginga, the keyboards,

the EU list disables the daemon, AirPlay needs it) and screen mirroring (com.tcl.miracast).

no Samba-ACR ttvs build, no AirplayAPK, no hotelmenu/channelplus/e-sticker/TV+/usercenter, no Android 14
ad services. The US list (examples/tcl-g08-us-google-tv) applies only partially here; this list is the
subset that exists on this build, applied by hand with `pm disable-user --user 0`.

HDMI/Live TV and opens the source menu normally.

Ethernet, 25 October 2026, with the Clean Your TV launcher as Home (README). The list below applied unchanged

end, disabled on that set for one day only.

mau.header:
TCL 75" T7 Series 4K 144Hz QLED Google TV (75T7, device G08, model "Smart TV Pro", MediaTek tcl9618 / mt5896), US
Android 14 (Google TV), firmware UTT2.250416.001 AU16, product G08_4K_US. About 2.4 GB RAM.
Same G08 board as examples/tcl-c755-google-tv, tcl-qm6k-google-tv and tcl-85rm7l-google-tv, on the US
firmware build. Those lists were the starting point; this one adds what the US set ships on top (streaming
preloads and a few TCL extras) and the Android 14 ad and privacy services.
Second unit: TCL 55Q77K (55", model "Smart TV Pro", G08_4K_US, client type TCL-NA-MT9653-S1, MediaTek MT9653),
same firmware UTT2.250416.001 AU16, on Ethernet. That owner applied this list on 23 October 2026 except AirPlay,
the TCL browser and the streaming apps, kept by choice, and the set came through a reboot the same day.
README.md has that unit's remote button codes and notes. No package changes from it: a few more it disabled
have one day of use, not a few.

Tested 20-21 October 2026 on one set, 37 packages in all. The first 35 were disabled, the TV was rebooted and
all 35 were still disabled afterwards. The last two (launcherx and setupwraith) were added later for a custom
launcher and the TV has not been rebooted since. That is about one day of use, not weeks. Everything was
disabled by hand with `pm disable-user --user 0` (one call each, in batches of ten or fewer), not with
tools/disable.sh.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-g08-us-google-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g08-us-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv.
Left enabled on purpose: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.suspension (the input menu), com.tcl.autopair,
com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.useragreement,
com.tcl.globalkeyoverlay, com.tcl.systemui.plugin, com.tcl.factory.view, com.tcl.gamebar (the game bar on
this 144 Hz gaming set), com.google.android.katniss (voice), Netflix, YouTube, Play Services and all
com.mediatek.* and com.dolby.* except the AirPlay ones.
Also left enabled, not tried: com.tcl.ttvs (analytics; the C755 list disables it as Samba TV ACR, and on
some TCL sets it is also the firmware updater), com.tcl.partnercustomizer, com.tcl.interactive,
com.tcl.smartlink.core, com.tcl.UpdatePeripheral, com.google.android.partnersetup.

Differences from the C755 list: com.tcl.dashboard, com.tcl.hearaid and com.tcl.t_solo are disabled here
(the C755 list keeps them); everything under "Streaming preloads" is the US set's own.

mau.ten: TCL 55" 4K Google TV, 2023 model year, US (device G10, product G10_4K_US_NF, Realtek RTD2875P)
mau.header:
TCL 55" 4K Google TV, 2023 model year, US (device G10, product G10_4K_US_NF, Realtek RTD2875P)
Android 12 (Google TV, basic mode), firmware STT2.230203.001, software V8-R75PT01-LF1V499
Likely a good starting point for other 2023+ TCL Google TV sets on the Realtek G10 platform.

Also confirmed on a TCL 55P6K (Spain retail name for the same G10 platform), product
G10_4K_GB_NF_32BIT, identical firmware build STT2.230203.001 — this list applies unchanged.
On a 55P6K set to the RU region (same G10_4K_GB_NF_32BIT, STT2.230203.001), with launcherx
off and no key helper bound, the firmware answers the remote's gear (83), TV (4001) and
Input (178) buttons itself through
com.android.server.policy.TclShortCutKeyManager: 83 opens TV Settings, 4001 opens Live TV
(com.tcl.tv) at its EPG, and 178 opens the input switcher (com.tcl.suspension), so app_keys
and settings_key_keycodes are redundant there. The framework's synthetic KEYCODE_GUIDE (172)
for the TV button goes to the disabled launcherx and does nothing. TCL Live
(com.tcl.channelplus) is kept enabled on this 55P6K: with no antenna channels it is Live TV's
only source, and its own Channel Up/Down keys (166/167) change channels only while its
PlayActivity is on screen. On Home or an HDMI input they do nothing, because the RU region
config has Enable_ChannelUpDownSwitchSource=false and the TV does not switch to TCL Live on a
channel key. Some TCL Live channels show "no signal" even with working internet: the streams
are region/content limited. Checked by injecting 83, 172, 4001, 178 and 166/167 over ADB with
no helper bound.

Also tested on a TCL 43P69K, Netherlands (G10_4K_GB_NF_32BIT, Android 12 / SDK 31,
build STT2.230203.001, ro.adb.secure=1). Unlike the original US unit, logkit, Samba TV ACR
and ttvs shipped enabled; all three were disabled and stayed off after a reboot (2026-10-22).
Its TCL Channel package is com.tcl.waterfall.overseas. That unit also disabled TGuard and
MagiConnect, but kept TalkBack and re-enabled dreamx to keep the screensaver menu in Settings.
Comment out TalkBack and dreamx below to match that choice; the unit-specific additions are optional.
Tweakers groups the Netherlands range as "TCL P6K/P69K/P61K":
https://tweakers.net/televisies/tcl/p6k-p69k-p61k_p1739438/vergelijken/
Only the 43P69K unit above was tested here; check the product and build before using this list.

Also used on a TCL C69B (EU, product G10_4K_GB, software V8-R75PT01-LF1V548, same build
STT2.230203.001; tv.plus and smartlink.core are not installed there). That set kept
partnercustomizer, gamebar and tv.remote.service by choice, so those three are untested on it;
everything else on the list was disabled and lived with. Its BT_RC833 remote sends
YouTube 4065, Netflix 4062, Prime Video 4099 and Web 4159, which only app_keys brings back once
launcherx is off, and the gear as keycode 83 on scancode 233 (settings_key_keycodes).

Unit: TCL 55C69B, France (@danny-gca), product G10_4K_GB, software V8-R75PT01-LF1V548, build STT2.230203.001,
checked across a reboot. Forget and re-join the Wi-Fi in Settings before disabling setupwraith (it owns the setup
network). Its BT_RC833 remote sends Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065, Prime Video 4099 and Settings 83. TclAppBoot needs
APP_AUTO_START for the launcher's key services. Keep com.tcl.ttvs and com.tcl.tv. That unit also disabled
partnercustomizer, gamebar, Assistant and its French streaming apps (commented at the end of this list).

Also used on a TCL 55Q651G (US Q6, 2024; product G10_4K_US_NF, software V8-R75PT01-LF1V534, same
build STT2.230203.001). As on the 43P69K, Samba TV ACR and logkit shipped enabled; both were
disabled, along with the optional 55Q651G lines below. Kept by choice: ttvs (firmware updates),
partnercustomizer (the remote's YouTube button goes through it, as
googletvcustomer://com.tcl.partnercustomizer/startapp?packagename=com.google.android.youtube.tv),
dreamx, AirPlay and ui_mediaCenter (USB media). Re-enabled: com.tcl.channelplus and
com.google.android.tv.remote.service (see quirks). With launcherx kept for the remote's app and gear
buttons, key_filter false and stock_home_redirect set to launcherx, a held volume key over an HDMI
eARC soundbar (CEC) still ramps: 34 steps in about 6 s, as before any change. A cold boot stayed on
Google TV's home until the boot probe change in #1546.

Also used on a TCL 55Q6CS, India (product G10_4K_GB, software V8-R75PT01-LF1V534, same build
STT2.230203.001, Realtek rtd6748). Tested on 2026-10-28 for one day with one reboot check, not yet lived with
for several days. As on the 43P69K, Samba TV ACR, logkit and ttvs shipped enabled; they were disabled and stayed
off after the reboot, as did everything else applied. tv.plus and smartlink.core are not installed. That unit
kept tv.remote.service (the mic works), dreamx (screensaver switched to the launcher's ClockDream), AirPlay,
Miracast and MagiConnect, and also disabled the India-firmware extras in the optional section below.
The saved setup Wi-Fi belonged to setupwraith there too: forgotten and re-joined in Settings first.
Its remote sends the same app keycodes as the C69B (Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065, Prime Video 4099, Web 4159,
gear 83 on scancode 233), plus Input as 4514 (scancode 139; input_key_keycodes) and Dashboard as 4001
(scancode 365; app_keys "4001:settings"), all dead once launcherx is off. With INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 and
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 all of them worked from the real remote, but held volume then stepped once per press, as in
docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md; the owner kept the buttons. APP_AUTO_START (below) held across the
reboot. disable.sh skips android.autoinstalls.config.google.gtvpai there (no permission block to read for its
input check); it was disabled by hand there, but HDMI playback was not checked afterwards, so leave it enabled
unless you test your inputs.

Also used on a TCL 55C6KS, Italy (product G10_4K_GB, software V8-R75PT01-LF1V548, same build STT2.230203.001,
incremental AS50). Tested on 2026-10-30 for one day with two reboot checks, not yet lived with for several days.
As on the 43P69K, Samba TV ACR, logkit and ttvs shipped enabled; Samba TV ACR and logkit were disabled, ttvs kept
(firmware updates). Its TCL Channel package is com.tcl.waterfall.overseas, as on the 43P69K; tv.plus and
smartlink.core are not installed. Disabled from the optional lines: guard, messagebox, waterfall.overseas,
usercenter, t_solo, smartalexa, browser, play.games, videos and youtube.tvmusic. Kept by the owner's choice:
tv.remote.service (the mic works), dreamx, ui_mediaCenter, AirPlay, Miracast, MagiConnect, hearaid and
gtvpai (left enabled, as advised above). Everything disabled stayed off after both reboots.
The saved setup Wi-Fi belonged to setupwraith here too: forgotten and re-joined in Settings first, after which
disabling setupwraith kept Wi-Fi. Its remote sends the C69B and 55Q6CS codes (Netflix 4062, YouTube 4065,
Prime Video 4099, gear 83 on scancode 233); its TV button is 4001 (scancode 365), followed by a KEYCODE_GUIDE
with no scancode. All are dead once launcherx is off; with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1, HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, app_keys
(4001 mapped to com.tcl.tv) and settings_key_keycodes 83, each one worked from the real remote, and both
helpers stayed bound after a reboot. The owner accepted the held-volume trade (see the 55Q6CS note) without
it being measured here. Power-on lands on the new Home by itself (no power_on_home needed).
AdGuard Private DNS worked there.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-g10-google-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-g10-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it to restore.sh, the default is wrong here).
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv (keep it, it also owns HDMI/antenna playback). Keep com.tcl.tvinput,
com.tcl.dashboard, com.tcl.suspension, com.tcl.autopair and com.tcl.systemserver too.
Already disabled at the factory on the original US unit: com.tcl.logkit, tv.samba.ssm.ui
(Samba TV ACR), com.tcl.ttvs. These shipped enabled on the Netherlands 43P69K and the US 55Q651G
(see optional lines).

Known quirks on this firmware:
- The red "TV" tile disappears from the Google TV Home row after this list (probably
com.tcl.partnercustomizer). TV stays in the Apps row and behind the Inputs tile.
- Disabling dreamx leaves screensaver_components pointing at it. Switch to the AOSP fallback with
tools/tv.py 'settings put secure screensaver_components com.android.dreams.basic/.Colors'
On the 43P69K it also removes the screensaver menu from Settings. dreamx was re-enabled there;
leave its line commented out if you need that menu, even when using a third-party screensaver or the add-on photo-screensaver.
- screencap writes an empty file while Live TV/HDMI is on screen. Press Home first.
- The Google TV promo banner is drawn by launcherx itself, so only launcher/ removes it.
- Disabling the stock launcher alone is not enough to install a replacement:
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (the setup wizard) also claims Home at a lower
priority and takes over once launcherx is disabled. Disable it too before setting the new
launcher as Home — launcher/build-and-install.sh does this automatically and rolls back if
Home doesn't land on the new launcher. List it in your own debloat file so restore.sh brings
it back. Confirmed on two separate 55P6K units.
- On the 43P69K, the saved setup Wi-Fi belonged to setupwraith (dumpsys wifi: cname=...setupwraith).
Forget and re-join it in Settings BEFORE disabling setupwraith, so the network belongs to Settings;
otherwise disabling its owner drops Wi-Fi and the ADB connection.
- TclAppBoot blocks the launcher's key services (and WireGuard's VPN) at every boot until the
package has APP_AUTO_START (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). Run `appops write-settings` after
`appops set com.gathin.tvhome APP_AUTO_START allow`: app-ops are saved lazily, and a plain
`reboot` drops the change. Confirmed on the C69B over three reboots.
- The remote's mic button needs com.google.android.tv.remote.service, which is commented out below: a
press starts AtvSearchAssistantService inside that package, so with the package disabled the button
does nothing (no key on any /dev/input/event*) and logcat says the service is "not found".
`pm enable com.google.android.tv.remote.service` brings voice back without a reboot. Confirmed on a
43T6C (G10, Realtek, build STT2.230203.001) and on the 55Q651G; the phone-remote app pairing needs
it too. (#1441)
- With no antenna channels scanned, TCL Live (com.tcl.channelplus) is Live TV's only source: with it
disabled, Live TV opens the channel scan (com.tcl.tv/.scan.launch.ScanMainActivity). After
`pm enable com.tcl.channelplus` the channels come back only after a reboot, because com.tcl.tv
starts its BootService at boot. Comment its line out if you watch TCL Live. Confirmed on the 55Q651G.

mau.ten: TCL L40S66E (40" FHD, Latin America / Argentina; device C06, product C06_2K_GB, model "Smart TV",
mau.header:
TCL L40S66E (40" FHD, Latin America / Argentina; device C06, product C06_2K_GB, model "Smart TV",
TCL client type TCL-LA-MT9221-01), Android TV 11 (API 30), build AR2101,
TCL software V8-T221T01-LF1V030, fingerprint TCL/C06_2K_GB/C06:11/AR2101/AR14:user/release-keys.
MediaTek MT9221 (ro.board.platform mt5867), 1280x720 UI, about 920 MB RAM (ro.config.low_ram=true),
2.5 GB /data, ro.adb.secure=1. Same platform and firmware as examples/hitachi-cdh-le32smart21
(that one is a Hitachi-branded TCL); read examples/tcl-40s5400a too.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-l40s66e/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-l40s66e/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (the scripts' default, HOME priority 2, so it has to be
disabled). The only other HOME claimant is com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome.
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv. The remote's Input key opens its source picker.
Inputs come from com.tcl.tvinput: HDMI 1, HDMI 2, AV and the tuner.
launcher/ config used: live_tv_package com.tcl.tv; hidden_apps com.tcl.suspension and
com.tcl.partnercustomizer; reduced_motion true (see quirks). HDMI 1, HDMI 2, AV and Live TV all show
up in the Inputs menu.

Applied in four batches on one real unit on 2026-10-20, each batch checked with screenshots and key
injection (Home, Input key source picker, Settings, Wi-Fi, Netflix). Tested on one day only (shorter
than CONTRIBUTING.md asks); I will report back if anything breaks.
Checked after the full list: launcher/ installed with pm install and is Home after a reboot; the
Inputs menu lists HDMI 1/2, AV and Live TV; the Input key still opens com.tcl.tv's source picker;
Wi-Fi stays connected across reboots.
YouTube, Prime Video and Paramount+ open; the Chromecast receiver is enabled and its services run.
Memory, A/B on the same unit (launcher/ as Home in both, reboot, 5 min wait): disabling this list made
no measurable difference to MemAvailable (about 337 vs 335 MB; 386 vs 387 MB after `am kill-all`);
with 1 GB and low_ram, Android fills the freed memory with cached apps. The gain is the launcher:
stock tvlauncher 64 to 90 MB PSS vs 36 to 38 MB for launcher/, plus no TCL promo processes restarting.

Ad-blocking Private DNS was also enabled and validated (dns.adguard-dns.com); Netflix still opens,
YouTube's own ads are not blocked. Undo: tools/tv.py 'settings put global private_dns_mode opportunistic'

Known quirks on this firmware:
- screencap -p on stdout is corrupted by MediaTek log lines ("Init wrapper sys mutex successful").
Save to /sdcard and pull the file instead.
- launcher/ with normal motion was not smooth: 73% janky frames, median 28 ms per frame while moving
focus (dumpsys gfxinfo). reduced_motion true brought it to 27% janky, median 6 ms.
- com.tcl.usercenter (TCL account) is switched back on by the system at every boot, as on the
40S5400A. It stays idle, so it is left in the list.
- com.tcl.guard: here `pm disable-user` does stop TGuardService (not the case on the Hitachi).
With TGuard enabled there was LESS free RAM, not more (about 370 vs 388 MB MemAvailable after
`am kill-all`), so it stays off.
- setupwraith owned an old saved network, not the one in use; disabling it deleted only that old
network. Check `dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` first.
- After a reboot Play Store updates apps for a few minutes (com.android.vending about 90 MB), so
MemAvailable right after boot is not a fair measurement.

DO NOT DISABLE on this TV (kept and working):
com.tcl.tv                           # Live TV app, plays HDMI, source picker on the Input key
com.tcl.tvinput                      # TV input services for HDMI, AV and the tuner
com.tcl.suspension                   # Quick Panel / input menu; only hidden in the launcher config
com.tcl.providers.config             # TCL config provider
com.tcl.initsetup                    # setup flow, Wi-Fi
com.tcl.ttvs                         # firmware updater, not text-to-speech
com.tcl.rc.ota                       # remote control firmware updates
com.tcl.autopair                     # Bluetooth remote auto-pairing
com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service           # Bluetooth remote
com.tcl.keyhelp                      # remote-key help/virtual keys
com.tcl.system.server                # remote-key plumbing
com.tcl.settings                     # picture/sound settings
com.tcl.inputmethod.international    # keyboard
com.google.android.tv.remote.service # phone remote / Android TV remote
com.android.location.fused           # reported to boot-loop when disabled

Android 14 (SDK 34), build tcl9655_cn_an64-user 14 UTT2.250416.001 AU01, security patch
2025-09-05, 3.7 GB RAM, arm64-v8a. ro.adb.secure=1.
Retail name reported as "TCL Smart TV Pro" / IFFALCON (雷鸟); ro.product.model is generic, so
identify this unit by ro.product.name=MT9655_4K_CN and the build id above, not by the brand.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-mt9655-cn-android14/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-mt9655-cn-android14/debloat.txt com.tcl.cyberui

============================================================================
ADB: read this before anything else. This build is much harder than the 2026 MT9653 sets.
============================================================================
There is no "Developer options" screen and no "Wireless debugging" row anywhere in the UI.
TCL replaced the whole Settings app: com.android.settings is NOT installed, the stock settings
package is com.tcl.setting and it only declares MainActivity, SceneActivity,
StartOtherAppActivity and SlicePermissionActivity. Searching every activity for "adb", "debug"
or "develop" through an activity launcher returns nothing, and
android.settings.APPLICATION_DEVELOPMENT_SETTINGS has no handler.

The only switch is 通用设置 -> 更多 -> ADB. It opens adbd in **TLS mode on a random high port**
(observed 40769, 35879, 41629, 46493 on the same unit, a new one on every toggle):
- the port answers an ADB CNXN with STLS and never speaks plaintext;
- `adb connect ip:port` fails, daemon trace shows
"Post-handshake SSL_peek failed [SSLV3_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_UNKNOWN]";
- mDNS advertises _adb-tls-connect._tcp (instance adb-<serial>-xxxx) but never
_adb-tls-pairing._tcp, so `adb pair` has nothing to talk to;
- 5555 is closed and no other listener speaks ADB (full 1-65535 scan: adbd, two TCL services,
DLNA on 16626, AirPlay on 38171).
Switching Wi-Fi shows the stock Android prompt "要允许通过此网络进行无线调试吗" (per-BSSID), which
proves the wireless-debugging framework is present but the pairing UI was removed.

The working path is USB:
1. dual male USB-A cable, PC side in a USB 3.0 port, TV side in a **USB 2.0** port;
2. ADB toggle ON, then `adb devices`: Windows enumerates USB\VID_18D1&PID_4EE7 with the serial
that matches the mDNS instance, and the TV shows "Allow USB debugging";
3. accept it (and "always allow"), then `adb tcpip 5555` and `adb connect <ip>:5555`.
The USB path only works while the ADB toggle stays on, and 5555 is lost on every reboot
(re-run `adb tcpip 5555` with the cable attached).

============================================================================
Sideloading and the launcher: both are locked, and the lock is not in the installer app.
============================================================================
Every APK is refused over adb, including apps that do not declare HOME:
adb install / pm install / cmd package install
-> INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE: Install not allowed for file:///data/app/vmdl*.tmp
Spoofing the installer package (-i com.tcl.guard, com.tcl.appmarket2, com.android.packageinstaller)
changes nothing. The rejection is logged by system_server (PackageManager), not only by the
com.android.packageinstaller verifier.

The only channel that installs normal APKs is a USB stick through 电视卫士 (com.tcl.guard).
Driving the system installer UI over adb gets further but still fails: file:// URIs are refused
outright on Android 14, and a MediaStore content:// URI
am start -a android.intent.action.VIEW -t application/vnd.android.package-archive \
-d content://media/external/file/<id> --grant-read-uri-permission \
-n com.android.packageinstaller/.InstallStart
does show "应用未被认证，是否继续安装" and then fails with
verifier: signature not match for tcl com.gathin.tvhome, will not be installed !

Root cause, readable with:
content query --uri content://com.tcl.providers.config/all | grep InstallConfig
{"enable":"true","strategies":[
{"name":"safeStrategy","enable":"true","priority":"0"},
{"name":"blackListStrategy","enable":"true","packages":[],"priority":"1"},
{"name":"thridStrategy","enable":"false","packages":["com.dangbeimarket","com.shafa.market","com.ant.store.appstore"],"priority":"2"},
{"name":"launcherStrategy","enable":"true","packages":[],"priority":"3"},
{"name":"overDueStrategy","enable":"true","packages":[],"priority":"4"},
{"name":"pmStrategy","enable":"true","priority":"5"}]}
launcherStrategy is enabled with an empty allowlist, so a HOME package is only accepted if it is
signed with com.tcl.cyberui's key. The row cannot be edited from the shell: `content update`
returns 0 and silently ignores the write (verified by writing the Version row and reading it
back), the `content` CLI splits --bind on every ':' so a JSON value cannot be passed at all, and
/data/user_de/0/com.tcl.providers.config/databases/ is not readable as shell.

Stock launcher: com.tcl.cyberui, the only activity that resolves MAIN+HOME. Never disable it.
Net effect for this generation: debloat only. A replacement launcher is impossible without a
TCL-signed build, root, or a firmware downgrade.

Tested on a real unit: 28 packages disabled, one full `reboot` afterwards, Home, source panel,
Settings, app store, 电视卫士, Media Center and Multi-screen all still worked, crash buffer empty,
free RAM went from 1.97 GB to 1.15 GB (of 3.7 GB). Wait at least 10 seconds after applying before
rebooting.

Not present on this unit, so they are absent from the list: com.tcl.bi,
com.tcl.recognize.service, com.tcl.weixin, com.tcl.videocall.
Kept on purpose: com.tcl.cyberui, com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.ttvs,
com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.guard (USB install), com.tcl.appmarket2 (store),
com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter (USB playback), com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv (only keyboard),
com.tcl.autopair (remote pairing), com.tcl.miracast, com.tcl.MultiScreenInteraction_TV,
com.tcl.systemui.plugin.* (source panel and quick settings), com.tcl.usercenter,
com.tcl.walleve (voice, left on by owner choice).

mau.ten: TCL 55Q10G Pro (China), device tcl_mt5879_cn / product tcl_mt5879_cn_db, MediaTek MT9952,
mau.header:
TCL 55Q10G Pro (China), device tcl_mt5879_cn / product tcl_mt5879_cn_db, MediaTek MT9952,
Android 11 (SDK 30), build RQ3A.210705.001 / 2026012200 (2026-01-22), 3.5 GB RAM.
32-bit only: ro.product.cpu.abilist = armeabi-v7a,armeabi. No Google services — apps come from
com.tcl.appmarket2 or a USB stick. Likely a starting point for other 2026 China MT5879 sets.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-q10g-pro/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-q10g-pro/debloat.txt com.tcl.cyberui
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

ADB, read this before anything else: there is no "Build number" tap seven times on this firmware
and no ADB row in developer options. Settings → About this device (关于本机) → Device info (本机信息),
then press UP DOWN LEFT RIGHT on the remote; the ADB toggle appears at the bottom. The sequence
often has to be repeated two or three times before it fires — a single pass looks like it did
nothing, so keep going instead of assuming the path is wrong. Once on, it stays on across
reboots:
persist.adb.tcp.port=5555, persist.service.adb.enable=1.

Stock launcher: com.tcl.cyberui — the only activity that resolves MAIN+HOME, so never disable it
(no HOME handler means a black screen on boot). A third-party launcher cannot be installed here:
the refusal is a package verification step, not a parse error (see tcl-ak30a5 for the older
Android 9 variant). Any APK declaring android.intent.category.HOME fails with
INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE and logs:
OverseasAppConfig: Verifying begin
verifier: fetch signature info from: com.tcl.cyberui
verifier: signature does not match for tcl <pkg>, will not be installed!
The gate is com.android.packageinstaller → verifier/InstallStrategyManager → LauncherStrategy,
which allows a HOME package only if it is in that strategy's package list, or is signed with
com.tcl.cyberui's key and carries <meta-data com.tcl.app.type="com.tcl.ui">. The list is TCL's
InstallConfig, readable with `content query --uri content://com.tcl.providers.config/all`
(project_id=InstallConfig) and not writable from the shell.

Sideloading is blocked for everything else too, not just launchers. On this unit `adb install`,
`pm install`, `pm install-commit` and launching the exported InstallStart activity by hand all
end in INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE — including an APK signed by TCL itself, and with
`-i com.tcl.appmarket2` spoofing the store as installer. Apps arrive through the TCL app store
(com.tcl.appmarket2) or a USB stick via 电视卫士. Don't spend an afternoon on adb install.

Live TV app: com.tcl.tv — keep it, it owns DTV/HDMI playback and the remote's source key.
Kept on purpose:
com.tcl.guard                 电视卫士; on this firmware the USB install path is the remaining
way to sideload, so keep it
com.tcl.appmarket2            TCL app store, the other install channel
com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv the only input method; disable it and there is no keyboard at all
com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter        USB playback; the whole Media Center app goes with it
com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.ttvs (holds DEVICE_ADMIN_ENABLED)

Applied on a real unit and re-checked after a full reboot (`reboot`, not standby): Home, the
source panel (HDMI 1-4 plus TV/AV/cast), Media Center, the app store, 电视卫士 and Settings all
still worked, with no entries in the crash buffer and no ANRs. Memory available went from 1.97 GB
to 2.24 GB. Voice and TCL account services are off by choice, noted per group below.

Expected in logcat afterwards, harmless: `Unable to start service ... com.tcl.usercenter` about
every 20 seconds. The bind fails immediately and starts no process.

mau.header:
TCL Q7C QD-Mini LED, Europe (device G08, model "Smart TV Pro", product G08_4K_GB, MediaTek tcl9618)
Google TV, Android 14 (SDK 34), firmware UTT2.250416.001 AU02 - the same build as examples/tcl-85rm7l-google-tv.
About 2.4 GB RAM. Set up on Ethernet in Austria (German/Austrian apps: ORF ON, Joyn, ServusTV, ZDF).
This list goes further than the 85RM7L one: launcherx and setupwraith are off for the Clean Your TV launcher,
and voice, AirPlay, mirroring and several streaming apps are off by the owner's choice.

Tested on one set from 21 October 2026. Disabled by hand with `pm disable-user --user 0`, one call each, in five
batches with a screenshot after each. The first 35 survived a reboot, none came back (three self-installed
apps disabled alongside them are not listed here). launcherx and setupwraith were disabled afterwards, once the
new launcher was installed. YouTube, Live TV and the HDMI input list checked.
Second unit: TCL 65Q7D Pro, Greece, same build (AU02), on Wi-Fi, one day from 22 October 2026: this list minus
AirPlay and com.tcl.UpdatePeripheral (kept), plus mediashell; Wireless debugging only. See README.
Third unit: TCL 55Q6C (Smart TV Pro, G08_4K_GB), Vietnam, same build (AU02), on Wi-Fi, one day from 23 October 2026:
24 of this list (voice, Chromecast, AirPlay, Miracast, Netflix, the USB player, T-Solo, hearing test and soundbar
updater kept), plus com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic. launcherx and setupwraith stay ENABLED so Chromecast keeps
its credentials; Home goes to the new launcher through stock_home_redirect instead. Survived two reboots. See README.
Fourth unit: TCL 65T8C, same build (AU02), on Wi-Fi, from 23 October 2026: AirPlay, Prime Video and mediashell kept,
more TCL extras and the TCL keyboard off (Gboard set first); Wireless debugging only. See README.
Fifth unit: TCL G08 EU/UK set, OTA from Android 12 (fingerprint UTT2.250416.001 AU02, 21 October 2026): the groups
marked "fifth unit" below were verified disabled there. OTA-survival audit: the update re-enabled none of this list
and newly installed com.tcl.channelplus (in the list); com.iplayer.android.webview from the Android 12 days is gone
from this firmware. See README.
Sixth unit: TCL 55C69K (G08_4K_GB, client type TCL-EU-MT9653-S1), Europe, same build (AU02), on Wi-Fi, one day from
26 October 2026: 43 disabled and checked after three reboots; katniss, tclhome_passive, onetimeinitializer and
UpdatePeripheral kept; dashboard, eva, gallery, mediashell, gamebar, youtube.tvmusic and the fifth-unit webview and
MediaTek groups off too. Port 5555 opened with USB + Network debugging. See README.
Ninth unit: TCL 98Q6C (G08_4K_GB), Poland, newer build AU04, on Ethernet, eight days from 24 October 2026: 31 of
this list (Netflix, its token manager and Prime Video kept; launcherx and setupwraith stay ENABLED for Chromecast,
Home through stock_home_redirect), plus com.tcl.browser and com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic. A ttvs update
re-enabled com.tcl.channelplus once; nothing else came back. key_filter false kept the volume ramp. See README.
Tenth unit: TCL 55T8C (Smart TV Pro, G08_4K_GB), same build (AU02), on Wi-Fi, from 26 October 2026 to
1 November 2026: this list minus Netflix (ninja, tokenmanager) and Prime Video (kept), plus mediashell and
com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic; launcherx and setupwraith off for the launcher. Reboot-checked. See README.

the updater), com.tcl.eva (boot service with camera and TCL BI permissions), com.tvos, com.tpa.kb,
tv.mopa.ginga (broadcast interactive-TV middleware), com.tcl.gallery (also TCL's screensavers),
com.tcl.partnercustomizer, com.tcl.interactive. Never launch com.tcl.factory.view.

Android 14 (Google TV), firmware UTT2.250416.001 AU16
Also seen on the same G08 board with AU14 firmware, a "Smart TV Pro" sold outside the US (prasta1, PR #23);
that set needed Wireless-debugging pairing (docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "USB debugging never opens port 5555").

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-qm6k-google-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-qm6k-google-tv/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. Live TV / HDMI app: com.tcl.tv.
Keep: com.tcl.tv, com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.dashboard, com.tcl.suspension, com.tcl.autopair,
com.tcl.systemserver, com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.useragreement,
com.tcl.globalkeyoverlay, com.tcl.systemui.plugin, com.tcl.factory.view and all com.mediatek.*.
Unlike the 2023 G10 sets, com.tcl.ttvs and com.tcl.logkit ship ENABLED here.
Do NOT disable com.tcl.providers.config, com.tcl.initsetup or com.tcl.factory.view: together they dropped
the Wi-Fi connection outright on the AU14 set and it took a re-pair over ADB to get back in (#23).

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Play Protect blocks the launcher ("built for an older version of Android") unless targetSdk >= 34.
- With launcherx disabled, setupwraith's RecoveryActivity claims HOME at priority 1 and shows a blank
screen. Shell can't disable that one component, so the whole package is disabled below (it only
runs first-time setup). While Home was blank the TV fell back to HDMI 1 and woke a console over CEC.
- Gear (keycode 83) and YouTube (190) only reach launcherx, so both go dead once it is disabled.
config.json here maps them again; install the launcher with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 so the accessibility
service binds and reads them, then push the theme:
TV_HOST=<tv ip> HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh
TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/theme.sh examples/tcl-qm6k-google-tv
- Soundbar on optical (S/PDIF) can't be powered or volume-controlled by the TV. Use HDMI 4 (eARC) and
`cmd hdmi_control cec_setting set system_audio_control 1` (it ships 0 here).

mau.header:
TCL UnionTV, Latin America (ro.product.model UnionTV, TCL; persist.tcl.client_type SEM-LA-RT41KB-S1),
Realtek RTD284x (RT2841), Android TV 9 (API 28), build PPR2.180905.006.A1 (2020-11-15), 1.4 GB RAM with
ro.config.low_ram=true, wired Ethernet. Sold in Brazil.
Fingerprint: TCL/UnionTV/UnionTV:9/PPR2.180905.006.A1/builder.20201115.105034:user/release-keys
Same platform and build as examples/thomson-32he5800 (THOM-EU-RT2841-S1); this is the TCL-branded
Latin America variant. The differences are noted below.

Tested: applied 2026-10-19 in batches with screenshots between them; launcher/ installed with the default
build-and-install script, Home, Inputs menu (HDMI 1/2, AV, Live TV), HDMI switching, Settings,
Netflix/Prime/YouTube launch and the Clock screensaver checked on the device. Not yet lived with for days.

Also confirmed 2026-10-26 on a TCL 32S6500S, identical fingerprint but persist.tcl.client_type
TCL-LA-RT41KB-S1 (not SEM-LA-RT41KB-S1 above) and Wi-Fi only, no Ethernet. Applied in six batches with
screenshots between them and a reboot check (all 34 disabled packages, including the launcher's own
second pass below, survived it); launcher/ installed, Home confirmed with mFocusedApp/mResumedActivity,
Inputs menu, D-pad from all four edges and YouTube launch checked. Not yet lived with for days either.

Also confirmed 2026-10-27 on a TCL L40S6500 (40"), same fingerprint and
persist.tcl.client_type TCL-LA-RT41KB-S1 as the 32S6500S, Wi-Fi only. Applied in four batches with
screenshots between them, keeping katniss and speech.pumpkin (Assistant wanted) and the streaming apps;
com.tcl.waterfall.overseas, Red Bull TV and Twitch were not installed. After a reboot everything stayed
disabled except com.tcl.usercenter, which the system re-enables at every boot (as on the TCL Android 9
sets in the PROMPT); left in the list, it stays idle. launcher/ installed, Home confirmed with
mResumedActivity, Inputs menu (HDMI 1/2, Live TV) and the remote's app buttons checked. Tested one day.
Power-on: this unit opens com.tcl.tv at every boot, so Home at power-on needs power_on_home with
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 - which worked, but with HomeKeyService bound, holding Volume Up moved the volume
one step per press instead of ramping (the key-repeat loss in docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md,
seen here too). The owner chose the volume ramp and pressing Home once after power-on, so the helper is off.

Also confirmed 2026-10-31 on a TCL UnionTV with persist.tcl.client_type TCL-CA-RT41KA-S1 and a later build
of the same release (PPR2.180905.006.A1, builder.20210125), Wi-Fi only. Applied in five batches with
screenshots between them. Both TVINPUT_ALLOW lines below disabled cleanly on this unit, and after two
reboots every disabled package stayed disabled, com.tcl.usercenter included. This unit has no
com.tcl.tvpassthrough or com.tcl.sourcemananger; the Input key, HDMI switching, Settings, the app keys and
the Volume Up ramp all worked on the real remote. It opens com.tcl.tv at every boot too, and the owner kept
that (no HOME_KEY_SERVICE). launcher/ installed, Home confirmed with mResumedActivity, Inputs menu (HDMI 1/2,
AV, Live TV) and D-pad edges checked. Tested the same day. It adds com.tcl.dashboard and
com.tcl.tv.tclhome_passive below, and two off-by-choice apps, commented out.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tcl-uniontv-latin-america/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tcl-uniontv-latin-america/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (restore.sh / build-and-install defaults work). Other HOME
claimants are only the two FallbackHome activities (com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice,
com.android.tv.settings); setupwraith does not claim HOME here. com.google.android.leanbacklauncher is
also installed and stays enabled as a fallback.
Live TV app: com.tcl.tv (keep it, it owns tuner/HDMI playback; its TVActivity has a leanback entry, so
launcher/ needs live_tv_package com.tcl.tv - and hidden_apps needs com.tcl.tv added too, or it still
shows as a duplicate grid tile alongside the Inputs menu's "Live TV" row; the default hidden_apps only
excludes the placeholder com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter). Keep com.tcl.tvinput, com.tcl.tvpassthrough (the
HDMI TvInputServices) and com.tcl.sourcemananger (source key / input panel). Inputs come from the
standard TvInputManager, so the launcher's Inputs menu lists them with the default config, but the HDMI
port states land on the wrong port (the empty HDMI 1 reads Connected): set inputs_cec_state_only true
(docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md, "The Inputs list shows the empty HDMI 1 as connected").
Standby: Quick start ("Iniciar rapido", STR, sys.tcl.str.switch) suspends to RAM and takes Ethernet down
with it, so ADB, Cast and Wake-on-LAN cannot wake the TV; there is no network-standby option on this
firmware. TCL's picture/system panel opens with `am start -a com.tcl.settings.action.NETWORKSETTINGS`.
Not tested on the Wi-Fi-only 32S6500S unit above.
Wi-Fi pill name on Android 9: showing the connected network's name (not just "Wi-Fi") needs both the
launcher's own ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION grant (build-and-install.sh does this) and the TV's system Location
turned on (`settings put secure location_mode 3` and `settings put secure location_providers_allowed
+network`, then restart the launcher) - unlike config.xml's show_network_pill comment, which only
mentions this gate on Android 14. Ask before turning system Location on; it is a privacy-relevant change
beyond the app's own permission grant.

Differences from the Thomson list, which keeps these three: com.tcl.partnercustomizer,
com.tcl.copydatatotv and com.tcl.common.terminalmanagerplus were disabled here with the remote, HDMI
switching, Settings and the launcher all still working. The remote's T key (partnercustomizer's TKey
activity) was not tested; re-enable partnercustomizer if your remote has one and it stops working.
Kept here but disabled in the Thomson list: the TCL media players (com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter,
audioplayer, imageplayer, videoplayer) for USB playback, and com.google.android.partnersetup.

The 32S6500S unit shipped with a few packages this list's first unit did not have:
com.tcl.waterfall.overseas, com.tcl.useragreement, com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.partnerwidget,
com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer and com.tcl.partnercustomizer.resource - all
disabled below with the remote, HDMI, Settings and the launcher still working.
com.android.vending, com.tcl.browser and com.globo.globotv (Globoplay) were the apps still enabled and
on the leanback home screen afterward on that unit, besides the ones kept below by choice; which survive
depends on what the retailer and the owner's own account preloaded, so check `pm list packages` on yours.

Two lines below (com.google.android.leanbacklauncher.recommendations and
android.autoinstalls.config.tcl.device) disabled cleanly on the first unit, but on the 32S6500S unit
tools/disable.sh's own TVINPUT_ALLOW safety check skipped both: dumpsys showed neither package's
permission block, so the input-driver check could not clear them and left them enabled. Harmless either
way (both are content/auto-install helpers, not input drivers) - set TVINPUT_ALLOW=1 once every other
input still works after a reboot if you want them off too (#321).

Deliberately NOT disabled (system-relevant or unclear): com.tcl.framework.custom, com.tcl.keyhelp,
com.tcl.keycustomfunctionservice (remote keys), com.tcl.autopair, com.tcl.tcl_bt_rcu_service (remote
pairing), com.tcl.settings, com.tcl.initsetup, com.tcl.appstatecontroller,
com.tcl.xian.StartandroidService, com.tcl.ui_mediaCenter (USB playback), com.realtek.netflix.setting
(Netflix ESN/config), Chromecast (mediashell), firmware updates
(versionUpdateApp, rc.ota).
Also left alone on the 32S6500S unit, none of them tested further: com.tcl.factory.view (a BootUpReceive
receiver and a .MainMenu activity; the name alone puts it in PROMPT.md's "never even open a factory
package" category, so it was left exactly as found, neither disabled nor started - treat it the same way
on any TCL set until someone reports what it actually does), com.google.android.sss.authbridge and
com.tcl.systemuioverlay (both gave dumpsys almost nothing to go on), and com.android.ListenNetStateService
(one BootBroadcastReceiver, unclear what it feeds; low risk but untested, so left enabled out of caution).

mau.ten: Thomson 43RT1055 FA Series, India, built by SPPL (ro.product.model "SPPL 2K ANDROID TV", product
mau.header:
Thomson 43RT1055 FA Series, India, built by SPPL (ro.product.model "SPPL 2K ANDROID TV", product
SPPL_2K_RT41, device sauve), Realtek RTD2841A (32-bit ARM), Android TV 14 (API 34), build UKRE.260524.055,
fingerprint THOMSON/SPPL_2K_RT41/sauve:14/UKRE.260524.055/16101080:user/release-keys.
1 GB RAM (about 210 MB available on the stock Home), 1080p panel drawn at 1280x720, density 213.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/thomson-43rt1055/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/thomson-43rt1055/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (plain Android TV, not Google TV; restore.sh and
build-and-install.sh defaults work). The only other HOME claimants are com.realtek.systemservice's and
com.android.tv.settings' FallbackHome; setupwraith is installed but does not claim HOME, so no handover trap.
Live TV app: com.realtek.tv (TvActivity has a leanback entry). HDMI 1-3 and AV come from
com.realtek.tv.passthrough, the tuners from com.realtek.dtv (Cable, Antenna) and com.realtek.tv.atv.
launcher/ config: config.json here (live_tv_package com.realtek.tv, its tile hidden).
Remote: infrared (input device IR_HKIR), no Bluetooth remote bonded. Sideloading works: pm install accepts
a third-party APK that declares HOME.

Applied and checked on a real unit on 2026-10-21, in small batches with a screenshot after each: Live TV,
HDMI and AV still switch, YouTube plays, and with launcher/ installed the real remote's Home, Input,
Settings, app buttons and mic work. A reboot afterwards re-enabled none of the packages below.

Kept on purpose, do not disable:
- com.realtek.tv, com.realtek.tv.passthrough, com.realtek.dtv, com.realtek.dtmb, com.realtek.tv.atv,
com.realtek.tv.isdb, com.realtek.tv.atsc, com.android.providers.tv: Live TV, HDMI, AV and the tuners.
- com.realtek.menu, com.realtek.slices, com.realtek.globalkeyhandler: the source menu and the remote's
Input and Settings keys (on Input, globalkeyhandler opens com.realtek.tv/.SelectInputActivity).
- com.realtek.systemservice, com.realtek.power, com.realtek.energymode, com.realtek.display.monitor.
- com.realtek.connecteddevices: the Bluetooth "Connected devices" settings page.
- com.android.bluetooth, com.google.android.tv.googletvremotepairer (and its customizationsample).
- com.google.android.tv.remote.service: despite the name it holds AtvSearchAssistantService, which the
mic button needs here too (as on tcl-c755-google-tv). Disabled, pressing the mic logged "Unable to start
service ... AtvSearchAssistantService" and nothing happened; re-enabling it brought voice search back.
- Factory packages, never launched: com.hk.factorymenu (HikeenFactory), com.factory.factoryautomation
(HikeenAutoTest).
- com.realtek.mdnsoffload, com.android.tv.mdnsoffloadmanager, com.realtek.media.notification (codec notices).

Already disabled from the factory (stays disabled on restore): com.android.tv (an empty RtkLiveTv stub).

Quirks on this firmware:
- The apex packages below (adservices, ondevicepersonalization, federatedcompute) accepted pm disable-user.
- TvInputManager reports every HDMI port as connected-standby (state 1) with or without a cable, so the
launcher shows no HDMI status; AV reports "No device" correctly.
- launcher/'s Inputs menu switches HDMI and AV, but its Live TV row only reopens com.realtek.tv on the last
input while no channels are scanned: the TV app ignores the tuner's passthrough URI. The stock source
picker (remote's Input key, then Antenna) opens the DVB channel scan instead.
- Network ADB on port 5555 comes back by itself after a reboot while debugging is on: switch debugging off
in Developer options and reboot to close it.

The DVB-T tuner input (com.technicolor.android.dtvinput, dtvscan.project) was left enabled although unused.
it.telecomitalia.digitalsupport stays enabled: tools/disable.sh skips it because it requests
TV_INPUT_HARDWARE.

After a reboot this box starts in standby (mWakefulness=Asleep, black screenshots); the remote's power
button or `input keyevent WAKEUP` brings up Home. Nothing in this list was re-enabled by the firmware at boot.
Private DNS does not exist on Android 8.0.

mau.header:
TiVo Stream 4K (SEI Robotics IPA1104HDW, SKU RA2400, device SEI400TV, Amlogic S905Y2, NES middleware), 2 GB RAM
Android TV 12 (SDK 31), build SC.1272, 32-bit (armeabi-v7a), security patch 2025-07-05

Apply and undo: the commands in README.md here, NOT tools/disable.sh (this firmware refuses it).
Everything is SUSPENDED and barred from the background, not disabled or uninstalled.
Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV). HOME priority 2, so set-home-activity says
"Success" and changes nothing; README.md here explains how Home reaches another launcher. A streaming stick: no
HDMI inputs and no tuner. Suspending the stock launcher only works after it stops owning the HOME role.

Known quirks on this firmware:
- Every pm disable-user, pm disable <component> and pm hide is refused ("This command is illegal!"); pm uninstall
--user 0 is refused for core apps. pm suspend and appops work and survive a reboot.
- Port 5555 opens as soon as USB debugging is on, with a per-computer prompt; there is no separate network toggle.
- com.nes.coreservice runs EvoBlackListAppsFun at every start (its BootReceiver, kicked by the persistent
com.nes.daemon): it uninstalls every non-system app whose activity declares android.intent.category.HOME, and a
fixed list of 53 packages from array/evo_black_list_to_uninstall_pkgs (alternative launchers, Downloader,
Magisk, IPTV "Magis TV" variants). Suspending it does not stop its boot receiver.
- A suspended package still gets its boot broadcasts: coreservice, sageservice, tvlauncher, katniss,
tvrecommendations and tvbugtracker are running again after a boot. Stop them with am force-stop.

Kept on purpose (checked with dumpsys package):
com.uei.uas.tivo               UEI QuickSet: the remote switches the TV on and off
com.sei.hdmi.services          HDMI-CEC
com.nes.tivo.remote.pair       Bluetooth remote pairing; remote.ota updates the remote's firmware
com.google.android.apps.mediashell   Chromecast (suspending it saved no memory: another component binds it)
Play Store, Play Services, keyboard, TV Settings

mau.ten: Tornado 65UA1400E (El Araby, Egypt; Skyworth-built SW4H, product SW4H_Tornado, board SW4, MediaTek m7332),
mau.header:
Tornado 65UA1400E (El Araby, Egypt; Skyworth-built SW4H, product SW4H_Tornado, board SW4, MediaTek m7332),
Android TV 11 (API 30), firmware RTM5.220609.106 (built 2023-12-08), security patch 2023-10-06.
Fingerprint Tornado/SW4H_Tornado/SW4H:11/RTM5.220609.106/20231126:user/release-keys.
ro.product.model "TORNADO Android TV", manufacturer skyworth. armeabi-v7a, 1.7 GB RAM, 1920x1080 @ 320 dpi.
Same Skyworth SW4H platform as examples/panasonic-4ktv-0su and examples/karbonn-swtv-20ae.
Unit 2: realme Smart TV (India), product SW4H_FF_realme, device SW4H_FF, board SW4, MediaTek m7332, the same
build RTM5.220609.106 (built 2023-12-08, security patch 2023-10-06), armeabi-v7a only, 1.7 GB RAM,
1920x1080 @ 320 dpi. Its notes are under "Unit 2" below.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/tornado-65ua1400e/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/tornado-65ua1400e/debloat.txt com.google.android.tvlauncher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher:  com.google.android.tvlauncher (classic Android TV home, not Google TV launcherx)
Live TV app:     com.smartdevice.livetv (Skyworth Live TV / input OSD); inputs in com.mediatek.tvinput.
HOME claimants:  tvlauncher, com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (priority 4), Settings' FallbackHome.
setupwraith does NOT own the saved Wi-Fi network here (android.uid.system), but it is
kept anyway: nothing on this list needs it gone.
Updates:         no separate firmware-update package; updates live in Settings.

Disabled at the factory, so not listed (restore.sh would turn them ON): com.sky.market,
com.smartdevice.tvworkwithalexa. Unit 2 also ships com.homwee.howtocast, com.smartdevice.dtv.icast (CastPlay)
and com.liskovsoft.leankeyboard disabled, and has no com.smartdevice.recommendation or
com.Smartdevice.emanual installed at all (disable.sh only reports them as missing).

KEEP, even though the names look like bloat (checked on this TV with dumpsys package):
- fusion.android.tv.demo: receives com.mstar.android.intent.action.TV_INPUT_BUTTON (the remote's Input
key), as on examples/jvc-android-tv-menlo. The Panasonic SW4H list disables it; do not copy that here.
- com.mediatek.partner.netflix: serves a TvInputService and handles the Netflix button.
- com.mediatek.wwtv.tvrecommendation: asks for TV_INPUT_HARDWARE (disable.sh would skip it anyway).
- com.smartdevice.firewall (purpose unclear), com.smartdevice.dtv.icast (CastPlay), com.tianci.localmedia
(USB media), com.google.android.backdrop (kept; the launcher's Clock is set as the active screensaver),
katniss (Assistant), mediashell (Chromecast), tv.remote.service: kept by the owner's choice.
- Every streaming / user app is kept and shows in the launcher grid.

Status: applied in four batches on one TV on 2026-10-22, with a screenshot and a Live TV / Input-key check
after each; tools/restore.sh tested after batch 1 (package lists and Home identical to a snapshot), then
re-applied. Verified after two reboots: nothing re-enabled (tools/check.py clean), launcher/ is Home, Inputs
menu (HDMI 1-3, AV, Live TV), Live TV, Netflix, and on the real remote Home, Back, Input (Skyworth source
panel), Netflix, YouTube, mic and Settings keys all work with no key service. Hours of use, not days yet.
Measured at 180 s uptime after a reboot: Home drawn at 48.2 s -> 40.2 s, used PSS 810 MB -> 739 MB.

Quirks on this firmware:
- /proc/meminfo MemAvailable and dumpsys "Free RAM" report impossible values (hundreds of GB of cached
kernel memory on a 1.7 GB set): compare Used RAM (PSS) instead.
- The Home handover needs the stock launcher disabled: with tvlauncher enabled (priority 2) Home keeps
resolving to it even after `set-home-activity` prints Success, so run launcher/build-and-install.sh with
the default STOCK_LAUNCHER (it disables tvlauncher, checks Home and rolls back on its own). setupwraith
(priority 4) did not take Home afterwards.
- /vendor/etc/global_settings.txt forces animator_duration_scale=0.6 at every boot; window and transition
scales set to 0.5 stick.
- USB debugging alone opened port 5555; ro.adb.secure=1.
- Yango Play, Jawwy TV and STARZ ON wake at every boot from their own WorkManager/recommendation
receivers (~300 MB together). Kept installed here; `cmd appops set <pkg> RUN_ANY_IN_BACKGROUND ignore`
then `cmd appops write-settings` (survives reboot) leaves them cached-empty and stops Yango's
:passport and :AppMetrica processes; used PSS 739 MB -> 679 MB. Undo: `cmd appops reset <pkg>`.

Unit 2 (realme Smart TV), applied 2026-10-28 in five batches with a screenshot after each, then the
CleanYourTV launcher, two reboots and several days of daily use. Every disable held across both reboots.
Seen on that unit:
- com.smartdevice.speedchannels is installed there and is not in unit 1's list: Coocaa's recommendation
channels (TvRecommendationMainActivity), with a notification-listener service and Coocaa's dataer and
upgrader components. Disabled with batch 2 (below); Home and Live TV were unaffected.
- tools/disable.sh skipped six packages in the first pass because they request no permissions, so its
input-driver check could not read them: android.autoinstalls.config.SW,
com.mstar.android.tv.disclaimercustomization, com.android.htmlviewer, com.android.wallpaperbackup and
both com.android.cts.*ctsshim. They were disabled afterwards with TVINPUT_ALLOW=1, once HDMI 1 and Live TV
had been checked after a reboot. After that Live TV still opened and the TV rebooted onto the launcher;
HDMI was checked before these six went, not again straight after.
- The Home handover worked as on unit 1: launcher/build-and-install.sh with the default STOCK_LAUNCHER
disabled tvlauncher, Home resolved to com.gathin.tvhome, and setupwraith (left enabled) did not take it.
dumpsys wifi listed the saved network's owners as android.uid.system and com.google.uid.shared.
- After each reboot the TV came up on the launcher, not on Live TV (no boot_to_live_tv or power_on_home).
- On the real remote Home, Back, Input, the app buttons and Settings all worked with no key helper (no
HomeKeyService or InputKeyService). This remote has no mic button, so the mic-button check on
com.google.android.tv.remote.service (it runs AtvSearchAssistantService) could not be made; it is kept
anyway, with the Assistant, Chromecast (mediashell) and the other streaming apps.
- Private DNS works on this set (see the README's optional DNS extra).

- Port 5555 is closed until USB debugging has been toggled/authorised; it opened without a
separate Network-debugging switch on this unit. No Wireless-debugging (pairing) menu exists.
- The uk.co.freeview.* pack (BBC, ITV, Ch4/5, Freeview explore...) ships already disabled on
Spain-market units; it is not listed below because `pm list packages -d` already held it.
- The remote's YouTube and Prime Video buttons are handled by Vestel firmware below Android: the
IR driver logs "u4IRKey after convert: 0xffffffff" and no keycode reaches InputDispatcher
(getevent shows scancodes 0x129/0x13e, but the IR device's vendor keylayout drops them). With
their apps disabled the buttons simply do nothing; no launcher key service can remap them.
- Volume keys do reach Android (KEY_VOLUMEUP/DOWN on event0), but the firmware changes the volume
before the accessibility filter and never passes them on, so no app (InputKeyService included)
can replace the system volume slider.
- The TV closes Wi-Fi (and ADB with it) in standby. Accessibility services survived days of
standby cycles; only a force-stop of the launcher switched InputKeyService off.
- No microphone (no android.hardware.microphone) and an IR-only remote, so voice comes from a
phone or Nest speaker ("Hey Google, ... on the TV"). That needs katniss: keep it if you use it.

Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.
Tested on one box the same day, including several reboots; not a multi-day soak.

A streaming box: no HDMI-in or tuner, so set live_tv_package empty in config.xml. Stock launcher:
com.google.android.tvlauncher (the scripts' default). It is a Google-certified Android TV: Play Store, Play Services
and the standard launcher, no operator home screen. No user restrictions or device owner; sideloading works.

Notes from this box:
- Network debugging opens port 5555 with ro.adb.secure=1, so each computer is accepted on screen.
- The remote's app buttons are global keys handled by com.sdmc.GlobalKey (keylayout Vendor_7545_Product_0171.kl):
YouTube = KEYCODE_BUTTON_4 (KEY_F1), Play Store = BUTTON_5 (KEY_F3), TV+ = BUTTON_10 (key 185, which
GlobalKey calls "SDMCEXTEND2"). GlobalKey starts the mapped app; if the app is not installed it opens its Play
Store page instead. The keylayout also maps a Prime Video key (63, BUTTON_8), but this box's remote has none.
- DISABLING YOUTUBE BREAKS THE PLAY STORE BUTTON: GlobalKey only checks that a package is installed, so the
YouTube button on a disabled com.google.android.youtube.tv throws ActivityNotFoundException and crashes
GlobalKey. After repeated crashes Android marks the process bad and every app button (Play Store, TV+)
is dead until a reboot. If you
disable YouTube, take the buttons away from GlobalKey with app_keys and INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1, e.g.
"KEYCODE_BUTTON_4:<your YouTube app>", "KEYCODE_BUTTON_5:com.android.vending", "KEYCODE_BUTTON_10:<package>".
InputKeyService gets the keys before the global-key broadcast. Checked with the real remote after a reboot.
- com.google.android.tv.remote.service comes back at every boot, after both pm disable-user and pm uninstall --user 0,
so it is not listed here (about 14 MB).
- com.sdmc.disablecec turns HDMI-CEC off on first boot only (com_sdmc_disablecec_first_run=1); switching CEC on in
Settings sticks.
- The test unit was on a 1080p PC monitor and the box had picked 2160p59.94 with YCbCr 4:2:0 (cur_VIC 353 in
/sys/class/amhdmitx/amhdmitx0/config). Settings > TV settings > Display > Screen resolution set to 1080p-59.94hz
switched it to VIC 16, YCbCr 4:4:4, and it survives a reboot.
- Free RAM after boot went from about 460 MB to about 930 MB; ZRAM in use from about 185 MB to about 25 MB.
- AdGuard Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) works.

Kept on purpose: com.sdmc.GlobalKey (remote app buttons), com.sdmc.standbyserver (standby), com.sdmc.bluetoothconnect
(remote pairing), com.sdmc.disablecec, com.sdmc.factorymonitor (watches package removal, purpose unclear),
com.droidlogic* (Amlogic settings, display and Bluetooth), com.droidlogic.otaupgrade (firmware updates),
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith, com.google.android.inputmethod.latin (keyboard), Play Store, Play Services.

Same-day test, not a multi-day soak: six batches and two reboots, the last after the Home handover.
Home, Inputs, HDMI, YouTube playback and the real remote checked; no FATAL or ANR in logcat.
Differences from the TD43 unit:
- com.google.android.videos is not installed; skip that line on the TD50.
- com.google.android.partnersetup was disabled on the TD50; optional below, not tested on the TD43.
- Netflix, Prime Video and YouTube Music were off on both units by the owners' choice; Chromecast,
AirPlay, screen sharing, Miracast and USB file/photo viewers were also off on the TD50. These
choices are commented out below so another household can keep the apps it uses.
- Voice search and MediaTek partnercustomizer were left enabled on the TD50.
- Forgetting and re-joining Wi-Fi moved its owner from setupwraith to android.uid.system:1000
before disabling setupwraith. Home and Wi-Fi still worked after the last reboot.
- The firmware forces Location off, so the launcher's network pill says "Wi-Fi", not the SSID.
- config.json and home.png show the TD50's dock/layout; see README.md for this unit's notes.
