Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- Port 5555 answered after the reboot that follows turning on USB + Wireless debugging (as on the BenQ).
- `cmd package set-home-activity com.gathin.tvhome/.MainActivity` prints Success but Home stays on
launcherx while it is enabled (priority 2). Home moves only once launcherx is disabled; set it again
after that and confirm with `dumpsys activity activities | grep mFocusedApp` (held across 4 reboots).
- The Wi-Fi network saved in the first-run wizard belonged to setupwraith (cname=...setupwraith).
Forget and re-join it in Settings first; it then belongs to android.uid.system and setupwraith can go.
With setupwraith disabled, RecoveryActivity never started (logcat) and Home has no delay.
- com.mediatek.android.leanbacklauncher.partnercustomizer comes back by itself: it lives in
/vendor/odm and is enabled=0 (default) again after every reboot. Disabling it changed nothing
visible and broke nothing (tv.service kept one PID, no tvlauncher.widget errors, Input worked),
so it is left commented out below rather than disabled again.
- The IR remote ("MStar Smart TV IR Receiver", vendor 3697 product 0001):
Input sends KEYCODE_TV_INPUT, routed by com.mediatek.tv.service to the system Inputs menu: works
without any helper. KEYCODE_TV opens the Live TV app. YouTube works with the stock launcher gone.
The Settings (gear) button arrives as scancode 498 (KEY_BRL_DOT2) and does nothing once launcherx
is disabled. settings_key_scancodes 498 with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 brings it back, BUT with any
key-filtering accessibility helper bound, a held volume button steps only once or twice instead of
ramping (volume repeat is back as soon as the helper is off). Kept off here; Settings stays reachable
from the launcher's Settings pill.
The Netflix button is KEYCODE_STEM_1 -> com.mediatek.tv.service NetflixKeyReceiver; with Netflix
disabled it does nothing (app_keys could map it to another app).
- com.mediatek.androidbox (WFDSinkTest_CH) has a MiracastService and uses com.mediatek.wfdsink: on
this set it is the Miracast receiver, not just a test app.
- Standby is MediaTek suspend: from deep standby the Bluetooth remote cannot wake the TV, the IR remote
and the power button can. That is not damage.
- Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) validates and YouTube plays with it.

KEEP, do not disable:
- com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter, com.mediatek.wwtv.setupwizard,
com.google.android.tv.inputplayer, com.mediatek.android.tv.globalkeyoverlay: Live TV, HDMI, Inputs key.
- com.mediatek.autopair (remote pairing), com.homwee.synckey (remote keys),
com.google.android.tv.remote.service (phone remote).
- com.homwee.factory, com.mediatek.tv.factorykey: also handle key broadcasts. Never LAUNCH them.
- com.homwee.dynamicbacklight, com.homwee.lightsensorservice: picture and auto brightness.
- com.homwee.upgrade, com.homwee.dmt.upgrade: firmware updates.
- com.dolby.android.audio.service, Play Store / Services / GSF, Gboard, WebView.

Android 12 (API 31), build SC.v6.6.3-20250328, security patch 2025-03-01. About 2 GB RAM, 1080p, Ethernet.
ro.product.manufacturer=wnc, ro.product.model=Stream TV, ro.adb.secure=1. A streaming box: HDMI out only, no inputs.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/verizon-stream-tv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/verizon-stream-tv/debloat.txt com.verizon.tv.launcher
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Applied in small batches on 2026-10-20 with a screenshot after each, then a custom launcher installed and
the real remote pressed after each batch. Not yet lived with for days; if something breaks, re-enable it with
`pm enable <package>` and please report it.

Stock launcher: com.verizon.tv.launcher (HomeActivity). Home claimants: the Verizon launcher and
com.android.tv.settings FallbackHome (-1000). setupwraith does NOT claim Home here. Live TV app: com.google.android.tv
(TvActivity; set it as live_tv_package). The box has no HDMI or tuner inputs. Live Channels is EMPTY unless an app
registers a TV input: with Pluto TV (tv.pluto.android, LiveTVInputService) enabled, Inputs > Live TV shows its channels
(checked); with Pluto disabled there was nothing, and live_tv_package is better left empty. Tablo and IPTV apps are
standalone apps (own guide), they do not feed Live Channels.
Already disabled at the factory, so not listed (restore.sh would turn them ON): com.google.android.tvlauncher,
com.google.android.tvrecommendations, com.google.android.feedback, com.google.android.play.games.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the TV:
- Port 5555 opened with USB debugging and Network debugging on; stock adb and tools/tv.py both worked, with an
"Allow USB debugging?" prompt on the first connect. Sideloading works (pm install -r), including a package that
declares HOME; a base-only reinstall of a split APK gives INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE, which is not a block.
- The remote is a Bluetooth remote. To pair a new one, hold OK + Apps (bottom right button) together for 6 seconds and release;
the "Pairing your remote" screen is part of the stock launcher. Its buttons: D-pad, OK, Back, Home, Apps (sends
KEYCODE_APP_SWITCH), Mic (KEY_SEARCH), Mute, Play/Pause, Volume. No app buttons. Non-functional buttons: INPUT, center color button
- With the stock launcher off the Apps button does nothing. The custom launcher answers it through HomeKeyService
(HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1) once it also accepts KEYCODE_APP_SWITCH.
- The TV installed a firmware update (Android 10 QTT8.201201.004 to this build) while the work was in progress, so keep
the OTA package if you want updates. A new build removed com.bc360.*, com.omni.sci, org.lineageos.tvcustomizer and
added com.wnc.wnclogger, com.wnc.logger_provider_1 and com.wnc.tvcustomizer.
- com.verizon.tv.ams records app, screen and power events (AppState, Screen, TurnOff, Health) in a local event table
and ships Firebase Crashlytics. Disabling it left the remote, Bluetooth pairing and Home working.
- Screenshots work on Home and in apps. AdGuard Private DNS (dns.adguard-dns.com) works and YouTube still loads.

Kept on purpose: com.omni.ota (firmware updates, by owner's choice), com.omni.simplesetup, com.google.android.tv
(Live TV), tv.pluto.android (Pluto TV: the only TV input on this box, see the Live TV note above), com.google.android.tv.remote.service (phone remote), com.google.android.inputmethod.latin (keyboard),
Play Store, Play Services, Bluetooth, com.droidlogic.* and com.android.tv.settings, Netflix, Prime Video, YouTube,
Disney+, Hulu.
Left alone because their purpose is unclear from their components: com.wnc.wnclogger, com.wnc.logger_provider_1
(holds INTERNET), com.wnc.tvcustomizer.

mau.ten: Vidda C1S 4K laser projector (Hisense sub-brand; device MT9669, board m7642), Android 9,
mau.header:
Vidda C1S 4K laser projector (Hisense sub-brand; device MT9669, board m7642), Android 9,
build PPR2.180905.006.A1 (02.02.60.02), VIDAA 6.6, China JuUI. 3.6 GB RAM, 1080p UI.
Same com.jamdeo.* / com.hisense.* namespace as examples/vidda-mt9653/, an older and
stricter firmware: several of its locks are documented below.
Stock launcher: com.jamdeo.tv.vod (聚好看 JuUI). It STAYS ENABLED on this list — see
the Home-key note. The C1S kept 聚好看 as Home; on the C1 unit (below) the reference
launcher took the Home key with 聚好看 still enabled, see README.md in this folder.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<projector ip> tools/disable.sh examples/vidda-c1s-mt9669/debloat.txt
Undo:    tools/restore.sh examples/vidda-c1s-mt9669/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

ADB: unlike the MT9653 sets, ro.adb.secure=1. Turning on debugging shows "允许 USB 调试吗?"
on screen and the host's key must be confirmed there (勾选一律允许) before adb works.

The firmware ships a package install blacklist (settings global install_black_list; it
names Dangbei launcher, IPTV loaders, TVBox forks), but it is not enforced on adb
installs — sideloading works. Launchers are fought differently: PackageManager keeps
resolving HOME to com.jamdeo.tv.vod no matter what. cmd package set-home-activity
reports Success and writes a preferred record (dumpsys package shows it), yet
resolve-activity and real Home launches still return the stock launcher.
persist.vt.use_home_pkg is shell-writable here but empty by default and the Home key
ignores it.

Home key: third-party accessibility services receive window changes for ordinary apps
but NONE for com.jamdeo.tv.vod — Aerial's unpatched Home Guard never sees 聚好看 come to
the front (the binding is not deaf: events for other apps arrive; only the launcher is
shielded). UsageStats still records its MOVE_TO_FOREGROUND with the right class, so
Aerial works once foregroundCheck runs on every Android version instead of SDK <= M:
one-line patch proposed upstream in pengchujin/aerial-tv#545 (applies to 1.47). With
that build, Home from any app lands on 聚好看 and is brought back to Aerial in about a
second; boot goes straight to Aerial. Keep the stock launcher enabled — it stays the
system Home, plays its content from Aerial's grid, and gives the Home key somewhere to
land that the guard can see. 聚好看 renders normally with both ad sidecars below
disabled (screenshot-checked).

⚠ com.hisense.tv.tiletransition is NOT in this list on purpose: it hosts
TileAnimationService, which the source panel binds to before switching inputs. Disabled,
picking HDMI does nothing (same as the mt9653 note). Re-enabling fixes it immediately.

Voice is deliberately kept on this list (the owner uses the mic): keylab.speech.view.vidaa
and the whole com.keylab / iflytek / hisense voice stack stay enabled — unlike
examples/vidda-mt9653/, which trades the voice UI for removing its second home screen.
On this firmware that app raises no home-screen problem worth the loss.

The active screensaver was the desk clock (com.google.android.deskclock), not the ad
screensaver below; aerial's install.sh switches screensaver_components to Aerial's
dream, so com.jamdeo.screensaver disables safely.

Verified: applied in three batches (telemetry/push, ads/screensaver, factory leftovers)
with a focus check between batches, then two cold reboots. Home, Wi-Fi, casting, IMEs,
Bluetooth remote, voice, 聚好看 playback all checked the same day; not yet lived with
for weeks.

Second unit: Vidda C1 4K tri-colour laser projector (China), the same device MT9669, board
m7642 and build PPR2.180905.006.A1 (02.02.60.02), VIDAA 6.6, 3.6 GB, ro.adb.secure=1.
Nothing was disabled at the factory on this one. No Aerial: the active screensaver stayed
the desk clock, so com.jamdeo.screensaver is not the dream either; the screensaver timeout
was not waited out after disabling it. Two packages the C1S notes do not name were found
and disabled (cloudfalcon, fusion.android.tv.demo, marked C1 below); the owner's own picks
are the commented block at the end. Applied in six batches with a screenshot between them,
then reboot-checked twice on 2026-11-01: every entry stayed disabled; Wi-Fi, the source
panel and the Bluetooth remote kept working (casting was not tried), and free memory went
from about 1.87 GB to 2.38 GB. The 双11 skin and side banner on 聚好看's home
went with the ad services; its sponsored rows did not. Not yet lived with for days.

mau.ten: Vidda VIDAA_TV (Hisense sub-brand; device MT9653, board mt5879), Android TV 11, build
mau.header:
Vidda VIDAA_TV (Hisense sub-brand; device MT9653, board mt5879), Android TV 11, build
RP1A.200720.011 (02.02.70.01). Vidda is Hisense's youth sub-brand, sold in China with 聚好看 JuUI:
the model string is VIDAA_TV and the package namespace is com.jamdeo.* / com.hisense.*, so it shares
nothing with the export Hisense lists in this folder (com.hisense.evservice, com.mediatek.*).
3.8 GB RAM, 41 GB storage, UI at 1080p / 320 dpi.
Same build as examples/hisense-e5q-pro/, a smaller list that keeps the stock home.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/vidda-mt9653/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/vidda-mt9653/debloat.txt com.jamdeo.tv.vod
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

ADB: turning USB debugging on opens network ADB on 5555 directly; no wireless pairing needed.
ro.adb.secure=0, so the TV does not even show "Allow USB debugging?" — any device on the LAN gets a
shell with no prompt. Close the port when you are done, or keep the TV on a trusted network only.

⚠ com.hisense.tv.tiletransition is NOT in this list on purpose. Its name reads like a transition or
boot-ad layer, but it hosts TileAnimationService, which the vendor source panel binds to before it
switches inputs. Disabled, the panel still opens and still animates, but picking HDMI does nothing:
W/ActivityManager: Unable to start service Intent {
act=com.hisense.tv.tiletransition.TileAnimationService
pkg=com.hisense.tv.tiletransition } not found
W/a: switchToAppViaRemote, no service found
Re-enabling it fixes input switching immediately. This is the "package names often don't say what a
package does" warning in PROMPT.md, made concrete.

Stock launcher: com.jamdeo.tv.vod (JuUI). launcher/build-and-install.sh does not know that name:
TV_HOST=<tv ip> HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 STOCK_LAUNCHER=com.jamdeo.tv.vod launcher/build-and-install.sh
Enabling it again (pm enable) makes the TV reclaim Home even after an explicit set-home-activity;
to go back, disable it first and set Home afterwards.

Remote Home key: the physical button is Linux scancode 102, but the keylayout maps it to
KEYCODE_F12 (142), and the vendor SysUIMerge app used that to switch to the previous app — which was
the stock launcher until it got disabled, so Home stopped working. WARNING: the fix the author tested
(a home_key_scancodes=[102] option for HomeKeyService) is not in the launcher on main yet, so with the
stock launcher disabled the remote's Home button does nothing until that option lands. Injected
KEYCODE_HOME cannot test it: the vendor framework swallows injected keycode 3 and the scancode is 0.

Second vendor home: com.keylab.speech.view.vidaa hosts com.ju.secondscreen.HomeActivity, started by
component name at boot, so it takes the foreground even though Home resolves to your launcher. It
carries a "39% memory boost" nag, music/video card rows and a NewTV badge. Component-level disable is
refused (SecurityException from setEnabledSetting), so this list disables the whole package instead:
that also removes the voice-assistant UI (AgentDisplayService, ViewService, SIWindowMonitorService,
memo, task master) and the remote's mic key. Re-enable it if voice matters more than the card home.

Inputs menu: dumpsys tv_input is empty on this firmware (no TvInputManager inputs), so the launcher's
Inputs pill uses source_panel_service = com.hisense.tv.inputs/com.hisense.tv.InputsUIService with
action com.hisense.tv.start_inputs. That panel does perform the switch itself. With nothing to list,
showInputs() now opens it on the first OK instead of showing a one-row dropdown.

Debloat does NOT change the visual home screen on this set: the sponsored rows and the VIP banner are
fetched by com.jamdeo.tv.vod itself, not by the ad sidecars this list disables. Only the launcher swap
removes them. What this list buys is the telemetry, the push channel, the persistent poller and the
stray ad processes.

Verified: applied in batches with a screenshot between them, then two cold reboots. Home survived,
Wi-Fi (owned by android.uid.system) survived, casting, the input panel, the IME, Bluetooth pairing and
the remote all still work. Applied and reboot-verified on day one; not yet lived with for weeks.

mau.ten: Vision 2024VISION43STV (CVTE TP.T950D4T.PB751, Amlogic T950D4), Android 13 (SDK 33), Europe.
mau.header:
Vision 2024VISION43STV (CVTE TP.T950D4T.PB751, Amlogic T950D4), Android 13 (SDK 33), Europe.
1 GB RAM, 1920x1080 at 240 dpi (1280x720 dp UI). Not Google TV: CVTE's own launcher
(com.cvte.tv.launcher.space, "LauncherSpace4") and CVTE settings (com.cvte.settings); no stock
Android settings, so Developer options are unreachable. Build fingerprint is spoofed
(google/shamu/...), so don't use it to match your set; match the board name instead.
Tested on one set for a day, not yet a few days; launcher half done too.
Stock launcher: com.cvte.tv.launcher.space (pass it to restore.sh, as the Undo line below does).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/vision-2024vision43stv/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/vision-2024vision43stv/debloat.txt com.cvte.tv.launcher.space
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Kept on purpose: com.cvte.tv.api.impl (TIF player, hotkeys),
com.cvte.tv.setting (the live-TV UI: CH+/-, number keys, info banner), com.cvte.tv.globalui (source
menu), com.cvte.tvservice, com.droidlogic.* (tvinput, dtvkit), com.cvte.fac.menu, com.cvte.factory.*.

ADB: factory menu. Switch to a source first (TV or HDMI; it does not open from the launcher), then on
the remote (H620DF-DS) press MENU 1 1 4 7 quickly -> DEBUG -> ADB ENABLE -> ON. Don't touch SHIPPING
INIT / BOARD INIT (factory reset), AGING MODE, PANEL SETTING, EMC SETTING or SW UPGRADE. Network ADB
on 5555 then has NO authorisation (ro.adb.secure empty, no prompt) and survives reboots until it is
switched OFF in the same menu.

Screenshots: screencap returns 0 bytes ("FB is protected") whenever a TV SurfaceView is on screen,
and that includes the stock launcher, which embeds a live-TV preview. Open Settings for real ones.
pm disable state is written to disk with a delay: wait ~30 s before rebooting.

STOCK LAUNCHER - READ BEFORE DISABLING IT. This firmware has no FallbackHome. At boot the user is still
locked (FBE) and only a direct-boot-aware Home can start; the stock launcher is one, a normal launcher
is not. With the stock launcher disabled and a non-direct-boot-aware Home, boot never completes: black
screen, LED on, remote and power key dead, no Wi-Fi (sys.boot_completed empty, dumpsys user shows
State: BOOTING, "No home screen found for Intent { act=MAIN cat=[HOME,COMMON_HOME] }").
The new Home needs android:directBootAware="true" on the activity (application-level alone did not
mark it), prefs in createDeviceProtectedStorageContext(), and a reload on ACTION_USER_UNLOCKED.
Recovery: LAN cable straight into a laptop. Android's Ethernet asks for DHCP; answer it from the
laptop's 169.254.x.x address (only for the TV's MAC) and adb connects. Then pm enable the stock
launcher and am start -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME
-c android.intent.category.COMMON_HOME.

Launcher notes for this firmware (the stock launcher did these jobs):
- Home key sends MAIN + HOME + COMMON_HOME (CvteHomeManager, ro.CVT_EN_COMMON_HOME_INTENT=1):
the new launcher needs a second intent-filter with android.intent.category.COMMON_HOME.
- Inputs: no standard passthrough handler. Use
am start -a com.cvte.intent.ACTION_TIF_PLAYER
-n com.cvte.tv.api.impl/com.cvte.tv.api.vendor.common.base.tif.TvSupportActivity
--ez tune true --ei sourceId N --es toActivity com.cvte.tv.setting.TvSettingActivity
N is the number after /HW in dumpsys tv_input: DTV (DTVKit, the scanned DVB-T channels) 19,
HDMI1/2/3 5/6/7, AV 1. 16 (ADTV) is a second tuner with no channels.
sys.current.source.name does not update; check dumpsys tv_input | grep -A2 sessionStateMap.
- Channel keys and numbers are handled by com.cvte.tv.setting/.TvSettingActivity, not the player.
Without toActivity, CH+/- do nothing. At power-on CVTE starts only the player, so an accessibility
service opens the TV UI when TvSupportActivity comes up on its own (same intent with tune=false).
- Input/Source key: an accessibility key filter maps KEYCODE_TV_INPUT to
com.cvte.tv.globalui/.InputSourceActivity. Injected keys bypass the filter; test the real remote.
- Wi-Fi network belongs to android.uid.system (cname=android.uid.system:1000), so the setup wizard
(com.droidlogic.setupwizard) is not a Wi-Fi risk; it did not claim Home once setup was done.
- Boot logo and animation can't be turned off without root.

mau.header:
Vu 4K (ro.product.model "VU 4K", device lushan, manufacturer HVCL, MediaTek), Google TV / Android 12
(SDK 31), firmware STT2.230929.001.080. Sold in India. About 1.8 GB RAM.
Vu's own packages use the com.vt prefix (the same VIDAA/Hisense stack as examples/hisense-smarttv-4k-ffm,
with many com.hisense class names inside).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/vu-4k-lushan/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/vu-4k-lushan/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (build-and-install.sh finds and disables it; do not
list it here, it must go only after the new launcher is running). Live TV app: com.vt.tv.tvcenter (set it
as live_tv_package and hide it in launcher config.xml). HDMI 1-3 and AV come from com.vt.source.external.
Already disabled at the factory, so not listed: com.mediatek.tis, com.mediatek.dtv.tvinput.isdbtuner,
com.vt.source.tuner.

USB debugging alone opens port 5555 (no wireless-debugging pairing needed). With the new launcher, the
remote's Input key still opens Vu's own input panel (com.vt.tv.input), so INPUT_KEY_SERVICE is not needed.
Tested on the day of the debloat (2026-10-19), not yet lived with for days: two reboots, both normal;
HDMI switching from the launcher's Inputs menu (opens com.vt.tv.tvcenter); apps launch from the dock.

Do NOT disable com.vt.tv.smartsense, com.vt.tv.smartsense.ui or com.vt.tv.aiot: on the Hisense with the
same stack, disabling them sent the TV to Android Recovery on the next boot.
Kept on purpose: com.vt.tvservice, com.vt.avmiddleware, com.vt.edv.drmp, com.vt.tv.commonui,
com.vt.tv.input, com.vt.tv.videocolor (picture settings), com.vt.eula (consent state other apps read),
com.vt.tv.protector, com.vt.tv.customerlauncher, com.vt.udpserver, com.vt.fte, tv.mopa.ginga,
com.vt.tv.mediacenter (USB media player), com.vt.tv.dlna, the factory apps (com.vt.factory,
com.factory.tv.at, com.at.factory.androidtvaidlservice), com.mediatek.*.
Firmware updates left ON: com.vt.tv.ota, com.vt.remoteupgrade, com.vt.tv.usbota.
Casting left ON by choice: Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), AirPlay (com.mediatek.AirplayAPK,
airplaydaemon, partner.airplay_sys, com.vt.tv.airplaykeycheck), Miracast (com.vt.tv.mobiledeviceconnectiontips).
Google Assistant (com.google.android.katniss) left ON by choice.

Applied on 2026-10-19 (first unit, v2.3 launcher) and 2026-10-21..2026-10-26 (second unit, five days
of daily use across cold reboots): Home, D-pad navigation, launching apps from the dock, Bluetooth
audio, projector autofocus/keystone and casting all verified. Nothing re-enabled itself after reboot.

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. setupwraith .RecoveryActivity also claims HOME
(priority 1): with only launcherx disabled, Home went to it and it restarted itself every ~60 ms.
Disabling just that component is refused (SecurityException), so the whole package is in this list.

Quirks on this firmware, all checked on the device:
- USB debugging opened port 5555 without pairing. After a reboot it was closed again until
debugging was toggled back on (Wireless debugging also offers a random port with pairing).
- The Wi-Fi network had been saved during first setup, so disabling setupwraith deleted it and the
projector dropped off the network mid-command. Rejoining from the projector's own Wi-Fi settings
fixed it, and the network then belonged to android.uid.system. Check first:
`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'`.
- `adb install` over Wi-Fi hung; most likely Play Protect's prompt was waiting behind the screensaver.
Pushing the APK as base64 chunks and running `pm install` worked. Wake the screen before installing.
- com.android.devicelockcontroller is protected: `pm disable-user` is refused.
- Second unit (remote buttons): `com.sdt.globalkey` routes the remote's four app buttons and Settings
gear to launcherx. Once launcherx is disabled, the Settings gear emits KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION (83) and
the four app buttons emit KEYCODE_STEM_1 (265, Netflix), KEYCODE_STEM_2 (266, YouTube),
KEYCODE_F8 (138, Prime Video) and KEYCODE_F6 (136, Disney+). Enabling HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 and
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 with `settings_key_keycodes` `[83]` and `app_keys` for `265`, `266`, `138` and
`136` restores all five buttons. The projector's physical autofocus and keystone buttons are handled
by `com.sdt.projector.observer` and keep working without launcherx.

Kept on purpose: com.sdt.projector.observer (projector accessibility service, autofocus and keystone),
com.mft.rcupair (remote pairing), com.sdt.globalkey (remote hot keys), com.mft.frontpanelledsservice,
com.google.android.tv.dfuservice (remote firmware and backlight), com.droidlogic.* (Amlogic settings
and connected devices), com.dolby.android.audio.service, the keyboard, Play Store, Play Services.
Kept by choice here (safe to add if you don't use them; all tested for five days on the second unit):
com.google.android.apps.mediashell (Chromecast), com.sdt.ota and com.sdt.upgrade (firmware updates),
com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx (Ambient screensaver, can be replaced with ClockDream).

Tested for one session (a few hours) on 2026-10-24, including one reboot, not the several days
CONTRIBUTING asks for. Every entry was applied and checked on the real unit; what has not been
proven is that nothing surfaces after days of use. See README.md in this folder.

Same board (altai) as examples/xgimi-mogo-3-pro, one firmware build older, so that list applies
closely. Differences on this unit: com.nbcast.wirelessscreen (MagiCast) is replaced by
com.xgimi.starmirror, com.xgimi.screensaver and com.google.android.videos are not present, and
nothing was disabled from the factory (com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic ships enabled here).

Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (HOME priority 2), with the setup wizard's
RecoveryActivity at priority 1, so setupwraith is listed below.
setupwraith owned one saved Wi-Fi network, a phone hotspot, and NOT the network the projector was
using: `dumpsys wifi` showed cname=android.uid.system:1000 on the entry with
"Currently Connected: true". Checking which entry is connected before trusting disable.sh's
skip message is worth it; FORCE_SETUPWRAITH=1 was used after that check, and ADB and Wi-Fi held.
Only the unused hotspot entry was lost.

Launcher notes (applied and verified on a real unit on 2026-10-24):
- Install with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1, and put this in config.xml or a theme's config.json
(config.json in this folder has them):
"live_tv_package": ""                    no tuner
"columns": 5
"settings_key_keycodes": [83]            the gear button sends KEYCODE_NOTIFICATION
"app_keys": ["KEYCODE_F4:com.google.android.youtube.tv",
"KEYCODE_F9:com.netflix.ninja",
"KEYCODE_F8:com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom"]
"stock_home_redirect": "com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx"
- THE STOCK LAUNCHER DOES NOT STAY DISABLED. launcherx re-enabled itself across the reboot and
again within minutes of being disabled during use (XGIMI's com.xgimi.xrmservice, as on the
MoGo 3 Pro). Do not re-disable it after every boot: stock_home_redirect is what holds the new
home screen. Measured: with HomeKeyService unbound, one press of Home landed on the stock
Google TV launcher. Disabling only its home activity
(`pm disable --user 0 com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx/.home.HomeActivity`) is refused with
a SecurityException on this firmware, so package-level disable plus the redirect is the only route.
- HOME_KEY_SERVICE costs volume-key auto-repeat on this firmware: holding volume up/down moves one
step instead of ramping, the same CAPABILITY_CAN_FILTER_KEY_EVENTS mechanism as
docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md (dumpsys accessibility shows capabilities=8). Holding a
D-pad direction still repeats normally; only the volume keys were affected. Unlike the sets in
that note, the helper is not optional here: dropping it gives the stock launcher back (above),
so the trade is the new launcher against the volume ramp, not buttons against the volume ramp.
The owner kept the helper.
- HDMI 1 (the only port) opens through com.google.android.tv.inputplayer from the Inputs menu, so
no input_action is needed (unlike the Horizon S Pro).

Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

A streaming box: no HDMI-in or tuner, so the Inputs menu has nothing to list; set live_tv_package empty in
config.xml. Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (the scripts' default).

Notes from this box:
- Leave alone: com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer (receives the remote's shortcut buttons as
GLOBAL_BUTTON, and runs the remote-pairing steps of setup), mitv.service (Xiaomi TvServer, persistent),
com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith (remote pairing), com.droidlogic* (Amlogic system, Bluetooth).
- USB debugging alone opens network ADB on port 5555 (service.adb.tcp.port=5555).
- USB debugging CUTS POWER to the USB port: with sys.usb.config=adb, /vendor/etc/init/hw/init.amlogic.usb.rc
writes 0xFDFFFFFF to register 0xc883443c and the port switches to ADB device mode, so a USB speaker or drive
goes dead; sys.usb.config=mtp (debugging off) writes 0xFD7FFFFF and powers it again. Turn debugging off when done.
- cmd package set-home-activity needs the component on Android 9 (com.gathin.tvhome/.MainActivity).
- Location is off, so Android 9 hides the Wi-Fi name from apps and the launcher's pill just says "Wi-Fi".
- Remote (Vendor_2717_Product_32b9): the Netflix key still opens Netflix; BUTTON_2 opened Live Channels and
does nothing once it is disabled; BUTTON_3/4 and ALL_APPS did nothing even on stock. No crashes either way.
- Survives a reboot: nothing is re-enabled at boot, the launcher stays Home. Free RAM after boot went from
about 770 MB to 1.15 GB.
- A process of the disabled stock launcher can linger until the next reboot; `am force-stop` clears it.

Second unit (same PI.3933 build), 2026-10-21. Details: docs/devices/xiaomi-mi-box-s.md
- Every package below was present and disabled cleanly; nothing was re-enabled after a reboot.
- Nothing was disabled beforehand: the "already disabled" apps at the bottom were all enabled there.
Google Play Music (com.google.android.music, closed in 2020) was installed too.
- The saved Wi-Fi belonged to android.uid.system, not setupwraith; setupwraith was not needed.
- The Apps button (scancode 580, ALL_APPS) opens Home with the launcher's HomeKeyService
(build-and-install -HomeKeyService). Home, Back, voice and Netflix work without it.
- On remotes with a Live button (scancode 399), disabling com.google.android.tv triggers
partnercustomizer to open Google Play unless remapped via app_keys ("scan:399:<package>",
build-and-install -InputKeyService).

Third unit (same PI.3933 build), Turkey, 2026-09-17 to 2026-10-24 (37 days):
- Xiaomi's update service enables PatchWall again. Its component applife.LifeKeeper installs
com.mitv.tvhome.atv again about 3 minutes after you disable it. The install changes the package
state to enabled. Logcat shows "PatchWallUpdateService: ... LifeKeeper ... package:com.mitv.tvhome.atv
event:INSTALL". On this unit, PatchWall was disabled in one batch and the updater in a later batch.
- For this reason, this list disables the update service before PatchWall. After the updater was disabled,
PatchWall stayed disabled for 37 days and after each reboot.
- Five minutes after you apply the list, do a check: compare `pm list packages -d` with this file.

Fifth unit (same PI.3933 build), 2026-10-25. Details: docs/devices/xiaomi-mi-box-s.md

step instead of ramping, the same trade as docs/devices/tcl-55p71b-g09-key-repeat.md. Checked on the

Notes from this box:
- The stock adb on macOS connected fine on port 5555 once USB debugging was on; no wireless-debugging
pairing and no tools/tv.py needed.
- Disabling launcherx alone makes Home resolve to setupwraith's RecoveryActivity; `cmd package
set-home-activity` reports Success but does not take effect until setupwraith is disabled too.
- Right after disabling setupwraith, Wi-Fi dropped for about 20 seconds and the box asked for the Wi-Fi
password again. Once it was re-entered, it stayed saved across a reboot.
- 772: forgetting and re-joining the network was not enough for tools/disable.sh: `dumpsys wifi` still
listed a second, older saved network (a hidden one from first setup) with cname=setupwraith. Forget that
one too (`cmd wifi list-networks` shows its id, `cmd wifi forget-network <id>`), then the guard passes
and Wi-Fi stays up when the wizard is disabled.
- 772: Prime Video (com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom) came back enabled after the first reboot and again
after the stock launcher was started once; the firmware (or Play) re-enables it. Disable it again or
hide it from the launcher with hidden_apps; tools/check.py reports it as drift.
- After living with it: Wi-Fi, USB playback (with debugging off), Google Home, the phone remote,
Chromecast from a Pixel and Google Assistant all still work. On 737, display is 1920x1080 UI
with Settings > Tela e som > Resolução = 4k 60Hz (video 4K, HDR none on Philco 2016 EDID).
- The remote's shortcut buttons (Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Xiaomi TV+, Apps) all do nothing once
launcherx is disabled. Prime Video and Xiaomi TV+ are disabled anyway; Netflix, YouTube and Apps were
handled by launcherx, as on the Chromecast with Google TV (see that list for a Key Mapper remap).
The launcher brings them back: the Bluetooth remote ("Xiaomi RC", Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl) sends
Netflix as KEY_VIDEOPHONE -> 193 (BUTTON_6), YouTube as KEY_PRESENTATION -> 190 (BUTTON_3) and Prime
Video as KEY_PLAY -> 194 (BUTTON_7). app_keys 193:com.netflix.ninja, 190:<youtube app>,
194:<any app> with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 launcher/build-and-install.sh; checked on 737 with the real
remote (190 sent to SmartTube, 194 to Nuvio). The remote sleeps after a few seconds and drops the
first press that wakes it, so press OK before each button while reading them with getevent -lt.
772, from /vendor/usr/keylayout/Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl: Xiaomi TV+ is KEY_WWW -> scan 150 ->
BUTTON_5 (192), Apps is KEY_CHAT -> scan 216 -> ALL_APPS (284), and there is a Settings key at scan 577
(SETTINGS, 176) that this remote has no button for. The Apps button makes a good quick-settings button:
settings_key_keycodes 284 with settings_key_panel and HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 (Android itself grabs ALL_APPS
before any app window sees it, so the Home helper has to filter it). With both helpers enabled a mapped
button fires twice (a mute toggled back at once); enable one of them, HOME_KEY_SERVICE reads app_keys too.

untested disabled, so it stays a comment under Telemetry),

use the Netflix/YouTube/Prime shortcut keys; tested disabled on 737 with no other effect), mitv.service,

Notes from this firmware:
- Default IME is already Gboard, so the Mi TV 4A missing-keyboard quirk doesn't apply.
- The remote's Home button sends KEYCODE_ALL_APPS (284), not HOME. Android 9 sends that key only
to the system launcher, so with tvlauncher disabled Home does nothing. Fix: install with
HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 TV_HOST=<tv ip> launcher/build-and-install.sh
which enables the launcher's HomeKeyService. Android switches it off on every reinstall,
so always pass HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1.
`input keyevent 284` over adb skips the accessibility filter; test with the real remote.
- No HDMI/AV inputs: the launcher hides its Inputs pill by itself on this stick.
- Kept on this set: voice assistant (katniss/pumpkin), Chromecast (mediashell),
Mi Cast (com.mitv.milinkservice) and firmware updates (com.xiaomi.mitv.updateservice).

Second verified set (Indonesia-region unit, same firmware PI.2055, in daily use since
21 Oct 2026 with Netflix / Jellyfin / SmartTube / Vidio): the groups marked
"second set" below are disabled on that stick on top of the original list.
Region note: the ID unit has only the misspelled autoinstalls package below, and
none of the preloaded apps in the original list (DAZN, Red Bull TV, Duo, TCL browser).

Third verified set (France unit, same firmware PI.2055, patch 2022-08-05, debloated 21 Oct 2026; the group
marked "third set" below is on top of the original list, plus voice, Chromecast, Mi Cast, the phone remote and
the updater off by the owner's choice). Notes from that unit:
- The Home key arrived as KEYCODE_HOME (3), not ALL_APPS: `interceptKeyTq keycode=3` in logcat, then HOME
started the launcher. HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 was used anyway and does no harm; check your remote's revision.
- The Netflix key is Xiaomi keycode 1001, consumed by the system in interceptKeyBeforeQueueing without
POLICY_FLAG_PASS_TO_USER, which launches Netflix itself. Accessibility services never see it, so it cannot
be remapped (app_keys, Button Mapper) without root; with Netflix disabled the key just does nothing.
- Closing ADB: switching off "USB debugging" alone, then rebooting, left 5555 open. Switching off the
Developer options master switch and rebooting closed it (tools/adb-closed.py: refused).
- Free memory: about 150 MB stock, about 265 MB right after a reboot with the list and the launcher.

Fourth verified set (Peru unit, older firmware PI.1241, debloated 29 Oct 2026 with the launcher, HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1
and a dock of Netflix / YouTube / Disney+ / Prime Video). Every uncommented line below that this firmware has was
disabled, except setupwraith; the commented-out ones (voice, Mi Cast, the updater) stayed enabled, and so did
Chromecast. Notes from that unit:
- setupwraith owned the saved Wi-Fi network (`dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'` showed
cname=com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith), so it stayed enabled: disabling it would have taken the stick off
Wi-Fi and ADB. Check this before applying the list as it is.
- Not installed on PI.1241: android.autoinstalls.config.xiaomi.mibox3 (only the "xioami" one is), com.dazn, Red Bull TV,
Duo, the TCL browser, com.mitv.tvhome.atv, com.mitv.download.service, com.mitv.videoplayer, com.xm.webcontent and
Alphonso. tools/disable.sh reports those lines and goes on.
- After the last batch, `sync` and a 15 s wait were not enough: after the reboot the last eight packages
were enabled again. Disabling them again and waiting about 40 s before the reboot kept all of them.
- The real Home button returned to the launcher with HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1.
- Closing ADB: revoking the USB debugging authorisations, switching off the Developer options master switch and
rebooting closed 5555 (tools/adb-closed.py: refused), as on the third set.

Notes from this box:
- The stock home is com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx. launcher/build-and-install.sh disables it.
- setupwraith's RecoveryActivity (HOME priority 1, launcherx 2, a sideloaded launcher 0) takes Home once
launcherx is off, so setupwraith has to go too, and it has to go FIRST. Redone in that order (setupwraith,
then launcherx), Home went straight to the new launcher. This is the same crash-loop xiaomi-tv-a-pro-2026
describes. Re-enable setupwraith to re-pair the remote.
- Disabling setupwraith takes the box off Wi-Fi in either order if the network was saved during first setup:
that network belongs to setupwraith, and Android deletes it with the app. The first run here most likely lost
Wi-Fi this way; the redo stayed online because the network had been re-joined by hand in between. Seen on a
second box (V816.0.7.0.UZFAABX): disabling setupwraith alone, launcherx still Home, logged
"WifiConfigManager: Remove all networks for app ... setupwraith" and dropped Wi-Fi and ADB within a second.
The network re-joined in Settings is a new entry owned by android.uid.system and survived disabling
launcherx and dreamx. Check before disabling: tools/tv.py "dumpsys wifi" | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*'
- Leave alone: com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer, mitv.service, com.droidlogic*.
- With the stock launcher gone, apps without a dock slot just appear in the grid.

A second unit, same firmware (V816.0.11.0.UZFAABX), one evening and one reboot, applied this list with
YouTube Music, Assistant, Chromecast, Miracast/Mi share and the updater kept, plus the Privacy Sandbox group below:
- setupwraith owned no saved network here (every cname= was android.uid.system), so Wi-Fi and ADB stayed up.
- After the reboot, `pm list packages -d` matched what was disabled: the firmware re-enabled nothing.
- Wireless debugging leaves port 5555 open across reboots: switch off USB/Wireless debugging when done.
- Remote (Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl): once launcherx is off, Netflix (BUTTON_6) still opens Netflix, but
YouTube (BUTTON_3, scan 425), Prime Video (BUTTON_7, scan 207), Xiaomi TV+ (BUTTON_5, scan 150) and Apps
(ALL_APPS, scan 216) do nothing. config.json in this folder maps them back with app_keys, which needs
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1 when running build-and-install.sh. The real Home button worked without HOME_KEY_SERVICE.
- The volume buttons send IR to the TV: `getevent -lt` shows no event on the box while they are held, so a held
button not repeating is the TV's doing, with or without a key helper.
- Remote shortcut keys (Vendor_2717_Product_32b9.kl): YouTube sends BUTTON_3 (scancode 425), Prime Video sends
BUTTON_7 (scancode 207), and Apps button sends ALL_APPS (scancode 216). Enable HomeKeyService
(settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services com.gathin.tvhome/.HomeKeyService) and push
examples/xiaomi-mitv-afmu0/theme/config.json with tools/theme.sh to restore YouTube, map Prime Video, and make
the Apps button open Home. See README.md.

Notes from this firmware:
- Home: disabling com.mitv.tvhome drops HOME to com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome
(priority -1000 in the manifest, but it still wins once nothing else is left), which shows a
black screen. Keeping PatchWall enabled and setting the new launcher as the preferred home
works, and survives a reboot; PatchWall is then never shown. Verified with
`cmd package set-home-activity --user 0 com.gathin.tvhome/.MainActivity`.
- Standard settings intents DO resolve here: android.settings.SETTINGS ->
com.android.tv.settings/.MainSettings, android.settings.WIFI_SETTINGS ->
com.android.tv.settings/.connectivity.NetworkActivity. The launcher's pills need no fallback keys.
- Inputs: com.droidlogic.tvinput registers the ports (Hdmi1InputService/HW5,
Hdmi2/HW6, Hdmi3/HW7, AV1InputService/HW1), but nothing answers ACTION_VIEW on the standard
TvContract passthrough URI, so the launcher lists the ports without being able to switch them.
The TV app switches with EXTSRC_PLAY and an integer extra instead; see
docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-ansp0-jobs.txt.
- Network ADB (port 5555) closes on every reboot; re-enable it in
Settings -> 账号与安全 (Account & Security) -> ADB 调试 after each power cycle.
- `pm disable-user` is accepted for the shell user on this build (unlike MiTV-ANTL0, which needs
`pm hide`).
- mitv.service is the core MiTV service: do not touch it. It registers TvService, which Xiaomi's own
Settings reads the hardware configuration through; with it disabled, Settings freezes for 20-30 s and
then crashes the Sound page (#1310). Why:
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#xiaomi-cn-firmware-settings-freezes-or-crashes-after-the-debloat
- Voice: disabling voicecontrol, wakeupservice, the Mico MQTT service and the two Mi Home
packages also stops an external Xiao Ai speaker from controlling the TV (its "turn the TV
off" command). Verified both ways on this set; see the Voice group below.
- com.xiaomi.mitv.settings is the vendor settings UI; the standard com.android.tv.settings app is
also present and answers the plain settings actions.
- No Google apps at all. Content comes from CN streaming apps; casting (smartshare / miplay /
wfdsinkhelperservice / duokan.airkan.tvbox / upnp) and the app store are deliberately kept.
- com.mitv.care is disabled by the factory already.

Owner's-choice removals NOT listed below (disabled here, re-enable in Settings > Apps if needed):
com.douyu.xl.douyutv (Douyu), net.cibntv.ott.sk (CIBN 4K), com.lutongnet.nldmxXiaomiChildren
(children's training app) and one sideloaded tool.

Notes from this firmware:
- Same family as xiaomi-mitv-astp1; this list starts from that one, minus what this build lacks
(com.gitvdemo.video, com.duokan.videodaily, com.xiaomi.tv.gallery, com.newtv.cboxtv).
- No CN streaming apps preinstalled; no Google apps besides the YouTube and katniss the owner sideloaded.
- Network ADB (port 5555) closes on every reboot; re-enable it in
Settings -> Account & Security -> ADB debugging after each power cycle. Wi-Fi also sleeps in
standby, so the TV drops off the network until it is woken.
- mitv.service is the core MiTV service: do not touch it. The owner chose to drop payment, Mi Home,
Mi Video, the voice assistant and every casting receiver but AirPlay (in com.xiaomi.mitv.smartshare).
The app store and com.mitv.videoplayer (USB files) stay. It registers TvService, which Xiaomi's own
Settings reads the hardware configuration through; with it disabled, Settings freezes for 20-30 s and
then crashes the Sound page (#1310). Why:
docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#xiaomi-cn-firmware-settings-freezes-or-crashes-after-the-debloat
- com.xiaomi.mitv.remotecontroller.service looped at 100-190% CPU and flooded logd (~490 MB in
30 min): its relay host is gone, so it is disabled below. ES File Explorer ran DLNA and a WebView
in the background; it is replaced by Material Files (F-Droid, me.zhanghai.android.files).
- Home stays com.mitv.tvhome: set-home-activity succeeds but resolution ignores it, and with
com.mitv.tvhome disabled Home falls to com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome. Keep it
enabled; an accessibility service that answers the Home key (HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1) brings the new
launcher up instead.
- The firmware has no night mode setting: cmd uimode night yes|no|auto. Auto needs a location for
sunset and the TV has none, so it stays in day mode.
- The remote has no Input button; its Menu key (three lines) is KEYCODE_MENU, scancode 127. Inputs
switch only through Xiaomi's player: am start -a com.xiaomi.mitv.tvplayer.EXTSRC_PLAY
-n com.xiaomi.mitv.tvplayer/.ExternalSourceActivity --ei input N (HDMI1-3 = 23-25, AV = 2).
Starting the HDMI channel URI with a plain VIEW lets any app that claims every VIEW catch it.
- The time zone ships as Asia/Shanghai, an hour ahead in Vietnam. Set the one the IP locates
(get.geojs.io/v1/ip/geo.json "timezone"): service call alarm 3 s16 Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh
- Picture: Settings -> Image settings -> Display model is kept per source; "Picture" is the vivid
one (contrast 55, saturation 60, cold), "Standard" is flat.

`settings delete system boot_ad_switch`. Keep PatchWall enabled; the com.ts.launcher build does not take

Google TV 14 quirk: HOME is resolved by intent priority on this set. launcherx has priority 2,
the setup wizard's RecoveryActivity priority 1, and any third-party launcher priority 0.
Disabling launcherx alone causes Home presses to land on RecoveryActivity, which crash-loops
system_server (soft reboots every ~60 s, Wi-Fi drops). Disabling com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
allows CleanYourTV to take over Home cleanly, but it can cost casting (re-enable it if Cast stops working).
IMPORTANT: com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith owns the Wi-Fi network credentials if the TV was
configured via the Google Home app. Ensure Ethernet is connected or verify credentials before
disabling setupwraith, and re-enable it before a factory reset (restore.sh does this).

mau.header:
Xiaomi TV S Pro 100 Mini LED 2025 (小米电视 S Pro 100, L100MB-SP, MiTV-MFFU0, codename finch;
China-market firmware), Android 14 (SDK 34), firmware OS3.0.115.0.UFFMATV (HyperOS 3),
MediaTek mt5877, 4 GB RAM.
Disabled on 2026-10-20 in batches; after each batch Home, Xiaomi settings, HDMI 1 and the
screensaver were checked. All but com.xiaomi.tv.gallery (added last) were also checked after a reboot.
Stock launcher: com.mitv.tvhome (HOME activity .MainActivityUserMode). This list leaves it enabled;
disable it only after the allowlisted launcher build in "Home" below is installed.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mitv-mffu0/debloat.txt com.mitv.tvhome
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Notes from this firmware:
- Home: HyperOS keeps only system apps and package names on Xiaomi's third-party-home allowlist as
HOME candidates (ResolveIntentHelper.chooseBestActivity; the list is
/data/system/mitv_security_center.xml, pushed by cloud control, not readable from the shell). It is
the mechanism documented for MiTV-AETP0 (docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-aetp0-dofus.md). The standard
com.gathin.tvhome build installs and opens, but `cmd package set-home-activity` prints Success and
changes nothing, and with com.mitv.tvhome disabled Home lands on
com.xiaomi.mitv.settings/.entry.FallbackHome, a black screen.
What works: the launcher built under an allowlisted package name, with com.mitv.tvhome disabled.
This set has used it as Home since 2026-10-20, and boots straight into it: after a full reboot on
2026-10-22 the system started it as Home at systemReady, with no FallbackHome or chooser.
tools/tv.py 'pm path com.thunderstone.idun.dev'       # must print nothing
(cd launcher && ./gradlew assembleRelease -PlauncherApplicationId=com.thunderstone.idun.dev)
install the APK as in the AETP0 note, then: pm disable-user --user 0 com.mitv.tvhome
cmd package resolve-activity --brief -a android.intent.action.MAIN -c android.intent.category.HOME
-> com.thunderstone.idun.dev/com.gathin.tvhome.MainActivity
Unlike AETP0, the stock launcher must be disabled: with both enabled, Home opens the system's
launcher chooser, because a third-party preferred Home is refused. Re-enabling com.mitv.tvhome (as a
firmware update might) brings the chooser back; disabling it again restores the launcher.
The allowlist is printed at boot: `logcat -d | grep 'MitvConfigParser: \[White\]'` soon after a
boot gives <package>=<flags> lines, and Home needs the flag value 4 set (flags & 4). 42 of the 125
entries here have it, com.ts.launcher (511) among them, but only com.thunderstone.idun.dev (511) was
tested. The check is on the package name only, not the signature. tools/theme.sh and
launcher/build-and-install.sh still use com.gathin.tvhome; a theme overlay for this build goes in
/sdcard/Android/data/com.thunderstone.idun.dev/files/config.json.
Undo: pm enable com.mitv.tvhome, then remove com.thunderstone.idun.dev like any app you installed
(with both present Home shows the chooser).
- Network ADB (port 5555) closes on every reboot; re-enable it in
Settings -> 账号与安全 (Account & Security) -> ADB 调试 after each power cycle.
- Not touched: mitv.service, com.xiaomi.mitv.tvplayer (input switching, HDMI/AV/DTMB),
com.mediatek.* (TV inputs), com.xiaomi.mitv.settings (the only full settings UI),
com.xiaomi.mitv.smartpanel (the Menu-button panel), com.mitv.overseaservice and com.mi.bluetooth
(Bluetooth remote), com.sohu.inputmethod.sogou.tv (the only keyboard), the app store,
com.xiaomi.account, com.mitv.codec.update, com.xiaomi.mitv.mediaexplorer (USB/media browser).
- Kept by choice: XiaoAI voice (com.xiaomi.voicecontrol, com.xiaomi.wakeupservice), casting
(com.xiaomi.miplay, com.xiaomi.mitv.smartshare, com.xiaomi.mi_connect_service,
com.xiaomi.hyper_connect.tv), Mi Home (com.xiaomi.smarthome.tv), firmware updates
(com.xiaomi.mitv.upgrade), the Hyper screensaver (com.xiaomi.mitv.hyper.screensaver, com.xiaomi.tweather).
- com.mitv.tvhome takes the short-press power key on this build, and the two screensaver packages
(com.xiaomi.mitv.aod.screensaver, com.xiaomi.mitv.hyper.screensaver) draw the off screen: with the stock
launcher disabled as the Home section below does, the power button stops turning the TV off. The chain,
and the 2 s force-stop of every installed app that follows a screen-off with the settings key that
stops it: docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md#xiaomi-hyperos-3-the-power-key-does-nothing-and-music-stops-when-the-screen-goes-off
- A black screen right after a reboot with an HDMI-CEC set-top box plugged in is the box's CEC
"active source" switching the TV to its port (HdmiCecLocalDeviceTv), not this list. Home brings
the TV back; turning HDMI device control (CEC) off in the input settings stops it.
- Do not disable com.xiaomi.mitv.tvmanager ("TV Manager"): XiaoAI's "open <app>" runs through its
com.xiaomi.aicr.action.provider. Without it XiaoAI answers "OK" and nothing opens (logcat:
"Failed to find provider info for com.xiaomi.aicr.action.provider"). It was disabled here at first.
- MemAvailable went from about 1.57 GB to 1.77 GB with the stock launcher still running (measured
while TV Manager was also disabled).
- A firmware update may re-enable some of these; apply the list again afterwards.

docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mftr0-freeguy.txt.

mediaexplorer, videoplayer) with Netflix/YouTube/VieON still playing afterwards.

---- The remote's Input/Source button (#243, #1368) ----
It sends KEYCODE_MEDIA_RECORD (130, kernel KEY_RECORD), not KEYCODE_TV, so after the handover it does
nothing until the launcher is told to answer it. Either of these, in config.xml or a theme's config.json:
- "input_key_keycodes": [130] and "handle_view_inputs": true, built with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1. Checked on
the firmware 5135 unit: pressed inside another app, the button opens the launcher's Inputs menu (Home
comes to the front first).
- "app_keys": ["KEYCODE_MEDIA_RECORD:inputs"], with either key helper (HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 or
INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1). The "inputs" target opens the launcher's own Inputs menu directly, so
handle_view_inputs is not needed. Read from the launcher code (RemoteKeys), not yet tried on a MOOQ0.
Keep com.mediatek.hotkey.dispatcher enabled (it is in the keep list below): if `pm list packages -d`
shows it, `pm enable com.mediatek.hotkey.dispatcher`. Other app buttons (Netflix, Prime Video) are mapped
the same way, as "<keycode>:<package>" in app_keys; `getevent -l` shows what a button sends. Test with the
real remote: `input keyevent` skips the key helpers.

---- Android TV 11 variant: Xiaomi Mi TV P1 43" (MiTV-MOOQ0, croods, EU) ----
Firmware RTM4.220307.164.8835 (2026-10). The selected subset was applied and the TV remained
usable after a reboot; this does not claim every Android TV 10 entry was tested on Android TV 11.

---- Android TV 11, second unit: Xiaomi Mi TV Q1 75" QLED (L75M6-ESG, croods) ----
The label on the back reads L75M6-ESG; ADB reports MiTV-MOOQ0 / croods, on the same firmware as
the P1 43 above (RTM4.220307.164.8835). One session on 2026-10-24 (#1520), not a several-day

demo, com.xiaomi.tvqs.overseas below and tvrecommendations) plus the stock launcher, eleven in

Notes from this firmware:
- Before: swap full (200 of 200 MB) and over 200% iowait a few minutes after boot, so the UI froze.
After this list and the launcher: about 900 MB available instead of 570, swap nearly empty, no iowait.
The load average stays near 100 either way: MediaTek kernel threads (VMon_Task, DMX_Filt_Task,
hdcp22_hdmi_rx_) sit in D state permanently and count towards it while the CPU is idle.
- USB debugging alone opens port 5555; there is no network debugging toggle.
- Default IME is already Gboard and every package below exists on this build.
- The stock screensaver is com.mitv.dream/com.mitv.dream.MiDream, disabled below; point it elsewhere:
settings put secure screensaver_components com.gathin.tvhome/.ClockDream
- The voice assistant (katniss) does not stay disabled: at every boot the package manager rescans it
as an updated system app ("Expecting better updated system app for com.google.android.katniss"
in logcat -b events) and it comes back enabled, bound as voice_interaction_service. Disabling it is
all this list does. Beyond what this repo does, and your own call: removing it for user 0 and
clearing the voice services held across reboots here
settings put secure voice_interaction_service ''
settings put secure voice_recognition_service ''
pm uninstall --user 0 com.google.android.katniss
and is undone with
cmd package install-existing com.google.android.katniss
settings put secure voice_interaction_service com.google.android.katniss/.search.serviceapi.KatnissVoiceInteractionService
settings put secure voice_recognition_service com.google.android.katniss/com.google.android.apps.tvsearch.voice.recognition.KatnissRecognitionService
- Left alone on purpose: com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter / tvinput* (HDMI + tuner), mitv.service,
com.xiaomi.mitv.mediaexplorer (Media Player), com.google.android.tv.remote.service.
- Netflix, Prime Video, Pluto TV, YouTube Music and Chromecast kept by choice; com.mstar.netflixobserver
starts Netflix at boot (about 130 MB) and needs the same treatment as in examples/xiaomi-mitv-mssp3.

---- Physical Input/Source button (related to #1368; different model from MOOQ0) ----
Checked on MiTV-MSSP3 / machuca, Android TV 9, builds PI.7524 and PI.4663.
On PI.7524 the physical button sends KEYCODE_TV_INPUT (178). Xiaomi's
com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer/.GlobalKeyReceiver explicitly starts
com.google.android.tvlauncher/.inputs.InputsPanelActivity, which is unavailable after
the stock launcher is disabled. The Inputs pill still works, but the remote button does not.
Setting "handle_view_inputs": true alone did not fix the physical button on PI.7524.
Set "handle_view_inputs": true in config.xml or the theme's config.json and install
with INPUT_KEY_SERVICE=1. InputKeyService handles 178 already; no extra keycode is needed.
The owner confirmed the physical button works with that configuration on both builds;
pressing it from inside Spotify was checked on PI.7524. Injected keys do not test the helper.
Tradeoff observed on PI.7524: holding Volume Up advances just one step while the helper
is bound. The owner accepted this tradeoff in exchange for the Input shortcut.
These observations concern the remote-button setup only, not every package in this list.

Notes from this firmware (details in docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-mteq0-baymax.md):
- Home: the framework only accepts system apps or allowlisted package names as HOME, like the
MiTV-AETP0. The opt-in build -PlauncherApplicationId=com.ts.launcher (docs/devices/xiaomi-mitv-aetp0-dofus.md)
was accepted here: HOME resolved to it, also after a reboot and after a force-stop like the one
standby does. With the standard com.gathin.tvhome ID, disabling com.mitv.tvhome leaves
FallbackHome (a black screen).
- Network ADB closes at every boot: com.xiaomi.mitv.settings writes adb_enabled=0 a few seconds after
boot. Re-enable it under Settings > Account & Security > ADB debugging.
- Standby (power key) force-stops every non-system app after 2 s (MitvPowerManagerService ->
killAllThirdApp) unless a cloud allowlist exempts it. Android then drops any accessibility service
of those apps, so do not rely on an accessibility helper on this set.
- com.xiaomi.mitv.upgrade and com.mediatek.TimeMeasurementAgent are persistent: the firmware starts them
at boot even when disabled. Disabling still blocks their components; the processes stay.
- Shell cannot disable single components, `pm hide` (no MANAGE_USERS) or `pm uninstall --user 0`
(DELETE_FAILED_INTERNAL_ERROR) on this firmware, so whole-package disables are the only tool.
- Wi-Fi 5 GHz: the Wi-Fi country code comes from Settings.Global service_region and falls back to CN,
which hides 5 GHz networks on channels 100-144. `settings put global service_region <CC>` and a Wi-Fi
off/on fixes it.
- Xiaomi's package installer has no CONFIRM_INSTALL screen: stores that install split APKs through a
PackageInstaller session (Aptoide) hang at 80%. Stores using ACTION_VIEW (single APKs) work.
- No Google services: the official YouTube TV app refuses to run; SmartTube works.
- Privacy toggles worth flipping as well: settings put secure allow_oaid_used 0 (OAID ad ID),
settings put global individual_privacy_enabled 0 (personalised recommendations).

Xiaomi MiTV4I (codename magnolia), Android TV 9 (SDK 28), firmware PI.3698 release-keys, Amlogic SoC.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.tvlauncher (disabled only after launcher takeover).
Live TV app: com.droidlogic.droidlivetv (preserved for tuner & HDMI).
TV input service: com.droidlogic.tvinput (HDMI 1, HDMI 2, HDMI 3, AV).

Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-mitv4i-magnolia/debloat.txt

tools\disable.ps1 -TvHost <tv ip> examples\xiaomi-mitv4i-magnolia\debloat.txt
tools\restore.ps1 -TvHost <tv ip> examples\xiaomi-mitv4i-magnolia\debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED with `pm disable-user --user 0`, never uninstalled.

Notes:
- Live TV & HDMI inputs are handled by com.droidlogic.droidlivetv and com.droidlogic.tvinput.
Never disable them.

mau.ten: Xiaomi Smart Projector (model C025RGN, codename/product "tianshanrm", board tianshan, FORMOVIE ODM,
mau.header:
Xiaomi Smart Projector (model C025RGN, codename/product "tianshanrm", board tianshan, FORMOVIE ODM,
MediaTek T32 / MT9630), Google TV on Android 14 (SDK 34), firmware build UKNV.260130.001,
security patch 2026-01-01, ro.vendor.mtk.system.marketregion=us, 1920x1080, Wi-Fi only,
Bluetooth remote, ro.adb.secure=1.
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (left enabled; see the handover note below).
The reference launcher takes Home through the Home-key redirect instead, see config.json here.
Factory-disabled on this unit BEFORE anything was changed, so leave both disabled when restoring:
com.mediatek.wwtv.tvcenter        (no tuner on a projector; also the stock LauncherX Live TV entry)
com.google.android.youtube.tvmusic
Prime Video (com.amazon.amazonvideo.livingroom) is ENABLED on this unit, unlike the L1 Pro
(examples/xiaomi-smart-projector-l1-pro-tianshan) where it ships disabled. It is kept here because the
owner uses it, so this list does not disable it.

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-smart-projector-c025rgn/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-smart-projector-c025rgn/debloat.txt
Everything is DISABLED for user 0, never uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

How far this was tested: applied in two batches in one session and checked after one reboot. All 19
were still disabled afterwards and the firmware re-enabled none. Netflix, YouTube, AIS Play, Viu,
Apple Music, the Play Store, Google Assistant, Chromecast, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth remote, focus and keystone
were confirmed working, and the real remote's Home button was pressed. That is one session, not the
several days CONTRIBUTING asks for, so treat this as a starting point rather than a long soak.

Despite the Xiaomi branding (ro.product.brand=Xiaomi) this is a FORMOVIE international Google TV build
on the same tianshan board as the L1 Pro above: there is NO com.xiaomi.*, com.mitv.* or com.miui.*
package on it at all, so no PatchWall, MiChannel, TV Manager or com.xiaomi.tvqs* to disable. Its only
vendor packages are com.fengmi.projector.imaging, com.fengmi.Autopair, com.fengmi.testsuite,
com.fengmi.platform and com.fengmi.fmsettings.

Kept because the projector needs them: com.fengmi.projector.imaging (focus and keystone),
com.fengmi.Autopair (BLE remote pairing), com.fengmi.fmsettings, com.fengmi.platform,
com.mediatek.tv.service, com.mediatek.tvinput, com.mediatek.wwtv.*, com.google.android.tv.inputplayer
(HDMI), com.google.android.tv.remote.service, com.android.bluetooth, com.android.tv.settings.
Kept by choice: com.dolby.android.audio.service, Play Store and Play Services, Gboard, the Google
Assistant (katniss, tv.assistant), Chromecast (com.google.android.apps.mediashell), TalkBack, the
Ambient screensaver (com.google.android.apps.tv.dreamx, the active screensaver_components here),
com.google.android.syncadapters.calendar (the L1 Pro list disables it; this set keeps it),
the three uk.co.freeview.* services, and Netflix, YouTube, Prime Video, Apple Music, AIS Play and Viu.
Never launch com.fengmi.testsuite or mediatek.factorymenu.ui (factory tools; both are present here).
No firmware updater package of its own was found on this build.

One package behaved oddly and is worth knowing about: after `pm disable-user --user 0
com.google.android.videos` reported "new state: disabled-user", `dumpsys package` showed user 0 with
installed=false (the package had been removed for that user, not just switched off). It was put back
with `pm install-existing --user 0 com.google.android.videos` and disabled again, which gave
installed=true and enabled=3 (DISABLED_USER), and `pm list packages -d --user 0` then lists it.
If a restore ever skips it, `pm install-existing --user 0` is the way back.

Launcher handover on Android 14. HOME is resolved by intent priority and the saved default home is
ignored, so `cmd package set-home-activity` prints Success and changes nothing. Measured on this unit
with `cmd package query-activities`:
launcherx/.home.HomeActivity                    priority 2
setupwraith/.RecoveryActivity                   priority 1
a sideloaded launcher                           priority 0
com.android.tv.settings/.system.FallbackHome    priority -1000
The saved Wi-Fi network belongs to com.google.android.tungsten.setupwraith
(dumpsys wifi | grep -o 'cname=[^ ]*') and this projector is Wi-Fi only with no wired fallback, so
disabling setupwraith would take it off the network and off ADB with no way back. setupwraith and
launcherx therefore both stay enabled, and the reference launcher gets Home through the Home-key
redirect: HOME_KEY_SERVICE=1 plus "stock_home_redirect": "com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx"
(config.json in this folder).
Because of that, launcher/build-and-install.sh (and .ps1) stops with "Home resolves to
...launcherx/.home.HomeActivity, not to the new launcher" and exits before it enables the Home-key
service. The APK is installed and working at that point; only the accessibility service still has to be
switched on. Trade-off, the same one the L1 Pro reports: with the helper on, holding Volume Up gives
one step per press instead of a ramp.
Sideloading works here, including a package that declares HOME: no INSTALL_FAILED_VERIFICATION_FAILURE.
Optional extra, not part of this list: Private DNS with an ad-blocking resolver (see README.md at the
repository root).

mau.ten: Xiaomi TV A Pro 75" 2026 (MiTV-MZTU0, codename river, MediaTek), Google TV / Android 14 (SDK 34),
mau.header:
Xiaomi TV A Pro 75" 2026 (MiTV-MZTU0, codename river, MediaTek), Google TV / Android 14 (SDK 34),
firmware UKN1.240806.017.V816.0.25.3.10.URTMIXM. Likely a good start for other 2024+ Xiaomi Google TVs.
Second unit: 55" (same MiTV-MZTU0 / river), India region, firmware UKN1.240806.017.V816.0.26.6.2.6.URTMIXM.
Every active line below applied cleanly there; its own extras are in the commented section at the end.
Live TV app: com.mitv.livetv (set it as live_tv_package and hide it in launcher config.xml).
Stock launcher: com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx (pass it to restore.sh and build-and-install.sh:
STOCK_LAUNCHER=com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx launcher/build-and-install.sh).

Apply:   TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/disable.sh examples/xiaomi-tv-a-pro-2026/debloat.txt
Undo:    TV_HOST=<tv ip> tools/restore.sh examples/xiaomi-tv-a-pro-2026/debloat.txt com.google.android.apps.tv.launcherx
Everything is DISABLED, not uninstalled. Comment out any line you want to keep.

Keep (TV needs them): mitv.service and com.mitv.overseaservice (remote keys, Netflix button, BT remote),
com.mediatek.* (extservice, tv.agent, tis, tuners, airplay), com.mitv.livetv, com.mi.bluetooth,
com.mitv.setup, com.xiaomi.android.tvsetup.partnercustomizer, com.xiaomi.mitv.scenemode (game mode).
Keep (apps, on this model): com.google.android.apps.mediashell. Stremio on Android TV plays
through it; disabling it leaves the Stremio server "online" but no video ever plays.
Already disabled at the factory: com.xiaomi.floatingframe, com.iwedia.tvinput, atsc/isdb tuners.
Default IME is Gboard, no keyboard quirk. 1.8 GB RAM.
Keep com.mitv.gallery if you play USB drives: Media player (com.xiaomi.mitv.mediaexplorer) opens photos
with it (55" unit). Videos play through com.mitv.videoplayer, also kept.

Google TV 14 quirk (the important one): HOME is resolved by intent priority here and the saved
"default home" is ignored. launcherx has priority 2, the setup wizard's RecoveryActivity priority 1,
a sideloaded launcher 0. Disable launcherx alone and Home lands on RecoveryActivity, which
crash-loops system_server (soft reboots every ~60 s, Wi-Fi drops). Shell may not disable that one
activity, so the whole setup wizard package is disabled below; it is only used for first-time setup.
Re-enable it (and launcherx) before a factory reset or to get the Google home back: restore.sh does.
The firmware re-enables com.netflix.ninja by itself (Netflix button), so don't bother disabling it.
